items.title: Affine spaces over a real vector space and displacement vectors
items.statement: Let V be a real vector space. An affine space over V is a nonempty set A together with a map +: A x V -> A such that (a) (p+v)+w = p+(v+w) and p+0 = p for all p in A and v,w in V, and (b) for all p,q in A there is exactly one v in V with p+v = q. That unique v is written q-p and called the displacement from p to q. Then p+(q-p) = q, p-p = 0, p+0 = p, (q-p)+(r-q) = r-p, and for each p in A the map v |-> p+v is a bijection V -> A. If V is 4-dimensional and E: R^4 -> V is a linear isomorphism, then x(p) := E^{-1}(p-o) is a bijection A -> R^4 for each o in A; such maps are the affine coordinate systems on A.
items.strategy: The uniqueness clause (b) is what makes q-p well defined. The identities follow from the action axioms and uniqueness: p+(q-p) = q is the defining property of q-p; p-p = 0 and p+0 = p come from p+0 = p; and p+[(q-p)+(r-q)] = [p+(q-p)]+(r-q) = q+(r-q) = r = p+(r-p) gives (q-p)+(r-q) = r-p by uniqueness. For each p, v |-> p+v is surjective by (b) and injective because an equality p+v = p+w and the action axioms give p+(v-w) = p = p+0, so v-w = 0 by (b) applied at (p,p).

items.title: Lorentz forms of inertia (3,1,0) on a 4-dimensional real vector space
items.statement: Let V be a 4-dimensional real vector space. A Lorentz form on V is a symmetric bilinear form eta: V x V -> R that is nondegenerate (both radicals are {0}) and has inertia (3,1,0): in some (equivalently, by Sylvester's law of inertia, in every) basis diagonalizing eta there are exactly three positive diagonal entries, exactly one negative diagonal entry, and no zero diagonal entry. The associated quadratic form is q(v) := eta(v,v). The pair (V,eta) is called a Lorentz vector space of signature (-,+,+,+).
items.strategy: Nondegeneracy is the statement that the radicals vanish; for finite-dimensional V it is equivalent to invertibility of the matrix of eta in any basis and hence to the absence of zero diagonal entries in every diagonalizing basis (the radical is the kernel of the associated map V -> V*, so its dimension is dim V minus the rank). The inertia (3,1,0) is the Sylvester normal form diag(I_3,-I_1,0_0) of the definition of definiteness/inertia; Sylvester's law makes it basis-independent. No positive-definite structure on V is assumed.

items.title: Timelike, null, spacelike and causal vectors of a Lorentz vector space
items.statement: Let (V,eta) be a Lorentz vector space. A vector v in V is timelike if eta(v,v) < 0, null (or lightlike) if v is nonzero and eta(v,v) = 0, spacelike if eta(v,v) > 0, and causal if it is timelike or null. The zero vector is none of timelike, null or spacelike. The sign of eta(v,v) is the causal character of v. The pairing eta itself is written <v,w> := eta(v,w) when no confusion arises. Each nonzero vector has exactly one causal character.
items.strategy: The classification is by the sign of the real number eta(v,v); the three alternatives eta(v,v) < 0, eta(v,v) = 0, eta(v,v) > 0 for v nonzero are mutually exclusive and exhaustive by trichotomy of the order on R, and the zero vector is excluded from the null case by definition.

items.title: Every Lorentz form admits an ordered basis with matrix diag(-1,1,1,1)
items.statement: Let eta be a Lorentz form on a 4-dimensional real vector space V. There is an ordered basis (e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3) of V with eta(e_a,e_b) = diag(-1,1,1,1)_{ab} for all a,b. Such a basis is called eta-orthonormal; in every eta-orthonormal ordered basis exactly one basis vector is timelike and the other three are spacelike, and the count is the inertia (3,1,0) of eta.
items.strategy: Sylvester's law of inertia supplies a basis in which the matrix of eta is the normal form diag(I_p,-I_q,0_r) with (p,q,r) the inertia of eta. The definition of a Lorentz form gives (p,q,r) = (3,1,0), so the matrix is diag(1,1,1,-1); reindexing the basis puts the single negative entry in the first slot and yields diag(-1,1,1,1). Since inertia is independent of the diagonalizing basis, every eta-orthonormal basis exhibits the same count.

items.title: eta-orthogonality and orthogonal complements in a Lorentz vector space
items.statement: Let (V,eta) be a Lorentz vector space. Vectors u,v are eta-orthogonal, written u orthogonal v, if eta(u,v) = 0. For a subset S of V the orthogonal complement is S^perp := {v in V : eta(v,s) = 0 for all s in S}, and for a vector u one writes u^perp := {u}^perp. For all subsets S the set S^perp is a linear subspace of V, S is contained in (S^perp)^perp, and S^perp = (span S)^perp; in particular u belongs to u^perp exactly when eta(u,u) = 0. Unlike a positive-definite inner product, a nonzero vector can be orthogonal to itself.
items.strategy: Bilinearity gives that S^perp is closed under addition and scalar multiplication (each condition eta(.,s) = 0 is linear), and the containments and the equality S^perp = (span S)^perp follow by linearity in the second argument. The final sentence is witnessed by the classification: any nonzero null vector v satisfies eta(v,v) = 0, so v lies in v^perp.

items.title: Time orientation, future and past timelike/null/causal vectors, and the closed cones
items.statement: Let (V,eta) be a Lorentz vector space and let T := {v in V : eta(v,v) < 0} be its timelike set. By the components lemma T has exactly two connected components; a time orientation of (V,eta) is a choice of one of them. Fixing such a choice and writing C^+ for the chosen component and C^- := T \ C^+ for the other, call v future timelike if v is in C^+, past timelike if v is in C^-, future null if v is nonzero, eta(v,v) = 0 and v lies in the closure cl(C^+), past null if v is nonzero, eta(v,v) = 0 and v lies in cl(C^-), future causal if it is future timelike or future null, and past causal if it is past timelike or past null. The sets cl(C^+) and cl(C^-) are the future and past closed cones; they are convex cones meeting only at 0, and a causal vector is future or past but not both.
items.strategy: Well-definedness rests on the components lemma: T has exactly two components, so 'a choice of one of them' names a definite pair {C^+,C^-}. The claimed properties of the closures (convexity, the intersection {0}, and exclusivity of the future and past causal sets) are proved in the components lemma via the orthonormal coordinate description {v^0 >= |v_vec|} and {v^0 <= -|v_vec|} of the two closed cones.

items.title: The timelike set has exactly two convex components, described in orthonormal coordinates
items.statement: Let (V,eta) be a Lorentz vector space and let (e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3) be an eta-orthonormal ordered basis; write v = v^0 e_0 + v^1 e_1 + v^2 e_2 + v^3 e_3 and |v_vec| := sqrt((v^1)^2+(v^2)^2+(v^3)^2). Then eta(v,v) = -(v^0)^2 + |v_vec|^2, and the timelike set T = {v : eta(v,v) < 0} satisfies T = T_+ union T_- with T_+ := {v : v^0 > |v_vec|} and T_- := {v : v^0 < -|v_vec|}. The sets T_+ and T_- are nonempty, disjoint, open in V, convex and path-connected, and they are exactly the two connected components of T; in every eta-orthonormal basis whose first vector is timelike the same description holds, with the two displayed sets possibly interchanged. Moreover cl(T_+) = {v : v^0 >= |v_vec|}, cl(T_-) = {v : v^0 <= -|v_vec|}, and cl(T_+) intersection cl(T_-) = {0}.
items.strategy: In the orthonormal basis, eta(v,v) = -(v^0)^2 + sum_i (v^i)^2, so eta(v,v) < 0 iff |v^0| > |v_vec|, which is the displayed union; the two sets are disjoint and nonempty (e_0 lies in the first, -e_0 in the second). Convexity of T_+: for u,w in T_+ and t in [0,1], (tu+(1-t)w)^0 = t u^0 + (1-t) w^0 > t|u_vec| + (1-t)|w_vec| >= |t u_vec + (1-t) w_vec| by the triangle inequality; T_- is handled by applying this to -v. Convex sets are path-connected, and T_+ and T_- are open (they are the preimages of (0,inf) under the continuous maps v |-> v^0 - |v_vec| and v |-> -v^0 - |v_vec|). Since T is the disjoint union of two nonempty relatively open connected sets, it is disconnected and these are its two components: any connected subset of T lies in one of them, because a connected subset meeting both would give a separation, while a path in T cannot change the sign of the continuous function v^0 (which is nowhere zero on T) by the intermediate value theorem. The closures are computed by continuity of v^0 -/+ |v_vec|; their intersection consists of vectors with v^0 >= |v_vec| and v^0 <= -|v_vec|, hence of 0 alone. Finally, any two orthonormal bases are related by a linear isomorphism, and the components of T are intrinsic to eta, so the coordinate description agrees with the components up to the naming of T_+ and T_-.

items.title: Oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space (the spacetime primitives)
items.statement: An oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space is a quadruple (A,V,eta,C^+) consisting of: a nonempty affine space A over a 4-dimensional real vector space V (def-affine-space-and-displacement); a Lorentz form eta on V (def-lorentz-form-and-inertia); an orientation of V, i.e. a positive ray of the determinant line Lambda^4 V, fixed once and for all (def-determinant-line-orientation-of-a-finite-dimensional-real-vector-space); and a time orientation C^+ of (V,eta) (def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets). The points of A are called events; q-p is the displacement from p to q; the interval of p,q in A is I(p,q) := eta(q-p,q-p); and p,q are timelike, null, spacelike or causally related when q-p is timelike, null, spacelike or causal, future-related when q-p is future causal, and past-related when q-p is past causal (def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors, def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets). No point of A is distinguished: for every v in V the translation p |-> p+v is a bijection of A preserving all the structure except the labelling of points. All later structure of this framework (frames, charts, tensor fields, worldlines) is built on this model, and no derived physical quantity is part of it.
items.strategy: The definition is a structure specification: the affine action, the form, the orientation and the time orientation are separately defined objects, and the definition only bundles them and fixes the terminology (events, displacement, interval, causal relations). Well-definedness of the bundled data requires the existence and uniqueness statements supplied by the cited items: affine coordinates are available by the affine-space definition, the orthonormal basis needed later exists by the orthonormal-basis lemma, and the two components of the timelike set needed to choose C^+ exist by the components lemma. The translation invariance claim follows from the affine axioms: displacements are unchanged by translations, and translations have identity linear part, so they preserve eta, the orientation and C^+.

items.title: Inertial frames and inertial charts of the affine Minkowski model
items.statement: Let (A,V,eta,C^+) be an oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space. An inertial frame of the model is a tuple (o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3) consisting of an event o in A and an ordered basis (e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3) of V that is eta-orthonormal (eta(e_a,e_b) = diag(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}), future (e_0 is in C^+) and positively oriented (the ordered basis class of (e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3) is the fixed orientation of V). Its inertial chart is the map x: A -> R^4, x(p) := E^{-1}(p-o), where E: R^4 -> V is the linear isomorphism E(u) := sum_a u^a e_a; its components x^a(p) are the inertial coordinates of the event p, and x(p) = 0 exactly at p = o. The family of all inertial frames and charts is the inertial atlas of the model; two inertial charts x, x' are related by x' = M^{-1}(x - x(o')) for M the change-of-basis matrix between the two ordered bases, so transitions are affine bijections of R^4.
items.strategy: Well-definedness requires the existence of eta-orthonormal bases (orthonormal-basis lemma) and the possibility of making them future and positively oriented (existence lemma below). The transition formula follows from the definitions: if e'_a = sum_b M^b_a e_b, then for p = o + sum_a x^a e_a one has p = o' + sum_a x'^a e'_a with x' = M^{-1}(x - x(o')), because applying E'^{-1} to the displacement identity p - o' = (p-o) + (o-o') gives exactly that expression; that x' = 0 iff p = o' is then immediate.

items.title: Existence of future-oriented inertial frames at every event
items.statement: In every oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space (A,V,eta,C^+) and for every event o in A there exists an inertial frame with origin o; consequently inertial charts are defined at every event. Explicitly: start from any eta-orthonormal ordered basis (f_0,f_1,f_2,f_3) of V; if f_0 is not in C^+ then replacing f_0 by -f_0 makes the first vector future (because the timelike set is the disjoint union of C^+ and C^- and eta(-f_0,-f_0) = eta(f_0,f_0)); the resulting ordered basis has some orientation class, and if that class is negative (det M = -1 relative to the fixed orientation) then replacing e_1 by -e_1 (or interchanging e_1 and e_2) produces a positively oriented ordered basis, without destroying eta-orthonormality and without changing the first, future vector.
items.strategy: Apply the orthonormal-basis lemma to get f_0,...,f_3. Since eta(f_0,f_0) = -1 < 0, f_0 lies in the timelike set T = C^+ disjoint-union C^-, so exactly one of f_0, -f_0 lies in C^+. Negating a basis vector preserves eta-orthonormality because eta is bilinear and (-1)^2 = 1, and negating one vector changes the orientation class by the sign of the change-of-basis matrix, which is -1; hence at most one further negation (or the interchange of two vectors, also of determinant -1) makes the ordered basis positively oriented while preserving eta-orthonormality and the future first vector. The origin o is appended freely since frames are allowed any origin.

references.title: H. S. Reall, Part III General Relativity (Cambridge, October 12, 2022 revision), sections 2.1-2.2 pp. 25-28 (PDF pp. 26-29); Internet Archive copy of the original https://www.damtp.cam.ac.uk/user/hsr1000/part3_gr_lectures.pdf

items.title: The affine atlas makes the Minkowski model a smooth 4-manifold diffeomorphic to R^4
items.statement: Let (A,V,eta,C^+) be an oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space and let x: A -> R^4 be one inertial chart. Give A the topology in which a set U is open exactly when x(U) is open in R^4 (the transported topology; it is the unique topology making x a homeomorphism onto R^4). Then: (i) A is a Hausdorff, second-countable topological 4-manifold; (ii) the one-chart family {x} is a smooth atlas, so A is a smooth 4-manifold and x is a diffeomorphism onto R^4 with its standard smooth structure; (iii) every affine chart of A, i.e. every map of the form y(p) = M x(p) + b with M an invertible 4x4 real matrix and b in R^4, and in particular every inertial chart, belongs to the same smooth structure, and its transition with x is the smooth diffeomorphism u |-> M u + b of R^4 with inverse u |-> M^{-1}(u-b); (iv) the topology and smooth structure do not depend on the choice of the initial inertial chart x.
items.strategy: For (i): x is by construction a homeomorphism A -> R^4; R^4 is Hausdorff, second-countable and locally Euclidean, and each of these properties transfers along a homeomorphism (separate points by preimages of disjoint open neighbourhoods; pull back a countable basis; use x itself as a global coordinate chart). For (ii): a one-chart family vacuously satisfies smooth compatibility, so {x} is a smooth atlas; the maximal atlas it generates is the smooth structure, and in this structure the coordinate representation of x is the identity, so x is a diffeomorphism onto R^4 equipped with the standard structure. For (iii): if y = M x + b is an affine chart, then y is a homeomorphism for the same topology and the transition y o x^{-1} is the map u |-> M u + b, whose components are polynomials of degree at most 1 in the coordinates; linear maps and constant maps of R^4 are smooth, and sums of smooth functions are smooth, so y o x^{-1} is smooth (one can differentiate componentwise using the algebra of total derivatives and the theorem that continuous partial derivatives imply total differentiability). Its inverse u |-> M^{-1}(u-b) is again affine and smooth, so y belongs to the same smooth structure; every inertial chart has this form by the transition formula of the frame definition. For (iv): if x' is another inertial chart, then x' = M x + b for an affine map of the displayed form, so the topologies transported by x and x' coincide and the two suggested one-chart atlases generate the same maximal atlas.

items.title: The tangent space of the affine Minkowski model at any event is canonically V
items.statement: Let (A,V,eta,C^+) be an oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space with its smooth structure and let p be an event. For a smooth germ [f] at p define Phi_p(v)([f]) := (d/dt)|_{t=0} f(p+tv). Then Phi_p: V -> T_pA is a linear isomorphism of V onto the tangent space T_pA; in particular T_pA is canonically identified with V, independently of any chart. If x is an inertial chart and v = v^0 e_0 + v^1 e_1 + v^2 e_2 + v^3 e_3, then the coordinate derivations at p correspond under this identification to partial_a = e_a, i.e. Phi_p(v) = sum_a v^a partial_a|_p.
items.strategy: Well-definedness: for a smooth germ [f] the curve c(t) := p + t v has, in the inertial chart x, the coordinate representation x(p) + t u with u = E^{-1} v, hence is smooth; therefore f o c is smooth near 0 and the derivative at 0 exists. Differentiation of products of smooth functions gives Phi_p(v)([fg]) = f(p) Phi_p(v)([g]) + g(p) Phi_p(v)([f]) by the product rule, so each Phi_p(v) is a derivation, and Phi_p is linear in v by the chain rule applied to t |-> x(p) + t u. Injectivity: if Phi_p(v) = 0 and x is an inertial chart at p with coordinates x^a, then applying Phi_p(v) to the germs x^a - x^a(p) gives v^a for each a, so v = 0. Bijectivity: the coordinate derivations partial_0,...,partial_3 form a basis of T_pA, so dim T_pA = 4 = dim V, and an injective linear map between these spaces is an isomorphism. Canonicity: the curve t |-> p + tv is defined by the affine structure alone, so Phi_p does not depend on the chart; the final display follows from the coordinate computation in the chart.

references.title: S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), Ch. 1 pp. 2-7 (PDF pp. 9-14)

items.title: The oriented volume form epsilon and the permutation symbols of an inertial frame
items.statement: Let (A,V,eta,C^+) be an oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space and let (o;e_0,...,e_3) be an inertial frame. For v_0,...,v_3 in V let [v_j^a] be the 4x4 matrix whose j-th column lists the coordinates of v_j in the ordered basis (e_0,...,e_3), and define epsilon(v_0,v_1,v_2,v_3) := det([v_j^a]) in the sense of the determinant of a square matrix. Then epsilon is an alternating 4-linear form on V, called the oriented volume form of the model. Its components in the inertial frame are the permutation symbols epsilon_{abcd}, with epsilon_{0123} = +1 and epsilon_{abcd} the sign of the permutation taking (0,1,2,3) to (a,b,c,d) (zero if two indices repeat). The raised components are epsilon^{abcd} := eta^{aa'} eta^{bb'} eta^{cc'} eta^{dd'} epsilon_{a'b'c'd'}, where eta^{ab} is the inverse of the matrix eta_{ab}; epsilon^{0123} = -1. The spatial permutation symbol epsilon_{ijk} for i,j,k in {1,2,3} is defined by epsilon_{123} = +1 together with alternation.
items.strategy: epsilon is the determinant of the coordinate matrix of (v_0,...,v_3); the determinant is multilinear and alternating in the columns, hence epsilon is an alternating 4-linear form. Its components in the frame are by definition the determinant values, i.e. the permutation-sign symbols; epsilon^{0123} computes to eta^{00}eta^{11}eta^{22}eta^{33} epsilon_{0123} = (-1)(+1)(+1)(+1)(+1) = -1 because the inverse metric is diagonal in an eta-orthonormal frame. Well-definedness of epsilon as a form of the model, independent of the inertial frame used, is proved in the frame-independence lemma.

references.title: S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), Ch. 1 pp. 2-7 (PDF pp. 9-14)
B. Crowell, Special Relativity, rev. 2020-12-10, sections 1.3-1.4 pp. 23-31 and Ch. 2 pp. 43-51 (signature (+---) converted to (-+++))

items.title: The oriented volume form is independent of the positively oriented inertial frame
items.statement: The alternating 4-linear form epsilon of def-oriented-minkowski-volume-form does not depend on the inertial frame used to define it: if (e'_0,...,e'_3) is another inertial frame and e'_a = sum_b M^b_a e_b is the change-of-basis matrix, then det M = +1 (both ordered bases are positively oriented) and the coordinate matrices X, X' of a tuple (v_0,...,v_3) in the two frames satisfy X' = M^{-1} X, so det X' = det(M^{-1}) det X = det X. Consequently epsilon(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3) = 1 for every inertial frame, epsilon is the unique alternating 4-linear form on V taking value 1 on every positively oriented eta-orthonormal basis, and in every inertial frame the raised component epsilon^{0123} equals -1.
items.strategy: From eta(e'_a,e'_b) = eta_{ab} and e'_a = sum_b M^b_a e_b one gets the matrix identity M^T eta M = eta; taking determinants and using det eta = -1 gives (det M)^2 = 1, so det M = +1 or -1, and the orientation clause selects det M = +1. The coordinate columns of a fixed tuple in the two bases are related by X' = M^{-1} X, so multiplicativity of the determinant and det(M^{-1}) = (det M)^{-1} give det X' = det X; this is exactly the frame independence, and it also shows the normalized value 1 on the frame itself. Uniqueness of the normalized alternating 4-linear form is the uniqueness clause for the determinant as a normalized alternating multilinear function, transported to V by the coordinate isomorphism E. The raised component computation is the diagonal evaluation given in the definition.

items.title: SI units and coordinate conventions of the special-relativity framework
items.statement: This framework fixes the following SI coordinate and unit conventions. In every inertial chart the coordinates are x^0 = c t, x^1, x^2, x^3, where c > 0 is the adopted conversion constant in metres per second and the spatial coordinates are measured in metres along the frame's orthonormal spatial directions; all four x^a carry the unit metre, the matrix of eta in an inertial chart is diag(-1,1,1,1) with dimensionless entries, and the interval I(p,q) carries the unit m^2. For a timelike displacement the number tau := c^{-1} sqrt(-eta(q-p,q-p)) has the unit second and is the proper time of the straight timelike segment from p to q. A timelike worldline's four-velocity U = dx/dtau has unit m/s, four-acceleration m/s^2, four-momentum kg m/s, and observer energy joule. If instead a chart uses a temporal coordinate t in seconds, then the corresponding metric component is g_tt = -c^2 with unit m^2/s^2 and the mixed time-space components acquire the unit m/s; formulas derived in one convention are not reused unchanged in the other. Natural units (c = 1) may be used only together with an explicit restoration table for c. The numerical value of c is an empirical parameter of the model; SI unit status does not make a quantity primitive in this theory.
items.strategy: A convention definition: it fixes the coordinate normalization (x^0 = ct rather than t), the unit of each component, and the dimensional interpretation of the interval, of proper time along a timelike straight segment and of the derived kinematic quantities, all relative to the adopted model and its inertial charts. The dimensional statements follow by inspection of the inertial coordinate expressions out of the diagonal form of eta, and the warning about the temporal-coordinate convention records where the components change dimension.

The item declares units and dimensional bookkeeping only; it makes no claim that any quantity is fundamental in other frameworks and supplies no empirical measurement of c.

items.title: Adopted inertial covariance of the model equations
items.statement: Adopt as a physical assumption of this framework: (i) the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space (A,V,eta,C^+) is the spacetime of the framework; its points represent idealized physical events, displacements represent idealized spacetime separations, and the sign classification of eta is the adopted causal structure; (ii) the equations of the specific mechanical and electromagnetic models developed from this framework are covariant under the affine maps F: A -> A whose linear part L satisfies eta(Lv,Lw) = eta(v,w) for all v,w in V, has determinant +1 relative to the adopted orientation, and maps C^+ onto C^+; such maps are the inertial changes of description. These assumptions are adopted, not deduced from experiment nor from the verbal postulates of Einstein, and they define the framework's scope. Covariance is asserted for the specified model equations only: it does not select a force or matter law, does not forbid explicitly adopted background structure by a purely syntactic test, and carries no claim that the physical world is exactly described by the model.
items.strategy: A postulate, not a theorem: the item records the adopted formulation (affine Minkowski geometry with a fixed orientation and future cone) and the adopted covariance of the framework's model equations under future- and orientation-preserving eta-isometries of V. The maps are characterized by their defining properties rather than by a named group; the group structure, factorization and algebra of these maps are established on the Lorentz-transformations page. The exposition must state the scope limitation that covariance is a property of the specified model equations and neither proves the model nor selects dynamics.

items.physical_scope: Flat classical spacetime with ideal events; inertial descriptions related by affine maps preserving eta, orientation and the future cone. Excludes gravity (no curvature), global accelerated-frame structure, and quantum effects. Covariance is claimed only for the mechanical and electromagnetic model equations specified in this framework.

items.title: Adopted ideal-clock and ideal-vacuum-light interpretation
items.statement: Adopt as physical assumptions of this framework: (i) Ideal clocks. Along a curve x: I -> A whose coordinate representation in an inertial chart is C^1 with everywhere future timelike derivative, an ideal clock carried along the curve reads, between parameters a < b in I, the elapsed time sigma(b) - sigma(a) = c^{-1} integral_a^b sqrt(-eta(x'(s),x'(s))) ds; there is no additional acceleration-dependent term in the reading (clock hypothesis). (ii) Ideal light. In vacuum, ideal light rays are exactly the future null straight lines {p + lambda v : lambda in R} with p in A and v a future null vector; in every inertial chart x^a such a ray has x(lambda) = x(p) + lambda (v^0,v^1,v^2,v^3) and coordinate speed c, so the adopted conversion constant c is the same in all inertial charts. Scope: ideal apparatus, complete vacuum, and the geometric (nondispersive) ray regime. The assumptions are adopted, not experimentally proved; no dispersive medium is described; no quantum photon model is assumed and in particular frequency is not identified with energy by a factor hbar; and real clocks and light are not claimed to be exactly ideal.
items.strategy: A postulate, not a theorem: it fixes the physical interpretation of the mathematical objects (future timelike curves, future null straight lines) and the reading rule of an ideal clock, together with the exact scope of the idealization. The integral is well defined because the integrand -eta(x',x') is positive and continuous on a compact parameter interval for a future timelike C^1 curve; parametrization invariance and the resulting proper-time parametrization, as well as the general theory of worldlines, four-velocity and acceleration, are developed on the later worldlines-and-clocks page, which may not depend on this page by a forward edge; the postulate therefore states the reading rule for the model rather than a theorem about curves.

items.physical_scope: Ideal clocks and ideal vacuum light rays in flat classical spacetime, in the geometric optics regime with ideal apparatus. Excludes dispersive media, gravitational effects, quantum effects, and any claim that real clocks or light rays are exactly ideal; experimental agreement would be evidence about the specified model, not a proof of these postulates.

items.title: The Euclidean spatial structure and cross product of an inertial frame
items.statement: Let (A,V,eta,C^+) be an oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space and let (o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3) be an inertial frame. Put S := span(e_1,e_2,e_3) = {w in V : eta(e_0,w) = 0} and let delta be the restriction of eta to S. Then delta is a positive-definite symmetric bilinear form on S (the Euclidean spatial form of the frame), |w| := sqrt(delta(w,w)) is a norm on S, and (e_1,e_2,e_3) is a delta-orthonormal positively oriented ordered basis of S. Writing w = w^1 e_1 + w^2 e_2 + w^3 e_3, define the vector product w x z as the unique element of S with components ((w x z)^1,(w x z)^2,(w x z)^3) = (w^2 z^3 - w^3 z^2, w^3 z^1 - w^1 z^3, w^1 z^2 - w^2 z^1). Then delta(w x z, y) equals the determinant of the coordinate matrix with columns w,z,y for every y in S, and |w x z|^2 = |w|^2 |z|^2 - delta(w,z)^2. All these objects belong to the positive spatial three-space of the named inertial frame: they are equivariant under orientation-preserving spatial rotations of the frame and are not invariant under a general Lorentz map. The invariant structure of the model remains eta alone.
items.strategy: Since (e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3) is eta-orthonormal, for w = sum_i w^i e_i one has eta(e_0,w) = 0 and eta(w,w) = sum_i (w^i)^2, so the restriction delta is positive definite and (e_1,e_2,e_3) is delta-orthonormal; positivity of eta(w,w) on S also shows S = e_0^perp. The vector product is well defined by its displayed coordinate formula, and the identity delta(w x z,y) = det(w,z,y) is Lagrange's identity for the cross product in an orthonormal basis; the norm identity is the same computation in coordinates. Frame dependence: a general eta-orthonormal frame has a different time axis e_0 and hence a different S, so the construction depends on the frame; the final sentence records that only eta is invariant.

items.title: Primitive and derived notions of the spacetime-primitives page
items.statement: Status audit of the framework's adopted and derived notions, required before derived claims. Primitive mathematical structure of the model (def-sr-affine-minkowski-model): the affine space A with its action of V, the Lorentz form eta, the orientation of V and the time-orientation component C^+. Primitive physical interpretation and parameters adopted on this page: the physical event interpretation and the covariance assumption (post-sr-inertial-covariance); the ideal-clock and ideal-vacuum-light interpretation (post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light); and the conversion constant c, whose numerical value is empirical and whose unit is fixed by def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions. Derived (constructed, not adopted) on this page: displacements and intervals; the causal classification of displacements; inertial frames and their charts; the smooth structure; the oriented volume form; and the spatial Euclidean structure of a named inertial frame. Not introduced on this page and not primitive in its scope: proper time along general worldlines, four-velocity and four-acceleration, momentum, energy, charge and any force or matter law; later pages introduce their own adopted premises and must repeat this audit for them. The mathematical statements of this page concern the stipulated geometry only and do not assert that the model describes nature.
items.strategy: A status remark: it repeats, without proof obligations, the primitive/derived classification of the page's objects as required by the framework content model, and separates the mathematically constructed structure from the physically adopted interpretation. It carries no claim beyond that bookkeeping.

items.physical_scope: Bookkeeping remark for the spacetime-primitives page of the flat classical special-relativity framework: it classifies the page's notions as adopted or derived and asserts no physical law and no empirical claim.

items.title: Proper acceleration of a massive worldline and its agreement with the acceleration of an observer congruence
items.statement: Let c > 0 and let x: I -> A be a C^2 future timelike worldline with four-velocity U = dx/dtau and four-acceleration A = dU/dtau (def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration), so that eta(U,U) = -c^2 and eta(U,A) = 0 pointwise, and A(s) is spacelike whenever it is nonzero (thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition (a),(b)). (a) Definition. The proper acceleration of x at the parameter value s is the real number a(s) := sqrt(eta(A(s),A(s))), the nonnegative square root of def-rational-power. This is well defined for every s in I: if A(s) = 0 then eta(A,A) = 0, and if A(s) is nonzero then it is spacelike and eta(A,A) > 0 (def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors); in both cases the argument of the square root is nonnegative, so a(s) is a nonnegative real number. With the SI coordinate and unit conventions of def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions, in which x^0 = c t with t in seconds and the spatial coordinates are in metres while eta has the dimensionless matrix diag(-1,1,1,1) in an inertial chart, the components of A carry the unit metre per second squared and eta(A,A) carries the unit (metre per second squared)^2, so a carries the unit metre per second squared. The worldline is uniformly accelerated when a is constant on I. (b) Agreement with the acceleration of a congruence. Let Omega be a nonempty open subset of A and let n: Omega -> V be an observer congruence with acceleration field a_cg := nabla_n n, where nabla is the flat covariant derivative of def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space (def-sr-observer-congruence-and-kinematics (b)). If x is a flow line of n and U = c n along x, then A = c^2 a_cg along x, and consequently a = c^2 sqrt(eta(a_cg,a_cg)) along x: the proper acceleration is c^2 times the magnitude of the congruence acceleration. In particular the proper acceleration of a congruence worldline is determined by the congruence field alone, and such a worldline is uniformly accelerated exactly when eta(a_cg,a_cg) is constant along it. (c) Reading and scope. This item defines a quantity of the model and fixes its name, its unit and its physical reading. The model reads a(s) as the magnitude that an ideal accelerometer carried along the worldline would register at the event x(s); this ideal-instrument identification is adopted with the model in the same sense as the framework's ideal-clock reading of proper time and is not derived here. No accelerometer response law, calibration, frequency dependence, force law or interaction is specified or asserted; the definition asserts nothing about which bodies follow which worldlines; no measurement outcome and no statistical, uncertainty or empirical claim is made. No choice principle is used.
items.strategy: Definition with its well-definedness and its unit and congruence clauses justified by the cited suppliers. (a) A is continuous because x is C^2 (def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline, def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration (b)); eta(A,A) is the sum of products of continuous component functions in any inertial chart (def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart, thm-algebra-of-continuous-functions); eta(A,A) >= 0 pointwise by thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition (b) together with the classification of nonzero spacelike vectors by def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors. Hence sqrt(eta(A,A)) is well defined for every s as the nonnegative real whose square is eta(A,A) (def-rational-power). Units are read off directly from def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions, which lists the unit metre per second squared for the four-acceleration and the dimensionless matrix diag(-1,1,1,1) for eta in an inertial chart. (b) If U = c n along x with c a constant, then A = dU/dtau = c d(n o x)/dtau; the derivative of the field n along the worldline is the covariant derivative nabla_{dx/dtau} n = nabla_{cn} n = c nabla_n n = c a_cg by the defining properties of the flat covariant derivative along curves (def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space (d)); hence A = c^2 a_cg and eta(A,A) = c^4 eta(a_cg,a_cg), so a = c^2 sqrt(eta(a_cg,a_cg)) because c > 0. The acceleration a_cg is spacelike or zero by def-sr-observer-congruence-and-kinematics (b), so eta(a_cg,a_cg) >= 0. (c) The scope clause records that the accelerometer reading is an ideal-instrument identification of the model and that no apparatus, force or measurement model is asserted; this mirrors the treatment of clock readings in post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light and of wave frequencies in def-sr-null-wave-covector-and-observer-frequency. No choice principle is used. Here s denotes the original arbitrary parameter in I; d/dtau denotes the quotient by the positive proper-time derivative tau'(s), or equivalently the derivative of the field reparametrized on tau[I]. For a flow line with U=cn, (n o x)'/tau'=nabla_{x'/tau'} n=nabla_{cn}n, so the unchanged factor c^2 in(b) holds for every allowed parametrization, not only when I itself is labelled by proper time.

items.physical_scope: Conditional kinematic definition inside the flat classical special-relativistic model: the proper acceleration of a C^2 future timelike worldline, its SI unit, and its identification with the magnitude of an ideal accelerometer reading. It presupposes ideal clocks and rods and the model's SI conventions; it asserts no force law, no accelerometer response or calibration model, no gravity, no rotational or quantum effect and no measurement, statistical or empirical content, and it makes no claim about any material body.

items.title: The uniformly accelerated worldline: hyperbolic motion, constant four-acceleration magnitude, and identification as a Rindler flow line
items.statement: Let c > 0 and alpha > 0, set R := c^2/alpha, and let (A,V,eta,C^+) be the affine Minkowski space with an inertial chart chi = (chi^0,chi^1,chi^2,chi^3), chi^0 = c t (def-sr-affine-minkowski-model, def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart). Let x: R -> A be the curve x(tau) := chi^{-1}(R sinh theta, R cosh theta, 0, 0), where theta := alpha tau/c. (a) Regularity, causal character and parametrization. x is C^infinity, and x'(tau) = c(cosh theta, sinh theta, 0, 0) is future timelike for every tau (def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors, def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets), so x is a future timelike worldline (def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline). Since eta(x',x') = -c^2 is constant, the parameter tau is a proper-time parameter of the curve: the based proper-time function T_x of def-sr-proper-time satisfies T_x(b) - T_x(a) = b - a for all a < b in R (def-sr-proper-time, lem-sr-proper-time-parametrization), and the four-velocity is U := dx/dtau = c(cosh theta, sinh theta, 0, 0) with eta(U,U) = -c^2 (def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration, thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition (a)). (b) Constant four-acceleration magnitude. The four-acceleration A := dU/dtau = alpha(sinh theta, cosh theta, 0, 0) satisfies eta(A,A) = alpha^2 and eta(U,A) = 0. The chart coordinate velocity is dchi^1/dt = c tanh theta, so |dchi^1/dt| < c for every tau, and chi^1 = R cosh theta > R|sinh theta| = |chi^0| for every tau: the worldline lies in the right wedge W := {chi^1 > |chi^0|} and its speed in the chart tends to c only as tau -> +-infinity. (c) Rindler flow line. Let Phi(theta,rho,y,z) := (rho sinh theta, rho cosh theta, y, z) on R x (0,inf) x R^2 and let n := rho^{-1} partial_theta be the Rindler congruence of thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples (b), whose pullback metric is -rho^2 dtheta^2 + drho^2 + dy^2 + dz^2 and whose congruence acceleration a_cg := nabla_n n is rho^{-1} partial_rho, with eta(a_cg,a_cg) = rho^{-2} (def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space, def-sr-observer-congruence-and-kinematics). Then chi o x is exactly the coordinate flow line Phi(., R, 0, 0) reparametrized by theta = alpha tau/c, i.e. x=chi^{-1} o Phi along that line, and along x one has A = c^2 a_cg: the four-acceleration of the worldline is c^2 times the congruence acceleration, and eta(a_cg,a_cg) = 1/R^2 = alpha^2/c^4 on the flow line rho = R. (d) Asymptotic behaviour. Along x one has chi^1 - chi^0 = R e^{-theta} -> 0 with chi^0 -> +infinity as tau -> +infinity, and chi^1 + chi^0 = R e^{theta} -> 0 with chi^0 -> -infinity as tau -> -infinity: the worldline approaches each of the null planes {chi^1 = chi^0} and {chi^1 = -chi^0} asymptotically without meeting either, and the chart coordinate speed tends to c at both ends. (e) Scope. This is an exact kinematic computation in the affine model. It uses no force law, no mass, no clock hypothesis and no empirical input; beyond identifying the displayed parameter with the proper time of the curve, only the flow parametrization of the congruence is used. The curve is not asserted to be a geodesic and no statement is made about the forces that would maintain it. No choice principle is used.
items.strategy: Exact computation with the hyperbolic identities and their derivatives. (a) Differentiating the two components of x with the chain rule (thm-chain-rule, def-derivative) and thm-hyperbolic-identities-and-derivatives gives x' = c(cosh theta, sinh theta, 0, 0); cosh > 0 makes it future and eta(x',x') = c^2(-cosh^2 + sinh^2) = -c^2 (def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors, def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets). The integrand of def-sr-proper-time is the constant c, so its integral over [a,b] is c(b-a) and T_x(b) - T_x(a) = b - a; the assertions about the four-velocity then follow from lem-sr-proper-time-parametrization (iv) and thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition (a). (b) Differentiating U gives A = alpha(sinh theta, cosh theta, 0, 0); eta(A,A) = alpha^2(cosh^2 - sinh^2) = alpha^2 and eta(U,A) = c alpha(-cosh sinh + sinh cosh) = 0 (thm-hyperbolic-identities-and-derivatives); the chart velocity is dchi^1/dt = (dchi^1/dtau)/(dt/dtau) = c sinh/cosh = c tanh, and cosh > |sinh| gives the wedge and the speed bound. (c) Direct comparison: Phi(theta, R, 0, 0) = (R sinh theta, R cosh theta, 0, 0) = chi(x(tau)) with theta = alpha tau/c, and the congruence data are those of thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples (b); the identity A = c^2 a_cg is proved directly on the flow line: since dx/dtau = c n there, d(n o x)/dtau = nabla_{dx/dtau} n = c nabla_n n = c a_cg by the defining properties of the flat covariant derivative along curves (def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space (d)), so A = dU/dtau = c d(n o x)/dtau = c^2 a_cg. (d) The identities chi^1 -+ chi^0 = R(cosh -+ sinh) = R e^{-+theta} and e^{+-theta} -> 0 (thm-exponential-limits-and-range) give the limits; tanh -> +-1 gives the speed statement. (e) Scope only. No choice principle is used: all steps are finite-dimensional algebra and calculus. The symbol x denotes the A-valued curve and chi the chart throughout. All displayed tuples for x', U and A are their V-valued components in chi's ordered frame; chi^a in the along-curve formulas means chi^a o x. The based clock function T_x(tau)=tau+constant does not rebind the curve parameter tau.

items.title: The material metric of a congruence: evolution of rest separations and preservation of the internal metric under Born rigidity
items.statement:
Let $\Omega$ be a nonempty open subset of affine Minkowski space $A$, $c>0$, and let $n:\Omega\to V$ be a $C^1$ future unit timelike field, $\eta(n,n)=-1$. Define the following first-order quantities in any inertial chart:
$$h^a{}_b:=\delta^a{}_b+n^an_b,\qquad h_{ab}:=\eta_{ab}+n_an_b,\qquad a^b:=n^c\partial_cn^b,\qquad\theta_{ab}:=h_a{}^ch_b{}^d\partial_{(c}n_{d)},$$
where symmetrization means half the sum, $n_a:=\eta_{ab}n^b$, and $h(v,w):=h_{ab}v^aw^b$. Here $h$ is $C^1$ and $a,\theta$ are continuous. The rest projection $h(v):=v+\eta(n,v)n$ is as in [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]](c). For $C^1$ fields and tensors define
$$(L_nh)_{ab}:=n^c\partial_ch_{ab}+h_{cb}\partial_an^c+h_{ac}\partial_bn^c.$$
These first-order coordinate formulas transform tensorially under affine inertial chart changes and agree, on smooth fields, with [[def-sr-observer-congruence-and-kinematics]], [[def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space]] and the ordinary smooth Lie derivative. Say the $C^1$ field is Born rigid when $L_nh=0$; the identity $L_nh=2\theta$ makes this equivalent to $\theta=0$.
(a) Let $J$ be a nonempty open interval, $B\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ a nonempty open set, and $\Phi:J\times B\to\Omega$ an injective $C^2$ immersion with $\partial_s\Phi=n(\Phi)$. Put $e_I:=\partial_{\xi^I}\Phi$, $I=1,2,3$, and $G_{IJ}(s,\xi):=h(e_I,e_J)$ at $\Phi(s,\xi)$. Then $n,e_1,e_2,e_3$ are linearly independent, $G$ is symmetric positive definite at every point, and its entries are $C^1$. Thus for each $s$ it is a $C^1$ positive-definite material metric on $B$. If $n$ and $\Phi$ are smooth, $G$ is a smooth Riemannian metric, as in the original smooth branch.
(b) For all $I,J$,
$$\partial_sG_{IJ}=(L_nh)(e_I,e_J)=2\theta(e_I,e_J),\qquad\partial_\tau G_{IJ}=2c\theta(e_I,e_J),$$
where $\tau=s/c$ is the proper-time parameter along each flow line, whose four-velocity is $cn$. For a nonzero label direction $e_I$, put $\ell_I:=\sqrt{h(e_I,e_I)}>0$ and $u_I:=h(e_I)/\ell_I$. This $u_I$ is a horizontal unit rest vector, and
$$\partial_\tau\ell_I=c\theta(u_I,u_I)\ell_I.$$
The alternative normalized material vector $e_I/\ell_I$ need not be horizontal, but has the same $\theta$ contraction because $\theta$ is horizontal. Positive/negative expansion gives positive/negative fractional change of this material rest length per proper time.
(c) If $\theta=0$, then $\partial_sG_{IJ}=0$ and $G_{IJ}(s,\xi)$ is constant in $s$ for each fixed label, with no restriction on material-label separation: the entire internal metric is preserved exactly. Conversely, a nonzero contraction $\theta(e_I,e_J)$ gives a nonzero derivative of that metric component at the point and hence nonconstancy on a neighborhood. The smooth Born-rigid branch and its original conclusions are included.
(d) This is a local statement about the given family and its material metric. Integrating the material metric at a common flow parameter gives an internal label-space length; it does not identify that length with a finite endpoint distance on a single observer's orthogonal simultaneity hyperplane without an additional argument. No matter model, elasticity, field equation, global rigidity theorem, boundary condition or choice principle is used.
items.strategy:
Use only first derivatives of $n$ and two derivatives of $\Phi$. The coordinate rules are tensorial under constant Lorentz changes of inertial coordinates by [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]]; for smooth data they agree with the established smooth definitions. Differentiating $\eta(n,n)=-1$ gives $n_b\partial_an^b=0$, hence $\eta(n,a)=0$. Expansion of the projected symmetrization gives
$$2\theta_{ab}=\partial_an_b+\partial_bn_a+n_aa_b+a_an_b.$$
Differentiating $h_{ab}=\eta_{ab}+n_an_b$ in the displayed first-order Lie formula gives exactly this right side, proving $L_nh=2\theta$. The projectors make $\theta$ horizontal in both slots.
For the material fields, equality of the mixed partials of $C^2$ components of $\Phi$ ([[thm-clairaut-schwarz-mixed-partials]]) and the total chain rule ([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]]) give
$$\partial_se_I^a=\partial_{\xi^I}n^a(\Phi)=(\partial_bn^a)(\Phi)e_I^b.$$
Differentiating $G_{IJ}=h_{ab}(\Phi)e_I^ae_J^b$ by the product rule gives the displayed coordinate formula for $(L_nh)(e_I,e_J)$, and thus $\partial_sG_{IJ}=2\theta(e_I,e_J)$. This direct calculation does not invoke a smooth-only Lie-bracket supplier for $C^1$ fields. In the smooth branch, the same mixed-partial identity is the usual commuting material-coordinate calculation $[n,e_I]=0$ ([[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]], [[prop-coordinate-formula-for-the-lie-bracket]]), and recovers the original smooth route.
The derivative of $\Phi$ has four independent columns by immersion, so no nonzero linear combination of the three $e_I$ lies in $\operatorname{span}(n)$. The rest projection has that one-dimensional kernel and is positive definite on $n^\perp$ ([[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]](c)); hence $G$ is positive definite. $h(\Phi)$ and $e_I$ are $C^1$, so $G$ is $C^1$, and smooth if all data are smooth. Along a flow line $\partial_s\Phi=n$ is nonzero future timelike, and the proper-time definition gives $d\tau/ds=\sqrt{-\eta(n,n)}/c=1/c$, so $\partial_\tau=c\partial_s$ ([[def-sr-proper-time]], [[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]]). Apply the chain rule to $\ell_I^2=G_{II}$: $\partial_\tau\ell_I=c\theta(e_I,e_I)/\ell_I$. Since $h(e_I)-e_I$ is parallel to $n$, horizontality gives $\theta(e_I,e_I)=\ell_I^2\theta(u_I,u_I)$, proving the fractional-rate formula. If $\theta=0$, the interval zero-derivative corollary [[cor-zero-derivative-implies-constant]] proves constancy for each fixed label. A nonzero derivative prevents local constancy. All claims, including the smooth special case, are proved with the stated finite regularity and no zero tangent is called timelike.

items.title: The Rindler chart: causal horizons of a uniformly accelerated observer and the restrictions of radar time and distance
items.statement: Adopt post-sr-inertial-covariance, post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light and post-sr-causal-signal-propagation, and the SI conventions of def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions (x^0 = c t). Let x = (x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3) be the chart of an inertial frame (def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart) and let W := {x^1 > |x^0|} be the right wedge. Let Phi and n be the Rindler chart and congruence of thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples (b): Phi(theta,rho,y,z) = (rho sinh theta, rho cosh theta, y, z) on R x (0,inf) x R^2 with inverse rho = sqrt((x^1)^2 - (x^0)^2), theta = (1/2) log((x^1+x^0)/(x^1-x^0)), pullback metric -rho^2 dtheta^2 + drho^2 + dy^2 + dz^2, and acceleration field a_cg = nabla_n n = rho^{-1} partial_rho. Fix rho_0 > 0 and real y_0,z_0, and let O be the congruence worldline rho = rho_0, y = y_0, z = z_0, parametrized by its proper time tau with theta = c tau/rho_0; by def-sr-proper-acceleration its proper acceleration is c^2/rho_0. Write U(q) := q^0 + q^1 and V(q) := q^0 - q^1 for events q, so that U = rho e^{theta} and V = -rho e^{-theta} on W, and write <= and J^+, J^- for the causal reachability relations of def-sr-causal-reachability-in-affine-minkowski-space. Then, conditionally on the adopted model: (i) Chart domain and light rays. Phi is a smooth bijection of R x (0,inf) x R^2 onto W with the stated smooth inverse, so the chart domain is exactly W and rho = 0 is not part of its coordinate domain. The boundary of W in the affine model is {x^1 = |x^0|}, with arbitrary x^2,x^3: it is the union of the two null half-planes {x^1 = x^0 >= 0} and {x^1 = -x^0 >= 0}. These half-planes are portions of the full null planes appearing as causal horizons in (ii); the full planes are not the wedge boundary. Along the worldline rho = rho_0 one has V = -rho_0 e^{-theta} -> 0^- and U -> +infinity as theta -> +infinity, while U = rho_0 e^{theta} -> 0^+ and V -> -infinity as theta -> -infinity. The future null straight lines of the model that lie in the plane y = y_0, z = z_0 and meet O are exactly the lines of constant V (on which dtheta = +drho/rho) and the lines of constant U (on which dtheta = -drho/rho). (ii) Causal horizons. An event q satisfies q <= p for some event p of O if and only if V(q) < 0; an event q satisfies p <= q for some event p of O if and only if U(q) > 0. Consequently no event with V(q) >= 0 can ever influence O; this set contains the null plane {x^1 = x^0}, the left wedge {x^1 < -|x^0|} and the future wedge {x^0 > |x^1|}; and no event with U(q) <= 0 can ever be influenced by O, a set containing the null plane {x^1 = -x^0}, the left wedge and the past wedge {x^0 < -|x^1|}. The null plane {x^1 = x^0} is the boundary of the causal past of O (the future horizon: the surface its worldline approaches as theta -> +infinity), and the null plane {x^1 = -x^0} is the boundary of the causal future of O (the past horizon); every event of the left wedge is causally unrelated to O in both directions. The same criteria with O any other congruence worldline rho = rho_1, y = y_1, z = z_1 hold verbatim: the constants rho_0, y_0, z_0 do not enter. (iii) Radar time and distance to a coaxial congruence reflector. Fix rho_m > 0 with rho_m != rho_0 and let R_m be the congruence worldline rho = rho_m, y = y_0, z = z_0 (a second uniformly accelerated observer, coaxial with O, with proper acceleration c^2/rho_m). Let e_- be the event of O at parameter theta_e (so tau(e_-) = rho_0 theta_e/c up to the base point of tau), let q_m be the event of R_m lying on the future null straight line from e_- in the plane y = y_0, z = z_0, and let e_+ be the event of O lying on the future null straight line from q_m; the reflection at q_m is idealized as instantaneous and as leaving R_m's motion unchanged, as in def-sr-operational-radar-protocol. Then e_-, q_m, e_+ exist uniquely, the Rindler time of q_m is theta_m = theta_e + |log(rho_m/rho_0)|, the return event satisfies theta(e_+) = theta_e + 2|log(rho_m/rho_0)| and (theta_e + theta(e_+))/2 = theta_m, so the round trip lasts 2|log(rho_m/rho_0)| in Rindler time and (2rho_0/c)|log(rho_m/rho_0)| in O's proper time. The radar protocol therefore assigns to q_m the radar time tau_rad(q_m) = (rho_0/c) theta_m plus the base constant of tau and the radar distance rho_rad(q_m) = rho_0 |log(rho_m/rho_0)|; within this coaxial family the radar-time level sets are exactly the Rindler simultaneity slices theta = const, i.e. the rest slices of the congruence (def-sr-simultaneity-slice-and-rest-distance). The radar distance is not the rest distance: in the slice theta = theta_m the two worldlines are at rest distance |rho_m - rho_0|, whereas for rho_m = 2rho_0 the radar distance is rho_0 log 2 < rho_0, because log is strictly increasing and e > 2 implies log 2 < log e = 1 (cor-two-less-than-e-less-than-three, thm-natural-logarithm-laws); For every distinct positive reflector radius the notions differ: with $r=\rho_m/\rho_0$, one has $\log r<r-1$ when $r>1$ and $-\log r>1-r$ when $0<r<1$. The two distance formulas agree only at $r=1$, where both have the continuous degenerate value zero. The coincident case is not a nonzero emission-reflection-reception triple of the protocol, whose distinct-reflector hypothesis remains in force. As rho_m -> 0^+ the round-trip proper time and the radar distance grow without bound while the reflector's proper acceleration c^2/rho_m diverges; as rho_m -> +infinity the round-trip proper time and the radar distance also grow without bound while the reflector's proper acceleration tends to 0. (iv) Restrictions of the protocol. No event with V >= 0 - in particular no event of the horizon plane {x^1 = x^0}, of the left wedge or of the future wedge - can be assigned a radar time or radar distance by this protocol from O, because by (ii) it cannot causally precede any reception event on O: the required reflection-to-reception leg is impossible. Separately, every event with U <= 0 lacks an emission-to-reflection leg from O. Thus any event admitting this radar triple must satisfy U > 0 and V < 0, equivalently it must belong to W; the horizon is at infinite radar distance in the limit rho_m -> 0^+. For example q = x^{-1}(2rho_0,0,y_0,z_0) has U(q)=V(q)=2rho_0>0. It is causally after O at theta=0, since the displacement is (2rho_0,-rho_0,0,0), future timelike, and it even lies on a future null ray from O at theta=log 2, with displacement (5rho_0/4,-5rho_0/4,0,0). Nevertheless it cannot send a causal return to O, so receives no radar assignment from O. The protocol therefore does not extend to a global coordinate system of A. (v) Scope. All clauses are conditional computations and readings in flat classical spacetime with ideal clocks, ideal light rays and ideal reflectors, for the specified congruence worldlines. They are not empirical claims and contain no measurement, apparatus, source, detector or statistical content; gravitation, media, dispersion, finite resolution, quantum effects and material models of the reflector are excluded. No choice principle is used.
items.strategy: Instantiate the causality lemmas of the causal model in the Rindler chart. (i) The chart assertions are those of thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples (b), together with the identities U = rho e^{theta}, V = -rho e^{-theta}: on a line of constant V one has rho = rho_0 e^{theta - theta_0}, so dtheta = drho/rho and ds^2 = -rho^2 dtheta^2 + drho^2 = 0 exactly, and the tangent with increasing theta has positive time component, so the line is future null; on a line of constant U one has rho = rho_0 e^{theta_0 - theta} and dtheta = -drho/rho, and again ds^2 = 0 with a future tangent (def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors, def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets, post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light). The limits along rho = rho_0 use the defining exponentials. The wedge boundary follows from the continuous inequality x1>|x0|: its closure is x1>=|x0|, since a boundary point is approached by increasing x1 by a positive amount. Thus the boundary is x1=|x0|, comprising only the indicated half-planes; at fixed finite theta, rho tending to zero does not parametrize the entire boundary. (ii) Write p(theta)=(rho_0 sinh theta,rho_0 cosh theta,y_0,z_0), Up=rho_0 e^theta, Vp=-rho_0 e^(-theta), and r^2=(q^2-y_0)^2+(q^3-z_0)^2. For a displacement D, the future causal coordinate criterion is equivalent to DeltaU>=0, DeltaV>=0 and DeltaU DeltaV>=r^2: D0=(DeltaU+DeltaV)/2, D1=(DeltaU-DeltaV)/2 and D0^2-D1^2=DeltaU DeltaV. For q<=p, necessity gives Vp-Vq>=0, hence Vq<=Vp<0. Conversely if Vq<0, as theta tends to +infinity the difference Vp-Vq tends to the positive number -Vq and Up-Uq tends to +infinity. Therefore both differences are positive and their product exceeds the fixed r^2 for sufficiently large theta; the coordinate criterion proves q<=p. For p<=q, necessity gives Uq-Up>=0, hence Uq>=Up>0. Conversely if Uq>0, as theta tends to -infinity the difference Uq-Up tends to the positive number Uq and Vq-Vp tends to +infinity; again their product eventually exceeds r^2 and p<=q follows. These complete arguments include arbitrary transverse positions. The full planes V=0 and U=0 are respectively the boundaries of these open causal unions; direct coordinate signs give the left/future/past wedge inclusions. The signal reading is conditional on post-sr-causal-signal-propagation, and the criteria do not depend on rho_0,y_0,z_0. (iii) The null line of constant V through e_- has rho = rho_0 e^{theta-theta_e}, which is increasing in theta; it meets rho = rho_m at theta_m = theta_e + log(rho_m/rho_0) when rho_m > rho_0. The null line of constant U through e_- has rho = rho_0 e^{theta_e-theta}, decreasing in theta; it meets rho = rho_m at theta_m = theta_e + log(rho_0/rho_m) when rho_m < rho_0. In both cases the displacement from e_- to q_m is a positive multiple of (1,1,0,0) or (1,-1,0,0), hence future null, and theta_m = theta_e + |log(rho_m/rho_0)|. From q_m the return line is the other null family: it reaches rho = rho_0 at theta(e_+) = theta_m + |log(rho_m/rho_0)| = theta_e + 2|log(rho_m/rho_0)|, again along a future null displacement, and uniqueness holds because through a point of the plane there passes exactly one future null line of each family and a fixed congruence worldline is met by such a line in exactly one event. The proper time of O between the two events is rho_0 (theta(e_+) - theta_e)/c by def-sr-proper-time and lem-sr-proper-time-parametrization applied to the unit-tangent flow line; def-sr-operational-radar-protocol converts the round trip into radar time (tau(e_-)+tau(e_+))/2 and radar distance c(tau(e_+)-tau(e_-))/2, giving the displayed values. The comparison with the rest distance uses the slice metric drho^2 + dy^2 + dz^2 of thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples (b) and def-sr-simultaneity-slice-and-rest-distance; the numerical case rho_m = 2rho_0 uses log 2 < 1, which follows from e > 2, log e = 1 and strict increase of log (cor-two-less-than-e-less-than-three, thm-natural-logarithm-laws). For the full equality classification, put $r=\rho_m/\rho_0>0$. By thm-logarithm-derivative-and-integral, log is differentiable on $(0,\infty)$ with derivative $1/u$, and therefore continuous there by cor-differentiable-implies-continuous. If $r>1$, cor-mean-value-theorem on $[1,r]$ gives $\xi\in(1,r)$ with $\log r=(r-1)/\xi<r-1$. If $0<r<1$, the same theorem on $[r,1]$ gives $\xi\in(r,1)$ with $-\log r=(1-r)/\xi>1-r$. Multiplying by $\rho_0>0$ proves radar distance strictly smaller than rest distance for an outer reflector and strictly larger for an inner reflector. Only $r=1$ gives zero in both formulas. Their continuity at $r=1$ follows from continuity of log and absolute value; this is the degenerate formula extension, not an assertion that a zero-length null leg satisfies the distinct-reflector protocol. The limits as rho_m -> 0^+ and rho_m -> +infinity follow from |log| -> +infinity and from c^2/rho_m. (iv) A radar triple requires e_-<=q and q<=e_+ with e_-,e_+ on O, indeed both displacements null in the protocol. By (ii), Vq>=0 makes q<=e_+ impossible, while Uq<=0 makes e_-<=q impossible. This is a return obstruction in the former case and an emission obstruction in the latter; both are needed for the round trip. The displayed q=(2rho_0,0,y_0,z_0) has future timelike displacement (2rho_0,-rho_0,0,0) from O(0), norm -3rho_0^2<0. O(log2) has coordinates (3rho_0/4,5rho_0/4,y_0,z_0), yielding the displayed future null displacement to q. Since Vq=2rho_0>0 no causal return to O exists. The infinite radar distance as rho_m decreases to zero is the logarithmic limit in (iii), not a spacetime singularity. (v) Scope only. No choice principle is used.
