No force law, self-field or extended-body structure is included, and null curves are excluded from massive-particle uses.

items.title: The microscopic vacuum Maxwell equations: smooth and weak branches
items.statement:
Adopt as a physical postulate of this framework the following four equations for the fields of [[def-em-fields]] and the sources of [[def-em-sources]] on the laboratory region $U\cong I\times\Omega$ of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], with $\mu_0>0$, $c>0$, $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ and the SI units of [[def-em-si-conventions]]. (a) [Smooth branch] Let $E,B$ be jointly $C^1$ fields with the additional derivatives required by each equation existing and continuous, and let $\rho,J$ be continuous. Then, with the divergence and curl of [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]] and the partial derivative $\partial_t$ at fixed position of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]],

$$\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0,\qquad \operatorname{div}B=0,\qquad \operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB,\qquad \operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE.$$

(b) [Weak branch] Let instead $E,B$ be locally integrable $\mathbb R^3$-valued fields and $\rho,J$ locally integrable scalar and vector fields on $I\times\Omega$, paired with tests by their regular distributions ([[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]]). For each given locally integrable component this pairing and its order-zero continuity are choice-free: on compact K its absolute value is bounded by sup_K|psi| times the finite integral of its absolute value, and [[thm-local-finite-order-characterization-of-distributions]] applies. The further identification as a faithful embedding of almost-everywhere equivalence classes, and the strong local-L1 embedding interface of [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]], use exactly its additional assumption of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]); they are not prerequisites for merely writing the given-L1 weak pairings. Let $\operatorname{div}$, $\operatorname{curl}$ and $\partial_t$ act as distributional derivatives, and let $\psi$ range over $C_c^\infty(I\times\Omega)$ ([[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]]). Then the same four identities hold in the sense of [[def-distribution]]: the pairings $\langle\operatorname{div}E-\rho/\varepsilon_0,\psi\rangle$, $\langle\operatorname{div}B,\psi\rangle$, $\langle\operatorname{curl}E+\partial_tB,\psi\rangle$ and $\langle\operatorname{curl}B-\mu_0J-c^{-2}\partial_tE,\psi\rangle$ vanish for every such $\psi$, all derivatives being distributional derivatives ([[def-distributional-derivative]]). (c) [Scope] The postulate contains no magnetic charge: $\operatorname{div}B=0$ and no magnetic-source term appears in $\operatorname{curl}E$. Sources that are not locally integrable functions (point or sheet sources) are covered by neither branch and require their own definition. The equations are adopted classical vacuum physics in the named inertial chart; they are not deduced from charge conservation, from empirical agreement or from the special-relativity postulates, and this item by itself asserts no covariance under changes of inertial frame.
items.strategy: A postulate, not a theorem. Obligations and conventions: the fields and sources are those of [[def-em-fields]] and [[def-em-sources]], the operators are the published divergence and curl of [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]] and the partial derivative of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]], and the weak reading uses the given-L1 regular pairing, the test space and distributional derivative named in the statement. The compact-support absolute-integral bound and the choice-free local finite-order criterion prove continuity without invoking injectivity. Only a faithful a.e.-quotient identification invokes the Countable Choice assumption of the actual embedding theorem; the smooth and given-L1 pairing branches do not acquire that extra premise. The exposition must state that the four equations are adopted, that the choice of the sign and constant conventions is the one fixed by [[def-em-si-conventions]], and that no magnetic charge is included; the sources not covered by either branch are excluded explicitly. Empirical support for Maxwell's equations is a nonlogical relation of the framework, not a proof, and no verification is claimed here.

items.title: The electromagnetic two-form, its observer decomposition and the four-current
items.statement:
Let the laboratory region, its inertial chart and the fields and sources be those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], [[def-em-fields]] and [[def-em-sources]], with the units of [[def-em-si-conventions]]; fix the ordered basis $(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ of the chart and the oriented volume form $\varepsilon$ of [[def-oriented-minkowski-volume-form]], with $\varepsilon_{0123}=+1$ and $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$. (a) [Components] For a field pair $(E,B)$ of class $C^k$, $k\ge1$, define the covariant components of the electromagnetic two-form $F$ in the chart by $F_{00}=0$, $F_{0i}:=-E_i/c$, $F_{ij}:=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$ ($i,j,k\in\{1,2,3\}$) and $F_{ab}:=-F_{ba}$, the index-raised components being $F^{0i}=E_i/c$, $F^{i0}=-E_i/c$ and $F^{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$. Then $F$ is a $C^k$ type-$(0,2)$ tensor field on $U$ in the sense of [[def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space]], alternating at every event, and the components above are exactly its component functions. (b) [Observer decomposition] Let $n:=e_0$ be the future unit timelike vector of the chart and let $e_a:=F_{ab}n^b$, $b_a:=(*F)_{ab}n^b$ be the observer components of [[thm-sr-antisymmetric-observer-decomposition]]; then $e_i=+E_i/c$, $b_i=-B_i$ and $e_0=b_0=0$, and the invariants and square wedge of that theorem read $	frac12F_{ab}F^{ab}=|B|^2-|E|^2/c^2$, $F_{ab}(*F)^{ab}=+4\,(E\cdot B)/c$ and $F\wedge F=-2\,(E\cdot B)\,\varepsilon/c$, where $|\cdot|$ and $\cdot$ are the spatial Euclidean structure of the frame. (For the same pair $(E,B)$, that theorem's optional clause (d) uses $F_{m optional}^{i0}=E_i/c$ and $F_{m optional}^{ij}=-\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$, so $F_{m optional}=-F$ in all six components, not only the magnetic block. This framework fixes clause (a) and uses the theorem's general algebra; its optional SI dictionary must be converted by negating the entire tensor.) (c) [Potentials when they exist] If $\varphi$ and $A$ are $C^1$ with $E=-
abla\varphi-\partial_tA$ and $B=\operatorname{curl}A$, and $A^\mu:=(\varphi/c,A)$, $A_\mu:=\eta_{\mu
u}A^
u$, then $F_{\mu
u}=\partial_\mu A_
u-\partial_
u A_\mu$; conversely, if a $C^1$ covector field $A_\mu$ on $U$ satisfies $F_{\mu
u}=\partial_\mu A_
u-\partial_
u A_\mu$, then $E,B$ recovered from $F$ by clause (a) obey $E=-
abla\varphi-\partial_tA$ and $B=\operatorname{curl}A$ with $\varphi:=-cA_0$ and the spatial potential vector $A:=(A_1,A_2,A_3)$. The definition does not assert that every field pair admits such a potential; where a $C^1$ potential represents the $C^1$-or-better field of clause (a), the field is closed in the explicit sense $\partial_\lambda F_{\mu
u}+\partial_\mu F_{
u\lambda}+\partial_

(d) [Four-current and index-raising operator] With the adopted four-current $j=(cho,J)$ of [[def-em-sources]], the raised-index operator $\Phi$ of [[lem-em-antisymmetric-tensor-contraction]], defined pointwise on $V$ by $\eta(\Phi(u),w)=F(w,u)$, satisfies $\Phi(u)^\mu=\eta^{\mu\alpha}F_{\alpha eta}u^ eta$; the components of $F$ carry the tesla (T), those of $j$ carry A m$^{-2}$, and those of a four-potential $A^\mu$ carry T m.
items.strategy:
An explicit definition computed from the components. The components $F_{ab}$ of clause (a) are $C^k$ functions of the inertial coordinates, because they are built from the $C^k$ functions $E_i,B_k$ and the constants $c,\epsilon_{ijk}$; hence $F$ is a $C^k$ tensor field by the component criterion of [[def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space]], and it is alternating because $F_{ab}=-F_{ba}$ by construction. Clause (b) is a direct substitution into clauses (a)-(c) of [[thm-sr-antisymmetric-observer-decomposition]] with $n=e_0$: $e_i=F_{i0}=+E_i/c$, $b_i=-	frac12\epsilon_{ijk}F_{jk}=-B_i$, the invariants $	frac12F_{ab}F^{ab}=|b|^2-|e|^2$ and $F_{ab}(*F)^{ab}=-4\,e\cdot b$ are evaluated with these values, and the square wedge uses the theorem's normalisation $F\wedge F=2\,(e\cdot b)\,\varepsilon$. For the same E,B, the optional tensor in the supplier is the negative of the entire adopted tensor; no magnetic-only sign conversion is used. Clause (c) is the component computation $F_{0i}=\partial_0A_i-\partial_iA_0=(\partial_tA_i+\partial_i\varphi)/c=-E_i/c$ and $F_{ij}=\partial_iA_j-\partial_jA_i=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$ with $B=\operatorname{curl}A$, together with the inverse reconstruction; the non-existence of potentials on general regions is not asserted either way. For closedness retain the field regularity $F\in C^1$ from clause (a) and allow the potential to be only $C^1$. Put $H_{\lambda\mu
u}=\partial_\lambda F_{\mu
u}+\partial_\mu F_{
u\lambda}+\partial_
u F_{\lambda\mu}$, which is continuous. For each smooth compactly supported real test $\psi$, integrate by parts with its compactly supported factor using [[lem-sr-compact-variation-and-fundamental-lemma]] (b): $\int H\psi=-\int[F_{\mu
u}\partial_\lambda\psi+F_{
u\lambda}\partial_\mu\psi+F_{\lambda\mu}\partial_
u\psi]$. Substitute $F=dA$ and integrate by parts once more, now with the compactly supported first derivatives of $\psi$, to obtain $\int A_
u(\partial_\mu\partial_\lambda\psi-\partial_\lambda\partial_\mu\psi)+A_\mu(\partial_\lambda\partial_
u\psi-\partial_
u\partial_\lambda\psi)+A_\lambda(\partial_
u\partial_\mu\psi-\partial_\mu\partial_
u\psi)=0$. Only the smooth test derivatives are commuted, by [[thm-clairaut-schwarz-mixed-partials]], not nonexistent second classical derivatives of $A$. The continuous fundamental lemma [[lem-sr-compact-variation-and-fundamental-lemma]] (a) makes $H=0$ pointwise. This is the complete weak mixed-derivative cancellation using compact Riemann test identities, with no choice assumption and no narrowing to $C^2$ potentials. The spatial curl/gradient dictionary is the exact coordinate definition [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]] at fixed time. Clause (d) restates the raised-index operator of [[lem-em-antisymmetric-tensor-contraction]] and the units of [[def-em-si-conventions]]. No physical law is proved and no empirical claim is made.

items.title: Superposition for prescribed Maxwell fields and sources
items.statement: Assume the vacuum Maxwell postulate [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] on the laboratory region $U\cong I\times\Omega$ of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] with the fields of [[def-em-fields]] and the sources of [[def-em-sources]], and fix the constants $\mu_0>0$, $c>0$, $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ of [[def-em-si-conventions]]. Let $n\ge1$, let $(E_1,B_1,\rho_1,J_1),\dots,(E_n,B_n,\rho_n,J_n)$ be $n$ field-source pairs each satisfying one and the same branch of the postulate on the same region (all in the smooth branch, or all in the weak branch), and let $a_1,\dots,a_n\in\mathbb R$. Put $E:=\sum_{j=1}^na_jE_j$, $B:=\sum_{j=1}^na_jB_j$, $\rho:=\sum_{j=1}^na_j\rho_j$ and $J:=\sum_{j=1}^na_jJ_j$. Then: (a) $(E,B,\rho,J)$ satisfies the same branch of the postulate on the same region with the same constants: pointwise in the smooth branch and in the sense of the pairings of clause (b) of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] in the weak branch. (b) Nothing beyond this linearity is asserted: the result does not apply to a source whose density depends nonlinearly on the fields (a nonlinear constitutive law), and no convergence statement is made for infinite series or integrals of solutions or for infinite linear combinations. (c) The theorem is conditional on the adopted postulate and is not an empirical claim about nature.
items.strategy: **Proof technique:** direct termwise computation, smooth branch and distributional branch separately. In the smooth branch, the divergence and curl are linear in their arguments because they are finite sums of first partial derivatives ([[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]), and $\partial_t$ is linear likewise; hence $\operatorname{div}E=\sum_ja_j\operatorname{div}E_j=\sum_ja_j\rho_j/\varepsilon_0=\rho/\varepsilon_0$ and, in the same way, $\operatorname{div}B=0$, $\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB$ and $\operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE$. In the weak branch the distributional derivatives are linear and the pairings are linear in the distributions ([[def-distribution]], [[def-distributional-derivative]]), so the four vanishing pairings of the postulate for the sum follow by summing the finitely many vanishing pairings of the summands with the same test function. The scope clauses (nonlinear sources, no infinite superposition) are recorded in the theorem itself; no physical premise beyond the postulate is used, and no empirical premise occurs, so no empirical qualifications are inherited beyond the postulate's own.

items.physical_scope: Superposition of finitely many prescribed Maxwell field-source pairs on a common laboratory region, within the adopted vacuum Maxwell postulate, in either its smooth or its weak branch. The theorem excludes nonlinear constitutive laws and makes no convergence claim for infinite superpositions; it is a conditional deduction and not an empirical claim, and it inherits only the postulate's physical assumptions.

items.title: The Lorentz coupling: external force on a test charge and the continuum force and power densities
items.statement:
Adopt as physical postulates of this framework, on the spacetime and particle model of [[post-em-minkowski-physical-model]] and [[def-em-relativistic-worldlines-frames]] and on the special-relativity particle model [[post-sr-massive-particle-dynamics]]: (i) [Test charge in a prescribed external field] Let $q\in\mathbb R$ be a constant charge parameter ([[def-em-sources]]), $m>0$ an externally supplied rest mass, $x:J\to A$ a future timelike $C^2$ massive worldline with four-velocity $U$, and let $F$ be a prescribed field of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] that is $C^1$ on a neighbourhood of the graph of $x$ and is generated externally to the particle. Adopt the equation of motion

$$m\,\frac{dU}{d\tau}=q\,\Phi(U),$$

where $\Phi$ is the raised-index operator of the field at the event $x(\tau)$, defined by $\eta(\Phi(u),w)=F(w,u)$ ([[lem-em-antisymmetric-tensor-contraction]]); equivalently $m\,dU^\mu/d\tau=q\,F^{\mu\nu}U_\nu$. The particle's own field is excluded from $F$: this is the external-field coupling, and it defines no self-force. (ii) [Continuum matter coupling] For a smooth source $(\rho,J)$ of [[def-em-sources]] interacting with the field through an explicitly stated matter model to which this coupling applies, adopt the force density $\rho E+J\times B$ (unit N m$^{-3}$) and the power density $J\cdot E$ (unit W m$^{-3}$) as the electromagnetic source terms of that matter model; they describe the local interaction of the field with matter and are not a property of a prescribed current alone. (iii) [Scope] The rest mass and the charge are inputs; $m$ is not derived within electromagnetism. The coupling is adopted for constant $q$ and $m>0$; no magnetic-monopole coupling, no radiation reaction and no self-force are included. In particular the nonrelativistic coordinate statement $mr''=q(E+r'\times B)$ is not adopted as exact: the adopted statement is the covariant one of clause (i), and any low-speed statement requires its own approximation hypotheses and error bounds.
items.strategy: A postulate, not a theorem. The exposition must state the exact data (constant charge, externally supplied positive rest mass, future timelike C^2 worldline, prescribed external field C^1 near the graph), name the raised-index operator $\Phi$ with its defining identity and index form from [[lem-em-antisymmetric-tensor-contraction]] so that the equation is unambiguous, and state the exclusion of the particle's own field. Clause (ii) is a formulation premise for matter models, with its units fixed by [[def-em-si-conventions]] and its cross product the spatial one of [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]; it is not a derivation from the field equations. Clause (iii) records the scope: no self-force, no radiation reaction, no magnetic monopole, and no exact Newtonian law. Empirical support for the coupling is a nonlogical relation of the framework; the item claims no verification and no measured value.

items.physical_scope: The adopted coupling of the classical framework between the electromagnetic field and matter: the covariant equation of motion of a test charge in a prescribed external field with constant charge and positive rest mass, and the continuum force and power densities for a matter model to which the coupling applies. The postulate excludes self-fields, radiation reaction, magnetic monopoles and any exact nonrelativistic law; it is a model assumption and not an experimental result.

items.title: Localization of a continuous function by axis-parallel cube integrals
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), the convention of the Lebesgue-measure interface used below ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $n\ge1$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open and let $g:U\to\mathbb R$ be continuous. Suppose that $\int_Qg\,d\lambda_n=0$ for every closed axis-parallel cube $Q=\prod_{i<n}[a_i,a_i+\ell]$ with $\ell>0$ and $Q\subseteq U$, the integral being that of [[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]]. Then $g=0$ on $U$. In particular, for $n=2$, a continuous function on an open subset of the plane whose integral over every closed axis-parallel square contained in its domain vanishes is identically zero. The hypothesis requires all such cubes with every centre and every side length; a single cube or only the cubes centred at one fixed point do not suffice. For the latter restriction, on $U=\mathbb R^n$ the nonzero continuous function $g(x)=x_1-p_1$ integrates to zero over every cube centred at $p$ by cancellation in its first coordinate. This restriction differs from testing all cubes that merely contain $p$.
items.strategy: The Countable Choice convention is the Lebesgue interface of [[thm-lebesgue-measure-of-a-box-of-every-kind]] and [[def-countable-choice]]. Suppose $g(p)\ne0$ for some $p\in U$; replacing $g$ by $-g$ if necessary, assume $g(p)>0$. By continuity at $p$ ([[def-metric-continuity]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]], [[def-metric-ball]]) choose $\delta>0$ with $B(p,\delta)\subseteq U$ and $g(x)>g(p)/2$ whenever $d(x,p)<\delta$. The closed cube $Q:=p+[-\delta/(2\sqrt n),\delta/(2\sqrt n)]^n$ satisfies $Q\subseteq B(p,\delta)$, has side length $\ell=\delta/\sqrt n>0$ and satisfies $g\ge g(p)/2$ on $Q$. By [[thm-lebesgue-measure-of-a-box-of-every-kind]], $\lambda_n(Q)=(2\delta/(2\sqrt n))^n=\ell^n>0$; the continuous $g$ is Borel measurable ([[cor-continuous-functions-are-borel-measurable]]) and bounded on the compact cube $Q$ ([[thm-extreme-value-metric]]), so the signed integral over $Q$ is defined ([[def-integrable-real-and-complex-functions-and-their-integrals]]). Monotonicity and the scalar rules ([[thm-monotonicity-of-the-integral]], [[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]]) give $\int_Qg\ge\int_Q(g(p)/2)\,d\lambda_n=(g(p)/2)\lambda_n(Q)>0$, contradicting the hypothesis $\int_Qg=0$. Hence $g(p)=0$ for every $p\in U$. The planar clause is the case $n=2$. No regularity beyond continuity, and no choice beyond $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is used.

references.title: J. K. Hunter, Measure Theory (UC Davis lecture notes)
references.locator: Sets of finite measure, measure of boxes; the localization argument uses only continuity, the positive measure of a nondegenerate cube and monotonicity of the integral, as in the notes' treatment of continuity and measure.

references.title: T. Tao, An Introduction to Measure Theory (GSM 126), section 1.2
references.locator: Section 1.2, measure of boxes and the elementary properties of Lebesgue measure used in the localization argument.

items.title: Surface densities with vanishing test pairings vanish
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), the convention of the surface-measure interface cited below ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open, let $S\subset\Omega$ be a compact embedded $C^2$ hypersurface in the sense of [[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]], and let $a:S\to\mathbb R$ be continuous. If $\int_Sa\psi\,dS=0$ for every $\psi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$ ([[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]]), then $a=0$ on $S$. Equivalently, if two continuous densities on $S$ pair equally against every test function, they are equal pointwise on $S$. The conclusion is pointwise and uses the continuity of $a$; a merely locally integrable density would satisfy only an almost-everywhere conclusion, which this statement does not claim.
items.strategy: Assume the stated Countable Choice convention. If $a(x_0)\ne0$, replace $a$ by $-a$ if needed and put $m=a(x_0)/2>0$. Continuity of $a$ on $S$ gives an ambient neighbourhood $N$ of $x_0$ on which $a\ge m$ on $S\cap N$. By the embedded $C^2$ hypothesis, the inverse/implicit-function suppliers give, after permuting coordinates, a graph chart $X(u)=(u,g(u))$ on an open $D\subset\mathbb R^2$ with $X(u_0)=x_0$ and $g\in C^2(D)$. Choose an open ambient chart neighbourhood $O\subset\Omega\cap N$ containing $x_0$, meeting $S$ only in this graph chart. Choose $0<r<R$ with $\overline B_R(x_0)\subset O$. The actual ambient bump supplied by [[lem-scaled-euclidean-bumps-with-compact-support-and-gradient-bound]] is a function $\psi\in C_c^\infty(B_R(x_0))$, $0\le\psi\le1$, equal to one on $\overline B_r(x_0)$; extended by zero it is in $\mathcal D(\Omega)$ by [[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]]. There is no product-extension assertion for arbitrary planar tests. By continuity of $X$, choose a closed nondegenerate parameter square $C\subset D$ around $u_0$ with $X(C)\subset B_r(x_0)$. The graph density is $J_X=\sqrt{1+|\nabla g|^2}\ge1$ by [[lem-surface-integral-is-independent-of-c-one-boundary-charts]]. The surface measure and restriction to Borel chart subsets are exactly those of [[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]]; chart independence lets the integral of a function supported in $S\cap O$ be computed in this chart. Equivalently one may choose a compact Jordan region $C'\Subset D$, obtained as a finite union of closed parameter squares lying in $D$ and covering the compact parameter preimage of its support and use [[thm-surface-integrals-over-c-one-graphs]] followed by [[lem-riemann-lebesgue-comparison-for-distribution-test-integrands]] for the continuous graph integrand on $C'$. On the support of $\psi|_S$ we have $a\ge m$, and $\psi=1$ on $X(C)$. Consequently monotonicity gives $\int_S a\psi\,dS\ge m\int_{X(C)}1\,dS=m\int_C J_X\,d\lambda_2\ge m\lambda_2(C)>0$; [[thm-lebesgue-measure-of-a-box-of-every-kind]] gives $\lambda_2(C)=\ell^2>0$. This contradicts the given zero pairing. Every $x_0\in S$ therefore has $a(x_0)=0$, and applying this to the difference proves the equal-density clause. The compact embedded $C^2$ interface here is within the published compact embedded $C^1$ surface-measure class, with no change to its measure convention; in particular the closed stationary interfaces used by the jump theorem are covered. No new Choice principle is used. The empty-surface case is immediate.

items.title: Fixed volume and patch test geometries, outward normals and induced orientations
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), the convention already carried by the imported finite piecewise $C^1$ boundary presentations and by the compact $C^1$ surface measure cited below ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $U\cong I\times\Omega$ be the laboratory region of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], with $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ open and $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ a nonempty open interval. This definition fixes the time-independent spatial test geometries of the integral form of the Maxwell equations.

(a) [Volume test geometry] A volume test geometry in $\Omega$ is a pair $(V,\nu_V)$ where $V\subseteq\Omega$ is a nonempty bounded open set with $\overline V\subseteq\Omega$ and a specified finite piecewise $C^1$ presentation of its boundary ([[def-bounded-piecewise-c-one-euclidean-domain]]) and $\nu_V$ is the outward unit normal of that presentation off its edge set ([[def-bounded-c-one-domain-boundary-charts-and-outward-normal]]). The closed-surface flux of a field $F$ continuous on a neighbourhood of $\overline V$ is the finite face sum
$$\oint_{\partial V}F\cdot\nu_V\,dS:=\sum_j\int_{S_j}F\cdot\nu_V\,dS,$$
with the face surface integrals of [[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]]. For every closed axis-parallel box $K=\prod_{i<3}[a_i,b_i]\subseteq\Omega$ with $a_i<b_i$, its open interior $V=\prod_{i<3}(a_i,b_i)$ is a volume test geometry and $\overline V=K$. Its natural six-face presentation is the boundary of $K$, with outward normals $\pm e_i$. The volume variable is $V$, while $K$ denotes its compact closure. Each face is a degenerate three-dimensional box and hence has $\lambda_3$-measure zero by [[thm-lebesgue-measure-of-a-box-of-every-kind]]; their finite union $K\setminus V$ is null. Thus for continuous $h$ on a neighbourhood of $K$, $\int_Vh\,d\lambda_3=\int_Kh\,d\lambda_3$: the positive and negative integrals over the null difference vanish by [[cor-integral-over-a-null-set-vanishes]] and [[def-integrable-real-and-complex-functions-and-their-integrals]].

(b) [Patch test geometry] A patch test geometry in $\Omega$ is a regular $C^2$ surface patch $(D,r)$ over a finite elementary Green region in the sense of [[def-the-induced-boundary-chain-of-a-c2-surface-patch]] ([[def-type-i-type-ii-and-elementary-green-regions]], [[def-admissible-regular-parametrized-surface-patch]]): $D\subseteq\mathbb R^2$ is a finite elementary Green region, $r$ is of class $C^2$ on an open neighbourhood of $D$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]), $r_u\times r_v\ne0$ on the interior of $D$ ([[def-cross-product-in-r3]]) and no interior parameter point shares its image with a distinct point of $D$. Its induced boundary chain $\partial S=r(\partial D)$ and its circulation $\oint_{\partial S}F\cdot d\mathbf r$ for a field continuous on the image are those of [[def-the-induced-boundary-chain-of-a-c2-surface-patch]] ([[def-scalar-and-vector-line-integrals-along-piecewise-c1-paths]]); its oriented flux of a field $F$ continuous on the image is
$$\int_SF\cdot n_S\,dS:=\int_D(F\circ r)\cdot(r_u\times r_v)\,dudv,$$
the scalar Riemann integral of the continuous integrand on the compact Jordan parameter region, in the orientation induced by $r$ ([[def-oriented-unit-normal-and-flux-of-a-surface-patch]]). The pair $(D,r)$ is part of the data. Every affine graph patch $r(u,v)=(u,v,\varphi(u,v))$ over an axis-parallel square $D=[c_1,c_1+\ell]\times[c_2,c_2+\ell]$ with $\ell>0$, whose graph lies in $\Omega$ with $\varphi$ affine (for instance constant), and more generally every affine regular patch over such a square, is a patch test geometry: the square is a finite elementary Green region, and $r$ is smooth and regular with $\varphi_u,\varphi_v$ constant.

(c) [Regularity convention] When an integral identity of this framework is asserted for a volume test geometry $V$, respectively for a patch test geometry $S$, with respect to a field $F$ of stated class $C^k$, it concerns fields defined and of class $C^k$ on an open neighbourhood of $\overline V$ in $\Omega$, respectively of the image $r[D]$ in $\Omega$; when the identity involves a time derivative of a flux, the field is defined with the stated regularity on a neighbourhood of that compact set times the compact time interval of the assertion. No regularity away from these neighbourhoods is asserted.

(d) [Conventions and scope] Test geometries are fixed spatial subsets of $\Omega$ and carry no motion. A patch's orientation is the one induced by its parametrization, and its induced boundary chain has the compatible orientation of [[def-the-induced-boundary-chain-of-a-c2-surface-patch]], so that the classical Stokes theorem applies with a plus sign. The definition retains the $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ convention of the imported boundary and surface-measure definitions; it asserts no differential equation, no physical law and no existence of fields.
items.strategy: An explicit type/domain/convention definition. Clause (a) composes the imported finite piecewise $C^1$ presentation with its outward normal and the compact-hypersurface face integral; the open box interior, with compact closure $K$, is verified as an instance by listing its six faces (each a compact subset of a regular $C^1$ hypersurface patch, namely a coordinate plane), its twelve edges and eight vertices as the edge set, and noting that the face-edge intersections have surface measure zero and that outside the edges the boundary is locally a coordinate $C^1$ graph with the box on one side. Clause (b) composes the $C^2$ patch over a finite elementary Green region with the induced boundary chain and the oriented patch flux; an affine graph over an axis-parallel square is verified as an instance because a rectangle is both a type $I$ and a type $II$ region with the natural elementary decomposition, so the square carries a finite elementary Green presentation. Clause (c) is a regularity convention recording that all integral identities of this page quantify over fields on neighbourhoods of the compact test sets, which is exactly the hypothesis class of the imported divergence and Stokes theorems. Clause (d) records the orientation and countability conventions and states explicitly that the definition introduces no physical law. Nothing here asserts that every bounded domain is admissible, that a disc is a legal parameter region, or that a physical test geometry is realised by an apparatus. The requirement $\overline V\subseteq\Omega$ makes clause (c)'s existing neighbourhood requirement explicit and restores the canonical definition contract. The closed-box integral bridge follows from the six degenerate faces being volume-null and the signed-integral definition, independently of their nonzero surface areas.

items.title: Distributional Maxwell equations with point and stationary-sheet sources
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), the convention of the surface-measure interface inherited from [[def-em-surface-distribution]] ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $U\cong I\times\Omega$ be the laboratory region of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] with the units and constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]], and let $\mathcal D'(U)$ be the space of distributions on $U$ ([[def-distribution]], [[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]]); recall that the pairing $\langle T,\psi\rangle$ is bilinear with no conjugation and that the distributional partial derivatives are $\langle\partial_\mu T,\psi\rangle=-\langle T,\partial_\mu\psi\rangle$ ([[def-distributional-derivative]]).

(a) [Fields as distributions] Locally integrable fields and source densities on $U$ are identified with their regular distributions ([[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]], [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]]).

(b) [Point sources] Let $I_0\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open interval, let $z:I_0\to\mathbb R^3$ be a $C^1$ trajectory whose graph map $\gamma(t)=(z(t),t)$ is proper into the open set $U$, and let $q\in\mathbb R$ (coulombs). By [[lem-em-point-current-continuity]],
$$\langle\rho_{\mathrm{pt}},\psi\rangle:=q\int_{I_0}\psi(z(t),t)\,dt,\qquad \langle J_{\mathrm{pt}},\psi\rangle:=q\int_{I_0}z'(t)\,\psi(z(t),t)\,dt$$
define distributions on $U$ with $\partial_t\rho_{\mathrm{pt}}+\operatorname{div}J_{\mathrm{pt}}=0$. If instead $I_0=(a,b)$ has finite endpoints, $z$ extends continuously to $[a,b]$, the absolute improper integral $\int_a^b|z'(t)|\,dt$ is finite and both endpoint events lie in $U$, the same formulas define distributions with
$$\partial_t\rho_{\mathrm{pt}}+\operatorname{div}J_{\mathrm{pt}}=q\,\delta_{\gamma(a)}-q\,\delta_{\gamma(b)}$$
([[def-dirac-delta-and-its-derivatives]]); a finite-history point source therefore contributes an endpoint term unless that term is included explicitly, and the pairings above exclude it only by the stated properness or endpoint hypotheses.

(c) [Stationary-sheet sources] Let $S\subset\Omega$ be a fixed compact embedded $C^2$ hypersurface with a chosen unit normal $n$ pointing from the side $\Omega_-$ to the side $\Omega_+$ ([[def-em-surface-distribution]], [[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]]), and let $\sigma:S\times I\to\mathbb R$ and $K:S\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ be continuous with $K(x,t)\cdot n(x)=0$ for all $(x,t)$ (a tangential surface current density; the sheet is stationary). Then
$$\langle\rho_S,\psi\rangle:=\int_I\int_S\sigma(x,t)\psi(x,t)\,dS(x)\,dt,\qquad \langle J_S,\psi\rangle:=\int_I\int_SK(x,t)\psi(x,t)\,dS(x)\,dt$$
define distributions on $U$: for $\psi$ with compact support the inner integrals are continuous in $t$ on a compact parameter interval and the functionals are bounded by $(\sup|\sigma\psi|)\,\mathrm{area}(S)\,\mathrm{length}$ of the time projection of the support, and likewise in the vector case. A normal sheet current (one with $K\cdot n\ne0$), a line current and a moving sheet are not source types of this definition.

(d) [Unrestricted weak fields and optional interface branches] The general field class for the solution predicate (e) consists of all locally integrable pairs $(E,B)$ on $U$, also when the source has a stationary-sheet part. No classical one-sided trace or off-sheet $C^1$ regularity is required to define those four distributional pairings. Additional trace hypotheses are optional hypotheses of interface/jump results, not admission requirements of the general weak model.
For a pointwise classical jump branch, one may additionally assume that $E,B$ are $C^1$ off $S\times I$ and, around every $(x_0,t_0)\in S\times I$, each side is the restriction of a $C^1$ function on an open spacetime neighborhood of the corresponding closed side of a smaller stationary graph cylinder. These joint one-sided extensions make the field traces and first spatial/temporal derivatives continuous up to that side, locally uniformly on compact cylinders.
For the broader weak-trace branch, one may instead assume the original one-sided spatial $C^1$ extensions at each time, with the explicit additional conditions that the piecewise first spatial and temporal derivatives are in $L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(U)$ and the field traces are measurable and locally integrable on $S\times I$ for $dSdt$. This branch supports sheet-distribution and almost-everywhere jump identities; spatial continuity at each time gives pointwise spatial identities for almost every time, and joint continuity of the jump densities gives the further all-time upgrade. Separate spatial $C^1$ traces at each time alone do not imply that joint regularity or upgrade. Whenever such traces exist, $[F]:=F_+-F_-$ denotes their jump in the chosen normal convention. (e) [Weak Maxwell equations with a distributional source pair] Let $E,B$ be a field pair of class (d), let $\rho=\rho_v+\rho_s$ and $J=J_v+J_s$ be source distributions on $U$ whose volume parts $\rho_v,J_v$ are locally integrable volume densities with the charge/current quantity types of [[def-em-sources]] (the weak predicate requires this stated $L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}$ regularity, not the classical continuous-source regularity) and whose singular parts $(\rho_s,J_s)$ are point sources as in (b) or stationary-sheet sources as in (c), and let $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ with the constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]]. Say that $E,B$ satisfy the weak Maxwell equations with the source pair $(\rho,J)$ when, for every $\psi\in C_c^\infty(U)$, the four pairings
$$\langle\operatorname{div}E-\rho/\varepsilon_0,\psi\rangle,\quad \langle\operatorname{div}B,\psi\rangle,\quad \langle\operatorname{curl}E+\partial_tB,\psi\rangle,\quad \langle\operatorname{curl}B-\mu_0J-c^{-2}\partial_tE,\psi\rangle$$
all vanish, all derivatives being distributional derivatives of the regular distributions of the fields and the source pairings being those of (b) and (c). This clause defines a solution predicate. When the singular parts vanish, its four identities are the same as the locally integrable weak branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]]. That earlier postulate explicitly excludes point and sheet distributions and does not imply their physical adoption here; adoption for the declared singular-source models is made separately, after this definition. No physical field equation is deduced merely from defining this predicate.

(f) [Scope] No product of two distributions is formed anywhere: the fields occur only through their distributional derivatives paired with a test function, and the source densities $\sigma,K$ occur only inside the ordinary surface and time integrals of (b) and (c); products such as $\rho_sE$ or $J_s\times B$ are not defined by this item. The definition asserts no existence theorem for fields with singular sources, no conservation law (continuity for these sources is proved separately where used), and no regularisation. Sources that are not locally integrable and are not point or stationary-sheet sources, moving sheets, line currents, and arbitrary products of distributions are outside the definition. In the optional weak interface branch, a temporal derivative represented in $L^1_{\rm loc}$ means a genuine weak derivative on the open sides (or the classical derivative when joint interior $C^1$ regularity supplies integration by parts), not merely an ordinary derivative existing almost everywhere. For the fixed-sheet jump conclusions it is also sufficient to have the stated spatial derivative/trace integrability and the actual weak Maxwell equations with regular volume sources: the fixed-sheet tube-test argument below forces the sheet jump identities and then the required regular temporal derivatives. This includes the originally stated temporal-L1 specialization and never restricts the unrestricted given-L1 admission in(d)/(e).
items.strategy: An explicit definition-contract item. Clause (a) is the regular-distribution identification. Clause (b) restates the pairings and the continuity theorem of [[lem-em-point-current-continuity]] with its properness hypothesis, and its finite-endpoint variant with the two endpoint deltas. Clause (c) defines the stationary-sheet pairings by explicit iterated integrals; well-definedness uses the finiteness of the surface measure of the compact $S$ ([[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]], [[def-em-surface-distribution]]), continuity of $\sigma,K,\psi$ on compact sets and compactness of the time projection of the support of a test function, so both functionals are continuous of finite order on each test-support space. Clause (d) retains the unrestricted locally integrable field pair for the weak predicate, including sheet sources. It records optional interface hypotheses separately: joint one-sided spacetime C1 extensions support the pointwise branch; the weaker per-time spatial C1 trace branch needs the explicit piecewise-derivative and sheet-trace L1 hypotheses for its distribution/a.e. conclusions. Neither branch is a general weak-field admission condition, and separate spatial C1 traces alone are not claimed to give joint continuity or temporal bounds. Clause (e) defines the weak equations by the four vanishing pairings, with distributional derivatives of the regular distributions of the fields; the singular source terms enter only as the explicitly defined functionals of (b) and (c), never as products with the fields. Clause (f) records the exclusions; in particular the product of a singular source density with a field, which would be an undefined product of distributions, is not part of the definition. The vanishing-pairing clause is a precise mathematical solution predicate. It agrees with the old postulate on its original locally integrable source class, but does not extend that physical postulate deductively to singular sources; physical adoption is a separate postulate. It remains possible for a declared source pair to be incompatible with those equations, and no existence is asserted. Mere ordinary a.e. temporal differentiation is insufficient: a spatially constant Cantor function has a.e. derivative zero but a nonzero distributional derivative. For a fixed sheet and the actual Maxwell solution predicate, use bounded tube cutoffs equal to one on S and shrinking to S. In a temporal-derivative pairing the cutoff is time independent, so only the test's time derivative occurs. Given-L1 fields make that pairing tend to zero on shrinking tubes; regular spatial bulk and volume-source pairings do likewise. The remaining sheet coefficients are therefore fixed by Maxwell. Once their identities are obtained, Maxwell equates the temporal derivatives to the regular spatial bulk and volume sources, proving the temporal-L1 conclusion rather than assuming an ordinary-a.e. derivative is a weak derivative. No joint continuous boundary extension is inferred.

items.title: Vacuum Maxwell equations adopted for the declared distributional-source models
items.reference: necessary same-A physical-adoption repair of def-em-weak-sources(e); exact formulation from its solution predicate

items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) as carried by the declared distributional/surface source objects of [[def-em-weak-sources]]. In the flat classical laboratory model of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], with the positive constants and SI conventions of [[def-em-si-conventions]], adopt the following additional physical assumption for models using the declared point or stationary-sheet sources: the locally integrable field pair and the volume-plus-singular source pair of [[def-em-weak-sources]](a)-(d) must satisfy its solution predicate (e). Explicitly,
$$\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0,\qquad\operatorname{div}B=0,\qquad\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB,\qquad\operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE$$
are required in $\mathcal D'(U)$, meaning that all four residual pairings defined there vanish for every compact smooth test. This is a physical adoption of the classical vacuum idealization in that source class, not a theorem about sources or a consequence of the original locally-integrable-source branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]]. When the singular part vanishes, the adopted identities coincide with that earlier weak branch.
Only source/field tuples satisfying these identities are models of this postulate; it does not assert existence for every prescribed source pair, and compatibility conditions remain consequences to be checked. Sources are the exact point and stationary-sheet types defined earlier, including their properness/endpoint and tangential-current qualifications. No moving sheet, line current, magnetic source, product of distributions, self-force, regularization, matter dynamics or material constitutive law is introduced. This postulate reports no experiment or measurement and does not infer empirical certainty from its mathematical formulation.
items.strategy: Nonproof formulation and scope review: adopt the already-defined four residual identities for the specified classical point/sheet source idealizations. Textbook point-delta and sheet-delta Maxwell treatments support this model choice; the exact compact-test formulation is supplied by the preceding definition. This is an explicit further physical premise, not an application of the old L1-only postulate outside its domain and not a fabricated deductive proof. items.title: Charge continuity as a compatibility condition of the Maxwell equations
items.statement:
Let $U\cong I\times\Omega$ be the laboratory region of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] with the constants and units of [[def-em-si-conventions]], let $E,B$ be the fields of [[def-em-fields]] and $\rho,J$ the source fields of [[def-em-sources]], with $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$.

(a) [Smooth branch] Let $E,B$ be jointly of class $C^2$ on $\Omega\times I$ and $\rho,J$ of class $C^1$, and suppose the smooth branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] holds with these fields and sources, in particular $\operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE$. Then the continuity equation
$$\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=0$$
holds pointwise on $\Omega\times I$, where $\operatorname{div}$ is the divergence of [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]] and $\partial_t$ the partial time derivative of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]].

(b) [Distributional branch] Let $E,B,\rho,J$ be distributions on $\Omega\times I$ ([[def-distribution]], [[def-distributional-derivative]]); in particular they may be locally integrable fields and sources identified with their regular distributions ([[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]], [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]]). Suppose the four equations
$$\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0,\qquad \operatorname{div}B=0,\qquad \operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB,\qquad \operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE$$
hold in $\mathcal D'(\Omega\times I)$ with distributional derivatives. This includes the original locally integrable weak branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] and the separately adopted declared singular-source models of [[post-em-distributional-vacuum-maxwell]], when their source/field hypotheses hold. More generally the formal compatibility implication applies to every distributional source pair for which the four identities hold, without asserting physical adoption of arbitrary distributions. Then
$$\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=0$$
in $\mathcal D'(\Omega\times I)$.

The conclusion is a compatibility condition: it does not assert that every source pair is compatible with the Maxwell equations, and by itself it proves no conservation of physical charge. The derivative compatibility argument is choice-free. An application to the declared singular-source model retains the Countable Choice assumption of its defining source/surface-measure formulation ([[def-countable-choice]]).
items.strategy:
(a) Smooth branch. By [[thm-the-divergence-of-a-curl-vanishes]] applied to the $C^2$ field $B$, $\operatorname{div}(\operatorname{curl}B)=0$ pointwise. Taking the divergence of the displayed Amp\`ere equation and using linearity of the coordinate derivatives in the sum defining the divergence ([[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]) gives $0=\mu_0\operatorname{div}J+c^{-2}\operatorname{div}(\partial_tE)$, and [[thm-clairaut-schwarz-mixed-partials]] lets the two coordinate-derivative types be interchanged: $\operatorname{div}(\partial_tE)=\partial_t(\operatorname{div}E)$. The Gauss law of the smooth branch gives $\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0$ and hence $\partial_t(\operatorname{div}E)=\varepsilon_0^{-1}\partial_t\rho$, using $\rho$ of class $C^1$ ([[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]). Substituting, $0=\mu_0\operatorname{div}J+c^{-2}\varepsilon_0^{-1}\partial_t\rho=\mu_0(\operatorname{div}J+\partial_t\rho)$, because $c^2\varepsilon_0\mu_0=1$ by the definition $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ of [[def-em-si-conventions]] and $\mu_0>0$; division by $\mu_0$ gives the claim.

(b) Distributional branch. Only the two pairings with $\operatorname{curl}B$ and with $\operatorname{div}E$ are used. By [[thm-distributional-differentiation-is-continuous-and-commutes]] the distributional derivatives commute, so for every test function $\psi$
$$\langle\operatorname{div}(\operatorname{curl}B),\psi\rangle=\sum_{i,j,k=1}^3\varepsilon_{ijk}\langle\partial_i\partial_jB_k,\psi\rangle=\sum_{i,j,k=1}^3\varepsilon_{ijk}\langle\partial_j\partial_iB_k,\psi\rangle=0$$
after reindexing $i\leftrightarrow j$ and using the antisymmetry of $\varepsilon_{ijk}$: the two expressions are negatives of each other. The weak Amp\`ere equation therefore gives $\mu_0\operatorname{div}J+c^{-2}\partial_t\operatorname{div}E=0$ in $\mathcal D'(\Omega\times I)$, again by [[thm-distributional-differentiation-is-continuous-and-commutes]] and linearity of the pairing ([[def-distribution]], [[def-distributional-derivative]]). The weak Gauss law gives $\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0$ and hence $\partial_t\operatorname{div}E=\varepsilon_0^{-1}\partial_t\rho$; substituting and dividing as in (a) gives $\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=0$ in $\mathcal D'(\Omega\times I)$. The locally integrable case is clause (a) of the embedding: the fields' regular distributions are well defined ([[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]], [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]]), and the computation is unchanged. Every step is either an identity for distributions or the definition of the distributional derivative applied to a constant multiple, so no choice principle and no convergence theorem is used. The statement does not claim that every source pair admits fields satisfying the four equations: it claims only that whenever they do, continuity follows. Actual physical use with point/stationary-sheet source models invokes [[post-em-distributional-vacuum-maxwell]], not an extension inferred from the old L1-only postulate. The formal distributional cancellation itself remains choice-free; the source-object formulation retains its explicit Countable Choice assumption.

items.title: Smooth differential-integral equivalence for every admissible test geometry
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), the convention of the imported piecewise $C^1$ boundary and surface-measure definitions ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $U\cong I\times\Omega$ be the laboratory region of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] with the constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]]; let $E,B$ be fields of [[def-em-fields]] and $\rho,J$ source fields of [[def-em-sources]] on $\Omega\times I$; and let $(V,\nu_V)$ and $(D,r)$ be the volume and patch test geometries of [[def-em-fixed-test-geometry]]. Assume the fields are jointly $C^1$ on $\Omega\times I$ and that the additional derivatives appearing below exist and are continuous there; for instance $E,B$ jointly of class $C^2$ and $\rho,J$ of class $C^1$ is sufficient.

(a) [Differential implies integral] If the smooth branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] holds pointwise on $\Omega\times I$, then for every volume test geometry $(V,\nu_V)$ and every $t\in I$,
$$\oint_{\partial V}E(\cdot,t)\cdot\nu_V\,dS=\frac{1}{\varepsilon_0}\int_V\rho(\cdot,t)\,d\lambda_3,\qquad \oint_{\partial V}B(\cdot,t)\cdot\nu_V\,dS=0,$$
and for every patch test geometry $(D,r)$ the flux functions $t\mapsto\int_SB(\cdot,t)\cdot n_S\,dS$ and $t\mapsto\int_SE(\cdot,t)\cdot n_S\,dS$ are differentiable on $I$ and, for every $t\in I$,
$$\oint_{\partial S}E(\cdot,t)\cdot d\mathbf r=-\frac{d}{dt}\int_SB(\cdot,t)\cdot n_S\,dS,\qquad \oint_{\partial S}B(\cdot,t)\cdot d\mathbf r=\mu_0\int_SJ(\cdot,t)\cdot n_S\,dS+c^{-2}\frac{d}{dt}\int_SE(\cdot,t)\cdot n_S\,dS.$$

(b) [Integral implies differential] Conversely, suppose the two volume identities of (a) hold for every volume test geometry and every $t\in I$, and that for every patch test geometry the two flux functions are differentiable on $I$ and the two patch identities of (a) hold for every $t\in I$. Then the four smooth-branch equations of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] hold pointwise on $\Omega\times I$:
$$\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0,\qquad \operatorname{div}B=0,\qquad \operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB,\qquad \operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE.$$

The equivalence is asserted for the exact class of test geometries of [[def-em-fixed-test-geometry]], which contains the open interiors of all closed axis-parallel boxes compactly contained in $\Omega$ and the affine square patches; it is not a recovery from one selected volume or one selected patch, and the divergence and curl of [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]] and the time derivative of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]] are the operators used.
items.strategy:
(a) Differential implies integral. Fix $t\in I$ and a volume test geometry $V$; $E(\cdot,t)$ is $C^1$ on a neighbourhood of $\overline V$, so [[thm-divergence-theorem-for-bounded-piecewise-c-one-domains]] applies (the theorem assumes the specified finite piecewise $C^1$ presentation and the stated $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$) and gives $\oint_{\partial V}E\cdot\nu_V\,dS=\int_V\operatorname{div}E\,d\lambda_3=(1/\varepsilon_0)\int_V\rho\,d\lambda_3$ by the Gauss law of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]]; the same computation with $\operatorname{div}B=0$ gives the second identity. For a patch test geometry, [[thm-the-classical-stokes-theorem-for-a-c2-surface-patch]] applied to the $C^1$ fields gives $\oint_{\partial S}E\cdot d\mathbf r=\int_S\operatorname{curl}E\cdot n_S\,dS$ with the induced orientation of [[def-em-fixed-test-geometry]], and $\int_S\operatorname{curl}E\cdot n_S\,dS=-\int_S\partial_tB\cdot n_S\,dS$ by Faraday's law. The flux function is $t\mapsto\int_D\langle B(r(u,v),t),r_u\times r_v\rangle\,dudv$, a Riemann integral over the compact Jordan parameter region of a function whose time derivative $\langle\partial_tB(r(u,v),t),r_u\times r_v\rangle$ is continuous on a neighbourhood of $D$ times a compact interval around $t$; [[lem-riemann-lebesgue-comparison-for-distribution-test-integrands]] identifies this Riemann integral with the Lebesgue integral to which [[lem-em-parameter-integrals]] applies, giving differentiability on $I$ with $\frac{d}{dt}\int_SB\cdot n_S\,dS=\int_S\partial_tB\cdot n_S\,dS$. Combining gives the Faraday identity; the Amp\`ere identity is the same with $\operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE$.

(b) Integral implies differential. Fix a point $p\in\Omega$, an index $i$, and the cyclic pair $(j,k)$ with $e_j\times e_k=e_i$. For every closed box $K=\prod_{i<3}[a_i,b_i]\subset\Omega$ with positive sides take its admitted open interior $V$. The volume identities and [[thm-divergence-theorem-for-bounded-piecewise-c-one-domains]] give $\int_V(\operatorname{div}E-\rho/\varepsilon_0)\,d\lambda_3=0$. The integrand $h=\operatorname{div}E-\rho/\varepsilon_0$ is continuous on $\Omega$ and bounded on $K$. The six faces of $K\setminus V$ are volume-null by [[thm-lebesgue-measure-of-a-box-of-every-kind]], so [[cor-integral-over-a-null-set-vanishes]] applied to the positive and negative parts gives $\int_Kh=\int_Vh=0$. In particular this holds for every closed cube $K\subset\Omega$; [[lem-em-coordinate-cell-localization]] gives $h=0$ on $\Omega$. The same argument applied to $h=\operatorname{div}B$ gives $\operatorname{div}B=0$. For the curl components, take the affine patch $r(u,v):=p+ue_j+ve_k$ over the square $D_\ell=[-\ell/2,\ell/2]^2$ (a patch test geometry whose parameter region is a rectangle and whose normal is $r_u\times r_v=e_i$); the Faraday identity of (b), Stokes' theorem and the differentiability of the flux function give $\int_{D_\ell}\bigl(\operatorname{curl}E+\partial_tB\bigr)(p+ue_j+ve_k)\cdot e_i\,dudv=0$ for every sufficiently small $\ell>0$. Because the identities hold for every affine square patch contained in $\Omega$, for each fixed coordinate plane every closed square in its open slice is covered (translate its centre to $p$); this is the hypothesis of the planar clause of [[lem-em-coordinate-cell-localization]] for the continuous function $u\mapsto(\operatorname{curl}E+\partial_tB)(p+ue_j+ve_k)\cdot e_i$ on the corresponding coordinate plane; hence $(\operatorname{curl}E+\partial_tB)\cdot e_i=0$ at every point of $\Omega$, for each coordinate $e_i$. The same argument with the Amp\`ere identity gives $(\operatorname{curl}B-\mu_0J-c^{-2}\partial_tE)\cdot e_i=0$. Therefore the four equations hold pointwise. The argument shows why a single selected test geometry is insufficient: the recovery uses the full families of boxes and affine square patches of [[def-em-fixed-test-geometry]], and the marked $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is exactly the convention of the divergence theorem and the surface-measure interface.

items.title: Stationary-sheet jump conditions of the weak Maxwell equations
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), the convention of the interface and surface-measure definitions cited below ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $U\cong I\times\Omega$ be the laboratory region of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] with the constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]] and the fields of [[def-em-fields]] and source fields of [[def-em-sources]].

Let $S\subset\Omega$ be a fixed compact embedded $C^2$ hypersurface with a chosen unit normal $n$ pointing from the side $\Omega_-$ to the side $\Omega_+$ ([[def-em-surface-distribution]]), and let $\sigma:S\times I\to\mathbb R$ and $K:S\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ be continuous with $K(x,t)\cdot n(x)=0$ for all $(x,t)$ (a tangential surface current density). Let $E,B$ be locally integrable on $\Omega\times I$ and $C^1$ on $(\Omega\setminus S)\times I$ with the following explicit joint one-sided regularity: around every $(x_0,t_0)\in S\times I$, each side is the restriction of a $C^1$ function on an open spacetime neighbourhood of the corresponding closed side of a smaller stationary graph cylinder. Thus the fields and their first space/time derivatives extend continuously to that side of $S\times I$, locally uniformly on compact cylinders, and let $\rho_v,J_v$ be continuous on $(\Omega\setminus S)\times I$ and locally integrable on $\Omega\times I$. Write $[F]=F_+-F_-$ for the jump of the one-sided traces of such a field $F$.

Under the separate singular-source physical adoption [[post-em-distributional-vacuum-maxwell]], suppose that $E,B$ satisfy the weak Maxwell equations with the source pair
$$\rho=\rho_v+\rho_S,\qquad J=J_v+J_S,$$
where $(\rho_S,J_S)$ is the stationary-sheet source of [[def-em-weak-sources]](c) with densities $\sigma,K$ and the pairings there, in the sense of [[def-em-weak-sources]](e), and where the volume parts $\rho_v,J_v$ are identified with their regular distributions ([[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]], [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]]). Then, pointwise on $S\times I$,
$$n\cdot[E]=\frac{\sigma}{\varepsilon_0},\qquad n\times[B]=\mu_0K,\qquad n\cdot[B]=0,\qquad n\times[E]=0,$$
with the ordinary Euclidean inner and cross products of the one-sided traces ([[def-cross-product-in-r3]]). Equivalently, the surface current density is $K=(\mu_0)^{-1}\,n\times[B]$ and the surface charge density is $\sigma=\varepsilon_0\,n\cdot[E]$.

The theorem assumes a stationary interface: the hypersurface $S$ and its normal do not depend on $t$, so the one-sided $C^1$ traces also make $\partial_tE$ and $\partial_tB$ locally bounded near $S$ and hence locally integrable, contributing no delta terms. No magnetic surface charge or magnetic surface current is present in the sources, and correspondingly the last two identities assert the absence of magnetic sheet delta terms. A moving interface, a normal sheet current, or a sheet whose support changes with time is outside this statement and would require additional terms.

[General weak trace branch] The weak Maxwell framework continues to allow the full locally integrable field/source class, without asserting undefined classical trace values. If instead of the joint extension condition the fields have the original one-sided spatial $C^1$ extensions at each time, assume in addition that their piecewise first spatial and temporal derivatives are in $L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega\times I)$ and that their one-sided field traces are measurable and locally integrable on $S\times I$ with respect to $dS\,dt$. Then the same four jump identities hold as equalities of sheet distributions and for $dS\,dt$-almost every $(x,t)$; since the traces are spatially continuous at each fixed time, they hold for every $x\in S$ for almost every $t\in I$. They hold at every $(x,t)$ whenever the jump densities are additionally jointly continuous. Merely having one-sided spatial $C^1$ traces separately at every time does not justify this last upgrade. In this weak branch temporal derivatives in $L^1_{\rm loc}$ are genuine weak derivatives, or classical derivatives with the joint interior $C^1$ integration-by-parts justification already assumed. More generally, that temporal integrability hypothesis may be omitted when the stated spatial derivative and trace integrability and the actual fixed-sheet weak equations with regular volume sources hold: those equations themselves imply the same jumps and regular temporal derivatives. No joint boundary continuity is imposed on this broader branch.
items.strategy:
First justify the spacetime use of the spatial supplier. For a compactly supported spacetime test $\psi$, let $K\subset\Omega$ be its compact spatial support projection and let $L\Subset I$ be a compact interval containing its time support. Choose finitely many spatial stationary graph neighbourhoods and interior open sets covering $K$. [[lem-finite-ambient-partitions-for-euclidean-boundary-integration]] gives smooth nonnegative spatial functions $\phi_j$ compactly supported in those sets with $\sum_j\phi_j=1$ near $K$. Explicitly, first choose finitely many nonnegative ambient bumps $\chi_j$ subordinate to that cover whose sum $s$ is positive near $K$; a cutoff $\theta\in C_c^\infty(\{s>0\})$ equal to one near $K$ exists by [[lem-test-function-cutoffs-and-euclidean-localization]], and $\phi_j=\theta\chi_j/s$ on $\{s>0\}$, extended by zero elsewhere, is smooth since $\operatorname{supp}\theta$ stays compactly inside the positive set. Their sum is $\theta=1$ near $K$, so $\psi=\sum_j\phi_j\psi$. This partition is independent of time, hence $\partial_t(\phi_j\psi)=\phi_j\partial_t\psi$ and temporal integration by parts acquires no partition derivative. On each spatial chart times $L$, the local joint one-sided extensions have a finite subcover of the relevant compact sheet-time subset, giving the compact bounds used below; interior compact supports are already covered by the ordinary joint $C^1$ assumption. In the joint branch the one-sided $C^1$ extensions and their derivatives are bounded on each compact closed half-cylinder, so the piecewise derivatives are locally integrable and the jumps are jointly continuous and bounded there. Apply [[lem-em-interface-derivatives]] to each component of the spatial slice at every fixed $t$ and integrate in $t$. The terms $F\partial_i\psi$, $(\partial_i F)\psi$ and $n_i[F]\psi$ are absolutely integrable on the compact support (the last uses the finite compact surface measure of [[lem-surface-integral-is-independent-of-c-one-boundary-charts]]), so [[thm-fubini-theorem-for-l-one-on-sigma-finite-product-spaces]] justifies integrating the identity. This gives $\partial_iF_j=\{\partial_iF_j\}+n_i[F_j]\delta_{S\times I}$, and contraction/antisymmetrization gives the divergence/curl formulas. For the temporal derivative, on each fixed spatial side, [[thm-integration-by-parts]] on a compact time interval containing the test support, followed by [[lem-riemann-lebesgue-comparison-for-distribution-test-integrands]], gives $-\int F_j\partial_t\psi=\int (\partial_tF_j)\psi$, with no endpoint term since the test support is compact in $I$. Integrate in $x$ by the same Fubini theorem. The sides are stationary, so no derivative of a moving spatial indicator occurs and $\partial_tF_j=\{\partial_tF_j\}$ with no sheet term.

The spatial sheet $S$ has three-dimensional Lebesgue measure zero: in each finite graph chart every normal section is a singleton, so Fubini gives zero volume, and the coordinate permutation preserves Lebesgue measure. Consequently $S\times I$ is locally four-dimensional null. Restrict each weak Maxwell identity to tests away from $S\times I$. The resulting ordinary residuals are continuous on the open complement, so the existing sign-and-ambient-bump argument forces them to vanish pointwise there. The ordinary residuals are locally integrable and differ from zero only on the null sheet, hence represent zero regular distributions by [[cor-integral-over-a-null-set-vanishes]]. Subtract them to obtain the four sheet identities with densities $n\cdot[E]-\sigma/\varepsilon_0$, $n\cdot[B]$, $n\times[E]$, $n\times[B]-\mu_0K$. For every spatial $\varphi\in\mathcal D(\Omega)$, each scalar component $H(t)=\int_S a(x,t)\varphi(x)\,dS$ is continuous: on a compact time interval, joint continuity on the compact sheet gives uniform convergence as $t\to t_0$, and the bound $|H(t)-H(t_0)|\le S(S)\|\varphi\|_\infty\sup_{x\in S}|a(x,t)-a(x,t_0)|$ tends to zero. Testing $\varphi(x)\eta(t)$ and using the one-dimensional sign-and-bump argument shows $H(t)=0$ at every time. Apply [[lem-em-surface-density-localization]] at that time and componentwise to get the four pointwise jumps. Tangentiality of $n\times[B]$ gives the stated current formula.

For the general weak trace branch, the additional local $L^1$ hypotheses on piecewise derivatives and traces justify the same Fubini arguments without compact uniform bounds. Temporal integration by parts is valid first on compact subintervals for each fixed off-sheet $x$, since the field is $C^1$ there; its integrable derivative and the test's compact support justify the integrated identity. The sheet residuals are therefore zero as distributions. For each fixed ambient spatial test $\varphi$, Fubini gives the locally integrable time function $H_\varphi(t)=\int_S a(x,t)\varphi(x)\,dS$, and testing $\varphi(x)\eta(t)$ shows its regular distribution is zero. The one-dimensional case of [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]] gives $H_\varphi(t)=0$ for almost every time. To obtain one exceptional time set, use the countable explicit ambient bumps with rational centres $q\in\mathbb Q^3$ and rational radii $0<r<R$ for which $\overline B_R(q)\subset\Omega$, equal to one on $\overline B_r(q)$ and supported in $B_R(q)$. They are defined by the fixed smooth-step formula in [[lem-scaled-euclidean-bumps-with-compact-support-and-gradient-bound]], so no arbitrary choice of a test for each triple is needed. Remove the countable union of the null time sets for these tests, which remains null by [[thm-finite-and-countable-subadditivity-of-measures]]. For a remaining time, a nonzero continuous spatial residual at any $x_0\in S$ has one strict sign on a sufficiently small graph neighbourhood. Density of the rationals ([[lem-q-and-irrationals-dense-r]]) gives one of those ambient balls wholly inside that neighbourhood whose inner ball contains $x_0$. A positive-area graph cell in its inner ball, as in [[lem-em-surface-density-localization]], makes its pairing nonzero, contradiction. Thus each residual vanishes at every spatial point for almost every time, which also proves the sheet-a.e. assertion. Joint continuity, if separately assumed, similarly upgrades to all times using positive-area cells times nondegenerate time intervals. The counterexample recorded in this proposal proves why this qualification cannot be omitted. All four electromagnetic conclusions and the unrestricted weak Maxwell framework are retained at their strongest justified regularity level; no Sobolev trace theorem or undeclared Choice principle is used. To justify the broader weak branch directly, first apply the regular-L1 specialization of the spatial interface lemma at each admissible time and integrate by Fubini. Its spatial distributional sheet coefficient is the stated trace jump. Work on a compact graph patch with a smooth tube cutoff chi_epsilon(y), independent of time, equal to one on the sheet, bounded between zero and one, and supported where |z-g(y)|<2epsilon; multiply by a fixed compact test. This cutoff need only be C2 for a C2 graph: all equations involved are order at most one. To use it legitimately, approximate the resulting compactly supported C1 test in the C1 norm by smooth tests via [[thm-convolution-with-a-mollifier-is-smooth-and-differentiates-under-the-integral-sign]], using its actual kernel-footprint margin. For each derivative of order at most one, move the derivative to the compact C1 input by classical integration by parts and write the error as integral eta(v)[D^alpha f(x-epsilon v)-D^alpha f(x)]dv. Uniform continuity on one compact enlarged support and the finite integral of |eta| make this error uniformly vanish; no unit-support assumption is made. The L1 and finite sheet measures make all pairings continuous in that norm, so the weak identities extend to it. For a temporal term its absolute pairing is at most the integral over the shrinking spatial tube of |F| times the fixed time-derivative bound. For a regular spatial bulk or volume source use its absolute L1 majorant. The sheet has ambient volume zero, and [[thm-dominated-convergence]] sends all these integrals to zero. The sheet term survives unchanged because chi_epsilon=1 on S. Thus the four weak equations force exactly their four displayed sheet coefficients, without assuming a temporal classical derivative is integrable or demanding joint continuous boundary values. After cancelling these coefficients, the curl evolution equations identify the weak temporal derivatives with their regular spatial bulk and volume-source expressions, which are L1loc. The existing scalar-test localization and Countable Choice a.e.-time argument then give the stated sheet-a.e., spatial-continuity and joint-continuity upgrades. The original jointly C1 interior branch is included and supports its classical temporal integration by parts; the general given-L1 Maxwell admission stays unrestricted.

items.physical_scope: The stationary-sheet jump conditions of the classical electromagnetic framework in a named inertial laboratory frame: for locally integrable fields that are piecewise $C^1$ across a fixed compact interface, solving the weak Maxwell equations with a prescribed surface charge density $\sigma$ and tangential surface current density $K$ forces $n\cdot[E]=\sigma/\varepsilon_0$, $n\times[B]=\mu_0K$, $n\cdot[B]=0$ and $n\times[E]=0$, with the jump taken along the chosen normal from the minus to the plus side. The statement excludes moving interfaces, normal sheet currents and magnetic sheet sources, asserts no measurement or apparatus realisation, and carries the declared $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of the interface and surface-measure items. Pointwise classical jumps use the explicit joint one-sided regularity or an independently established jointly continuous jump; the specified locally integrable trace branch gives sheet-distribution and almost-everywhere jumps. The unrestricted L1 weak framework does not by itself define pointwise classical traces.

items.title: Evolution preserves the Gauss constraints
items.statement:
Let $U\cong I\times\Omega$ be the laboratory region of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], with nonempty open time interval $I$ ([[def-interval]]), positive constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]] and $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$. Define the Gauss defects
$$D_B:=\operatorname{div}B,\qquad D_E:=\operatorname{div}E-\rho/\varepsilon_0.$$
(a) Smooth evolution branch. Let $E,B$ be jointly $C^2$ fields and $\rho,J$ $C^1$ source fields of [[def-em-fields]] and [[def-em-sources]]. Assume only the two evolution equations
$$\partial_tB=-\operatorname{curl}E,\qquad\partial_tE=c^2\operatorname{curl}B-c^2\mu_0J,$$
and, separately, source continuity $\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=0$. No Gauss constraint is assumed. Then $\partial_tD_B=\partial_tD_E=0$ pointwise. For each fixed $x$, both defects are constant on $I$. Initial zero constraints at any $t_0\in I$ persist at every time; a nonzero defect at a point persists with the same value. Thus evolution and continuity cannot repair a nonzero initial Gauss defect.
(b) Distributional evolution branch. The same derivative conclusion holds for arbitrary scalar/vector distributions $E,B,\rho,J$ on $U$ satisfying the two evolution identities and, independently, continuity in $\mathcal D'(U)$ ([[def-distribution]], [[def-distributional-derivative]]). This includes the original locally integrable field/source branch identified with regular distributions and the declared singular-source class when its equations hold. Thus $\partial_tD_B=\partial_tD_E=0$ distributionally. If a defect has a continuous representative $h$ on $U$, assume Countable Choice for the indicated Lebesgue integral/localization interface ([[def-countable-choice]]); then $h(x,t)$ is independent of $t$. In this continuous-representative case its zero or nonzero value at a time persists. No restriction of an arbitrary distribution to a time slice is assumed.
(c) Full-Maxwell corollaries. Smooth solutions of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] satisfy the evolution and source-continuity hypotheses by [[pthm-em-charge-continuity]](a), and their Gauss defects are identically zero by the two Gauss equations. Its original locally-integrable weak branch has the same distributional conclusion. For admitted point/stationary-sheet models under [[post-em-distributional-vacuum-maxwell]], [[pthm-em-charge-continuity]](b) supplies compatibility and the four identities again give zero defects. Conversely, in (a), or in (b) when both defects have continuous representatives, evolution plus continuity and zero Gauss defects at one time give all four Maxwell identities on $U$, pointwise in (a) and distributionally in (b).
This theorem is conditional on the stated equations and regularity. It proves no existence, matter dynamics, observation or empirical fact. The derivative algebra is choice-free; Countable Choice is confined to the continuous-representative localization and inherited declared singular-source formulation.
items.strategy:
(a) Smooth algebra. For $C^2$ fields, [[thm-the-divergence-of-a-curl-vanishes]] and [[thm-clairaut-schwarz-mixed-partials]] give
$$\partial_tD_B=\operatorname{div}(\partial_tB)=-\operatorname{div}(\operatorname{curl}E)=0,$$
and, with the positive commutation sign,
$$\partial_tD_E=\operatorname{div}(\partial_tE)-\varepsilon_0^{-1}\partial_t\rho=c^2\operatorname{div}(\operatorname{curl}B)-c^2\mu_0\operatorname{div}J-\varepsilon_0^{-1}\partial_t\rho=-\varepsilon_0^{-1}(\operatorname{div}J+\partial_t\rho)=0.$$
Here $c^2\mu_0=\varepsilon_0^{-1}$ and the final equality is the separately assumed continuity, not a consequence of the evolution equations alone. The coordinate operators and product/linear rules are [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]], [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]] and [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]. For fixed $x$, [[cor-mean-value-theorem]] on compact subintervals of $I$ proves constancy, propagation and nonzero persistence.
(b) The identical componentwise cancellation holds for distributions by [[thm-distributional-differentiation-is-continuous-and-commutes]], whose derivative-commutation clause is choice-free: in $\sum_{i,j,k}\epsilon_{ijk}\partial_i\partial_jB_k$ the exchanged $i,j$ terms cancel. The two evolution identities and the independent continuity identity therefore give $\partial_tD_B=\partial_tD_E=0$ without multiplying distributions.
For the continuous-representative conclusion, assume the stated Countable Choice and let $\partial_th=0$. Fix a spatial test $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$ and put $F(t)=\int_\Omega h(x,t)\varphi(x)d\lambda_3(x)$. On any compact time subinterval the integrands have fixed compact spatial support and a uniform bound, by [[thm-extreme-value-metric]] and [[prop-lebesgue-measure-is-sigma-finite-and-finite-on-bounded-sets]]. Hence [[thm-dominated-convergence]] makes $F$ continuous. All products with compact temporal tests are absolutely integrable; [[thm-borel-products-of-euclidean-spaces-are-euclidean-borel]], [[thm-lebesgue-product-measure-agrees-with-euclidean-lebesgue-on-borel-sets]] and [[thm-fubini-theorem-for-l-one-on-sigma-finite-product-spaces]] identify their multiple integrals with $\int_I F\eta$.
If $\eta\in C_c^\infty(I)$ has zero integral, extend it by zero and put $H(t):=\int_{-\infty}^t\eta(v)dv$. Equivalently start at a point strictly left of its support. The compact-test integral agrees with its Riemann integral by [[lem-riemann-lebesgue-comparison-for-distribution-test-integrands]], and [[thm-ftc-first-part]] gives $H\prime=\eta$. Since the total integral is zero, $H$ vanishes both left and right of the support interval; it is smooth and compactly supported inside $I$. Therefore $\Psi(x,t):=\varphi(x)H(t)$ is a legitimate compact test with $\partial_t\Psi=\varphi\eta$. Apply the derivative equation to THIS primitive test:
$$0=\langle\partial_th,\Psi\rangle=-\langle h,\partial_t\Psi\rangle=-\int_I F(t)\eta(t)dt.$$
Choose a real nonnegative compact bump $\beta$ in $I$ with integral one, using [[lem-scaled-euclidean-bumps-with-compact-support-and-gradient-bound]] and the positive finite measure of an inner interval ([[lem-euclidean-balls-have-positive-finite-lebesgue-measure]]). Decompose an arbitrary temporal test as $\eta_0=\eta-(\int_I\eta)\beta$. The preceding equality gives $\int_I(F-C)\eta=0$ for every $\eta$, where $C:=\int_IF\beta$. A continuous function with all such pairings zero vanishes pointwise: if a real or imaginary component is nonzero, continuity gives a subinterval where that component has one sign and is bounded away from zero; a nonnegative bump supported there, equal to one on a smaller interval, contradicts integral monotonicity ([[thm-monotonicity-of-the-integral]], [[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]], [[lem-euclidean-balls-have-positive-finite-lebesgue-measure]]). Thus $F$ is constant. The same argument for the continuous spatial difference $h(\cdot,t_1)-h(\cdot,t_2)$, now using bumps in $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$, shows it is identically zero, since its pairing with every $\varphi$ is zero. This establishes independence of time. Compact support of every test, the actual derivative-test slot, and the public Countable Choice cost are explicit; no arbitrary-basepoint primitive is used.
(c) In the smooth full-Maxwell branch, [[pthm-em-charge-continuity]] supplies continuity, while Gauss gives $D_B=D_E=0$ directly; the original weak branch is the identical distributional argument. The separately adopted singular-source postulate uses the preceding solution predicate and the distributional continuity result. Conversely the propagated zero defects are exactly the missing two Gauss identities, so adding them to the evolution pair yields all four equations. No existence or empirical claim is inferred.
