items.title: Proper time is invariant under regular increasing weak piecewise changes of parameter
items.statement: Let c>0 and let x:[a,b]->A be a weak piecewise C^1 future timelike worldline. Let phi:[u,v]->[a,b] be an increasing continuous surjection, C^1 on the open pieces of a finite partition, with phi'>0 at every interior smooth point and finite positive one-sided difference-quotient derivatives at both endpoints of each piece. Then phi is strictly increasing with continuous inverse, y=x composed with phi is a weak piecewise C^1 future timelike worldline, and Delta tau_[u,v](y)=Delta tau_[a,b](x). The same equality holds for every pair of corresponding restricted parameter intervals; based proper-time functions differ only by their base-point constant. The relevant partition is the common refinement of phi's partition and the inverse images of x's partition points. This statement gives worldline/clock consequences only for positive derivatives, including all one-sided endpoint derivatives. It leaves intact the separate global-C^1 curve-integral identities allowing zero tangents in lem-sr-proper-time-reparametrization-invariance; a zero-tangent composition is not asserted to be a worldline.
items.strategy: On each closed piece phi is continuous and differentiable inside with phi'>0, so the mean value theorem proves strict increase there; finite concatenation gives global strict increase, and the continuous monotone bijection has continuous inverse. The finite inverse-image refinement separates all x and phi corners. Inside each refined piece componentwise chain rule gives y'=phi' x'(phi), so y' is continuous and future timelike and sqrt(-eta(y',y'))=phi' f(phi), where f=sqrt(-eta(x',x')). At each one-sided endpoint the quotient of y is the product of the corresponding quotient of x and that of phi; strict monotonicity chooses the correct side and both finite limits exist, the latter positive. Thus y has finite future timelike one-sided tangents and lies in the same weak class. On any compact interior truncation [r,s] of a refined piece, f is continuous on the compact image interval and phi' is continuous and integrable on [r,s]; thm-substitution gives integral_r^s phi' f(phi)=integral_phi(r)^phi(s) f. As r and s approach the refined endpoints, continuity and strict monotonicity of phi make the image endpoints approach the corresponding x endpoints. Both improper limits exist by lem-sr-weak-piecewise-causal-integrability for x and y, so the identity passes to the limits. Finite summation and partition independence give the full and restricted interval identities. Oriented additivity gives the based-function constant. No boundedness of the derivative near a corner is assumed and no zero tangent is admitted as a worldline.

items.title: The proper-time function is a strictly increasing C^1 parametrization with C^1 inverse
items.statement: Let c > 0 and let x: I -> A be a C^1 future timelike worldline with proper-time function tau, tau(s) = c^{-1} integral_{s_0}^{s} sqrt(-eta(x'(u),x'(u))) du (def-sr-proper-time). Then: (i) tau is differentiable at every s in I, with one-sided derivatives at the endpoints of I, and tau'(s) = c^{-1} sqrt(-eta(x'(s),x'(s))) > 0 for every s in I; since tau' is this composition of continuous maps, tau is C^1 on I. (ii) tau is strictly increasing on I, hence injective, and its image J := tau[I] is an order-convex subset of R with at least two elements, so tau: I -> J is a bijection. (iii) The inverse rho: J -> I of tau is continuous and strictly increasing, and it is differentiable at every point tau(s) of J with rho'(tau(s)) = 1/tau'(s) = c / sqrt(-eta(x'(s),x'(s))) > 0; hence rho is C^1 on J. (iv) The reparametrized curve y := x o rho: J -> A is a C^1 future timelike worldline whose tangent at the proper-time parameter tau(s) is (x o rho)'(tau(s)) = x'(s)/tau'(s) = c x'(s)/sqrt(-eta(x'(s),x'(s))); in particular y is parametrized by its own proper time up to the additive constant of the base point, and the derivative formula is the four-velocity of the following definition.
items.strategy: (i) thm-ftc-first-part applied to the continuous integrand u |-> c^{-1} sqrt(-eta(x'(u),x'(u))) on a compact neighbourhood of s (contained in I using def-interval) gives tau'(s) equal to that value, with the one-sided reading at endpoints; positivity is the future timelike hypothesis. (ii) For a < b in I, monotonicity of the integral (thm-monotonicity-of-the-integral) gives tau(b) - tau(a) >= 0, and equality would force the continuous nonnegative integrand to vanish on [a,b] (thm-nonnegative-continuous-with-zero-integral-vanishes), contradicting its strict positivity; so tau is strictly increasing and injective, and its image is order-convex and nondegenerate by cor-continuous-image-of-an-interval-is-an-interval (tau is continuous). (iii) A continuous injective map on an interval has a continuous strictly monotone inverse (thm-continuous-inverse), and the reciprocal derivative formula is thm-derivative-of-an-inverse, applicable since tau'(s) > 0; tau' continuous gives rho C^1. (iv) Differentiating componentwise in an inertial chart and applying the one-variable chain rule to each coordinate (def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral, thm-chain-rule) gives (x o rho)' = (x' o rho) rho' at interior points, with one-sided readings at endpoints; rho' > 0 preserves future timelikeness. The base point shifts rho's argument and leaves derivatives unchanged. No choice principle is used.

items.title: Elapsed proper time is invariant under increasing C^1 reparametrizations
items.statement: Let c > 0, let x: I -> A be a C^1 future timelike worldline, let a < b with [a,b] contained in I, and let c_0 < d_0. Let phi: [c_0,d_0] -> [a,b] be a strictly increasing C^1 surjection, with one-sided endpoint derivatives as in def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline. Then phi(c_0)=a, phi(d_0)=b and phi' >= 0. Put y=x o phi and f(s)=sqrt(-eta(x'(s),x'(s))). The C^1 curve y has tangent y'(u)=phi'(u)x'(phi(u)), future timelike exactly where phi'(u)>0 and zero where phi'(u)=0. Its nonnegative length integrand is sqrt(-eta(y'(u),y'(u)))=phi'(u)f(phi(u)); this integrand is defined even when y is not a worldline. The broad substitution identity is integral_{c_0}^{d_0} sqrt(-eta(y',y')) du = integral_a^b f(s) ds = c(tau_x(b)-tau_x(a)). If phi'(u)>0 at every point, including the one-sided endpoints, y is a C^1 future timelike worldline, its proper-time function tau_y is defined by def-sr-proper-time, and tau_y(d_0)-tau_y(c_0)=tau_x(b)-tau_x(a). More generally tau_y(u)-tau_y(v)=tau_x(phi(u))-tau_x(phi(v)) for all v,u in [c_0,d_0], so tau_y and tau_x o phi differ by a base-point constant. No tau_y is asserted for a zero-tangent curve outside that definition. For a strictly decreasing C^1 surjection phi onto [a,b], phi(c_0)=b, phi(d_0)=a and phi'<=0. The tangent of y is past timelike where phi'<0 and zero where phi'=0, so y is not a future timelike worldline. Its nonnegative length integral still equals integral_a^b f(s) ds: oriented substitution gives integral_{c_0}^{d_0} phi' f(phi)=integral_b^a f, and |phi'|=-phi' reverses that sign. These are mathematical curve-integral identities; physical clock reading is a separate premise.
items.strategy: By the componentwise chain rule, including its one-sided endpoint reading, y'=phi'(x' o phi). Bilinearity gives -eta(y',y')=(phi')^2(-eta(x' o phi,x' o phi)), so the nonnegative square root is |phi'|(f o phi). The function f is continuous on I by def-sr-proper-time, and the C^1 derivative phi' is continuous and therefore Riemann integrable on its compact interval. The published thm-substitution applies with f and phi even when phi' vanishes: for increasing phi its oriented endpoints are a,b and |phi'|=phi', proving the broad integral equality. The future cone is preserved by a positive scalar; at phi'=0 the tangent is zero, which is excluded by the worldline definition. Thus only the everywhere-positive derivative case permits applying def-sr-proper-time to y. Apply substitution on every subinterval [v,u] (with oriented reversal when u<v) to prove the proper-time difference formula and base-point constant. For decreasing phi, oriented endpoints b,a give the negative integral, while |phi'|=-phi' restores the positive integral; the tangent is past timelike where the scalar is negative and zero otherwise. No inverse of phi and no nonvanishing derivative are needed for the broad integral identities. No choice principle is used.

items.title: Four-velocity and four-acceleration of a future timelike worldline
items.statement: Let c > 0 and let x: I -> A be a C^1 future timelike worldline with proper-time function tau and inverse rho: J -> I (def-sr-proper-time, lem-sr-proper-time-parametrization). (a) The four-velocity of x is the map U: I -> V defined by U(s) := x'(s)/tau'(s) = c x'(s)/sqrt(-eta(x'(s),x'(s))); equivalently U(s) is the tangent at parameter value s of the proper-time parametrized worldline x o rho, read at the proper-time parameter tau(s). U is continuous, U(s) is future timelike for every s, and U does not depend on the base point chosen for tau. (b) If x is C^2, that is, x' is differentiable with continuous derivative, the four-acceleration of x is the map A: I -> V defined by A(s) := U'(s)/tau'(s) = c U'(s)/sqrt(-eta(x'(s),x'(s))); equivalently A is the derivative of the four-velocity with respect to the proper-time parameter along the worldline. A is continuous. (c) The dimensionless four-velocity of x is u := U/c. A point observer of the model at an event is a future unit timelike vector n in V, eta(n,n) = -1; the four-velocity of the observer's own worldline is cn at each of its events. (d) The names four-velocity and four-acceleration are the model's names for U and A; the physical interpretation, including the units in which U and A are measured, is supplied with the model's coordinate conventions and is not part of the affine geometry. The definition makes no claim that U has norm -c^2 or that A is orthogonal to U; those are proved in thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition.
items.strategy: Definition item: it introduces the two derived vector fields along a worldline and fixes their well-definedness. Obligations: (i) the division by tau'(s) is legitimate because tau' > 0 by lem-sr-proper-time-parametrization; (ii) the identification U(s) = (x o rho)'(tau(s)) is the chain rule applied componentwise in an inertial chart (def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral, thm-chain-rule), and it shows that U is the tangent field of the proper-time parametrized worldline; (iii) continuity of U follows from continuity of x' and tau' and continuity of division by the positive function tau'; (iv) A is defined only when x is C^2, in which case U' exists; (v) neither the norm of U nor the orthogonality of A with U is asserted here, so the definition cannot be used as if those identities were definitional. No choice principle is used.

items.title: Norms of four-velocity and four-acceleration, and the observer rest-space decomposition
items.statement: Let c > 0 and let (A,V,eta,C^+) be an oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space. (a) Norm of the four-velocity. Let x: I -> A be a C^1 future timelike worldline with four-velocity U (def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration). Then eta(U(s),U(s)) = -c^2 for every s in I; equivalently the dimensionless four-velocity u = U/c satisfies eta(u,u) = -1, and U(s) is future timelike. Thus U lies on the future hyperboloid eta(U,U)=-c^2, and the dimensionless u=U/c lies on the future unit hyperboloid eta(u,u)=-1. (b) Orthogonality of the four-acceleration. If x is C^2 at s, then eta(U(s),A(s)) = 0: the four-acceleration has no component along the four-velocity; if in addition A(s) is nonzero, then A(s) is spacelike. (c) Rest space and projection. Let n in V be future unit timelike, eta(n,n) = -1, and put n^perp := {v in V : eta(n,v) = 0}. Then n^perp is a 3-dimensional linear subspace of V, the restriction of eta to n^perp is positive definite, and the map h: V -> V, h(v) := v + eta(n,v) n, is linear, idempotent with h o h = h, has image n^perp and kernel span(n), satisfies h(n) = 0 and eta(n,h(v)) = 0 for all v in V, and every v in V has the unique decomposition v = -eta(n,v) n + h(v). Moreover |w| := sqrt(eta(w,w)) defines a norm on n^perp. (d) Relative velocity and Lorentz factor. Let n and u be future unit timelike vectors, put gamma := -eta(n,u) and w := c h(u)/gamma. Then gamma >= 1, w lies in n^perp, u = gamma (n + w/c), |w|^2 = c^2 (1 - gamma^{-2}) < c^2, gamma = (1 - |w|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}, and gamma = 1 if and only if u = n. The vector w is the velocity of a worldline with four-velocity c u relative to the observer n and gamma is its Lorentz factor. (e) Coordinate form. Let (o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3) be an inertial frame and let y be a C^1 future timelike worldline whose inertial coordinates are t |-> (c t, r(t)), with coordinate velocity w(t) := r'(t) in R^3 and, when y is C^2, coordinate acceleration a(t) := w'(t). Then |w(t)| < c, the four-velocity is U = gamma_w (c,w) with gamma_w := (1 - |w|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}, and the four-acceleration is A = gamma_w (d/dt)(gamma_w (c,w)), so that A^0 = gamma_w^4 (w.a)/c and A_vec = gamma_w^2 a + gamma_w^4 (w.a) w/c^2; consequently eta(A,A) = gamma_w^4 |a|^2 + gamma_w^6 (w.a)^2/c^2 >= 0, with eta(A,A) = 0 if and only if a = 0, and eta(U,A) = 0. For the observer n = e_0 of the chart, clauses (c) and (d) specialize to gamma = gamma_w and w_rel = w. (f) Scope. The statement is a theorem about the affine Minkowski model with a fixed positive constant c; it asserts no clock reading and identifies no physical four-velocity. No choice principle is used.
items.strategy: Proof in dependency order; the hard part is (c), which is pure algebra plus one coordinate computation, and the remaining clauses follow from it. (c) Fix an eta-orthonormal basis with e_0 timelike (lem-lorentz-form-has-orthonormal-basis; use an inertial frame of def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart). Write n = n^0 e_0 + n_s and v = v^0 e_0 + v_s with n_s,v_s in S = span(e_1,e_2,e_3), where eta restricts to the positive definite delta with norm |.| (def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame). From eta(n,n) = -(n^0)^2 + |n_s|^2 = -1 one gets (n^0)^2 = 1 + |n_s|^2 > 0. For v with eta(n,v) = -n^0 v^0 + delta(n_s,v_s) = 0 one has v^0 = delta(n_s,v_s)/n^0, hence eta(v,v) = -(v^0)^2 + |v_s|^2 = |v_s|^2 - delta(n_s,v_s)^2/(n^0)^2 >= |v_s|^2 (1 - |n_s|^2/(n^0)^2) = |v_s|^2/(n^0)^2 >= 0 by the finite Cauchy-Schwarz inequality for delta (thm-cauchy-schwarz-finite); equality forces |v_s| = 0 and then v^0 = 0, so v = 0 and the restriction is positive definite. The map v_s |-> v^0 e_0 + v_s with v^0 = delta(n_s,v_s)/n^0 is a linear bijection S -> n^perp, so n^perp is 3-dimensional. The properties of h are immediate from bilinearity of eta (def-lorentz-form-and-inertia, def-linear-map): eta(n,h(v)) = eta(n,v) + eta(n,v)eta(n,n) = 0, so h(v) lies in n^perp; h(n) = n + eta(n,n)n = 0; h(h(v)) = h(v) + eta(n,h(v))n = h(v); and v = -eta(n,v)n + h(v) is unique because the two summands lie in span(n) and n^perp, which meet only in 0. (a) By def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration, U = x'/tau' with tau' = c^{-1} sqrt(-eta(x',x')), so eta(U,U) = eta(x',x')/(tau')^2 = eta(x',x') c^2/(-eta(x',x')) = -c^2; timelikeness and the future direction of U follow from those of x' and positivity of 1/tau'. (b) eta(U,U) is the constant -c^2 along a C^2 worldline; differentiating componentwise in an eta-orthonormal basis with thm-algebra-of-derivatives gives 0 = (d/ds) eta(U,U) = 2 eta(U,U'), hence eta(U,U') = 0, and dividing by tau' > 0 gives eta(U,A) = 0. If A(s) is nonzero, then A(s) lies in (U(s)/c)^perp, a positive definite space by (c), so eta(A,A) > 0: A(s) is spacelike. (d) By (c), h(u) lies in n^perp and u = gamma n + h(u) with gamma = -eta(n,u). First, gamma > 0: in the inertial frame of (c), future timelikeness of n and u gives n^0 > |n_s| and u^0 > |u_s| (lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components), so eta(n,u) = -n^0 u^0 + delta(n_s,u_s) <= -n^0 u^0 + |n_s||u_s| < 0. Second, eta(u,u) = gamma^2 eta(n,n) + eta(h(u),h(u)) = -gamma^2 + |h(u)|^2 = -1, so |h(u)|^2 = gamma^2 - 1 >= 0, giving gamma >= 1; substituting w = c h(u)/gamma gives |w|^2 = c^2 (gamma^2-1)/gamma^2 = c^2(1 - gamma^{-2}) < c^2, and solving for gamma gives gamma = (1 - |w|^2/c^2)^{-1/2} and gamma = 1 iff h(u) = 0 iff u = n. (e) In the chart the coordinate path is t |-> (c t, r(t)), so x' = (c,w) and -eta(x',x') = c^2 - |w|^2 > 0 by future timelikeness, giving |w| < c and tau' = c^{-1} sqrt(c^2-|w|^2) = (1 - |w|^2/c^2)^{1/2} = 1/gamma_w; hence U = x'/tau' = gamma_w (c,w). For C^2 paths, d gamma_w/dt = gamma_w^3 (w.a)/c^2 by thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives (applied to the power -1/2) with the chain rule, and collecting terms in A = gamma_w dU/dt gives the displayed components; expanding eta(A,A) in the diagonal form and using gamma_w^2(1-|w|^2/c^2) = 1 gives eta(A,A) = gamma_w^4 |a|^2 + gamma_w^6 (w.a)^2/c^2 >= 0 with equality iff |a| = 0, and eta(U,A) = 0 agrees with (b). (f) The specialization n = e_0 is the evaluation h(u) = u - u^0 e_0 = (0, w/c gamma_w) and gamma = u^0 = gamma_w, so w_rel = w. No choice principle is used; all arguments are finite-dimensional or one-variable calculus.

items.title: Adopted free trajectories of massive particles and the clock hypothesis
items.statement: Adopt as physical assumptions of this framework, extending the ideal-clock reading rule of post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light to the general worldline calculus of this page: (i) Free trajectories. A massive test particle that is subject to no interaction (a free particle) has as its worldline a straight future timelike line of the affine model: there are an event p in A and a future timelike vector v in V with x(s) = p + (s - s_0) v for all s (the kinematical consequences of this shape for the four-velocity are derived, not assumed, in pthm-sr-four-velocity-norm-and-orthogonality). Interactions, forces and collisions are not part of this assumption: a particle that is not free may have any future timelike worldline admitted by its own dynamical model, and no force law is adopted here. (ii) Clock hypothesis. An ideal clock carried along a future timelike worldline of the model, including an accelerated one and a piecewise C^1 one with finitely many kinks, reads between any two parameter values the proper-time difference of def-sr-proper-time for C^1 histories and of def-sr-piecewise-proper-time for weak piecewise C^1 histories, with no additional term depending on acceleration, jerk or any higher derivative; a kink is an idealization of a finite short acceleration phase whose contribution is included through the integral on the smooth pieces, and the reading does not depend on an increasing regular change of parameter admitted by the curve definition: its derivatives on smooth pieces and all finite one-sided endpoint derivatives are positive, as in lem-sr-proper-time-reparametrization-invariance and lem-sr-piecewise-proper-time-reparametrization-invariance. Zero-tangent compositions are not worldlines of this model. (iii) Scope and qualification. The assumptions concern ideal point particles, ideal clocks and flat classical spacetime. They are adopted, not proved; they are not consequences of the affine geometry, and no experiment is claimed here to establish them. They inherit the idealizations of post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light: real clocks have finite resolution, calibration and apparatus limitations, and real particles are not exactly free.
items.strategy: A postulate, not a theorem: it fixes the physical interpretation of straight future timelike lines as the histories of free massive test particles and makes the clock-reading rule applicable to the general worldline class of this page. Obligations: (i) straight future timelike lines are declared objects of the affine model, and each is a future timelike worldline with constant tangent (def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline); (ii) the reading rule is an identification of a physical clock reading with the mathematical proper-time difference, so def-sr-proper-time and its reparametrization invariance are the mathematical suppliers carrying the content, while the identification itself is adopted; (iii) the free-trajectory clause is deliberately silent about interactions and force laws, so it cannot be used to infer conservation laws, mass-shell relations or collision kinematics, which require the separate momentum postulate of the later energy-momentum page; (iv) the clock hypothesis is the assertion that ideal clocks have no acceleration-dependent term, so it must not be presented as following from the geometry. No proof is manufactured; the item is an adopted premise with an exact scope. The weak piecewise mathematical referent is supplied by def-sr-piecewise-proper-time and its integrability lemma, and regular increasing weak-piecewise parameter independence by lem-sr-piecewise-proper-time-reparametrization-invariance. This repairs the formulation of the already adopted clock assumption; it does not derive clock behavior or extend its empirical scope.

items.physical_scope: Free massive test particles and ideal clocks in flat classical special-relativistic spacetime: straight future timelike histories for free particles, and proper-time readings for arbitrary future timelike histories with no acceleration-dependent correction. Excludes interactions and force laws, gravitational and quantum effects, real clock imperfections and every empirical measurement claim; the assumptions are adopted, not derived, and their idealizations travel to all consumers.

items.title: Four-velocity norm and four-acceleration orthogonality for the model's clocks
items.statement: Adopt the postulates of the model: post-sr-inertial-covariance and post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light of the spacetime-primitives page together with post-sr-free-trajectories-and-clock-hypothesis of this page, and let c and the SI coordinates be those of def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions. Let x: I -> A be the history of an ideal clock of the model, a C^1 future timelike worldline (C^2 where acceleration is used), with proper time tau, four-velocity U = dx/dtau and, when x is C^2, four-acceleration A = dU/dtau (def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration). Then: (i) the reading of the ideal clock between parameter values s_1 < s_2 equals tau(s_2) - tau(s_1); (ii) eta(U,U) = -c^2 everywhere, so U is future timelike with eta(U,U)=-c^2 and the unit of a velocity, while the dimensionless u=U/c is future unit timelike with eta(u,u)=-1; (iii) if x is C^2 at s, then eta(U(s),A(s)) = 0 and A(s) is zero or spacelike, with unit of acceleration; (iv) if the clock is free (no interaction), then its four-velocity is constant along the worldline and A = 0 identically; (v) for an ideal observer at the same event, described by a future unit timelike vector n = U_o/c with eta(n,n) = -1, the clock's speed relative to the observer is |w| = c sqrt(1 - gamma^{-2}) with gamma = -eta(n, U/c) >= 1, so it is strictly less than c, and gamma = 1 exactly when the clock's four-velocity equals the observer's. Scope and qualification: this is a conditional statement about the adopted model; it asserts no measurement outcome, contains no statistical inference, and inherits the idealizations of the postulates (ideal point particles, ideal clocks, flat spacetime, no gravitational or quantum effects).
items.strategy: Conditional deduction from the adopted premises; the mathematical content is thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition. (i) is the clock hypothesis of post-sr-free-trajectories-and-clock-hypothesis together with the proper-time definition, restated for the page's worldline calculus. (ii) and (iii) are clauses (a) and (b) of thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition, with U identified with the clock's four-velocity by the clock hypothesis; the identification supplies the physical meaning of U, the identities are mathematical. (iv) By the free-trajectory clause there are p and future timelike v with x(s) = p + (s - s_0)v; then x' = v is constant, tau' = c^{-1} sqrt(-eta(v,v)) is constant and positive, so U = x'/tau' is the constant vector c v/sqrt(-eta(v,v)), and A = U'/tau' = 0. (v) is clause (d) of the mathematical theorem, with the observer vector n allowed to be any future unit timelike vector; post-sr-inertial-covariance licenses the interpretation of observers and clocks as model objects and def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions fixes c and the units of the speed. The proof must not upgrade the conditional statement to a claim about nature and must carry the idealizations to the conclusion.

items.physical_scope: Ideal clocks and massive test particles in the flat classical special-relativity model: unit timelike four-velocity, four-acceleration orthogonal to four-velocity, vanishing four-acceleration for free particles, and subluminal speed relative to every ideal observer. Conditional on the named postulates; excludes interactions and force laws, gravity, quantum effects, real apparatus corrections and all empirical claims.

items.title: Worked example: the clock at rest in an inertial chart
items.statement: Worked computation. In an inertial chart of the model with eta_0 = diag(-1,1,1,1) consider the worldline x(t) = (c t, a_1, a_2, a_3) of a clock at rest at the spatial position (a_1,a_2,a_3), parametrized by the coordinate time t. Then x'(t) = (c,0,0,0), so -eta(x',x') = c^2 and the proper-time function is tau(t) - tau(t_0) = t - t_0; the four-velocity is U = x'/tau' = (c,0,0,0), with eta(U,U) = -c^2, and the four-acceleration vanishes, A = 0. Relative to the chart's observer e_0 the dimensionless four-velocity is u = U/c = (1,0,0,0) = e_0, so gamma = -eta(e_0,u) = 1 and the relative velocity is w = c h(u)/gamma = 0: the clock is at rest in the chart. This is the c-retained, (-+++) form of the source statement that an object at rest has four-velocity (1,0) and dt/dtau = 1.
items.strategy: Direct evaluation: the diagonal form applied to (c,0,0,0) gives -c^2, so the proper-time integrand is the constant c/c = 1 and tau is t - t_0; U = x'/tau' = (c,0,0,0) and U' = 0, so A = 0. The relative-velocity clauses are clauses (c) and (d) of thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition evaluated at these vectors. Every step is a finite computation from the definitions.

items.title: Worked example: proper time and four-velocity of a straight worldline at beta = 3/5
items.statement: Worked computation. In an inertial chart with eta_0 = diag(-1,1,1,1) consider the worldline x(t) = (c t, (3c/5) t, 0, 0), parametrized by coordinate time, which describes a clock moving along the first spatial axis with speed 3c/5. Then x'(t) = (c, 3c/5, 0, 0) and eta(x',x') = -c^2 + (9/25)c^2 = -(16/25)c^2, so sqrt(-eta(x',x')) = 4c/5 and tau(t) - tau(t_0) = (4/5)(t - t_0): the moving clock runs slow by the factor 4/5 = 1/gamma with gamma = 5/4. The four-velocity is U = x'/tau' = (5/4)(c, 3c/5, 0, 0) = (5c/4, 3c/4, 0, 0), which satisfies eta(U,U) = -25c^2/16 + 9c^2/16 = -c^2, and the four-acceleration vanishes because U is constant: A = 0. The dimensionless four-velocity is u = U/c = (5/4, 3/4, 0, 0); the split of clause (d) with n = e_0 gives gamma = 5/4 and relative velocity w = (3c/5, 0, 0), which is exactly the coordinate velocity.
items.strategy: Direct finite computation: evaluate the diagonal form on x', obtain the constant integrand c^{-1}(4c/5) = 4/5, integrate over [t_0,t], divide to obtain U, and evaluate eta(U,U). The vanishing of A is the constancy of U. The split clauses are clause (d) of thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition evaluated at u = (5/4,3/4,0,0) and n = e_0; all numbers are exact rationals.

items.title: Worked example: invariance of elapsed proper time under a cubic reparametrization
items.statement: Worked computation. In an inertial chart with eta_0 = diag(-1,1,1,1) let d := (5,3,0,0), a future timelike displacement with -eta(d,d) = 25 - 9 = 16 and sqrt(-eta(d,d)) = 4. (a) The worldline x(s) := s d on the parameter interval [1,8] has x'(s) = d, integrand sqrt(-eta(d,d)) = 4, and elapsed proper time tau(8) - tau(1) = (1/c) integral_1^8 4 ds = 28/c. (b) The reparametrization phi(u) := u^3 is a strictly increasing C^1 surjection of [1,2] onto [1,8]; its derivative 3u^2 is strictly positive throughout [1,2], so the reparametrized curve y(u) := x(u^3) = u^3 d has y'(u) = 3u^2 d, hence sqrt(-eta(y',y')) = 3u^2 sqrt(-eta(d,d)) = 12u^2, and elapsed proper time (1/c) integral_1^2 12u^2 du = (4/c)(8 - 1) = 28/c. The two elapsed times agree, as lem-sr-proper-time-reparametrization-invariance requires, and the proper-time function of x is tau(s) = 4s/c up to an additive constant, with inverse rho(tau) = c(tau - tau_0)/4, where tau_0 is the chosen additive constant. (c) Boundary check: instead take the same straight curve x(s)=s d on [-1,1] and phi(u)=u^3 on [-1,1]. This is a strictly increasing C^1 surjection, but y'(0)=0, so y is not a worldline of def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline. The broad length-integral identity nevertheless holds: integral_{-1}^{1} 12u^2 du=8=integral_{-1}^{1} 4 ds. No proper-time function of y is invoked outside its defining worldline domain.
items.strategy: Two independent exact computations of the same elapsed time: in (a) the integrand is the constant 4; in (b) the chain rule gives y' = 3u^2 d and the integrand 12u^2, whose integral over [1,2] is 28. The equality is the concrete instance of the invariance lemma, and the inverse function is read off the linear proper-time function. All arithmetic is rational. On [1,2], 3u^2>=3>0 verifies the strengthened worldline consequence. For the boundary interval [-1,1], differentiate u^3 d to obtain the zero tangent at zero, and integrate 12u^2 to get 8; this checks precisely the distinction between the broad substitution identity and the regular-worldline consequence.

items.title: Worked example: four-velocity and four-acceleration of uniform circular motion
items.statement: Worked computation. In an inertial chart with eta_0 = diag(-1,1,1,1) let R > 0 and omega be real with R|omega| < c and consider the worldline x(t) = (c t, R cos(omega t), R sin(omega t), 0), parametrized by coordinate time: uniform circular motion in the first two spatial coordinates. Then w(t) = (-R omega sin(omega t), R omega cos(omega t), 0) has |w| = R|omega|, so -eta(x',x') = c^2 - R^2 omega^2 and the proper-time factor is tau' = c^{-1} sqrt(c^2 - R^2 omega^2) = 1/gamma with gamma := (1 - R^2 omega^2/c^2)^{-1/2}; the four-velocity is U = gamma (c, w). Since |w| is constant, gamma is constant; the coordinate acceleration is a(t) = (-R omega^2 cos(omega t), -R omega^2 sin(omega t), 0), with |a| = R omega^2 and w.a = 0. By clause (e) of thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition the four-acceleration is A = (0, gamma^2 a), so A^0 = 0, eta(U,A) = 0 and eta(A,A) = gamma^4 R^2 omega^4 >= 0. Its magnitude is gamma^2 R omega^2; for R>0 it is spacelike exactly when omega!=0, while omega=0 is the static limit with gamma=1, U=(c,0,0,0) and A=0. Numerical specialization: if R omega = 3c/5, then gamma = 5/4 and the magnitude of the four-acceleration is gamma^2 R omega^2 = (25/16) R omega^2 = (15 c omega)/16.
items.strategy: Finite computation: differentiate the coordinate path, evaluate the diagonal quadratic form to get tau', read gamma, and apply clause (e) of the theorem with w.a = 0 to obtain A = gamma^2 a; the numerical values are exact rational multiples of c and omega. The acceleration is centripetal and orthogonal to the velocity, so the four-acceleration is orthogonal to the four-velocity by the theorem. Since R>0 and gamma>0, gamma^4 R^2 omega^4 is zero exactly when omega=0 and positive otherwise. At zero frequency the path is (ct,R,0,0) and both the coordinate and four-acceleration vanish. The specialization R omega=3c/5 has omega>0 and preserves the displayed exact value and acceleration units.

items.title: Worked example: splitting a four-velocity in an observer's rest frame
items.statement: Worked computation. In an inertial chart with eta_0 = diag(-1,1,1,1) let the observer be n = e_0 = (1,0,0,0) and let u = (5/4, 3/4, 0, 0), a future unit timelike vector: eta(u,u) = -25/16 + 9/16 = -1. Then gamma = -eta(n,u) = 5/4 >= 1, h(u) = u + eta(n,u) n = u - (5/4)(1,0,0,0) = (0, 3/4, 0, 0) lies in n^perp = span(e_1,e_2,e_3), and the relative velocity is w = c h(u)/gamma = (0, 3c/5, 0, 0). One checks u = gamma (n + w/c) = (5/4)(1, 3/5, 0, 0) and |w|^2 = 9c^2/25 = c^2 (1 - gamma^{-2}) = c^2 (1 - 16/25). Also h(h(u)) = h(u) and eta(n,h(u)) = 0. This four-velocity is the one of the clock with coordinate velocity (3c/5, 0, 0) in ex-sr-proper-time-of-a-straight-worldline.
items.strategy: Direct evaluation of clauses (c) and (d) of thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition on the displayed vectors: the projection, its idempotence and its orthogonality to n, the split u = gamma(n + w/c) and the identity |w|^2 = c^2(1 - gamma^{-2}) are each finite computations with rational numbers.

items.title: Counterexample: a future null curve has no proper-time parametrization
items.statement: Statement refuted: 'every regular C^1 curve of the model admits a proper-time parametrization, with strictly increasing proper-time function and normalized timelike four-velocity'. Counterexample: in an inertial chart with eta_0 = diag(-1,1,1,1) let k := (1,1,0,0), a future null vector with eta(k,k) = -1 + 1 = 0, and let x(s) := p + s k be the corresponding future null straight line. Then x'(s) = k is nonzero and future null for every s, so x is a regular future null curve in the sense of def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline, but the proper-time integrand is sqrt(-eta(x',x')) = 0 identically: the associated integral is constant, its derivative vanishes, there is no strictly increasing reparametrization by it, and no normalized four-velocity U with eta(U,U) = -c^2 can be attached to the curve, since every tangent vector is null. For the same given curve, the coordinate increments are x^0(x(s))-x^0(p)=s and x^1(x(s))-x^1(p)=s. With laboratory time t=x^0/c, the elapsed time is s/c and the spatial coordinate speed is c. This is a mathematical future-null line with no massive proper-time parametrization; interpreting its complete oriented line as an ideal light ray is conditional on the separately adopted ideal-light premise, not a physical deduction of this counterexample.
items.strategy: Direct computation: eta(k,k) = 0 makes the integrand vanish identically, so the proper-time function is constant and cannot be inverted; the tangent vectors are null, so no timelike unit normalization exists. The example is the concrete reason why def-sr-proper-time carries the future timelike hypothesis and why null rays need their own parametrization. All steps are finite evaluations of the diagonal form.

items.title: Counterexample: the proper-time integrand of a spacelike curve is not real
items.statement: Statement refuted: 'the formula tau(b) - tau(a) = c^{-1} integral_a^b sqrt(-eta(x',x')) ds assigns an elapsed clock time to every regular C^1 curve of the model'. Counterexample: in an inertial chart with eta_0 = diag(-1,1,1,1) let d := (1,2,0,0), a spacelike displacement with eta(d,d) = -1 + 4 = 3 > 0, and let x(s) := p + s d. Then x'(s) = d is spacelike, -eta(x',x') = -3 < 0, and the square root of a negative real number is not defined: the proper-time construction of def-sr-proper-time produces no real value on this curve. The geometric spacing along the curve is governed by the spacelike length sqrt(eta(d,d)) = sqrt(3) per unit parameter, not by a clock reading: a spacelike interval is not elapsed clock time, and such curves are the reason def-sr-proper-time carries the future timelike hypothesis.
items.strategy: Direct evaluation: the diagonal form on d gives +3, so the integrand -eta(d,d) is negative and has no real square root; hence the claim that the construction assigns a clock time to every regular curve is false. The final clause records which hypothesis of the definition excludes the case and that the spacelike length of the curve is a different quantity, not an elapsed time.

items.title: Counterexample: a past-directed parametrization of a timelike line is not a worldline
items.statement: Statement refuted: 'if a C^1 curve parametrizes a straight timelike line, then it is a future timelike worldline of the model and the proper-time construction gives the clock reading of its history'. Counterexample: in an inertial chart with eta_0 = diag(-1,1,1,1) let d := (5,3,0,0), a future timelike displacement with -eta(d,d) = 16, and let x(s) := p - s d for s in [0,1]. Then x'(s) = -d is past timelike for every s, so x is not a future timelike worldline (def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline); but the integrand sqrt(-eta(x',x')) = 4 is the same as for the future parametrization y(u):=p-d+u d=x(1-u), u in [0,1], so the proper-time integral alone does not distinguish the two parametrizations. The images of x and y are exactly the same segment from p-d to p, traversed in opposite directions: y(0)=p-d, y(1)=p and y'=d is future timelike. Their equal nonnegative length integrals do not assign a proper-time function or clock reading to x outside the future-worldline definition. The separately adopted ideal-clock interpretation applies to the future-directed history y, and x is its orientation reversal. This is why the parametrization, and not merely the image of the curve, is part of the definition of a worldline.
items.strategy: Direct evaluation: eta(-d,-d) = eta(d,d) = -16, so the integrand is identical for x(s)=p-sd and y(u)=p-d+ud=x(1-u), since their tangents are -d and d; u|->1-u maps[0,1] onto itself, proving the same-image assertion; the future/past alternative is decided by the time orientation of the model, not by the sign of eta(x',x'). Every step is a finite computation.

items.title: Smooth scalar and vector potentials on a star-shaped space-time region
items.reference: core-conditional-proofs.md#K7 and mathematical-prerequisites.md#M05; interfaces aligned to lem-em-joint-smooth-potentials and def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions
items.design_state: complete-exact-conditional-research-argument; local second application of the published joint-regularity supplier; not an independent acceptance
items.statement: Let $c>0$. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be an open set that is star-shaped with respect to a point $a\in\Omega$ ([[def-star-shaped-open-subset-of-rn]]) and let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval with at least two elements ([[def-interval]]). For any non-open time interval I, every joint regularity class here uses the open-neighbourhood restriction convention explicitly supplied by lem-em-joint-smooth-potentials, including the finite-k, C(k-1) and smooth conclusions. For the physical laboratory's open time interval the ordinary open-domain definition applies without extension. Fix an integer $k\ge2$ and let $E,B:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ be fields of class $C^k$ jointly on $\Omega\times I$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]], [[def-em-fields]]) satisfying the two source-free Maxwell equations of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] on $\Omega\times I$ in their pointwise form $$\operatorname{div}B=0,\qquad \operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB,$$ with the divergence and curl of [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]] and the partial derivative $\partial_t$ at fixed position of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]. Then there are a scalar potential $\varphi:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R$ of class $C^{k-1}$ jointly and a vector potential $A:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ of class $C^k$ jointly ([[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]]) with $$B=\operatorname{curl}A,\qquad E=-\nabla\varphi-\partial_tA\qquad\text{on }\Omega\times I.$$ If $E$ and $B$ are of class $C^\infty$ jointly on $\Omega\times I$, then $\varphi$ and $A$ may be chosen of class $C^\infty$ jointly. Conversely, if $\varphi$ and $A$ are of class $C^\infty$ jointly on $\Omega\times I$ and $E:=-\nabla\varphi-\partial_tA$, $B:=\operatorname{curl}A$ are their field pair, then $(E,B)$ satisfies $\operatorname{div}B=0$ and $\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB$ on $\Omega\times I$. The theorem asserts existence on the stated star-shaped domain only: it claims no global potential on a general open $\Omega$, no boundary or decay condition on the potentials, and no uniqueness; potentials are auxiliary objects of the framework and not claimed to be observable.

items.physical_scope: The fields and potentials of the classical vacuum electromagnetic framework of [[def-em-fields]], [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] and [[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]] on a single inertial laboratory region over a star-shaped spatial region. The only physical hypothesis used is the pair of source-free Maxwell equations (absence of magnetic charge and Faraday's law) as adopted in the postulate; no source equation, no regularity beyond the stated joint class, and no assertion that the potentials are observable are included. The star-shaped hypothesis is a genuine restriction on the spatial region, and the companion examples exhibit a divergence-free field on a non-star-shaped region with no global vector potential.

items.title: Potential representations, gauge transformations and gauge equivalence of the framework's fields
items.design_state: explicit-definition-contract; class bookkeeping and the smooth group action are stated exactly; reachability is excluded by contract
items.statement: Let $c>0$, let the laboratory region $U\cong I\times\Omega$ with its restricted inertial chart be that of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], let fields and units be those of [[def-em-fields]] and [[def-em-si-conventions]], and let the potential-pair vocabulary (scalar-vector pair, field pair $E(\varphi,A),B(\varphi,A)$, Lorenz divergence $G$, Lorenz gauge, gauge transform $T_\chi$ and wave expression $W$) be that of [[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]] on that region. (a) [Representations] For a field pair $(E,B)$ of class $C^{k-1}$ on $\Omega\times I$ and an integer $k\ge2$, a **potential representation of class $C^k$** of $(E,B)$ is a pair $(\varphi,A)$ of class $C^k$ jointly on $\Omega\times I$ whose field pair is $(E,B)$, that is, $\varphi:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R$, $A:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ of class $C^k$ jointly ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]) with $$E=-\nabla\varphi-\partial_tA,\qquad B=\operatorname{curl}A\qquad\text{on }\Omega\times I,$$ the derivatives being those of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]. This definition asserts neither existence (supplied on star-shaped regions under their stated hypotheses by [[pthm-em-spacetime-potentials]]) nor uniqueness of a representation. (b) [Gauge functions and gauge equivalence] A **gauge function** of class $C^m$ ($m\ge2$) on $\Omega\times I$ is a function $\chi:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R$ of class $C^m$ jointly; its **gauge transformation** acts on a potential pair by $$T_\chi(\varphi,A):=(\varphi-\partial_t\chi,\ A+\nabla\chi),$$ the transform of a $C^m$ pair being a potential pair of class $C^{m-1}$. Two pairs are **gauge related** when one is the transform of the other by some gauge function. On pairs and generators of class $C^\infty$, $T_0$ is the identity and $T_{\chi_1}(T_{\chi_2}(\varphi,A))=T_{\chi_1+\chi_2}(\varphi,A)$ for all $C^\infty$ generators $\chi_1,\chi_2$ ([[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], componentwise); hence gauge relatedness is an equivalence relation on the $C^\infty$ potential pairs. (c) [Conditions] A pair is **in Lorenz gauge** on $\Omega\times I$ when $G=\operatorname{div}A+c^{-2}\partial_t\varphi=0$ there, and **in Coulomb gauge** in the chosen spatial chart when $\operatorname{div}A=0$ there. These are properties of a pair in the stated conventions. The existence of a gauge function achieving a condition, with or without prescribed initial or boundary data, is a separate PDE conclusion with its own hypotheses and is not part of this definition. (d) [Physical status] The physical content of a representation is its field pair $(E,B)$ of [[def-em-fields]]; the pair $(\varphi,A)$ and the gauge function are auxiliary, their values are convention dependent, and gauge related representations have the same field pair. The scalar potential carries the volt and the vector potential the tesla metre, consistently with [[def-em-si-conventions]]; no value of $\varphi$ or $A$ is by itself an observable or evidence for a field.
items.strategy:
A vocabulary and bookkeeping definition over the exact interfaces of [[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]]; it makes no existence or solvability claim. Obligations checked: (i) the field-pair formulas and the transform are those of the cited definition, so the regularity statements (a $C^m$ pair gives $C^{m-1}$ fields; a $C^m$ generator gives a $C^{m-1}$ transform) are inherited exactly; (ii) the composition identity is the componentwise linearity of the coordinate partial derivatives, $\partial_t(\chi_1+\chi_2)=\partial_t\chi_1+\partial_t\chi_2$ and $
abla(\chi_1+\chi_2)=
abla\chi_1+
abla\chi_2$ ([[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]), together with $T_0=\mathrm{id}$; the inverse of $T_\chi$ is $T_{-\chi}$, so the relation is reflexive, symmetric and transitive on $C^\infty$ pairs; (iii) the definition deliberately separates the two gauge conditions from their reachability: no conclusion that a pair can be put in either gauge, with or without prescribed data, is drawn here (compare [[pthm-em-spacetime-potentials]] for existence of representations and the gauge-reachability theorem later on this page for the two declared branches); (iv) no choice principle, no domain hypothesis beyond the laboratory region, and no Maxwell equation is used.

references.title: David Tong, Electromagnetism, University of Cambridge Part II Mathematical Tripos lecture notes (2026 printing, 236 pp.)
references.locator: §3.2.2 printed pp. 48-49 (the gauge transformation A' = A + grad chi and the use of chi to adjust the divergence) and §5.3.1 printed pp. 105-106, eq. (5.13): phi -> phi - dchi/dt, A -> A + grad chi, with chi = chi(x,t)

references.title: L. D. Landau and E. M. Lifshitz, The Classical Theory of Fields, Third Revised English Edition (Course of Theoretical Physics vol. 2, Pergamon Press 1971, 387 pp.)
references.locator: §18 printed pp. 49-50, eqs. (18.1) and (18.3): the four-potential transformation A'_k = A_k - df/dx^k, equivalently A' = A + grad f and phi' = phi - (1/c) df/dt, with f an arbitrary function of the coordinates and the time; the fields are unchanged and only gauge-invariant quantities have physical meaning

items.physical_scope: The auxiliary potential vocabulary of the framework: potential representations of the adopted field pairs of [[def-em-fields]], their gauge transformations and the two named gauge conditions, in the single inertial laboratory chart. The item records that only the field pair is physical content and that the definition asserts no existence of representations (a separate theorem does, under its own hypotheses) and no reachability of a gauge condition (a separate PDE conclusion with its own domain and data hypotheses). No empirical claim is made and no convention of another unit system or framework is imported.

items.title: Gauge transformations preserve the field pair: invariance of the electric and magnetic fields
items.statement:
Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open, $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ an interval with at least two elements ([[def-interval]]), $c>0$, and fix $k\ge2$. Let $(\varphi,A)$ be a potential pair of class $C^k$ jointly on $\Omega	imes I$ and let $\chi$ be a gauge function of class $C^k$ jointly on $\Omega	imes I$ ([[def-em-gauge-transformation]], [[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]]). Then the gauge transform $T_\chi(\varphi,A)=(\varphi-\partial_t\chi,\ A+
abla\chi)$ is a potential pair of class $C^{k-1}$ jointly and its field pair is the field pair of $(\varphi,A)$: $$E(T_\chi(\varphi,A))=E(\varphi,A),\qquad B(T_\chi(\varphi,A))=B(\varphi,A)\qquad	ext{on }\Omega	imes I,$$ the common value being a map $\Omega	imes I	o\mathbb R^3$ of class $C^{k-1}$ jointly (the field pair of $(\varphi,A)$ in the sense of [[def-em-fields]] and [[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]]). In particular, gauge related potential representations of a field pair ([[def-em-gauge-transformation]]) have equal field pairs: the electric and magnetic fields are gauge invariants of the framework, and no value of $\varphi$, $A$ or $\chi$ is asserted to be observable. The identity uses only the definitions $E=-
abla\varphi-\partial_tA$, $B=\operatorname{curl}A$, the vanishing of $\operatorname{curl}
abla\chi$ for the $C^2$ function $\chi$ and the equality of the mixed partials $\partial_t\partial_i\chi=\partial_i\partial_t\chi$; no Maxwell equation, no hypothesis on $\Omega$ beyond openness and no choice principle is used. For a nonopen nondegenerate interval I, jointly Ck here means restriction from a Ck map on an open neighbourhood of Omega times I, as in [[lem-em-joint-smooth-potentials]]; all endpoint derivatives are the restrictions of those derivatives. Their values are independent of the extension because equality on the interior determines derivatives there and continuity determines them at included endpoints. No open-domain Ck definition is applied directly to a nonopen product.
items.strategy:
Magnetic field: $\operatorname{curl}(A+
abla\chi)=\operatorname{curl}A+\operatorname{curl}
abla\chi=\operatorname{curl}A$ by linearity of the curl ([[lem-divergence-and-curl-are-linear-and-obey-the-scalar-product-rules]]) and $\operatorname{curl}
abla\chi=0$ ([[thm-the-curl-of-a-gradient-vanishes]], applicable because $\chi$ is $C^2$, indeed $C^k$ with $k\ge2$). Electric field: componentwise, $-
abla(\varphi-\partial_t\chi)-\partial_t(A+
abla\chi)=-
abla\varphi-\partial_tA+(
abla\partial_t\chi-\partial_t
abla\chi)$, where the bracket vanishes by equality of the mixed second partials of the $C^2$ function $\chi$ ([[thm-clairaut-schwarz-mixed-partials]]) and the componentwise linearity of $
abla$ and $\partial_t$ is [[thm-algebra-of-total-derivatives]] and [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]. Regularity: $\partial_t\chi$ and $
abla\chi$ are $C^{k-1}$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]), so the transformed pair is $C^{k-1}$ and the two displayed field expressions are legitimate there; the common value equals the $C^{k-1}$ map $E(\varphi,A)$, resp. $B(\varphi,A)$, supplied by [[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]]. No further hypothesis is used. On a nonopen I perform the displayed differentiations on the declared open extensions, then restrict. The nondegenerate interval has dense interior in I, so all derivatives through the available order at included endpoints are uniquely determined by the restricted functions. Thus the equalities and the regularity conclusion have the same meaning at the endpoints without an extra openness hypothesis.

references.locator: §3.2.2 printed p. 48 and §5.3.1 printed pp. 105-106: A -> A + grad chi and phi -> phi - dchi/dt leave B = curl A and E = -grad phi - dA/dt unchanged

references.title: L. D. Landau and E. M. Lifshitz, The Classical Theory of Fields, Third Revised English Edition (Course of Theoretical Physics vol. 2, Pergamon Press 1971, 387 pp.)

items.physical_scope: The gauge invariance of the field pair of the classical vacuum electromagnetic framework on a laboratory region: gauge related potential representations of the framework's fields, in the conventions of [[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]], define the same electric and magnetic fields. The statement is conditional on the joint regularity of the pair and the generator; it contains no claim about the existence of generators meeting prescribed data, no empirical claim, and no assertion that a particular gauge is convenient or available.

items.title: Maxwell's equations in potential form: the Lorenz divergence, the decoupled wave equations and residual generators
items.design_state: complete-exact-conditional-research-argument; the exact algebraic identities are stated with their pointwise-regularity hypotheses; solvability is left to the reachability theorem
items.statement:
Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open, $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ an interval, $c>0$, and let $(\varphi,A)$ be a potential pair of class $C^2$ jointly on $\Omega	imes I$ ([[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]], [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]) with field pair $(E,B)$ ([[def-em-fields]]) and Lorenz divergence and wave operator $$G:=\operatorname{div}A+c^{-2}\partial_t\varphi,\qquad W:=c^{-2}\partial_t^2-\Delta.$$ Let $ho:\Omega	imes I	o\mathbb R$ and $J:\Omega	imes I	o\mathbb R^3$ be continuous sources ([[def-em-sources]]). For a nondegenerate nonopen I, joint C2 means restriction from C2 maps on an open neighbourhood, with the endpoint derivative convention of [[lem-em-joint-smooth-potentials]]. For a singleton I={t0}, retain a formal jet branch only after specifying such open extensions and their time jets; values on the singleton alone determine no time derivative. In that branch the statements below are identities between these prescribed jets, rather than a time-history claim. The decoupling implication additionally requires partial_t G=0 at t0 along with G=0 there (spatial gradient G is then zero). The value-level gauge-shift and residual-generator identities still hold for the prescribed jets without this extra derivative condition. (a) [Exact identities] Independently of any field equation, on $\Omega	imes I$ $$\operatorname{div}E=W\varphi-\partial_tG,\qquad \operatorname{curl}B-c^{-2}\partial_tE=WA+
abla G.$$ Consequently the sourced Maxwell equations of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] hold for $(E,B,ho,J)$ if and only if $$W\varphi-\partial_tG= rac{ho}{\varepsilon_0},\qquad WA+
abla G=\mu_0J\qquad	ext{on }\Omega	imes I.$$ (b) [Gauge shift] If $\chi$ is a gauge function of class $C^2$ jointly on $\Omega	imes I$, then $G(T_\chi(\varphi,A))=G-W\chi$ on $\Omega	imes I$ ([[def-em-gauge-transformation]]), and the transformed pair has the same field pair $(E,B)$ ([[pthm-em-gauge-invariance]]). Hence $T_\chi(\varphi,A)$ is in Lorenz gauge if and only if $W\chi=G$ on $\Omega	imes I$. (c) [Decoupling in Lorenz gauge] Suppose additionally that the given potential pair is in Lorenz gauge, $G=0$ on $\Omega	imes I$, with the additional condition $\partial_tG=0$ for the formal singleton-jet branch only. Then its field pair solves the sourced Maxwell system of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] if and only if the pair satisfies the decoupled sourced wave equations
$$W\varphi=ho/\varepsilon_0,\qquad WA=\mu_0J\qquad	ext{on }\Omega	imes I.$$
The source-free equations $\operatorname{div}B=0$ and $\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB$ are automatic for a potential pair. For an arbitrary given $C^2$ potential pair, for nondegenerate I, the conjunction of Lorenz gauge and these wave equations implies the sourced Maxwell system, but Maxwell's equations alone do not impose $G=0$ on that representative. In full generality their exact equivalent conditions remain the residual equations in (a), including $-\partial_tG$ and $
abla G$. Thus the equivalence with decoupled waves holds within the declared Lorenz gauge, without asserting gauge reachability. (d) [Residual generators] If $W\chi=0$ then the transform of a pair in Lorenz gauge is again in Lorenz gauge with the same field pair; the Lorenz condition therefore does not determine the potential pair. (e) [Scope] The identities and equivalences are properties of a given potential representation of class $C^2$; they assert no existence of a generator with $W\chi=G$ (or with prescribed data), which is the subject of the gauge-reachability theorem on this page, and they impose no boundary, decay or initial condition. A pair of class $C^1$ defines $E,B$ but need not have the second derivatives appearing in $W\varphi$, $WA$, $\Delta$ or $\partial_tG$, so $C^2$ is the exact standing regularity here.
items.strategy:
(a) Componentwise expansion using the sum rules for divergence and curl ([[lem-divergence-and-curl-are-linear-and-obey-the-scalar-product-rules]]), the vector identity $\operatorname{curl}\operatorname{curl}A=
abla\operatorname{div}A-\Delta A$ for the $C^2$ field $A$ ([[cor-the-curl-of-a-curl-of-a-c2-field]]), the definition $\Delta\varphi=\operatorname{div}
abla\varphi$ ([[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]]) and the equality of mixed partials of the $C^2$ functions $\varphi,A$ ([[thm-clairaut-schwarz-mixed-partials]]): $\operatorname{div}E=-\Delta\varphi-\partial_t\operatorname{div}A=W\varphi-\partial_tG$, and $\operatorname{curl}B-c^{-2}\partial_tE=\operatorname{curl}\operatorname{curl}A+c^{-2}\partial_t
abla\varphi+c^{-2}\partial_t^2A=
abla\operatorname{div}A-\Delta A+c^{-2}\partial_t
abla\varphi+c^{-2}\partial_t^2A=WA+
abla G$. The two source-free equations hold automatically for a potential pair by [[thm-the-divergence-of-a-curl-vanishes]] and [[thm-the-curl-of-a-gradient-vanishes]] with the linearity of curl ([[lem-divergence-and-curl-are-linear-and-obey-the-scalar-product-rules]]); hence the equivalence with the sourced system. (b) Direct expansion of $T_\chi$: $G(T_\chi(\varphi,A))=\operatorname{div}A+\Delta\chi+c^{-2}\partial_t\varphi-c^{-2}\partial_t^2\chi=G-W\chi$, using linearity and the $C^2$ mixed-partials identity for $\chi$ ([[thm-clairaut-schwarz-mixed-partials]], [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]); the field part is [[pthm-em-gauge-invariance]]. (c) On nondegenerate I, G=0 on the product makes both derivatives zero on its interior and by continuity at its included endpoints. On singleton I the spatial derivative is zero but the time derivative is not determined by G=0; the separately stipulated time-jet condition partial_t G=0 supplies exactly the missing term. Substitution in (a) turns the two sourced residual equations exactly into $W\varphi=ho/\varepsilon_0$ and $WA=\mu_0J$. Conversely those two wave equations with $G=0$ make the residual equations hold, and the two source-free equations were already proved for every potential pair. There is no inference from Maxwell alone to a gauge condition; (d) is (b) with $G=0$ and $W\chi=0$. All statements are pointwise on $\Omega	imes I$; the constants $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ are those of the framework postulates ([[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]]). No choice principle, no hypothesis on the shape of $\Omega$ and no solvability of $W\chi=G$ is used. For singleton jets the field identities and gauge invariance follow directly on the declared C2 extensions by the same mixed-partial expansions; do not invoke the nondegenerate-interval gauge theorem as if its interval hypothesis held. For example phi=t^2/2, A=0 at t0=0 has zero field jets satisfying the residual Maxwell identities but G=0 and partial_t G=1/c^2; hence W phi=1/c^2 and value-only Lorenz gauge does not imply decoupling. Requiring the indicated jet condition restores the equivalence, without deleting any nondegenerate closed/half-open branch. Empty products have only vacuous equalities and no time jets. A singleton formal jet branch does not assert an adopted laboratory history on a degenerate time interval.

items.physical_scope: Exact pointwise identities for a given jointly C^2 potential representation of the adopted sourced vacuum Maxwell system. The sourced Maxwell equations are equivalent to the residual equations in (a). Within the separately declared Lorenz gauge G=0 they are equivalent to the two decoupled sourced wave equations. Maxwell alone does not select a gauge representative. Homogeneous-wave gauge generators preserve Lorenz gauge and the fields. items.title: Gauge reachability: Lorenz gauge on the all-space slab and Coulomb gauge on a bounded smooth domain, with residual freedom
items.reference: core-conditional-proofs.md#K7 and completed-expansion-arguments.md#W6; bounded-domain branch closed locally with the published elliptic resolvent and higher-order Dirichlet estimates; branch (b) parameter/ambient extension and compatible boundary-family estimates: physics-em-sr-40-2026-10-08-gauge-reachability-regularity-proposal.md
items.design_state: complete branch argument preserving the two Lorenz/Coulomb settings and restoring smooth parameter-dependent admissible Dirichlet/Neumann boundary data; incompatible data remain excluded
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ in branch (a) and the Axiom of Choice together with $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as declared by its weak-solvability lemmas in branch (b) ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $c>0$ and let $(\varphi,A)$ be a potential pair of the framework ([[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]], [[def-em-fields]]) with field pair $(E,B)$ and Lorenz divergence $G=\operatorname{div}A+c^{-2}\partial_t\varphi$. (a) [All-space slab; Lorenz gauge] Let $t_0<T$ and let $(\varphi,A)$ be of class $C^\infty$ in the extension sense on $\mathbb R^3\times[t_0,T]$ (the restriction of a $C^\infty$ pair on $\mathbb R^3\times J$ for some open interval $J\supset[t_0,T]$; [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]). Then there is a gauge function $\chi$ of class $C^\infty$ in the extension sense on $\mathbb R^3\times[t_0,T]$ with $\chi(\cdot,t_0)=0$, $\partial_t\chi(\cdot,t_0)=0$ and $W\chi=G$ on $\mathbb R^3\times(t_0,T)$; the transformed pair $T_\chi(\varphi,A)$ is in Lorenz gauge on $\mathbb R^3\times(t_0,T)$, has the same field pair $(E,B)$, and any two such gauge functions differ by a solution of $W\chi=0$. This is the exact content of [[lem-em-gauge-wave-reachability]] read for potential pairs of the framework; its physical content is that every smooth potential representation of a field pair on a slab admits a Lorenz-gauge representative with zero gauge Cauchy data at $t_0$, without changing the fields. (b) [Bounded smooth domain; Coulomb gauge with admissible boundary families] Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded $C^\infty$ graph domain ([[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]]), let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an arbitrary interval, possibly unbounded, and let $(\varphi,A)$ be $C^\infty$ on an actual neighbourhood of $\overline\Omega\times\overline I$. Prescribe either (i) a Dirichlet family $g_D(p,t)$ smooth in boundary charts on a neighbourhood of $\partial\Omega\times\overline I$, or (ii) an outward conormal family $\kappa(p,t)$ with the same smoothness and the compatibility $\int_{\Omega_j}\varepsilon_0\operatorname{div}A(\cdot,t)\,dx+\int_{\partial\Omega_j}\kappa(\cdot,t)\,dS=0$ for every connected component $\Omega_j$ and every $t\in I$. Then there is a gauge generator $\psi$, the restriction of one $C^\infty$ function on an actual open neighbourhood of $\overline\Omega\times\overline I$, such that $\operatorname{div}(A+\nabla\psi)=0$ on $\Omega\times I$. In case (i), $\psi(p,t)=g_D(p,t)$ on $\partial\Omega\times I$, and its restriction to $\Omega\times I$ is unique with those Dirichlet values. In case (ii), $\varepsilon_0\partial_\nu\psi(p,t)=\kappa(p,t)$ there, and imposing $\int_{\Omega_j}\psi(\cdot,t)\,dx=0$ for every component and every $t$ gives a unique generator on $\Omega\times I$; without that normalization it is unique modulo smooth time-dependent spatial constants on each component. The transformed pair $T_\psi(\varphi,A)$ is in Coulomb gauge and has the same physical field pair ([[pthm-em-gauge-invariance]]). Any two Coulomb-gauge generators differ by a function spatially harmonic at every $t$; equal Dirichlet data eliminate that residual freedom, whereas equal Neumann data leave only the componentwise constants just described. Zero Dirichlet data are the corresponding special case. Auxiliary ambient continuations away from the physical region need not be unique. (c) [Residual freedom on star-shaped domains] Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open and star-shaped ([[def-star-shaped-open-subset-of-rn]]) and let $(\varphi,A)$, $(\tilde\varphi,\tilde A)$ be two potential pairs of class $C^2$ jointly on $\Omega\times I$ ([[def-interval]]) with the same field pair, both in Lorenz gauge. If I is non-open, these C2 classes and the resulting generator use the open-neighbourhood restriction convention of lem-em-joint-smooth-potentials; for the physical open laboratory interval they have their ordinary C2 meaning. If a degenerate I is used in this branch, choose the ambient C2 extensions as part of the data: the same-field and Lorenz conditions refer to these extensions on an ambient time neighbourhood before restriction, and their time jets are not determined uniquely by the restricted values alone. Then there is a gauge function $\chi$ of class $C^2$ jointly with $(\tilde\varphi,\tilde A)=T_\chi(\varphi,A)$ and $W\chi=0$ on $\Omega\times I$. (d) [Scope] Nothing is asserted about gauge functions meeting arbitrary prescribed boundary or initial restrictions: in (a) the gauge function has zero Cauchy data at $t_0$ and no spatial boundary condition or decay, and $\Omega$ is all of $\mathbb R^3$; in (b) the datum is either a smooth time-dependent Dirichlet family or a smooth outward conormal family satisfying the stated componentwise compatibility at every physical time, with zero-mean normalization for Neumann uniqueness; the older promise of a global Lorenz gauge on a bounded domain with prescribed boundary data is explicitly outside this result. The Coulomb-gauge statement concerns the spatial divergence in the chosen inertial chart, and the instantaneous appearance of the Coulomb potential is a property of the representation, not a signal: only the field pair $(E,B)$ is physical content ([[def-em-fields]]).
items.strategy:
(a) is [[lem-em-gauge-wave-reachability]] with its hypotheses and countable choice carried verbatim; the pair of the framework enters only through the vocabulary, so nothing is reproved. (b) The fixed-time smooth Dirichlet and compatible Neumann interfaces are those of [[thm-em-elliptic-boundary-existence]], and their parameter-compatible ambient smoothness, exact boundary lifts, complete natural-Neumann estimates and normalized uniqueness are supplied by the earlier pure-mathematical [[lem-em-parameter-dependent-smooth-poisson-boundary-solvers]]. Use the original open neighbourhood of the potentials and of the boundary family to choose an open time interval $J$ containing $\overline I$ by compactness of each fixed spatial/boundary fibre; only $\overline\Omega	imes K$, with compact $K\subset J$, is used for derivative bounds, never compactness of all $\overline I$. Put $F_t=\varepsilon_0\operatorname{div}A(\cdot,t)$. In the Dirichlet case the supplier constructs a fixed finite-chart spatial lift $H_t=L_Dg_D(\cdot,t)$ and the zero-trace operator $R$ for $-\varepsilon_0\Delta$ from its exact weak solver, including every $L^2$ source, with its higher-order bounds. Set $\psi_t=H_t+R(F_t+\varepsilon_0\Delta H_t)$. Differentiation includes the lift at every order: $\partial_t^j\psi_t=L_D\partial_t^jg_D+R(\partial_t^jF_t+\varepsilon_0\Delta L_D\partial_t^jg_D)$. Thus the spatial equation is $-\varepsilon_0\Delta\psi_t=F_t$ and the Dirichlet family is exact. In the Neumann case use the same supplier's compatible normalized weak solver and natural-boundary estimates. Compatibility is imposed only for $t\in I$: on an open $J$, define $c_j(t)=\int_{\Omega_j}F_t+\int_{\partial\Omega_j}\kappa_t$ and the auxiliary bulk extension $\widehat F_t=F_t-c_j(t)/|\Omega_j|$ on each of the finitely many components. It is smooth, compatible for all $t\in J$ and agrees with $F_t$ on $I$; no equation for the gauge outside the physical interval is promised. Apply the parameter solver to $(\widehat F,\kappa)$ with zero mean on each component. In either case locally uniform compact-time difference-quotient estimates give all mixed derivatives up to the boundary, and the supplier's fixed parameter-preserving Seeley construction supplies one actual ambient $C^\infty$ continuation, not merely separate finite-order Sobolev representatives. The resulting generator obeys $\Delta\psi=-\operatorname{div}A$ on every physical time, with the requested boundary data, so it is Coulomb gauge and preserves the fields by [[pthm-em-gauge-invariance]]. Elliptic uniqueness gives the stated normalized uniqueness on $\Omega	imes I$; subtracting any two Coulomb generators gives $\Delta\chi=0$ and the listed Dirichlet/Neumann residual freedom. This argument retains the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice hypotheses of the variational, chart and Sobolev suppliers, and imposes no global time bounds or extra regularity restriction. (c) Put $\delta\varphi=	ilde\varphi-\varphi$ and $\delta A=	ilde A-A$. Equality of the field pairs gives $\operatorname{curl}\delta A=0$ and $
abla\delta\varphi+\partial_t\delta A=0$. Apply the corrected scalar lemma to $C=\delta A$ and denote its negative-gradient witness by $\phi_{\delta A}(x,t)=-\int_0^1\langle\delta A(a+s(x-a),t),x-aangle ds$. Then $
abla\phi_{\delta A}=-\delta A$ and $\phi_{\delta A}$ is jointly $C^2$. Take $$\chi_0=-\phi_{\delta A}=\int_0^1\langle\delta A(a+s(x-a),t),x-aangle ds,$$ so $
abla\chi_0=\delta A$. This additional negation is essential; using the lemma's negative-gradient witness itself as the gauge generator would reverse the vector-potential difference. Mixed partials of the $C^2$ function $\chi_0$ now give $
abla(\delta\varphi+\partial_t\chi_0)=
abla\delta\varphi+\partial_t\delta A=0$. For fixed t, restrict this $C^1$ scalar to each radial segment $a+s(x-a)$; the chain rule gives zero derivative, and cor-zero-derivative-implies-constant gives its common value $h(t)=\delta\varphi(a,t)+\partial_t\chi_0(a,t)$. Since $\chi_0(a,t)=0$ for every t, the time derivative there is zero, so $h(t)=\delta\varphi(a,t)$ (in particular h is C1; indeed C2 under the stated hypotheses). For nondegenerate I, fix $t_*\in I$ and set $$\eta(t)=-\int_{t_*}^{t}h(u)du.$$ cor-primitives-of-a-continuous-function gives $\eta'=-h$ on I, with relative endpoint derivatives; since h is C1, eta is C2. Put $\chi=\chi_0+\eta$. Then $
abla\chi=\delta A$ and $\partial_t\chi=\partial_t\chi_0-h=-\delta\varphi$, so $T_\chi(\varphi,A)=(	ilde\varphi,	ilde A)$. Finally the unchanged exact gauge-shift identity in pthm-em-lorenz-gauge-wave-form(b) gives $0=G(	ilde\varphi,	ilde A)=G(\varphi,A)-W\chi=-W\chi$, hence $W\chi=0$. The corrected radial construction gives chi0 as a C2 restriction from an open radial-admissibility neighbourhood. At the centre, the data extension gives h(t)=delta phi(a,t) on an open time neighbourhood; take the interval component containing I and construct the time primitive there. Adding this primitive to the chi0 extension yields a C2 extension on the intersection neighbourhood of Omega x I. Thus the asserted generator retains the same regularity convention at included endpoints of nondegenerate time intervals. Degenerate interval restrictions do not supply unique time jets: any use of this time-derivative branch there carries chosen ambient extensions and the same-field/Lorenz hypotheses on an ambient time neighbourhood, to which the nondegenerate construction applies before restriction. On an empty restriction there are no pointwise equations to prove. The physical laboratory branch already uses a nonempty open time interval.  This residual construction uses no choice principle; the preexisting Choice assumptions in branches (a)-(b) remain exactly as stated. The linearity of $
abla$ and $\partial_t$ used throughout is [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]] and [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]; $H^m$ notation is [[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]], and the elliptic problems use the domains of [[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]]. The declared Choice assumptions enter only through the elliptic existence theorem and the wave supplier and are carried in the statement. No claim beyond (a)-(c) is made.

items.physical_scope: Gauge reachability for potential representations of the classical vacuum electromagnetic framework, in exactly two declared branches: the all-space smooth slab branch, where a Lorenz-gauge representative with zero gauge Cauchy data exists (carrying countable choice through the wave supplier), and the bounded smooth-domain branch, where a Coulomb-gauge representative with prescribed smooth parameter-dependent Dirichlet data exists uniquely on the physical region, or with componentwise-compatible smooth Neumann flux data exists uniquely after zero-mean normalization (carrying the choice assumptions declared by the elliptic supplier). The item also classifies residual freedom on star-shaped domains. It makes no empirical claim, asserts nothing about arbitrary prescribed boundary or initial restrictions, and does not claim that gauge conditions are physically observable.

items.title: Calculus of separated phasor fields: real-part derivative identities and amplitude injectivity
items.reference: core-conditional-proofs.md#K9; scaffold-added necessary prerequisite (see batch-35 notes)
items.strategy: Differentiate each component of $\operatorname{Re}(we^{i\theta})$ with $w=\tilde F_j$ by the product and chain rules for real and imaginary parts ([[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[thm-complex-exponential-is-entire-with-derivative-itself]]), using $\operatorname{Re}(i\zeta)=-\operatorname{Im}\zeta$ and $\operatorname{Re}(-i\zeta)=\operatorname{Im}\zeta$; assemble the divergence and curl componentwise. For (d), write $C=a+ib$ with real $a,b$; the two scalar equations $a\cos\varphi_j-b\sin\varphi_j=0$ ($j=1,2$) form a real $2\times2$ system of determinant $\sin(\varphi_1-\varphi_2)$ for each component, The determinant is nonzero by [[thm-sine-cosine-zero-sets-and-fundamental-period]]; the determinant identity is the sine subtraction formula of [[thm-sine-and-cosine-addition-formulas]], with real-part encoding justified by [[cor-complex-exponential-cartesian-form-modulus-and-eulers-identity]]. Hence $a_j=b_j=0$. If $F=G$ on an open $U$, then for every $x_t$ in the projection fix one real $x_3$ in that open fibre and vary $t$ on a small open interval. Put $C=(\tilde F(x_t)-\tilde G(x_t))e^{i\beta x_3}$; the exponential is nonzero even for complex $\beta$. The real time phases $-\omega t$ contain an interval and hence two values with difference strictly between $0$ and $\pi$. Clause (d) forces $C=0$ and therefore $\tilde F(x_t)=\tilde G(x_t)$. Complex $\beta$ changes a fixed spatial amplitude factor, not this real time-phase injectivity. The projection of a nonempty open set is nonempty and open.

items.reference: core-conditional-proofs.md#G1; scaffold-added necessary prerequisite (see batch-35 notes)
items.statement:
Let $e_z$ be a unit vector of $\mathbb R^3$ and identify $\mathbb R^3=\mathbb R^2\oplus\mathbb R e_z$ with transverse coordinates $(x_1,x_2)$; write $
abla_t h=(\partial_1h,\partial_2h)$, $\Delta_t h=\partial_1^2h+\partial_2^2h$ and, for a transverse $C^1$ map $u_t$ with components $(u_1,u_2)$, $\operatorname{div}_t u_t=\partial_1u_1+\partial_2u_2$ and $\operatorname{curl}_2 u_t=\partial_1u_2-\partial_2u_1$; regard $h$, $
abla_th$, $u_t$ and $e_z	imes u_t$ as $z$-independent fields on $\Omega_t	imes\mathbb R$, with $e_z$ the third basis vector. Let $h:\Omega_t	o\mathbb R$ be $C^2$ and $u_t:\Omega_t	o\mathbb R^2$ be $C^1$. Then, with the divergence, curl, cross product and inner product of [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]], [[def-cross-product-in-r3]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]:
(a) $\operatorname{div}(e_z	imes
abla_th)=0$; $\operatorname{curl}(e_z	imes
abla_th)=e_z\,\Delta_th$; $e_z	imes(e_z	imes
abla_th)=-
abla_th$; $
abla_th\cdot(e_z	imes
abla_th)=0$; $e_z\cdot(e_z	imes
abla_th)=0$; $|e_z	imes
abla_th|=|
abla_th|$;
(b) $\operatorname{curl}(e_zh)=-e_z	imes
abla_th$ and $\operatorname{div}(e_zh)=\partial_3h$ (which vanishes for $z$-independent $h$);
(c) $\operatorname{curl}(u_t)=e_z\operatorname{curl}_2u_t$, $\operatorname{div}(u_t)=\operatorname{div}_tu_t$, and $e_z	imes u_t$ is transverse.
items.strategy: Work in the oriented orthonormal basis $(e_1,e_2,e_z)$ and write out the six component formulas: for $v=\nabla_th$ one has $e_z\times v=(-\partial_2h,\partial_1h,0)$, whence the divergence is $-\partial_1\partial_2h+\partial_2\partial_1h=0$ by equality of mixed partials ([[thm-clairaut-schwarz-mixed-partials]]), the curl is $(0,0,\partial_1^2h+\partial_2^2h)$ and the triple-product and norm identities reduce to $a\cdot(e_z\times a)=0$ and $|e_z\times a|=|a|$ for $a\perp e_z$ ([[lem-cross-product-is-bilinear-alternating-and-orthogonal]]). For (b) use $\operatorname{curl}(e_zh)=(\partial_2h,-\partial_1h,0)$ and the definition of the curl; for (c) note that a $z$-independent field with zero third component has curl $(0,0,\partial_1u_2-\partial_2u_1)$.

items.title: The separated sine and cosine rectangle profiles: eigen-identities, boundary traces, orthogonality and Dirichlet integrals
items.reference: completed-expansion-arguments.md#G1-G2; scaffold-added necessary prerequisite (see batch-35 notes)
items.strategy: Differentiate the products with [[thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives]] and the product rule ([[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]); the boundary values follow from $\sin(0)=\sin(m\pi)=0$ and $\cos'(t)=-\sin t$. The orthogonality and norm values are iterated one-dimensional integrals computed with the product-to-sum identities of [[thm-sine-and-cosine-addition-formulas]] and the second fundamental theorem ([[thm-ftc-second-part]]) applied to the continuous integrands; Fubini on the rectangle ([[thm-riemann-fubini-on-product-rectangles]], [[thm-continuous-on-a-rectangle-is-riemann-integrable]]) justifies iterated integration. For the mixed term use $\cos(m\pi x/L)\sin(p\pi x/L)=\tfrac12[\sin((p+m)\pi x/L)+\sin((p-m)\pi x/L)]$. If $p=m$, the second term is identically zero and the first integrates to zero. Otherwise FTC gives $L[(1-(-1)^{p+m})/(p+m)+(1-(-1)^{p-m})/(p-m)]/(2\pi)$, which is the stated parity formula (and includes $m=0$). The integer endpoint values are furnished by [[thm-sine-cosine-zero-sets-and-fundamental-period]] and [[thm-quarter-turn-values-and-shift-formulas]]. Rectangle Fubini then gives the product $J_{mp}J_{nq}$. For (d) integrate $\partial_1(h\partial_1h)=(\partial_1h)^2+h\partial_1^2h$ over the interval in $x_1$ for fixed $x_2$ with the FTC; the boundary term vanishes by (a), and the same in $x_2$; the $e_{mn}$ case is identical with the boundary term vanishing by (b). All steps are choice-free finite computations over the exhibited profiles.
