items.title: The sine and cosine systems are complete orthogonal systems of L^2 on an interval and on a rectangle
items.reference: completed-expansion-arguments.md#G2; scaffold-added necessary prerequisite (see batch-35 notes)
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $L>0$ and $R=(0,L_1)\times(0,L_2)$ with $L_1,L_2>0$.
(a) [One interval] The families $\{\cos(m\pi x/L)\}_{m\ge0}$ and $\{\sin(m\pi x/L)\}_{m\ge1}$ are orthogonal complete systems in the real Hilbert space $L^2(0,L)$ ([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]], [[lem-l-two-with-the-integral-pairing-is-a-hilbert-space]], [[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]): each is orthogonal, and its closed linear span is all of $L^2(0,L)$.
(b) [Rectangle] With $m,n$ ranging over $\mathbb N_0$ in cosine slots and over $\mathbb N_{\ge1}$ in sine slots, each of the four product families $\{\cos\frac{m\pi x_1}{L_1}\cos\frac{n\pi x_2}{L_2}\}$, $\{\cos\frac{m\pi x_1}{L_1}\sin\frac{n\pi x_2}{L_2}\}$, $\{\sin\frac{m\pi x_1}{L_1}\cos\frac{n\pi x_2}{L_2}\}$ and $\{\sin\frac{m\pi x_1}{L_1}\sin\frac{n\pi x_2}{L_2}\}$ is an orthogonal complete system in $L^2(R)$; in particular the Neumann family $\{h_{mn}\}_{m,n\ge0}$ and the Dirichlet family $\{e_{mn}\}_{m,n\ge1}$ of [[lem-em-rectangle-mode-profile-identities]] are orthogonal complete systems in $L^2(R)$.
items.strategy: (a) Rescale $x=L u/\pi$ to period $2\pi$ ([[thm-linear-change-of-variables-for-lebesgue-measure]]). For $f\in L^2(0,L)$ orthogonal to every $\cos(m\pi x/L)$, extend $f$ evenly to $(-L,L)$ and $2L$-periodically; the extended $F$ lies in $L^2$ of the torus and every character coefficient $\widehat F(k)$ is a fixed multiple of $\int_0^Lf(x)\cos(k\pi x/L)\,dx$, computed by splitting the integral at $0$ and substituting $x\mapsto-x$ on $(-L,0)$ ([[cor-c-one-change-of-variables-for-l-one-functions]]); hence all coefficients vanish and [[thm-trigonometric-system-is-complete-in-l-two-of-the-torus]] gives $F=0$, so $f=0$. The sine case uses the odd extension, whose character coefficients are the sine coefficients (the $k=0$ coefficient vanishes identically). (b) Orthogonality is product integration. If $f\in L^2(R)$ is orthogonal to every $c_m(x_1)d_n(x_2)$, then for each $m$ the function $g_m(x_2):=\int_0^{L_1}f(x_1,x_2)c_m(x_1)\,dx_1$ is in $L^2(0,L_2)$ by Cauchy-Schwarz and Fubini ([[cor-cauchy-schwarz-inequality-for-l-two]], [[thm-fubini-theorem-for-l-one-on-sigma-finite-product-spaces]]), and $\int_0^{L_2}g_md_n=0$ for all $n$ by Fubini, so $g_m=0$ a.e. by (a). Taking the countable union of the exceptional null sets, for a.e. $x_2$ one has $\int_0^{L_1}f(x_1,x_2)c_m(x_1)\,dx_1=0$ for all $m$, so $f(\cdot,x_2)=0$ a.e. in $x_1$ by (a), and Fubini gives $f=0$ a.e. Completeness as closed span is therefore established; the orthogonal expansions converge in $L^2$ by [[thm-hilbert-space-fourier-expansion]]. The argument is symmetric in the four parity choices.

items.title: Rectangular PEC guide and cavity geometry, the zero-normal-B reflection class, and axis-relative TE/TM/TEM
items.statement:
Let the laboratory region $U\cong I\times\Omega$, its frame basis $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$, its SI units and its fields $E,B$ be those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], [[def-em-si-conventions]] and [[def-em-fields]]. Fix $a,b>0$, write $x_t=(x_1,x_2)$, $e_z:=e_3$, and define $\nabla_t f=(\partial_1f,\partial_2f,0)$, $\Delta_t f=\partial_1^2f+\partial_2^2f$ and $\operatorname{div}_tu_t=\partial_1u_1+\partial_2u_2$ for the stated regularity, using [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]], [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]] and [[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]].
(a) [Straight guide] A straight guide region is $\Omega_A:=A\times\mathbb R$ where $A$ is either a bounded connected $C^1$ plane domain ([[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]]) or the explicit rectangular cross-section; the rectangle has corners and is treated by its open faces, not asserted to be a $C^1$ boundary domain, with longitudinal axis $e_z$; for a rectangular cross-section $A=R_{ab}:=(0,a)\times(0,b)$ the region is called the rectangular guide and its walls are the four open faces $\{x_1=0\},\{x_1=a\},\{x_2=0\},\{x_2=b\}$. A rectangular cavity region is $\Omega_c:=(0,a)\times(0,b)\times(0,d)$ for fixed $d>0$, with the six open faces as its walls. The separate smooth-cavity spectral branch uses an explicitly declared bounded $C^\infty$ domain in $\mathbb R^3$ with its smooth PEC boundary; it is not the rectangular reflection class. Spatial derivatives are taken at fixed $t$; the fields are defined on $\Omega\times I$ with the regularity declared by each theorem.
(b) [PEC boundary model] On every open wall (a wall minus its edges) the ideal perfectly conducting boundary model declares the two conditions $n\times E=0$ and $n\cdot B=0$, where $n$ is the outward unit normal of that wall ($-e_1,+e_1,-e_2,+e_2$ on the four rectangular walls, and $\pm e_j$ on the six cavity walls). Its physical reading is the ideal-conductor limit of the stationary interface conditions of [[pthm-em-material-stationary-jumps]]: with $E=B=0$ inside the ideal conductor the tangential electric field and the normal magnetic field vanish, while the surface-charge and surface-current readings $\sigma_f=-n\cdot D$ and $K_f=-n\times H$ are determined by the vacuum-side traces and are not prescribed here. Here n points outward from vacuum into the zero-field conductor, so the supplier jump is conductor minus vacuum. If n_c=-n is instead the conductor-outward normal pointing into vacuum, the same readings are sigma_f=n_c dot D and K_f=n_c cross H. The PEC zero conditions are unchanged under either normal sign. The supplier's hypotheses (a compact embedded $C^2$ hypersurface with one-sided $C^1$ fields) cover a smooth stationary interface, not the $\sigma\to\infty$ idealization nor the box edges; the guide/cavity conditions on the open walls are therefore declared as an idealization of this definition, and no pointwise statement on the edges is made.
(c) [Zero-normal-B reflection class] For the rectangular box $Q=\prod_{j=1}^3(0,L_j)$ with $L=(a,b,d)$, the reflection class is the class of locally integrable fields $E,B$ on $Q$ whose extensions to the rectangular torus $\prod_j\mathbb R/(2L_j\mathbb Z)$, defined by extending $E_1$ evenly across the $x_1$-walls and oddly across the $x_2$-, $x_3$-walls and cyclically for $E_2,E_3$, and extending $B_1$ oddly across $x_1$ and evenly across $x_2,x_3$ and cyclically for $B_2,B_3$, are $L^2$ fields, together with the distributional constraints that $\operatorname{div}E$ and $\operatorname{div}B$ vanish on the torus for the extensions. This is the declared weak PEC model used for the cavity initial-value problem; for smooth fields the parities give $n\times E=0$ and $n\cdot B=0$ on $\partial Q$. Initial data not in this class (for example data with trapped normal $B$) are excluded, as are the general $H(\operatorname{curl})$ boundary classes, which are defined by the mathematical suppliers and are not identified here with the classical conditions.
(d) [TE, TM, TEM] For a guide or cavity field $(E,B)$, the longitudinal components are $E_z:=E\cdot e_z$ and $B_z:=B\cdot e_z$; the field is called TE (transverse electric) if $E_z\equiv0$, TM (transverse magnetic) if $B_z\equiv0$, and TEM if both vanish, always relative to the named axis $e_z$.
(e) [Separated phasor convention] For $\omega>0$ and $\beta\in\mathbb C$, a $\beta$-$\omega$ separated phasor field on the guide is a real field of the form $F(x,t)=\operatorname{Re}\bigl(\tilde F(x_1,x_2)e^{i(\beta x_3-\omega t)}\bigr)$ with a complex amplitude $\tilde F$, componentwise; $\omega/(2\pi)$ is the frequency and $\beta$ the longitudinal propagation constant; when $\beta$ is real, $\beta>0$ describes propagation in the $+e_z$ direction under this phase convention, while a complex $\beta$ gives the spatial factor $e^{-\operatorname{Im}\beta x_3}$ and may grow in the opposite direction; each consuming branch states its selection.
(f) [Scope] The definition fixes the geometry, the PEC boundary model, the weak reflection class and the mode terminology; it asserts no field equation, no constitutive law and no existence or completeness of modes, Rectangular TE/TM candidates and the rectangular reflection class, declared smooth bounded PEC cavity spectral classes, and smooth straight-guide TEM potential branches (including the coaxial annulus) are within this geometry. No general non-rectangular TE/TM guide theory, circular-guide spectral classification, open-end or junction scattering, or lossy model is supplied.
items.strategy: An explicit type/domain/convention definition: geometry and transversality are fixed by coordinates and normals; the PEC model is declared with its interface reading and its excluded idealization/edges; the reflection class is defined by the reflection rules and distributional divergence constraints; the phasor convention is stated as an encoding of real fields. No differential equation is introduced. For the charge/current interpretation take the minus side to be vacuum and the plus side conductor, with supplier normal n pointing from minus to plus. With zero conductor fields, [D]=-D_vac and [H]=-H_vac, giving sigma_f=-n dot D_vac and K_f=-n cross H_vac. This is an orientation calculation, not a deduction of the ideal conducting limit or an edge trace theorem. Reversing to the conductor-outward n_c=-n gives the alternative positive formulas without changing n cross E=0 or n dot B=0.
items.physical_scope: The ideal PEC boundary model of the straight rectangular guide and cavity (and of straight guides with a bounded connected C1 cross-section) in the lossless laboratory chart, together with the zero-normal-B reflection class and the TE/TM/TEM classification. The boundary model is an idealization of an interface with a perfectly conducting medium on the open walls; the definition asserts no field equations, constitutive laws or mode completeness.

items.title: Complete mode expansions of the declared guide and cavity classes: transverse profile completeness, the rectangular reflection class and the smooth PEC cavity eigenbasis
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice as declared by the cited mathematical suppliers ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]), the lossless isotropic scalar constant branch of [[post-em-material-closure]] with $\varepsilon,\mu>0$ and $\sigma=0$, the source-free smooth macroscopic equations of [[pthm-em-macroscopic-maxwell]] in the smooth branches, with $\rho_f=0$, $J_f=0$, and the explicitly declared weak first-order material equations in the weak cavity branches below, and the guide, cavity, PEC and reflection-class conventions of [[def-em-guide-cavity-geometry]].
(a) [Transverse profile completeness] For the cross-section $(0,a)\times(0,b)$, the families $\{h_{mn}\}_{m,n\ge0}$ and $\{e_{mn}\}_{m,n\ge1}$ of [[lem-em-rectangle-mode-profile-identities]] are orthogonal complete systems in $L^2$ of the rectangle ([[lem-em-rectangular-transverse-mode-completeness]]); The full scalar Neumann and Dirichlet families have these $L^2$ expansions. The physical TE candidate family excludes $h_{00}=1$ by the full Maxwell equations: the remaining $h_{mn}$ are complete in the zero-mean subspace $\{f\in L^2:\int_Rf=0\}$, not in all scalar $L^2$. The Dirichlet TM profiles retain their full scalar completeness. The constant Neumann scalar profile is retained in the mathematical basis but is not asserted to be a nonzero positive-frequency TE mode.
(b) [Rectangular cavity reflection class] For the box $Q=(0,a)\times(0,b)\times(0,d)$ with the reflection class and distributional constraints $\operatorname{div}E=\operatorname{div}B=0$ of [[def-em-guide-cavity-geometry]](c): the finite separated Fourier modes are dense in the class at every time; every initial datum in the class has a unique $C(\mathbb R;L^2)$ weak solution of the lossless first-order system $\partial_tE=(\varepsilon\mu)^{-1}\operatorname{curl}B$, $\partial_tB=-\operatorname{curl}E$ in the same class, with derivatives as in [[def-distributional-derivative]]; this lossless first-order distributional system is the explicitly adopted weak material evolution of the reflection model, not inferred from the smooth-only hypotheses of [[pthm-em-macroscopic-maxwell]]; along the solution the total stored energy $\int_Q u\,dx$ equals $\frac12\int_Q(\varepsilon|E|^2+|B|^2/\mu)\,dx$ and is constant, where the weak stored-energy density is defined almost everywhere by this nonnegative quadratic expression, consistent with the smooth local definition of [[pthm-em-restricted-material-energy]]. Its integrability and constancy are furnished by the mathematical reflection-class energy result; no nonlinear weak Poynting identity is asserted. For $C^1$-in-time solutions the four macroscopic equations with $D=\varepsilon E$, $B=\mu H$ hold distributionally.
(c) [Smooth PEC cavity] For a bounded $C^\infty$ cavity domain $\Omega$ and the PEC class $X,V,H$ of [[thm-em-waveguide-spectral-completeness]](a): the curl form on $V$ has a complete orthonormal $L^2$ eigenbasis $\{u_j\}$ with nonnegative eigenvalues $\lambda_j$ of finite multiplicity, $\lambda_j\to\infty$ whenever $H$ is infinite dimensional, and a finite-dimensional zero eigenspace that is retained; the eigen-equation $\operatorname{curl}\operatorname{curl}u_j=\lambda_ju_j$ holds distributionally with the PEC trace, and each $u_j$ has a $C^\infty$ representative on the closure. Put $v_{\mathrm{wave}}=(\varepsilon\mu)^{-1/2}>0$. The associated second-order electric wave has the full supplied interface: for arbitrary initial displacement in $V$ and velocity in $H$, its displacement is in $C(\mathbb R;V)$, its velocity in $C(\mathbb R;H)$, and finite modal sums converge in these respective norms uniformly on compact time intervals. Its zero eigenmodes may be affine in time. Separately, let $J$ be an open time interval and let a strong first-order solution obey $E\in C^1(J;H)\cap C(J;V)$ and $B\in C^1(J;L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^3))\cap C(J;H(\operatorname{curl}))$, with the first-order equations as $L^2$ identities and both distributional divergence constraints. Electric tangential-zero boundary data are encoded by $E(t)\in V$. The magnetic normal-zero condition is declared weakly by $\int_\Omega B(t)\cdot\nabla\psi=0$ for every smooth scalar $\psi$ on the closure; when $B\in C^1(\overline\Omega)$ this is $n\cdot B=0$, using $\operatorname{div}B=0$. No magnetic membership in the electric tangential-zero class $X$ is assumed. Then $a_j(t):=\langle E(t),u_j\rangle$ is $C^2$ and satisfies $a_j''+v_{\mathrm{wave}}^2\lambda_ja_j=0$. For $\lambda_j=0$, the admissible first-order coefficients satisfy $a_j'=0$ and are constant, with the zero eigenfields retained. This extra compatibility distinguishes first-order Maxwell data from arbitrary second-order $V\times H$ data; it does not remove the broader supplied second-order wave or its affine zero modes.
(d) [Scope] The theorem asserts completeness only for the transverse $L^2$ profiles and for the two declared cavity classes with their exact hypotheses; it asserts no completeness for the unbounded guide's longitudinal expansion, and none for lossy, dispersive, open-ended, non-smooth or exterior problems, or arbitrary non-rectangular guide problems beyond the explicitly declared smooth-cavity spectral class, no trace regularity for arbitrary $H(\operatorname{curl})$ fields, and no identification of the weak classes with every maximal tangential-trace realization. The zero eigenvalues and zero modes are retained throughout.
items.strategy: Clause (a) is [[lem-em-rectangular-transverse-mode-completeness]](b) instantiated at the cross-section, whose profiles are those of the candidate theorem. Clause (b) is the rectangular reflection-class lemma [[lem-em-rectangular-pec-energy-completeness]] read physically, as packaged in [[thm-em-waveguide-spectral-completeness]](b): the class, the first-order system, density of finite separated modes, unique $C_tL^2$ weak solutions and constant energy all come from that supplier; the identification of the energy with $\int_Qu$ uses $D=\varepsilon E$, $B=\mu H$ and [[pthm-em-restricted-material-energy]](a), and the macroscopic equations follow from the two evolution equations together with the distributional divergence constraints of the class. For the scalar basis distinction in (a), every nonconstant Neumann product is orthogonal to $h_{00}=1$, and the complete orthogonal expansion of [[lem-em-rectangular-transverse-mode-completeness]] shows that deleting that one basis element gives precisely its orthogonal complement, the zero-mean subspace. The constant scalar element remains in the full basis and is excluded only as a monochromatic TE reconstruction. In (b), the explicit weak first-order model is solved by [[lem-em-rectangular-pec-energy-completeness]] as packaged in the wrapper; its Fourier energy proof gives the quadratic energy conservation without applying a smooth-only local balance to rough fields. For (c), [[thm-em-waveguide-spectral-completeness]] supplies the spectral and smooth-eigenfield assertions and the associated wave at the positive parameter $v_{\mathrm{wave}}=(\varepsilon\mu)^{-1/2}$, with its exact arbitrary $V\times H$ initial-data interface, displacement $C_tV$ and velocity $C_tH$. To derive the first-order coefficient equations, prove the actual curl pairing against each smooth PEC eigenfield $u_j$, not an unproved equality of electric and magnetic boundary classes. A smooth normal collar of the compact boundary exists by [[thm-euclidean-tubular-neighbourhood-theorem]]. Write $s$ for the inward normal coordinate (its gradient is the negative extended unit normal) and use the standard smooth step [[def-the-standard-smooth-step-function]] to set a cutoff $\eta_\delta=0$ for $s\le\delta$ and $1$ for $s\ge2\delta$. The normal tube has bounded Jacobians on the compact collar. Since $n\times u_j=0$ on the boundary and $u_j$ is smooth, $|n\times u_j|\le Cs$ in the collar. Thus $\eta_\delta u_j\to u_j$ and $\operatorname{curl}(\eta_\delta u_j)\to\operatorname{curl}u_j$ in $L^2$: the derivative-cutoff term is bounded on a layer of volume $O(\delta)$ because $|\nabla\eta_\delta|\le C/\delta$ and its cross product with $u_j$ is $O(s/\delta)$. For every $F\in H(\operatorname{curl})$, the distributional identity on the compactly supported smooth test $\eta_\delta u_j$ is $\langle\operatorname{curl}F,\eta_\delta u_j\rangle=\langle F,\operatorname{curl}(\eta_\delta u_j)\rangle$. Cauchy-Schwarz and the two $L^2$ limits give $\langle\operatorname{curl}F,u_j\rangle=\langle F,\operatorname{curl}u_j\rangle$. Apply this only to $F=B(t)$, which has the stated actual graph regularity. Then $a_j'=v_{\mathrm{wave}}^2\langle B,\operatorname{curl}u_j\rangle$. The assumed $B\in C^1_tL^2$ permits one further scalar derivative, giving $a_j''=v_{\mathrm{wave}}^2\langle B',\operatorname{curl}u_j\rangle=-v_{\mathrm{wave}}^2\langle\operatorname{curl}E,\operatorname{curl}u_j\rangle=-v_{\mathrm{wave}}^2\lambda_j\langle E,u_j\rangle$ by the full-$X$ eigenvariational identity of [[lem-em-smooth-pec-cavity-spectral-closure]], since $E(t)\in V\subset X$. No second time derivative of the whole field is assumed. If $\lambda_j=0$, that identity tested at $u_j$ gives $\operatorname{curl}u_j=0$, so the preceding formula for $a_j'$ is zero. Such electric zero modes are constant under first-order Maxwell evolution, while the associated unrestricted second-order equation retains affine zero modes. Divergence constraints and the declared magnetic normal condition remain part of the physical model; the pairing does not impose a magnetic electric-type trace. The inherited AC and AComega assumptions cover the spectral/Fourier and collar suppliers. No lossy or open-domain step is made.
items.physical_scope: The completeness statements available for the declared classes of the lossless isotropic scalar constant branch: transverse L^2 profile completeness of the TE/TM families on the rectangular cross-section, the rectangular cavity reflection class with its unique finite-energy weak solutions and constant stored energy, and the smooth bounded PEC cavity curl eigenbasis with modal expansions retaining zero modes. No open-guide, lossy, non-smooth or exterior completeness claim, nor a general non-rectangular guide claim beyond the stated smooth-cavity spectral class. Displacement and velocity topologies and first-order zero-mode compatibility are explicit.

items.title: Adopted retarded solution selection: the physical branch carries no incoming free field
items.statement: Adopt as a physical assumption of this framework the following solution-selection rule for the classical vacuum model on the laboratory region $U\cong I\times\Omega$ of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], with the constants and SI units of [[def-em-si-conventions]] (so $c>0$, $\mu_0>0$, $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$). (a) [Formulation] In the potential formulation of [[pthm-em-lorenz-gauge-wave-form]] with the conventions of [[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]], for a $C^2$ potential pair in Lorenz gauge the sourced Maxwell system of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] is equivalent to the decoupled sourced wave equations $W\varphi=\rho/\varepsilon_0$, $WA=\mu_0J$, where $W=c^{-2}\partial_t^2-\Delta$. The wave expression $W$ is invariant under $t\mapsto-t$; where explicit retarded or advanced constructions for a prescribed history exist, they give distinguished particular solutions built from the corresponding forward or backward fundamental kernels. Every other solution differs from a chosen particular solution by a source-free addition; retarded and advanced particular solutions also differ by such an addition. This describes the affine free-solution freedom, not a claim that arbitrary histories have exactly two solutions or that either construction always exists. (b) [Adopted rule] The framework adopts the retarded branch with no free field added: the physical potential pair of the model is the retarded one, that is, the one whose support and propagation lie in the forward light cones of the source and which carries no field arriving from the past independently of the source. For the zero-incoming model the selected sourced solution has no independently prescribed homogeneous addition. If nonzero Cauchy data are instead prescribed, their compatible homogeneous addition is a separate initial-data model; it is not equivalent to setting every free addition to zero. The advanced construction and independent incoming free fields are excluded by the present retarded selection. (c) [Status and scope] This is an adopted extra temporal condition carrying the model's arrow-of-time content. It is not a theorem, not a consequence of the time-symmetric wave or Maxwell equations (which admit advanced and free solutions as mathematical objects), and not a deduction from experiment; it asserts no existence, uniqueness, regularity, support or decay for any source class, all of which must be supplied separately by theorems of this page. It selects a solution only of the models to which it is applied; it introduces no product of distributions, no source model, no self-force, no radiation reaction, no measured signal and no statistical claim. The retarded compact-source branch to which this selection applies is developed on this page as a conditional theorem, and the point-source branch is developed later on this page; neither existence statement is part of this postulate. For the separately declared point-source branch assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), as in its exact source/field interfaces, and adopt the same no-free-addition retarded selection in the weak equations of [[post-em-distributional-vacuum-maxwell]], for the locally integrable field and proper point-current types of [[def-em-weak-sources]]. This extends the selection's model scope explicitly; neither existence nor an arbitrary convolution of noncompact distributions is postulated.
items.strategy: A postulate: the item records an adopted solution-selection rule, and receives a source/scope review rather than a proof. The review checks that (i) the formulation correctly displays the wave expression $W$, its time-reversal symmetry, the retarded and advanced fundamental-solution branches and the free-field freedom, all with the exact interfaces of [[pthm-em-lorenz-gauge-wave-form]], [[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]] and [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]]; (ii) the adopted rule is stated as a modelling choice with its arrow-of-time content, and is not presented as a consequence of the equations; (iii) the formulation does not pretend to prove existence or uniqueness for any source class and expressly defers those to the consuming theorems; (iv) no empirical, statistical, measurement or apparatus claim is made, and no quantitative precision is invented; and (v) the scope exclusions (advanced branch, free fields, arbitrary distributions, self-force) are explicit. The classical textbook treatments listed in the sources present the retarded/advanced distinction and the extra choice of the retarded Green function (Tong's 'extra choice' at the displayed page); they support the formulation and the honest status, and are not evidence for the physical correctness of the choice. The weak point-source extension is an explicit physical selection on the already-adopted singular-source equations, not a deduction from the old smooth-only potential theorem. A consuming mathematical theorem must construct its actual history integrals and prove weak admissibility.
items.physical_scope: Adopted selection rule for the classical vacuum Maxwell/wave model in the framework's inertial laboratory chart and SI conventions: the physical potential pair is the retarded one with zero incoming free field. Excluded: existence, uniqueness, regularity or decay claims for any source class (consuming theorems must supply them); empirical, statistical or measurement claims; the advanced branch and free fields as physical solutions; products of distributions, self-force, radiation reaction and any apparatus model.

items.title: Uniformly subluminal prescribed worldline, retarded root and retarded geometric data off the worldline
items.statement: Let the laboratory region, inertial chart, spatial Euclidean structure and SI units be those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] and [[def-em-si-conventions]], in particular $c>0$, $\mu_0>0$, $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$. A **retarded point-geometry datum** consists of a real charge parameter $q\in\mathbb R$ in coulombs ([[def-em-sources]](a)) and a prescribed map $z:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^3$ of class $C^3$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]) together with a constant $0\le v_*<c$ such that $|z'(s)|\le v_*$ for every $s\in\mathbb R$ ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]]); the spacetime curve $s\mapsto(z(s),s)$ is the laboratory reading of a prescribed massive future timelike worldline of the physical model ([[def-em-relativistic-worldlines-frames]]), and $v_*$ is a declared bound on its coordinate speed, not a measured quantity. Write $\Gamma:=\{(z(s),s):s\in\mathbb R\}$ and $D:=\{(x,t)\in\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R:x\ne z(t)\}$ for the open off-worldline observation domain. Then: (a) [Retarded root] For every observation event $(x,t)\in D$ there is exactly one $s=s(x,t)<t$ with $t-s=|x-z(s)|/c$; the map $s:D\to\mathbb R$ is of class $C^3$, and with the data of (b) below one has $\partial_ts=1/\kappa$ and $\nabla_xs=-n/(c\kappa)$ ([[lem-em-global-retarded-root]], whose $C^3$ branch applies because $z$ is $C^3$ and uniformly subluminal). (b) [Retarded data] For $(x,t)\in D$ define $R:=x-z(s(x,t))$, $r:=|R|>0$, $n:=R/r$, $\beta:=z'(s(x,t))/c$, $\kappa:=1-n\cdot\beta$, $\dot\beta:=z''(s(x,t))/c$; then $r=c(t-s)$ and $\kappa\in[1-v_*/c,\,1+v_*/c]\subseteq(0,\infty)$. On $D$ the objects $r$ and $n$ are of class $C^3$, $\beta$ and $\kappa$ are of class $C^2$, and $\dot\beta$ is of class $C^1$ (each is a composition of the $C^3$ root with $z$ or its derivatives). (c) [Emission-event data and emitted spheres] At an emission event $s_0\in\mathbb R$ and a direction $n\in S^2$ put $x_r:=z(s_0)+rn$, $t_r:=s_0+r/c$ for $r>0$, and $\beta_0:=z'(s_0)/c$, $\kappa_0:=1-n\cdot\beta_0$. Then $(x_r,t_r)\in D$ and $s(x_r,t_r)=s_0$ for every $r>0$: the sphere $\{x_r\}$ at observation time $t_r$ is emitted at the single event $s_0$. (d) [Branches and scope] Only the all-time uniformly subluminal branch (a)-(c) is defined by this datum. For a curve prescribed on a finite interval $J$ the same formulas define retarded data only at observation events for which the root equation has a solution $s\in J$; each consumer must assume that cone intersection explicitly. Pointwise subluminality $|z'(s)|<c$ for every finite $s$ does not imply (a): the companion example on the examples page exhibits a smooth curve with $|z'|<c$ pointwise for which the retarded equation has no root at some event, so the uniform bound $v_*<c$, or an explicit cone-intersection hypothesis, is part of the datum. This definition is kinematic: it fixes the root, the retarded data and the notation, and asserts no field, no dynamics, no force law, no self-force and no empirical content. The identification of these data with the emission data of the physical field is made by the selection postulate [[post-em-radiation-selection]] together with the theorems of this page.
items.strategy: An explicit definition with its well-definedness discharged by a cited mathematical supplier. Existence, uniqueness and $C^3$ regularity of $s$ on $D$, together with $\kappa\in[1-v_*/c,1+v_*/c]$ and the derivative formulas, are exactly the all-time uniformly subluminal $C^3$ branch of [[lem-em-global-retarded-root]] (its statement covers every event of $\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$, hence every off-worldline event, and identifies equality $s=t$ with $x=z(t)$); no new analysis is needed, and the phrase 'prescribed worldline' is licensed by [[def-em-relativistic-worldlines-frames]](a),(c), which relates chart readings $t\mapsto r(t)$ of massive worldlines to the condition $|r'(t)|<c$. Clause (c) is the elementary root check $t_r-s_0=|x_r-z(s_0)|/c=r/c$ combined with the uniqueness in (a); no boundedness of $z''$ is used. Clause (d) records the branch boundaries honestly: the finite-history and nonuniform cases are left to consumers, and the failure of existence under mere pointwise subluminality is not asserted here but exhibited on the examples page. The definition introduces no physical field, so no Maxwell, self-force or empirical assertion is made; the cross-reference to the selection postulate records that the retarded root is the kinematic object that the adopted selection turns into an emission time. No choice principle beyond that carried by the cited root lemma is used.
items.physical_scope: Kinematic definition of the retarded emission data of a prescribed uniformly subluminal $C^3$ worldline in the framework's laboratory chart: retarded root, distance, direction, speed ratio and emission-time Jacobian off the worldline, and the emitted-sphere family. Excluded: any field, Maxwell equation, dynamics, force law, self-force, radiation reaction, existence under a merely pointwise subluminal or finite-history curve, and every empirical or measurement claim.

items.title: Zonal and quadratic sphere moments for the polar surface measure on $S^2$
items.reference: scaffold-added necessary mathematical prerequisite for the dipole and emitted-power items (see research/physics-em-sr-40-2026-10-08-batch-36.notes.md)
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), as carried by the surface-measure interface below ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\sigma$ be the polar surface measure on the unit sphere $S^2\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ ([[def-polar-surface-measure-on-the-unit-sphere]]), let $e_3:=(0,0,1)$ be the third coordinate unit vector and write $n_3=n\cdot e_3$ for $n\in S^2$. Then: (a) [Zonal identity] for every continuous $f:[-1,1]\to\mathbb R$, $$\int_{S^2}f(n_3)\,d\sigma(n)=2\pi\int_{-1}^{1}f(u)\,du.$$ (b) [Linear weighted moment] for every continuous $f$ and every $a\in\mathbb R^3$, $$\int_{S^2}(n\cdot a)\,f(n_3)\,d\sigma(n)=2\pi\,a_3\int_{-1}^{1}u\,f(u)\,du.$$ (c) [Quadratic weighted moment] for every continuous $f$ and every $a\in\mathbb R^3$, $$\int_{S^2}(n\cdot a)^2f(n_3)\,d\sigma(n)=2\pi\,a_3^{2}\int_{-1}^{1}u^{2}f(u)\,du+\pi\,(a_1^{2}+a_2^{2})\int_{-1}^{1}(1-u^{2})f(u)\,du.$$ (d) [Moments] $\sigma(S^2)=4\pi$, $\int_{S^2}n\,d\sigma=0$, $\int_{S^2}n_in_j\,d\sigma=(4\pi/3)\delta_{ij}$, and for every $a\in\mathbb R^3$ $\int_{S^2}(n\cdot a)^2d\sigma=(4\pi/3)|a|^2$ and $\int_{S^2}|n\times a|^2d\sigma=(8\pi/3)|a|^2$, where $\delta_{ij}$ is the Kronecker symbol and $\times$ the cross product of [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]. (e) [Scope] (a)-(d) are identities for the polar surface measure of the unit sphere with only the stated continuity of $f$; they assert no physical field, flux or radiation statement. The measure is finite, so all displayed integrals are absolutely convergent; $f$ need not be nonnegative. For the uses on this page $f$ is a rational function with denominator bounded below by $1-b>0$, hence continuous on $[-1,1]$.
items.strategy: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. (a) Parametrize $S^2$ by $X(\theta,\varphi):=(\sin\theta\cos\varphi,\ \sin\theta\sin\varphi,\ \cos\theta)$ on $[0,\pi]\times[0,2\pi]$. Computing the coordinate cross product with the sin/cos derivatives and the Pythagorean identity ([[thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives]], [[cor-trigonometric-parity-and-pythagorean-identity]], [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]) gives $X_\theta\times X_\varphi=\sin\theta\,X(\theta,\varphi)$, whose norm is $\sin\theta\ge0$; by [[thm-surface-area-density-is-cross-product-norm]] and [[def-surface-area-and-scalar-surface-integral-of-a-patch]] the chart surface integral of $F(n)=f(n_3)$ is $\int_0^{2\pi}\int_0^{\pi}f(\cos\theta)\sin\theta\,d\theta\,d\varphi$, with the seam and the poles lying on the parameter boundary exactly as in the sphere-area computation, so this is the integral over $S^2$ ([[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]], [[lem-parameter-boundary-exceptions-do-not-affect-surface-integrals|the boundary-exception convention]]). The chart measure equals the polar measure $\sigma$ ([[lem-euclidean-chart-measure-agrees-with-polar-surface-measure]]). By [[thm-jordan-fubini-by-sections]] the $\varphi$-integral is the constant $2\pi$, and with $P(u):=\int_0^u f$ ([[thm-ftc-first-part]]) the chain rule and [[thm-ftc-second-part]] give $\int_0^{\pi}f(\cos\theta)\sin\theta\,d\theta=[-P(\cos\theta)]_0^{\pi}=P(1)-P(-1)=\int_{-1}^{1}f(u)\,du$, using $\cos0=1$, $\cos\pi=-1$ and the derivative $\cos'=-\sin$ ([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives]]). This proves (a), including the endpoint values by continuity of $P\circ\cos$ on $[0,\pi]$ and the two-sided fundamental theorem. (b) Write $n\cdot a=a_1n_1+a_2n_2+a_3n_3$. The maps $\eta_1(n_1,n_2,n_3):=(-n_1,n_2,n_3)$ and $\eta_2(n_1,n_2,n_3):=(n_1,-n_2,n_3)$ are orthogonal and preserve $\sigma$ ([[lem-euclidean-chart-measure-agrees-with-polar-surface-measure]]); since $n_1f(n_3)$ and $n_2f(n_3)$ change sign under $\eta_1$ and $\eta_2$ respectively, the substitution formula for the measure-preserving involution $\eta_i$ (indicators by definition, simple functions by linearity, bounded Borel functions by the usual approximation, exactly as in the vanishing-first-moment computation of [[lem-first-moment-of-the-unit-sphere-vanishes]]) gives $\int n_if(n_3)d\sigma=-\int n_if(n_3)d\sigma=0$ for $i=1,2$; the remaining term is $a_3\int n_3f(n_3)d\sigma=2\pi a_3\int_{-1}^1uf(u)du$ by (a) applied to $F(u)=uf(u)$. (c) Expanding the square, the mixed terms $n_in_jf(n_3)$ with $i\ne j$ vanish by the same reflection argument; the terms $n_1^2$ and $n_2^2$ are equal by the swap $(n_1,n_2,n_3)\mapsto(n_2,n_1,n_3)$, which is orthogonal and preserves $\sigma$. Hence $\int n_1^2f(n_3)d\sigma=\int n_2^2f(n_3)d\sigma=\tfrac12\int(1-n_3^2)f(n_3)d\sigma=\pi\int_{-1}^1(1-u^2)f(u)du$ by (a) applied to $F(u)=(1-u^2)f(u)$, while $\int n_3^2f(n_3)d\sigma=2\pi\int_{-1}^1u^2f(u)du$ by (a) applied to $F(u)=u^2f(u)$; linearity of the $\sigma$-integral on the (finite-measure) integrable functions is [[thm-linearity-of-the-lebesgue-integral-on-l-one]]. This proves (c). (d) Taking $f=1$ in (a) gives $\sigma(S^2)=2\pi\cdot2=4\pi$, The ball-volume comparison is $V_3(1)=\pi^{3/2}/\Gamma(5/2)=4\pi/3$ from [[cor-volume-of-the-unit-n-ball]] and $\Gamma(5/2)=3\sqrt\pi/4$ ([[thm-real-gamma-functional-equation]], [[cor-real-gamma-one-half-is-root-pi]]). The actual definition [[def-polar-surface-measure-on-the-unit-sphere]] gives $\sigma(S^2)=3\lambda_3(\overline B_1\setminus\{0\})=3V_3(1)=4\pi$, since the singleton has zero volume. Thus area is three times the ball volume, not the n=3 ball-volume value itself. Taking $f=1$ in (b),(c) gives $\int n_if(n_3)=0$ for $i=1,2$ and the matrix identity $\int n_in_jd\sigma=(4\pi/3)\delta_{ij}$ (equivalently $\int(n\cdot a)^2d\sigma=(4\pi/3)|a|^2$); the first moment statement is the three-dimensional case of [[lem-first-moment-of-the-unit-sphere-vanishes]]. Finally $|n\times a|^2=|a|^2-(n\cdot a)^2$ by the cross-product norm identity ([[def-cross-product-in-r3]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]), so $\int|n\times a|^2d\sigma=4\pi|a|^2-(4\pi/3)|a|^2=(8\pi/3)|a|^2$. Clause (e) records that no physical interpretation is attached. No choice principle beyond $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ (carried by the surface-measure interface) is used.

items.title: Retarded potentials, Lorenz gauge and Maxwell fields of a compactly supported conserved smooth source
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$) as carried by the retarded-kernel and Cauchy suppliers below ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let the laboratory region, chart and units be those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] and [[def-em-si-conventions]], so that $c>0$, $\mu_0>0$, $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ and $W:=c^{-2}\partial_t^2-\Delta$ is the wave expression of [[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]]. Let $a>0$, $t_0<T$ and let $ho:\mathbb R^3	imes\mathbb R	o\mathbb R$, $J:\mathbb R^3	imes\mathbb R	o\mathbb R^3$ be source fields of [[def-em-sources]] that are jointly of class $C^\infty$ in the sense of [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]], vanish identically outside the compact set $\overline B_a(0)	imes[t_0,T]$, and satisfy the continuity equation $\partial_tho+\operatorname{div}J=0$ everywhere -- the compatibility condition that [[pthm-em-charge-continuity]] shows to be forced by the Maxwell system, here assumed for the prescribed source. Define the retarded potentials by the explicit retarded integrals $$\varphi(x,t):= rac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\int_{\mathbb R^3} rac{ho igl(y,t-|x-y|/c igr)}{|x-y|}\,dy,\qquad A(x,t):= rac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\int_{\mathbb R^3} rac{J igl(y,t-|x-y|/c igr)}{|x-y|}\,dy,$$ and put $E:=-
abla\varphi-\partial_tA$, $B:=

Then: (a) [Smoothness and wave equations] $\varphi$ and each component of $A$ are of class $C^\infty$ on $\mathbb R^3	imes\mathbb R$, and $W\varphi=ho/\varepsilon_0$, $WA=\mu_0J$ pointwise. (b) [Lorenz gauge] With $G:=\operatorname{div}A+c^{-2}\partial_t\varphi$ one has $G=0$ on $\mathbb R^3	imes\mathbb R$: the retarded pair is in Lorenz gauge, and this is exactly where the continuity hypothesis is used. (c) [Maxwell fields] $E$ and $B$ are of class $C^\infty$ and the tuple $(E,B,ho,J)$ satisfies the smooth branch of the vacuum Maxwell equations of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] on the whole of $\mathbb R^3	imes\mathbb R$: $\operatorname{div}E=ho/\varepsilon_0$, $\operatorname{div}B=0$, $
abla	imes E=-\partial_tB$, $
abla	imes B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE$. (d) [No field before the source] $E=B=0$ at every event with $t<t_0$ (indeed $\varphi=A=0$ there): the selected retarded solution carries no field from before the source acted. (e) [Zero-data Cauchy identification] For every $t_1<t_0$ the pair $(\varphi,A)$ restricted to $\mathbb R^3	imes[t_1,\infty)$ is the unique $C^2$ extension solution of the wave Cauchy problem of [[thm-em-wave-cauchy-kirchhoff]] at time $t_1$ with zero Cauchy data and sources $ho/\varepsilon_0$, $\mu_0J$. (f) [Total charge] The total charge $Q(t):=\int_{\mathbb R^3}ho(y,t)\,dy$ is zero for every $t$: a source that is smooth, compactly supported in space and restricted to a compact time interval and satisfies continuity carries zero total charge, so this branch does not model an eternal isolated nonzero charge. (g) [Scope] This is the compact smooth branch with an adopted causal selection; it asserts nothing about point, line or sheet sources, about weak or distributional branches, about finite-energy or decay properties, about radiation reaction or self-force, and no empirical claim. In particular the fields of a prescribed isolated point charge with an eternal worldline are not covered by this theorem and are supplied separately by the point-source items of this page.
items.strategy:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. (a) $ho,J$ are $C^\infty$ with compact support, hence $C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3	imes\mathbb R)$; clause (b) of [[lem-em-retarded-wave-kernel]] applied to $h=ho/\varepsilon_0$ and componentwise to $h=\mu_0J_k$ states that $(K*h)(x,t)=\int h(y,t-|x-y|/c)/(4\pi|x-y|)dy$ is $C^\infty$ on $\mathbb R^3	imes\mathbb R$ and satisfies $W(K*h)=h$ pointwise, which is exactly the display. Note the identification $\varphi=\varepsilon_0^{-1}K*ho$, $A=\mu_0K*J$ is the framework's form of the adopted retarded selection of [[post-em-radiation-selection]]; the selected branch is the object being computed, not assumed to exist a priori. (b) Differentiate the explicit retarded integral. In the substitution $y'=x-y$, which leaves the integral unchanged by translation invariance of Lebesgue measure ([[thm-lebesgue-outer-measure-and-measurability-are-translation-invariant]]), the kernel $1/(4\pi|y'|)$ is independent of $x$, so differentiating under the integral sign in $x$ (direct dominated difference quotients: on each compact (x,t) parameter neighborhood all derivatives of h(x-y',t-|y'|/c) vanish outside one bounded y'-ball and are bounded by their appropriate derivative suprema; each quotient is dominated by that constant times |y'|^-1, integrable by [[thm-polar-coordinates-formula-for-lebesgue-measure]], so [[thm-dominated-convergence]] gives each derivative identity. The smooth nonsingular [[lem-em-parameter-integrals]] is used separately for the charge integral, not at this pole) gives $\partial_{x^i}(K*h)=K*(\partial_{y^i}h)$; differentiating in $t$ gives $\partial_t(K*h)=K*(\partial_th)$. Therefore $\operatorname{div}A=\mu_0K*(\operatorname{div}J)$ and $c^{-2}\partial_t\varphi=c^{-2}\varepsilon_0^{-1}K*(\partial_tho)=\mu_0K*(\partial_tho)$ because $c^{-2}\varepsilon_0^{-1}=\mu_0c^2\varepsilon_0\cdot\varepsilon_0^{-1}c^{-2}$ reduces to $\mu_0$ (equivalently $\mu_0c^2\varepsilon_0=1$, [[def-em-si-conventions]]). Adding, $G=\mu_0K*(\partial_tho+\operatorname{div}J)=0$ by the assumed continuity. (c) $\varphi,A$ are $C^\infty$, hence $C^2$, and clause (a) of [[pthm-em-lorenz-gauge-wave-form]] (instantiated at $\Omega=\mathbb R^3$, $I=\mathbb R$) states the exact identities $\operatorname{div}E=W\varphi-\partial_tG$ and $
abla	imes B-c^{-2}\partial_tE=WA+
abla G$; with (a) and (b) these read $\operatorname{div}E=ho/\varepsilon_0$ and $
abla	imes B-c^{-2}\partial_tE=\mu_0J$. The two source-free equations $\operatorname{div}B=0$ and $
abla	imes E+\partial_tB=0$ are automatic for a potential pair by the curl-divergence and curl-gradient cancellation recorded in clause (c) of the same item and [[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]]. This is the smooth branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]]. (d) If $t<t_0$ then for every $y$ the retarded argument satisfies $t-|x-y|/c\le t<t_0$, where $ho$ and $J$ vanish; both integrands vanish identically, so $\varphi(x,t)=A(x,t)=0$ and hence $E=B=0$ at such events. (e) Fix $t_1<t_0$. By (d), $\varphi(\cdot,t_1)=0$ and $\partial_t\varphi(\cdot,t_1)=0$, and likewise for $A$; by (a) the pair is $C^\infty$ on $\mathbb R^3	imes[t_1,\infty)$ and solves the sourced wave equations there. Clause (b) of [[thm-em-wave-cauchy-kirchhoff]] (uniqueness for $C^2$ extension solutions of the Cauchy problem with these data) identifies the pair with its zero-data solution; clause (d) of the same theorem gives the corresponding finite-speed support, consistent with (d). (f) $\int_{\mathbb R^3}\partial_tho(y,t)dy=-\int_{\mathbb R^3}\operatorname{div}J(y,t)dy=0$: for a ball $B_R$ with $R>a$ the divergence theorem ([[thm-divergence-theorem-for-bounded-c-one-euclidean-domains]]) converts the integral of $\operatorname{div}J$ into a boundary flux where $J=0$, and differentiation under the integral sign is licensed by compact support ([[lem-em-parameter-integrals]]); hence $Q$ is constant, and $Q(t)=0$ for $t<t_0$ by (d), so $Q\equiv0$. (g) records the branch boundaries. No self-force, no product of distributions and no empirical premise is used; the only choice assumption is $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, inherited from the kernel and Cauchy suppliers through the surface-measure and convergence interfaces cited inside them.

items.title: Controlled electric-dipole far field and retarded-time radiated power of a compact smooth source
items.statement: Assume the setting and hypotheses of [[thm-em-radiation-asymptotic-flux]] and $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as carried by its suppliers: $c>0$, $\mu_0>0$, $a>0$, $t_0<T$, jointly $C^\infty$ fields $\rho,J$ vanishing outside $\overline B_a(0)\times[t_0,T]$ and satisfying $\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=0$; let $\varphi,A$ be the retarded potentials and $E:=-\nabla\varphi-\partial_tA$, $B:=\nabla\times A$ the fields, with $S:=E\times B/\mu_0$ ([[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]], [[pthm-em-poynting-balance]]). Adopt the causal selection [[post-em-radiation-selection]]: these retarded fields are the fields of the source model (the compact smooth instance established by [[pthm-em-retarded-potentials]]). Define the **time-dependent electric dipole moment** $$p(u):=\int_{B_a}y\,\rho(y,u)\,dy\in\mathbb R^3$$ (componentwise, about the fixed chart origin of [[def-em-lab-geometry]]; it is the fixed-time analogue of the static source moment of [[def-em-electric-moments]]), and, as in the asymptotic theorem, $I(n,u):=\int_{B_a}J(y,u+n\cdot y/c)\,dy$, $V(n,u):=\partial_uI(n,u)=\int_{B_a}J_t(y,u+n\cdot y/c)\,dy$ and $$D(u):=\frac{a}{c}\int_{B_a}\sup_{|v-u|\le a/c}|J_{tt}(y,v)|\,dy.$$ Then: (a) [Moment identities] $p\in C^\infty(\mathbb R;\mathbb R^3)$, $p'(u)=\int_{B_a}J(y,u)\,dy$, $p''(u)=\int_{B_a}J_t(y,u)\,dy$, $\int_{B_a}\rho_t(y,u)\,dy=0$ and the total charge $\int_{B_a}\rho(y,u)\,dy$ vanishes for every $u$. (b) [Dipole replacement error] $|V(n,u)-p''(u)|\le D(u)$ for every $n\in S^2$ and every $u\in[t_0,T]$: the explicit absolute error of the dipole approximation to the source's transverse current moment. (c) [Leading fields] With $\Gamma_E$, $\Gamma_B$ the constants of [[thm-em-radiation-asymptotic-flux]](b) (depending only on $a,c,\mu_0$ and the listed source suprema), for every $n\in S^2$, $u\in[t_0,T]$, $r\ge2a$: $$\Bigl|E\bigl(rn,u+\tfrac rc\bigr)-\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi r}n\times(n\times p''(u))\Bigr|\le\frac{\Gamma_E}{r^2}+\frac{\mu_0D(u)}{4\pi r},\qquad \Bigl|B\bigl(rn,u+\tfrac rc\bigr)-\frac{n\times E(rn,u+\tfrac rc)}{c}\Bigr|\le\frac{\Gamma_B+\Gamma_E/c}{r^2}.$$ The leading far field is the electric-dipole field, with amplitude proportional to $p''(u)$; all errors are uniform in the direction $n$ at fixed $u$. (d) [Retarded-time radiated power] The limit of [[thm-em-radiation-asymptotic-flux]](c) equals $\mu_0|p''(u)|^2/(6\pi c)+R(u)$ with the explicit absolute error $$|R(u)|\le\frac{\mu_0\bigl(2|p''(u)|D(u)+D(u)^2\bigr)}{4\pi c},\qquad\text{so}\qquad \lim_{r\to\infty}\int_{S^2}r^2n\cdot S\bigl(rn,u+\tfrac rc\bigr)d\sigma=\frac{\mu_0}{6\pi c}|p''(u)|^2\ \text{ whenever } D(u)=0.$$ The evaluation uses the sphere moment $\int_{S^2}|n\times p''|^2d\sigma=(8\pi/3)|p''|^2$ of [[lem-em-sphere-zonal-moments]](d). The limit is at fixed retarded time $u$, not at fixed observation time. (e) [Scope] The compact smooth source branch only; the dipole error is absolute and explicitly controlled by $D(u)$, and no assertion is made that slow or 'nonrelativistic' source motion alone makes $D(u)$ small -- that is a hypothesis on the source's time variation. No point charge, no moving point source, no radiation reaction, no self-force and no empirical or measurement content; the failure of the correspondence with an oscillator for rapidly varying sources is retained through $D(u)$. Separately retain the sharper actual source estimate $|B(rn,u+r/c)-n\times E_{\rm lead}(n,u,r)/c|\le\Gamma_B/r^2$, with $E_{\rm lead}=\mu_0n\times(n\times V)/(4\pi r)$; the bound against the actual E uses the combined constant displayed in(c).
items.strategy: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as carried by [[thm-em-radiation-asymptotic-flux]]. (a) $\rho$ is $C^\infty$ with compact support, so $u\mapsto p(u)$ is $C^\infty$ by differentiation under the integral sign ([[lem-em-parameter-integrals]]) and $p'(u)=\int y\,\rho_t(y,u)dy$; integrating by parts componentwise over a ball containing the support via the divergence theorem ([[thm-divergence-theorem-for-bounded-c-one-euclidean-domains]], boundary term zero by compact support) gives $\int y_i\partial_t\rho\,dy=-\int y_i\operatorname{div}J\,dy=\int J_i\,dy$, since $\partial_i(y_iJ_k)$ contributes $J_i$ and the remaining divergence term integrates to zero. Replacing $J$ by $J_t$ (equivalently differentiating in $u$ under the integral sign) gives $p''=\int J_t$. The vanishing $\int\rho_t=0$ is the same divergence theorem with weight $1$ (equivalently clause (f) of [[pthm-em-retarded-potentials]]), and the total charge vanishes because $\rho$ is supported in $t\in[t_0,T]$. (b) For fixed $y\in B_a$ the one-variable function $v\mapsto J_t(y,v)$ is $C^1$ on the interval between $u$ and $u+n\cdot y/c$, whose length is at most $a/c$; for nonzero vector difference w choose its fixed unit direction e=w/|w| and apply the scalar mean value theorem ([[cor-mean-value-theorem]]) to e dot J_t; finite Euclidean Cauchy-Schwarz bounds |e dot J_tt| by |J_tt| (the zero difference is immediate), giving $|J_t(y,u+n\cdot y/c)-J_t(y,u)|\le(a/c)\sup_{|v-u|\le a/c}|J_{tt}(y,v)|$ componentwise, and integrating over $B_a$ with the integral triangle inequality and monotonicity ([[thm-integral-triangle-inequality]], [[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]]) gives (b). (c) Clause (b) of [[thm-em-radiation-asymptotic-flux]] writes $E(rn,u+r/c)=E_{\mathrm{lead}}(n,u,r)+$ remainder with $E_{\mathrm{lead}}=\mu_0\,n\times(n\times V(n,u))/(4\pi r)$ and remainder $O(r^{-2})$ bounded by $\Gamma_E r^{-2}$. Substituting $V=p''+(V-p'')$ and using $|n\times(n\times w)|\le|w|$ ([[lem-cross-product-is-bilinear-alternating-and-orthogonal]]) gives the first bound; The supplier bounds B-n cross E_lead/c by Gamma_B/r² and E-E_lead by Gamma_E/r²; the triangle inequality therefore gives the displayed (Gamma_B+Gamma_E/c)/r² bound against the actual E. D=0 suffices for exact dipole power; no converse is inferred from an error bound. (d) By clause (c) of [[thm-em-radiation-asymptotic-flux]] the limit equals $\mu_0/(16\pi^2c)\int_{S^2}|n\times V|^2d\sigma$. Replacing $V$ by $p''$ changes the integrand by at most $(2|p''|D+D^2)$ pointwise (expand $|n\times V|^2-|n\times p''|^2$ and use the bound (b), the linearity of the cross product and the integral triangle inequality), so the integral changes by at most $4\pi(2|p''|D+D^2)$ and the limit by $\mu_0(2|p''|D+D^2)/(4\pi c)$. The exact dipole value uses $|n\times p''|^2=|p''|^2-(n\cdot p'')^2$ and clause (d) of [[lem-em-sphere-zonal-moments]]: $\int_{S^2}|n\times p''|^2d\sigma=4\pi|p''|^2-(4\pi/3)|p''|^2=(8\pi/3)|p''|^2$, and $\mu_0/(16\pi^2c)\cdot(8\pi/3)=\mu_0/(6\pi c)$. (e) records that the error coefficient $D(u)$ constrains the source's own time variation and that the limit is a fixed-retarded-time limit, as in the supplier; no self-force, point-source, decay or empirical claim is added.
items.physical_scope: Far-zone electric-dipole radiation of a prescribed smooth conserved source of compact spatial support and compact time support: the dipole moment identities, the explicit absolute dipole-replacement error $D(u)$, the uniform leading far fields and the retarded-time radiated power with its absolute error. Excluded: point charges; sources without the compact smooth branch; claims that slowness alone controls $D(u)$; observation-time power and signal-speed readings; self-force, radiation reaction and every empirical or measurement claim.

items.title: Retarded point fields off the worldline: Lienard-Wiechert potentials, the velocity/acceleration split and the uniform far-zone remainder
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$) as carried by the point-source change-of-variables suppliers below ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let the laboratory region, chart and units be those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] and [[def-em-si-conventions]] ($c>0$, $\mu_0>0$, $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$), let $q\in\mathbb R$ and let $z$, $v_*$ be a retarded point-geometry datum of [[def-em-retarded-point-geometry]] (a prescribed $C^3$ uniformly subluminal worldline of a point charge, [[def-em-relativistic-worldlines-frames]], with the constants $C:=q/(4\pi\varepsilon_0)$), and let $\rho,J$ be the point-source distributions of that charge on the worldline in the declared point-source class of [[def-em-weak-sources]](b) (the $C^3$ branch of the point-current construction). Let $(\varphi,A)$ be the retarded history pairings of [[lem-em-point-retarded-potential-and-fields]](b) -- the framework's retarded construction for this source under the adopted selection [[post-em-radiation-selection]] -- and define $E:=-\nabla\varphi-\partial_tA$, $B:=\nabla\times A$ on the off-worldline domain $\Omega\setminus\Gamma$ ([[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]], [[def-em-fields]]). Then: (a) [Potentials] $\varphi=C/(\kappa r)$ and $A=\beta\varphi/c$ on $\Omega\setminus\Gamma$, where $r,\kappa,\beta$ are the retarded data of [[def-em-retarded-point-geometry]](b); the zero extensions of $\varphi,A$ to $\Gamma$ are locally integrable on $\Omega$. (b) [Exact fields] On $\Omega\setminus\Gamma$, $$E=E_{\mathrm{vel}}+E_{\mathrm{acc}},\qquad E_{\mathrm{vel}}=\frac{C(1-|\beta|^2)(n-\beta)}{\kappa^3r^2},\qquad E_{\mathrm{acc}}=\frac{C\,n\times\bigl((n-\beta)\times\dot\beta\bigr)}{c\,\kappa^3r},\qquad B=\frac{n\times E}{c},$$ and $E,B$ are of class $C^1$ there; the velocity part obeys $|E_{\mathrm{vel}}|\le|C|(1+v_*/c)(1-v_*/c)^{-3}r^{-2}$. (c) [Uniform far-zone remainder] For every emission event $s_0$ and direction $n\in S^2$, with $x_r:=z(s_0)+rn$, $t_r:=s_0+r/c$, $\beta_0:=z'(s_0)/c$, $\dot\beta_0:=z''(s_0)/c$ and $\kappa_0:=1-n\cdot\beta_0$: $(x_r,t_r)\in\Omega\setminus\Gamma$, $s(x_r,t_r)=s_0$, and $$E(x_r,t_r)=\frac{C\,n\times\bigl((n-\beta_0)\times\dot\beta_0\bigr)}{c\,\kappa_0^3\,r}+\rho_E(s_0,n,r),\qquad|\rho_E(s_0,n,r)|\le|C|\frac{1+v_*/c}{(1-v_*/c)^3}\,r^{-2},\qquad B(x_r,t_r)=\frac{n\times E(x_r,t_r)}{c};$$ the bound is uniform in $n$ at fixed $s_0$. (d) [Scope] These are the stipulated retarded model fields of the prescribed charge: the item identifies, through the same adopted causal selection used by [[pthm-em-retarded-potentials]] for the compact branch, the point-source potentials and fields of the model, and proves their exact form and bounds. It asserts no value of the fields on the worldline $\Gamma$ (where the formulas are undefined and the self-field is singular), no integral or energy statement, no self-force and no radiation reaction, and derives no mass. The uniform bound $v_*<c$ and the exclusion of $\Gamma$ are essential hypotheses; the companion example page shows that a merely pointwise subluminal curve can fail to have a retarded root, and no uniformity in the emission event $s_0$ is claimed ($z''$ is not assumed bounded). The signed constant $C$ is retained in every displayed formula while absolute-value bounds use $|C|$. (e) [Constructed weak solution] Let Phi,Upsilon be the global regular potential distributions in (a), and let mathcal E=-grad Phi-partial_t Upsilon, mathcal B=curl Upsilon. By [[thm-em-retarded-point-distributional-maxwell]], their representatives are exactly the locally integrable zero extensions of the displayed off-worldline fields. They satisfy all four identities of [[def-em-weak-sources]](e) with the proper all-time point pair rho,J; the volume source parts are zero. Thus they are an admitted point-source model of the explicit physical adoption [[post-em-distributional-vacuum-maxwell]], under the same retarded selection. Potentials satisfy W Phi=rho/epsilon0, W Upsilon=mu0 J and the distributional Lorenz identity. This existence and solution property is supplied by the mathematical theorem, not by the selection postulate or by the compact-source theorem. The zero extensions on the null graph give no physically defined self-field or nonlinear products there. All original exact field, regularity and uniform far-zone branches remain as stated. On each product neighborhood disjoint from Gamma the fields satisfy the smooth source-free Maxwell equations. Consequently any use of [[pthm-em-poynting-balance]] by the radiation items is local on such neighborhoods, with rho=J0; it neither applies that smooth theorem across the point source nor forms self-work or a global finite-energy identity.
items.strategy: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. The mathematical content is fully supplied by the two cited point-source suppliers, and the physical work of this item is the honest identification and the scope statement. (a) Clause (b) of [[lem-em-point-retarded-potential-and-fields]] identifies the history pairings with the regular distributions of the locally integrable zero extensions of $\varphi=C/(\kappa r)$ and $A=\beta\varphi/c$ on $\Omega\setminus\Gamma$, and proves finiteness of the pairings for every test and the exact change-of-variables identity with denominator $1-n\cdot\beta$. The retarded root and its derivative formulas, and the identification of the same formulas with the $C^3$ branch, are clause (a) of [[thm-em-retarded-root-and-fields]], which also supplies (b) and (c) there: the velocity/acceleration split, $B=n\times E/c$, the $C^1$ regularity and the velocity bound. (c) is clause (d) of the same theorem, whose remainder is $E_{\mathrm{vel}}$ evaluated at the emission event with the bound obtained from $1-|\beta|^2\le1$, $|n-\beta|\le1+v_*/c$ and $\kappa^3\ge(1-v_*/c)^3$; the root identification $s(x_r,t_r)=s_0$ is its uniqueness statement. (d) is the physical reading: the retarded construction is the one selected by [[post-em-radiation-selection]], so the model's point-charge fields off $\Gamma$ are exactly these; the new exact [[thm-em-retarded-point-distributional-maxwell]] separately proves the sourced wave identities, Lorenz condition, all four distributional Maxwell identities and L1loc field representatives. The graph is proper by its time coordinate, so [[def-em-weak-sources]](b),(d),(e) admits precisely this point source and field pair. Under [[post-em-distributional-vacuum-maxwell]] and the explicitly extended retarded selection, these constructed weak fields are the model fields. This supplies the solution property without applying the compact-only theorem to an eternal point source. No self-force, mass derivation, radiation reaction or empirical claim appears. The choice assumption $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is inherited from the change-of-variables and sphere-integration suppliers cited inside the two point-source items.
items.physical_scope: Retarded potentials and fields of a prescribed unit-charge-parameter point charge on a uniformly subluminal $C^3$ worldline, off the worldline: exact Lienard-Wiechert split, $B=n\times E/c$, the velocity-field bound and the uniform-in-direction far-zone remainder at a fixed emission event. Excluded: field values on the worldline; distributional Maxwell solution property; energy, flux or power (deferred to the emitted-power items of this page); uniform bounds in the emission event; self-force, radiation reaction and any empirical claim. Constructed proper point-source weak Maxwell solution with proved L1loc field representatives and distributional Lorenz-gauge potentials; no nonlinear self-interaction.

items.title: Instantaneous-rest Larmor power and uniform low-speed comparison for a prescribed point charge
items.reference: completed-expansion-arguments.md#R3; general weighted angular computation from R4 proved here using earlier suppliers
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as carried by the cited point-source suppliers. Let the laboratory region, chart and units be those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] and [[def-em-si-conventions]], let $q\in\mathbb R$, let $z,v_*$ be a retarded point-geometry datum of [[def-em-retarded-point-geometry]] (prescribed $C^3$ uniformly subluminal worldline, $C:=q/(4\pi\varepsilon_0)$), let $s_0$ be an emission event with $z'(s_0)=0$ (the charge is momentarily at rest in the laboratory chart), and put $a:=z''(s_0)$ and, for $n\in S^2$, $x_r:=z(s_0)+rn$, $t_r:=s_0+r/c$. Let $E,B$ be the retarded fields of the charge given by [[pthm-em-lienard-wiechert]] and $S:=E\times B/\mu_0$ ([[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]], [[pthm-em-poynting-balance]]). Then: (a) [Field on the emitted sphere] For every $r>0$ and $n\in S^2$, $$E(x_r,t_r)=\frac{C\,n\times(n\times a)}{c^2r}+\rho_E(s_0,n,r),\qquad|\rho_E(s_0,n,r)|\le|C|\frac{1+v_*/c}{(1-v_*/c)^3}r^{-2},\qquad B(x_r,t_r)=\frac{n\times E(x_r,t_r)}{c}.$$ (b) [Angular flux density] The limits $$\frac{dP}{d\sigma}(n):=\lim_{r\to\infty}r^2\,n\cdot S(x_r,t_r)=\frac{C^{2}\,|n\times(n\times a)|^{2}}{\mu_0c^{5}},\qquad P_{\mathrm{em}}(s_0):=\int_{S^2}\frac{dP}{d\sigma}(n)\,d\sigma(n),$$ exist with the convergence uniform in $n\in S^2$; $d\sigma$ is the polar surface measure of the unit sphere (equal to the chart surface measure by [[lem-euclidean-chart-measure-agrees-with-polar-surface-measure]]). (c) [Total power] $$P_{\mathrm{em}}(s_0)=\frac{C^{2}}{\mu_0c^{5}}\cdot\frac{8\pi}{3}|a|^{2}=\frac{q^2|a|^2}{6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3}},$$ the Larmor power of the momentarily resting prescribed charge. (d) [Angular distribution] Writing $\theta$ for the angle between $n$ and $a$ (with $\theta$ undefined only when $a=0$, in which case $dP/d\sigma\equiv0$), $$\frac{dP}{d\sigma}(n)=\frac{q^2|a|^2}{16\pi^2\varepsilon_0c^{3}}\sin^2\theta:$$ the radiation pattern vanishes along the instantaneous acceleration axis and is maximal in the perpendicular plane; $\int_{S^2}dP/d\sigma\,d\sigma=P_{\mathrm{em}}(s_0)$. If $a=0$ all displayed radiation quantities vanish. (e) [Scope and conventions] The result is exact at an emission event at which the charge is instantaneously at rest in the laboratory chart: then $\kappa_0(n)=1$ for every $n$, so no retarded-time conversion factor appears and the displayed limits are simultaneously the fixed-sphere flux and the emitted power per unit emission time. The item uses only the prescribed worldline and the retarded model fields -- it is not a mechanical evolution law, does not assert a self-force or radiation reaction, derives no mass, and makes no empirical or measurement claim. For a general emission event the exact formula and its low-speed comparison are the subject of the companion emitted-power theorem of this page; 'slow' motion alone is never substituted for an error bound. The prescribed curve, the uniform subluminal bound and $z'(s_0)=0$ are hypotheses; for a varying-velocity worldline the instantaneous rest event is a single parameter value, not an interval. (f) [General low-speed branch] At any emission event, without imposing z'(s0)=0 for this clause, define emitted power by the weighted far-zone flux integral kappa0(n) r² n dot S on the emitted spheres. The same field formula and angular computation give P_em=gamma0^6 (|a|²-|beta0 cross a|²) q²/(6pi epsilon0 c³). Put P_L=q²|a|²/(6pi epsilon0 c³). For |beta0|<=delta<1,
$$P_L\le P_{\rm em}\le(1-\delta^2)^{-3}P_L,\qquad |P_{\rm em}-P_L|\le3\delta^2(1-\delta^2)^{-3}P_L.$$
This includes q0 or a0 without division by P_L. Uniform angular comparison is also explicit: if N_beta=n cross((n-beta0) cross a), N0=n cross(n cross a), and H_beta=q²|N_beta|²/(16pi²epsilon0 c³ kappa0^5), then
$$|H_\beta-H_0|\le\frac{q^2|a|^2}{16\pi^2\varepsilon_0c^3}\,\delta\left[\frac{2+\delta}{(1-\delta)^5}+\frac{5}{(1-\delta)^6}\right]$$
for all n. The exact rest-event clauses(a)-(e) retain their hypotheses; this additional branch supplies the approved general low-speed comparison, not a mechanical loss law.
items.strategy: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. (a) At the emission event $s_0$ one has $\beta_0=z'(s_0)/c=0$, $\kappa_0=1$ and $\dot\beta_0=a/c$; clause (c) of [[pthm-em-lienard-wiechert]] (equivalently clause (d) of [[thm-em-retarded-root-and-fields]], which also supplies the uniform remainder bound and the root identification $s(x_r,t_r)=s_0$) gives $E_{\mathrm{vel}}=C(1-|\beta|^2)(n-\beta)/(\kappa^3r^2)=C\,n/r^2$ and $E_{\mathrm{acc}}=C\,n\times((n-\beta)\times\dot\beta)/(c\kappa^3r)=C\,n\times(n\times a)/(c^2r)$; the displayed remainder is their sum restricted to the leading term, bounded by $|E_{\mathrm{vel}}|\le|C|(1+v_*/c)(1-v_*/c)^{-3}r^{-2}$; $B=n\times E/c$. (b) For fields with $B=n\times E/c$ one has $n\cdot S=n\cdot(E\times B)/\mu_0=(|E|^2-(n\cdot E)^2)/(\mu_0c)=|n\times E|^2/(\mu_0c)$ ([[def-cross-product-in-r3]], [[lem-cross-product-is-bilinear-alternating-and-orthogonal]]). Hence $r^2n\cdot S=r^2|n\times E|^2/(\mu_0c)$; replacing $E=E_{\mathrm{lead}}+\rho_E$ and using the bound on $\rho_E$ together with $|n\times w|\le|w|$ gives $r^2n\cdot S=C^{2}|n\times(n\times a)|^{2}/(\mu_0c^{5})+O(r^{-1})$ uniformly on $S^2$ ([[thm-integral-triangle-inequality]], [[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]]); integrating over the compact sphere and passing to the limit ([[thm-dominated-convergence]]) proves the limits and their uniformity. (c) Expand $|n\times(n\times a)|^{2}=|a|^{2}-(n\cdot a)^{2}$ and apply [[lem-em-sphere-zonal-moments]](d): $\int_{S^2}(n\cdot a)^2d\sigma=(4\pi/3)|a|^2$, so the integral is $4\pi|a|^2-(4\pi/3)|a|^2=(8\pi/3)|a|^2$; with $C^2=q^2/(16\pi^2\varepsilon_0^2)$ and $\mu_0c^2\varepsilon_0=1$ the coefficient is $C^{2}/(\mu_0c^{5})\cdot(8\pi/3)=q^2/(6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3})$. (d) The vanishing of the pattern along $\pm a$ and the value $\sin^2\theta$ follow from $n\times(n\times a)=n(n\cdot a)-a$ and $|\cdot|^2=|a|^2\cos^2\theta-2|a|^2\cos^2\theta+|a|^2=|a|^2\sin^2\theta$; the displayed coefficient is $C^{2}/(\mu_0c^{5})=q^{2}/(16\pi^2\varepsilon_0c^{3})$ by the same unit relation. The integral statement is (c). (e) At $\beta_0=0$ the emission-time Jacobian $\kappa_0(n)=1-n\cdot\beta_0$ equals $1$ for all $n$, so the retarded-time conversion factor is trivial and the fixed-sphere flux limit is the emitted power per unit emission time ([[def-em-retarded-point-geometry]](a) for the Jacobian); the scope exclusions are those of the point-field supplier, and no mechanical, self-force or empirical conclusion is drawn. For (f), integrate the weighted angular density directly, without invoking a later item. Rotate beta=b e3 and resolve a=a_parallel e3+a_perp e1. Expanding |N_beta|² gives -(1-b²)(n dot a)²+2(1-bu)b a_parallel(n dot a)+(1-bu)²|a|², u=n3. The earlier zonal lemma supplies the azimuthal averages; the parallel coefficient reduces to1-u², perpendicular coefficient to (1-bu)²-(1-b²)(1-u²)/2. For 0<b<1, y=1-bu yields integral_-1^1 (1-u²)/(1-bu)^5 du=4/[3(1-b²)^3] and integral_-1^1 (1-bu)^-3 du=2/(1-b²)^2. An antiderivative in y for the former transformed integrand is b^-3[(1-b²)y^-4/4-2y^-3/3+y^-2/2]; the second is elementary. FTC and the chain/power rules give these identities; at b0 integrate directly, avoiding division by b. Thus integral |N_beta|²/kappa^5=(8pi/3)[gamma^6 a_parallel²+gamma^4 a_perp²], proving the general power formula. Eventwise gamma^4 P_L<=P_em<=gamma^6 P_L implies the uniform bounds since gamma>=1 and b<=delta. The difference bound follows from (1-delta²)^-3-1<=(3delta²)/(1-delta²)^3. For angular comparison |N_beta-N0|<=delta|a|, |N_beta|<= (1+delta)|a|, and the scalar mean-value bound |(1-n dot beta)^-5-1|<=5delta(1-delta)^-6 give the displayed estimate. These direct finite calculations use only the earlier point-field and zonal suppliers and the declared power/FTC rules.

items.title: Relativistic emitted power of a prescribed point charge at a general emission event
items.statement: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as carried by the cited point-source suppliers. Let the setting be that of [[pthm-em-lienard-wiechert]]: a charge $q\in\mathbb R$ ($C:=q/(4\pi\varepsilon_0)$) on a prescribed $C^3$ uniformly subluminal worldline $z$ in the laboratory chart of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] with the units of [[def-em-si-conventions]], with retarded fields $E,B$ off the worldline and the uniform far-zone remainder of that item; let $S:=E\times B/\mu_0$ ([[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]]). Let $s_0$ be an emission event, $\beta_0:=z'(s_0)/c$, $\gamma_0:=(1-|\beta_0|^2)^{-1/2}$, $a:=z''(s_0)$, and for $n\in S^2$ put $x_r:=z(s_0)+rn$, $t_r:=s_0+r/c$, $\kappa_0(n):=1-n\cdot\beta_0$. Define the **emitted power at the emission event $s_0$** by the $\kappa_0$-weighted far-zone flux $$P_{\mathrm{em}}(s_0):=\lim_{r\to\infty}\int_{S^2}\kappa_0(n)\,r^{2}\,n\cdot S(x_r,t_r)\,d\sigma(n),$$ $d\sigma$ the polar surface measure (equal to the chart surface measure). The weight $\kappa_0$ is the emission-time/observation-time conversion factor of the retarded root, $\partial_ts=1/\kappa$, equivalently the moving-boundary correction $S\cdot n-(z'\cdot n)u$ at leading radiation order, where $u=|S|/c$ for the transverse far field. Then: (a) [Weighted flux limit] The limit exists and $$P_{\mathrm{em}}(s_0)=\frac{C^{2}}{\mu_0c^{5}}\int_{S^2}\frac{\bigl|n\times\bigl((n-\beta_0)\times a\bigr)\bigr|^{2}}{\kappa_0(n)^{5}}\,d\sigma(n).$$ (b) [Closed form and four-acceleration form] If $b:=|\beta_0|<1$ and $a=a_\parallel e_3+a_\perp$ is decomposed along $\beta_0=|\beta_0|e_3$ and perpendicular to it, then $$P_{\mathrm{em}}(s_0)=\frac{q^{2}\gamma_0^{6}}{6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3}}\bigl(|a|^{2}-|\beta_0\times a|^{2}\bigr)=\frac{q^{2}}{6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3}}\,\eta(A,A),$$ where $A$ is the four-acceleration of the worldline at $s_0$ and $\eta(A,A)=\gamma_0^{4}|a|^{2}+\gamma_0^{6}(\beta_0\cdot a)^{2}=\gamma_0^{6}(|a|^{2}-|\beta_0\times a|^{2})$ ([[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]](e)). At $\beta_0=0$ the weight is $1$ and (b) reduces to the instantaneous-rest Larmor power of [[pthm-em-larmor-nonrelativistic]]. (c) [Low-speed comparison] For every $\delta\in(0,1)$ and every emission event with $|\beta_0|\le\delta$, $$\frac{q^{2}|a|^{2}}{6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3}}\le P_{\mathrm{em}}(s_0)\le\frac{(1-\delta^{2})^{-3}q^{2}|a|^{2}}{6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3}},\qquad\text{hence}\qquad \Bigl|P_{\mathrm{em}}(s_0)-\frac{q^{2}|a|^{2}}{6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3}}\Bigr|\le\frac{3\delta^{2}}{(1-\delta^{2})^{3}}\frac{q^{2}|a|^{2}}{6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3}},$$ a comparison uniform over the events with $|\beta_0|\le\delta$. In particular the instantaneous-rest formula is the exact $\delta=0$ case, and no term of the comparison is asserted to be small without the explicit hypothesis $|\beta_0|\le\delta$. (d) [Scope] $P_{\mathrm{em}}(s_0)$ is the power emitted at the single retarded event $s_0$ per unit emission time, defined by the weighted far-zone flux; it is not a coordinate-time loss rate of a dynamical particle, and no dynamics (self-force, radiation reaction, mass), no uniformity in $s_0$, and no empirical or measurement claim is made. The near fields are $O(r^{-2})$ with their uniform remainder as in [[pthm-em-lienard-wiechert]](c), so their contribution to the weighted $r^2$ flux vanishes; the $\kappa_0$-weighting is part of the definition of emitted power and is not an additional physical assumption.
items.strategy: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. (a) On the emitted sphere the retarded data are those of the emission event ($s(x_r,t_r)=s_0$, [[thm-em-retarded-root-and-fields]](d)), and the uniform remainder gives $E= E_{\mathrm{acc,lead}}+\rho_E$ with $E_{\mathrm{acc,lead}}=C\,n\times((n-\beta_0)\times\dot\beta_0)/(c\kappa_0^{3}r)$, $|\rho_E|\le|C|(1+v_*/c)(1-v_*/c)^{-3}r^{-2}$ and $B=n\times E/c$. For such fields $n\cdot S=|n\times E|^{2}/(\mu_0c)$ (expand $E\times(n\times E/c)$ and use the triple-product orthogonality, [[lem-cross-product-is-bilinear-alternating-and-orthogonal]], [[def-cross-product-in-r3]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]). Therefore $\kappa_0r^{2}n\cdot S=\kappa_0r^{2}|n\times E|^{2}/(\mu_0c)=\kappa_0|C|^{2}|n\times((n-\beta_0)\times\dot\beta_0)|^{2}/(\mu_0c^{3}\kappa_0^{6})+O(r^{-1})$ with a remainder controlled by the uniform bound ([[thm-integral-triangle-inequality]], [[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]]); note $C^{2}=|C|^{2}$ as squares. Integrating over the compact sphere and passing to the limit ([[thm-dominated-convergence]]) gives (a) with $\dot\beta_0=a/c$ absorbed: $|n\times((n-\beta_0)\times a)|^{2}$ replaces $c^{2}|n\times((n-\beta_0)\times\dot\beta_0)|^{2}$, giving $(C^{2}/(\mu_0c^{5}))\int|n\times((n-\beta_0)\times a)|^{2}/\kappa_0^{5}d\sigma$ because $|C|^{2}/(\mu_0c^{3}c^{2})=C^{2}/(\mu_0c^{5})$ and one power of $\kappa_0$ cancels. (b) Rotate the integration variable so that $\beta_0=be_3$ with $b=|\beta_0|$ and $a=a_\parallel e_3+a_\perp e_1$ (rotation invariance of $\sigma$, [[lem-euclidean-chart-measure-agrees-with-polar-surface-measure]]); put $u=n_3$ and $\kappa_0=1-bu$. Expanding the numerator with $N=n\cdot\beta_0=bu$, $d=n\cdot\dot\beta_0$ and $|n-\beta_0|^{2}=1-2bu+b^{2}$ gives, exactly as in the recorded research computation, $$\bigl|n\times\bigl((n-\beta_0)\times a\bigr)\bigr|^{2}=-(1-b^{2})(n\cdot a)^{2}+2\kappa_0 b\,a_\parallel(n\cdot a)+\kappa_0^{2}|a|^{2}.$$ Apply [[lem-em-sphere-zonal-moments]](b),(c) with $f(u)=(1-bu)^{-5}$ and $g(u)=(1-bu)^{-4}$: the azimuthal average turns $(n\cdot a)^2$ into $u^{2}a_\parallel^{2}+\tfrac12(1-u^{2})a_\perp^{2}$ and $n\cdot a$ into $ua_\parallel$, and $(1-bu)^{-3}$ weights the $|a|^{2}$ term. The resulting one-dimensional integrals are elementary: $\int_{-1}^{1}(1-u^{2})(1-bu)^{-5}du=\tfrac{4}{3}(1-b^{2})^{-3}$ and $\int_{-1}^{1}(1-bu)^{-3}du=2(1-b^{2})^{-2}$, both verified by the displayed antiderivatives in $y=1-bu$ using the power derivative, chain rule and fundamental theorem ([[lem-derivative-of-a-power]], [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[thm-ftc-second-part]], [[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]). Collecting terms gives $\int|\cdot|^{2}/\kappa_0^{5}d\sigma=(8\pi/3)[\gamma_0^{6}a_\parallel^{2}+\gamma_0^{4}a_\perp^{2}]= (8\pi/3)\gamma_0^{6}(|a|^{2}-|\beta_0\times a|^{2})$; multiplying by $C^{2}/(\mu_0c^{5})=q^{2}/(16\pi^{2}\varepsilon_0c^{3})$ produces (b). The four-acceleration identity is clause (e) of [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]], where $\eta(A,A)=\gamma_w^{4}|a|^{2}+\gamma_w^{6}(w\cdot a)^{2}/c^{2}$ with $w=z'(s_0)=c\beta_0$ reads $\gamma_0^{4}|a|^{2}+\gamma_0^{6}(\beta_0\cdot a)^{2}=\gamma_0^{6}(|a|^{2}-|\beta_0\times a|^{2})$; the $\beta_0=0$ case is the statement of [[pthm-em-larmor-nonrelativistic]]. (c) The strongest immediate eventwise bounds are gamma0^4 P_L<=P_em<=gamma0^6 P_L, since |a|²-|beta0 cross a|² lies between (1-b²)|a|² and |a|². With b<=delta, gamma0>=1 and gamma0^6<=(1-delta²)^-3, they imply P_L<=P_em<=(1-delta²)^-3 P_L. A larger inverse factor in the UNIFORM lower bound is not justified by an upper bound on b (the rest event b0 disproves it). The rational identity (1-delta²)^-3-1=(3delta²-3delta^4+delta^6)/(1-delta²)^3<=3delta²/(1-delta²)^3 proves the unchanged difference estimate, including P_L0. (d) records that the definition is per unit emission time, that the near-field contribution vanishes after weighting by the uniform remainder and that no dynamics or empirical content is added. To make the finite angular integration fully explicit: the parallel averaged numerator is1-u²; the perpendicular one is(1-bu)²-(1-b²)(1-u²)/2. For b>0 the first transformed antiderivative is b^-3[(1-b²)y^-4/4-2y^-3/3+y^-2/2], y=1-bu, evaluated from1-b to1+b. At b0 direct angular moments give8pi|a|²/3; never evaluate a b^-3 antiderivative at b0. The angle-axis rotation preserves the existing sphere measure.
items.physical_scope: Emitted power per unit emission time of a prescribed point charge at a general emission event on a uniformly subluminal $C^3$ worldline: the $\kappa$-weighted far-zone flux, the closed form $q^2\gamma^6(|a|^2-|\beta\times a|^2)/(6\pi\varepsilon_0c^3)=q^2\eta(A,A)/(6\pi\varepsilon_0c^3)$ and the uniform $\delta$-comparison with the instantaneous-rest Larmor value. Excluded: dynamical evolution, self-force, radiation reaction, mass derivation, coordinate-time loss rates, uniformity in the emission event and every empirical or measurement claim.
