items.title: Self-force, runaways and finite-size regularizations are not supplied by this page
items.statement: Record, with no speculative content, the limits of the radiation model built on this page. (a) [Self-energy] The truncated field energy of the idealized point charge diverges as the inner cutoff is removed ([[pthm-em-point-self-energy-divergence]]): the point source's own field carries infinite energy in this framework's idealization, and any finite-energy treatment of a point-like charge requires modifying the source or the field near the singularity, or an explicit cutoff, none of which is supplied here. (b) [Undefined self-interaction] The framework's source model [[def-em-weak-sources]] pairs distributions against compact smooth tests and expressly excludes arbitrary products of distributions; the point charge's field is singular on the worldline while its own current is a distribution supported there, so the pairing of the charge's own field with its own current -- the object a systematic self-force would have to use -- is not defined by these postulates, no regularization is adopted, and no equation of motion for the charge is derived. (c) [What the emitted-power items do and do not give] [[pthm-em-larmor-nonrelativistic]] and [[pthm-em-lienard-emitted-power]] are prescribed-source statements: they compute the emitted power of a stipulated worldline at a stipulated emission event and determine no worldline evolution, no back-reaction and no coordinate-time rate; they are not a mechanical model. (d) [Deferred, not claimed] Extended-charge or finite-size regularizations of the self-field, the well-posedness of any self-force dynamics, runaway solutions and an electromagnetic derivation of rest mass are outside this page and are neither stated nor proved here. No experiment, measurement, statistical estimate or precision is reported or implied, and nothing in this remark is a refutation of any physical theory.
items.strategy: A scope remark: no proof is claimed and the item is reviewed for formulation and scope only. The review checks that (i) the divergence statement is exactly the cited theorem's idealization and is not upgraded into a claim that a physical particle has infinite energy ([pthm-em-point-self-energy-divergence](c) makes that reading explicit); (ii) the product of distributions is correctly identified as undefined in the declared model [[def-em-weak-sources]], so no self-force expression is written down; (iii) the emitted-power theorems are quoted at their exact prescribed-source scope, with observation-time versus emission-time distinctions preserved; and (iv) the deferred list names what is genuinely absent instead of asserting a speculative result. No empirical content is introduced.

items.title: Charts, tetrads, observer congruences and adapted charts in affine Minkowski space
items.statement: Work in the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space (A,V,eta,C^+) (def-sr-affine-minkowski-model) with its inertial atlas (lem-affine-minkowski-charts-form-a-smooth-atlas) and the canonical identification T_pA = V (lem-tangent-space-of-affine-minkowski-space-is-v). The following objects are defined and are, in general, different objects. (a) Chart and inertial chart. A chart of the model is a diffeomorphism u: U -> u(U) from a nonempty open subset U of A onto an open subset of R^4 (def-diffeomorphism-and-local-diffeomorphism-of-manifolds, def-smooth-manifold), written with components (u^0,u^1,u^2,u^3). An inertial chart (def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart) is the global chart x(p) = E^{-1}(p-o) of an inertial frame (o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3). A general chart need not be inertial: if x is an inertial chart and N: x(U) -> R^4 is a diffeomorphism onto its image which is not the restriction of an affine map, then u := N o x is a chart that is not inertial, because if u were the inertial chart of a frame then x o u^{-1} = N^{-1} would be affine by lem-inertial-chart-transitions-are-affine-lorentz and hence N = (N^{-1})^{-1} would be affine as the inverse of an affine bijection, a contradiction; the map N(y) = (y^0, y^1 + (y^0)^2, y^2, y^3) on R^4 is an explicit example. (b) Tetrad at an event and tetrad field. A tetrad at p in A is an ordered basis (e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3) of V with eta(e_a,e_b) = diag(-1,1,1,1)_{ab} and e_0 future (e_0 in C^+); this is an inertial frame's basis without an origin and without the orientation condition. A tetrad field on a nonempty open subset Omega of A is a tuple (E_0,E_1,E_2,E_3) of smooth vector fields on Omega (def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space, type (1,0)) whose values at every p form a tetrad at p; it is observer-adapted when E_0 = U/c for a prescribed future timelike worldline or congruence. (c) Observer congruence. An observer congruence on a nonempty open subset Omega of A is a smooth vector field n: Omega -> V with eta(n,n) = -1 and n(p) in C^+ for all p; its observers are its maximal integral curves (def-integral-curve-of-a-vector-field, thm-unique-maximal-integral-curve-through-each-point), each of which is a future timelike worldline (def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline); n is nowhere zero because it is unit. Completeness of the integral curves, a global product structure of Omega and global synchronization are not asserted. (d) Adapted chart. For a congruence n on Omega, an n-adapted chart is a chart (u^0,u^1,u^2,u^3): U -> R^4 with U a nonempty open subset of Omega whose spatial coordinates u^1,u^2,u^3 are constant along every integral curve of n contained in U; no global adapted chart is asserted, and u^0 is not required to be affine. (e) Distinctions. A chart need not be inertial (a); a chart need not be n-adapted for any congruence; a tetrad field is not in general the coordinate frame of a chart: if (E_0,E_1,E_2,E_3) is the coordinate frame of a chart (v^0,v^1,v^2,v^3), i.e. E_a = partial/partial v^a, then [E_a,E_b] = 0 for all a,b (def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields, prop-coordinate-formula-for-the-lie-bracket), so a tetrad field whose members do not commute pairwise is not a coordinate frame; no converse is claimed here. A congruence need not be a coordinate flow, and its pointwise rest spaces need not assemble into hypersurfaces; that integrability question is decided below on this page. In an inertial chart the coordinate frame is simultaneously an inertial frame's basis, a constant tetrad field and the congruence of stationary observers, but the four notions are distinct in general.
items.strategy: Definition item; well-definedness and consistency obligations. (i) The non-inertial chart example is checked through lem-inertial-chart-transitions-are-affine-lorentz: transitions between inertial charts are affine bijections, and the inverse of an affine bijection of R^4 is affine, so the polynomial coordinate change N cannot arise from an inertial frame; N is a diffeomorphism of R^4 because (z^0, z^1-(z^0)^2, z^2, z^3) is a smooth two-sided inverse. (ii) Tetrads exist at every point by lem-lorentz-form-has-orthonormal-basis and lem-future-oriented-inertial-frames-exist; a tetrad field is componentwise smooth in an inertial chart (def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space). (iii) Maximal integral curves of a smooth field exist and are unique (thm-unique-maximal-integral-curve-through-each-point); a unit field is nowhere zero, so its curves are regular, and their future timelikeness is read pointwise from the causal classification and the time orientation. (iv) The commutation necessary condition for a coordinate frame is the coordinate formula for the Lie bracket. (v) No global assertions are made; the local adapted-chart and integrability questions are settled below on this page. All objects are finite-dimensional; no choice principle is used.

items.title: The flat covariant derivative on affine Minkowski space and fields along curves
items.statement:
Let (A,V,eta,C^+) be the affine Minkowski space with tangent spaces canonically identified with V, and let Omega be a nonempty open subset of A. (a) Vector fields. For smooth vector fields X,Y on Omega (def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space) define the covariant derivative of Y in the direction X at p by (nabla_X Y)(p) := (d/dt)|_{t=0} Y(p + t X(p)); in the inertial chart x of any inertial frame this is (nabla_X Y)^a = X^b partial_b Y^a. The value does not depend on the inertial chart: for another inertial chart x' = Lambda x + b one has partial'_a = (Lambda^{-1})^b_a partial_b and Y'^a = Lambda^a_b Y^b (thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation), and Lambda is constant, so (Lambda^{-1})^a_c X'^b partial'_b Y'^c = X^b partial_b Y^a. nabla_X Y is again a smooth vector field. (b) Covector and general tensor fields. For a smooth covector field alpha set (nabla_X alpha)(Y) := X(alpha(Y)) - alpha(nabla_X Y); for a type (r,s) tensor field T define nabla_X T by the derivation rule on the evaluation of T on smooth vector and covector fields, subtracting the covariant derivative of each vector argument and also subtracting the covariant derivative of each covector argument; Precisely, for $T:(V^*)^r	imes V^s	o\mathbb R$, $(
abla_XT)(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_r;Y_1,\ldots,Y_s)=X[T(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_r;Y_1,\ldots,Y_s)]-\sum_iT(\alpha_1,\ldots,
abla_X\alpha_i,\ldots,\alpha_r;Y_1,\ldots,Y_s)-\sum_jT(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_r;Y_1,\ldots,
abla_XY_j,\ldots,Y_s)$. In inertial coordinates every component of nabla_X T is X^b partial_b of that component, with no connection coefficients. (c) Properties. nabla is R-bilinear, C^infinity(Omega)-linear in X, satisfies nabla_X(fY) = X(f)Y + f nabla_X Y and the analogous Leibniz rules for tensor fields, is metric compatible (nabla eta = 0, because partial_a eta_{bc} = 0 in every inertial chart), is torsion-free (nabla_X Y - nabla_Y X = [X,Y], def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields and prop-coordinate-formula-for-the-lie-bracket) and has zero curvature (nabla_X nabla_Y Z - nabla_Y nabla_X Z - nabla_{[X,Y]} Z = 0), the last by equality of mixed partial derivatives of the components (thm-young-mixed-partial-theorem). (d) Fields along a curve. If gamma: I -> A is a C^1 curve and W: I -> V is a C^1 field along it (def-vector-field-and-section-along-a-smooth-curve), the covariant derivative of W along gamma is the ordinary V-valued derivative DW/ds := W' (def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral), because the canonical identification T_pA = V is independent of p; consequently parallel transport along any curve is the identity and a field is parallel exactly when it is constant. The derivative (d) is the one used for the acceleration of congruences, for Fermi-Walker transport and for the kinematic decomposition below; the model needs no Christoffel symbols or parallel-transport ODE in this formulation. (e) First-order C1 version. For C1 vector fields X,Y and C1 covector/tensor fields on Omega, the same directional/evaluation definitions are well-defined and have continuous coefficients: in an inertial chart $(
abla_XY)^a=X^b\partial_bY^a$ and each tensor component is differentiated in the same way. The component recovery and subtraction of all argument derivatives remain valid. C1 scalar multiplication satisfies the same first-order Leibniz rules, metric compatibility remains $
abla\eta=0$, and the first-order torsion identity uses the continuous coordinate bracket $[X,Y]^a=X^b\partial_bY^a-Y^b\partial_bX^a$. No C1 closure of this bracket or second covariant derivative of arbitrary C1 data is asserted. For C2 vector fields the second derivatives needed for the zero-curvature identity in(c) exist, and that identity follows by equality of the continuous mixed second partials. All original smooth-field properties and the C1 along-curve derivative in(d) are retained.
items.strategy: Definition with well-definedness obligations. (i) The directional derivative in (a) is the derivative of the V-valued composite t |-> Y(p+tX(p)); its coordinate expression is the chain rule, and chart independence is the corrected identity X'^b partial'_b Y'^a=Lambda^a_c X^b partial_b Y^c, equivalently inverse-Lambda recovery of the unprimed components, using that inertial transitions are affine (their second derivatives vanish, so no inhomogeneous term appears) and their linear parts are constant. (ii) The extension in(b) subtracts the derivative of every argument, whether vector or covector. In an inertial chart use the constant coordinate basis and constant dual basis; their covariant derivatives vanish, so evaluating the rule on those bases leaves only X acting on each tensor component. For variable arguments the ordinary product rule cancels all their derivatives with the displayed subtractions. This proves the stated coordinate formula and the evaluation derivation rule; the coordinate expression has no Gamma terms because eta is constant and transition matrices are constant in inertial charts. (iii) The properties in (c) are coordinate computations: torsion-freeness is X^b partial_b Y^a - Y^b partial_b X^a = [X,Y]^a, zero curvature is the interchange of mixed partials, and metric compatibility is the constancy of the component matrix eta_{ab}. (iv) In (d), the canonical isomorphism T_pA = V is independent of p, so the covariant derivative along a curve coincides with the ordinary derivative and parallel transport is trivial; this is exactly what makes Fermi-Walker transport below an ordinary linear ODE. No choice principle is used. For(e), a C1 map Y has continuous differential, and differentiating $Y(p+tX(p))$ at zero gives $dY_p[X(p)]$; the continuous product of dY and X yields the claimed C0 field. The coordinate tensor rule is identical on constant bases, with the ordinary C1 product rule for variable arguments. Only first derivatives occur in the C1 Leibniz/metric/torsion assertions. When X,Y,Z are C2, the fields $\nabla_YZ$ and $\nabla_XZ$ are C1, so the two iterated derivatives and the bracket term in the curvature identity are defined; expansion cancels the first-order bracket terms and the remaining mixed second partials commute. This supplies the actual first-order C1 interface used by dust/fluid and the C1 Bell generator with its explicitly given C2 flow family, without treating C1 fields as smooth or promising a joint C2 flow for every C1 field.

items.title: Kinematics of an observer congruence: acceleration, expansion, shear, vorticity and Born rigidity
items.statement: Let n be an observer congruence on a nonempty open subset Omega of A (def-sr-chart-tetrad-and-congruence-distinction), let nabla be the flat covariant derivative (def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space), and write n_b := eta_{bc} n^c for the associated covector field. (a) Rest metric and projection. Define h(v,w) := eta(v,w) + eta(n,v) eta(n,w) for vectors at the same point, so h = eta + n-flat (x) n-flat; then h(v,w) = eta(h(v),h(w)) where h(v) := v + eta(n,v) n is the orthogonal projection of thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition (c). At every point h is symmetric with radical spanned by n(p), and its restriction to n(p)^perp is positive definite. (b) Acceleration. The acceleration of the congruence is a := nabla_n n; then eta(n,a) = 0 pointwise, because 2 eta(n, nabla_n n) = n(eta(n,n)) = 0, so a(p) is spacelike or zero by the causal classification. In the model's physical interpretation the four-acceleration of the congruence observers is c^2 a and its magnitude is c^2 sqrt(eta(a,a)); the numerical units belong to the model's SI conventions and are not part of the affine geometry. (c) Kinematic decomposition. Set theta_{ab} := h_a{}^c h_b{}^d nabla_{(c} n_{d)} and omega_{ab} := h_a{}^c h_b{}^d nabla_{[c} n_{d]}, where nabla_{(c} n_{d)} = (1/2)(nabla_c n_d + nabla_d n_c) and nabla_{[c} n_{d]} = (1/2)(nabla_c n_d - nabla_d n_c). Then nabla_a n_b = -n_a a_b + theta_{ab} + omega_{ab}, with theta symmetric, omega antisymmetric, both horizontal (theta_{ab} n^b = omega_{ab} n^b = n^a theta_{ab} = n^a omega_{ab} = 0), and this decomposition is unique with these properties. theta is the expansion (and shear) tensor, theta := h^{ab} theta_{ab} is the expansion scalar, its trace-free part is the shear, and omega is the vorticity 2-tensor. (d) Born rigidity. The congruence is Born rigid (describes a rigid motion) if L_n h = 0. Since (L_n h)_{ab} = 2 theta_{ab}, Born rigidity is equivalent to theta = 0, equivalently to the projected symmetrized derivative of n-flat vanishing. (e) Scope. These are kinematic definitions for a prescribed smooth field n on the affine model; no dynamical equation, matter model, global synchronization or completeness is assumed, and a, theta, omega and h are local objects on Omega.
items.strategy: Definition item with content clauses proved by finite algebra. (i) h(v,w) = eta(h(v),h(w)) is expansion using eta(n,n) = -1; the radical and positive definiteness of the restriction to n^perp are clause (c) of thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition. (ii) eta(n,a) = 0 is the derivative of eta(n,n) = -1 along n, computed with metric compatibility; a is therefore spacelike or zero by the causal classification. (iii) The decomposition follows by splitting nabla_a n_b into its component along n and its horizontal part: n^a nabla_a n_b = a_b, the mixed terms are n_a a_b, the horizontal part splits uniquely into its symmetric and antisymmetric parts, and the stated contractions vanish because n is unit. (iv) L_n eta = nabla_a n_b + nabla_b n_a in a torsion-free metric-compatible connection; L_n(n-flat) = a-flat because L_n n_b = n^a nabla_a n_b + n_a nabla_b n^a = a_b and n_a nabla_b n^a = (1/2) nabla_b(eta(n,n)) = 0; substituting the decomposition gives (L_n h)_{ab} = 2 theta_{ab}, so Born rigidity is theta = 0. (v) All computations are pointwise finite algebra in the four-dimensional vector space, with no coordinate condition and no choice principle.

items.title: Simultaneity slices and rest distance relative to a future unit timelike vector
items.statement: Let (A,V,eta,C^+) be the affine Minkowski space and let n be a future unit timelike vector, eta(n,n) = -1. (a) Rest space. The rest space of n is the hyperplane n^perp = {v in V : eta(n,v) = 0}; by thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition (c) it is a three-dimensional linear subspace on which eta restricts to a positive-definite symmetric form, and the orthogonal projection onto it is h(v) = v + eta(n,v)n. (b) Simultaneity slice. For p in A the simultaneity slice of p relative to n is the affine hyperplane H(p,n) := p + n^perp = {q in A : eta(n,q-p) = 0}; it contains p and is three-dimensional, not a single point. (c) Simultaneity relation. Define q ~_n q' iff eta(n,q'-q) = 0, i.e. iff q'-q lies in n^perp. Then ~_n is an equivalence relation on A whose equivalence classes are exactly the slices H(p,n); reflexivity, symmetry and transitivity are consequences of n^perp being a linear subspace and not physical assumptions. (d) Rest distance. For p,q with q in H(p,n) define d_n(p,q) := sqrt(eta(q-p,q-p)). This is a real number >= 0, symmetric in p,q, vanishes exactly when p = q, and satisfies the triangle inequality on each slice, because the restriction of eta to n^perp is a positive-definite inner product. (e) Dependence on n and scope. The relation ~_n and the slices H(p,n) depend on the chosen future unit timelike n: an event q with eta(n,q-p) = 0 generally has eta(n',q-p) not equal to 0 for another future unit n' (an explicit witness is given on this page). Simultaneity here is defined relative to a prescribed observer vector and is not an absolute relation. For a congruence n(.) one may form each pointwise affine plane H(p,n(p)), but these entire affine planes need not be integral leaves. The integrability question concerns the varying rest distribution p|->n(p)^perp: Frobenius gives local hypersurface leaves tangent to it when its integrability condition holds. Such leaves need not themselves be affine; the affine-plane conclusion requires the additional irrotational Born-rigid hypotheses of the later rigidity theorem. No global foliation is asserted here.
items.strategy: Definition item. (i) n^perp is three-dimensional because eta is nondegenerate and n is nonzero; positive definiteness on n^perp is clause (c) of thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition. (ii) H(p,n) is the translate p + n^perp, hence an affine hyperplane of dimension three; eta(n,q-p) = 0 is equivalent to q-p in n^perp, so the classes of ~_n are exactly the slices; the equivalence-relation axioms follow from linearity of n^perp. (iii) The rest distance is the norm induced by the positive-definite restriction of eta to n^perp, so positivity, symmetry, nondegeneracy and the triangle inequality hold by the inner-product axioms on n^perp. (iv) The dependence on n is shown by the elementary witness on this page; no global foliation is claimed. No choice principle is used.

items.title: The operational radar protocol of an ideal observer
items.statement: Adopt the ideal-clock and ideal-light assumptions of post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light and the SI conventions of def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions. Let x: I -> A be a future timelike worldline (def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline) with proper-time function tau (def-sr-proper-time), and let s_- < s_+ be parameter values. Suppose an event q and the events e_- := x(s_-), e_+ := x(s_+) satisfy: q - e_- is future null and e_+ - q is future null (def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors, def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets). Under the adopted ideal-light assumption an ideal ray is emitted at e_-, reaches q, and an ideal ray emitted at q reaches e_+; the event q is idealized as an instantaneous reflection that changes nothing else. The radar protocol of the observer assigns to q (i) the radar time tau_rad(q) := (tau(s_-)+tau(s_+))/2, the ideal clock's reading midway between emission and reception, and (ii) the radar distance rho_rad(q) := c(tau(s_+)-tau(s_-))/2, half the round-trip light time multiplied by c. Two events measured by the same observer are radar-simultaneous when their radar times agree. Under an increasing C1 surjective reparametrization phi:I_new->I of the same history with everywhere positive derivative, transport the same ideal-clock zero (the based zero event has its unique preimage): tau_new=tau o phi. Then emission/reception clock values and both assignments are unchanged by lem-sr-proper-time-reparametrization-invariance. If instead tau_new=tau o phi+C for a common additive clock offset C, radar time shifts by C, while radar distance and radar-simultaneity of events measured by that same observer remain unchanged. No proper-time function is assigned to a reparametrized curve with zero tangent outside the worldline definition. Conventions and scope: (a) the protocol is a definition of an operational assignment conditional on the existence of the emission, reflection and reception events, and it assumes an available ideal reflector and ideal apparatus; (b) the split of the round trip into a 'time' and a 'distance' uses the symmetric convention in which half of the round-trip time is assigned to the outgoing and half to the returning segment; the protocol determines the round-trip quantity tau(s_+)-tau(s_-) operationally, while the derived one-way assignment is a convention and does not measure a one-way light speed independently of a synchronization convention; (c) nothing is claimed about accelerated observers, dispersive or absorbing media, finite-resolution apparatus, global single-valuedness or detector models, and no measurement outcome, statistical inference or empirical comparison is asserted.
items.strategy: Definition item with formulation obligations. (i) The assigned quantities are defined from the proper-time function and the events; the stated existence hypotheses make them well defined, and the supplier lem-sr-proper-time-reparametrization-invariance preserves proper-time differences for regular increasing reparametrizations and permits a base-point constant. Matching the transported ideal-clock zero makes the constant 0 and preserves absolute radar time. An arbitrary common offset C adds C to the arithmetic midpoint and cancels from the difference; it preserves radar distance and equality of two radar times. (ii) The two null segments are the operational content of the adopted ideal-light assumption (post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light); the reflection is an idealization, so the definition does not describe a physical mirror. (iii) The symmetric half-split is stated as a convention, not derived; its consequences for inertial observers are proved in pthm-sr-radar-synchronization-of-inertial-observers below, and the failure of global ring synchronization for rotating observers is exhibited by the explicit example on this page. (iv) No proof is manufactured: the item introduces an operational assignment, and its only mathematical content is well-definedness. The scope clause carries the idealizations of the postulates to every consumer.
items.physical_scope: Ideal radar measurement by a single observer with an ideal clock and ideal vacuum light rays modeled as future null straight lines, in flat classical special-relativistic spacetime; defines round-trip radar time and radar distance under a stated symmetric convention. Excludes real apparatus and finite resolution, dispersive or absorbing media, reflector and detector models, accelerated-observer global synchronization claims, one-way light-speed measurements, and every empirical or statistical claim; the idealizations of the adopted postulates travel to all consumers.

items.title: The radar round trip of an inertial observer halves at the midpoint of the reception interval
items.statement: Let n be a future unit timelike vector, eta(n,n) = -1, let o be an event, and let lambda_- < lambda_+ be real numbers; put e_- := o + lambda_- n and e_+ := o + lambda_+ n. For an event q the following are equivalent: (i) q - e_- is future null and e_+ - q is future null; (ii) there is u in n^perp with |u| := sqrt(eta(u,u)) = (lambda_+ - lambda_-)/2 such that q = o + ((lambda_- + lambda_+)/2) n + u. In that case q - e_- = ((lambda_+ - lambda_-)/2) n + u and e_+ - q = ((lambda_+ - lambda_-)/2) n - u, the affine midpoint m := o + ((lambda_- + lambda_+)/2) n = (e_- + e_+)/2 satisfies eta(n,q-m) = 0 (so q lies in the slice H(m,n)) and |q - m| = (lambda_+ - lambda_-)/2. In particular for fixed e_-, e_+ all admissible reflection events q have the same midpoint m and the same rest distance (lambda_+ - lambda_-)/2, and differ only in the direction u of n^perp.
items.strategy: (i) implies (ii): write d := q - e_- and decompose d = -eta(n,d) n + h(d) with the projection h of thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition (c). Future nullness of d gives eta(d,d) = -eta(n,d)^2 + eta(h(d),h(d)) = 0 with eta(n,d) < 0, so with mu := -eta(n,d) > 0 one has |h(d)| = mu. Likewise e_+ - q = ((lambda_+ - lambda_-) + eta(n,d)) n - h(d) is future null with eta(n,e_+ - q) < 0 and has the same horizontal part -h(d), so ((lambda_+ - lambda_-) + eta(n,d)) = |h(d)|; substituting eta(n,d) = -mu gives mu = (lambda_+ - lambda_-)/2. Then q = o + ((lambda_- + lambda_+)/2) n + h(d) with u := h(d) in n^perp and |u| = (lambda_+ - lambda_-)/2. (ii) implies (i): the displayed evaluations eta(q-e_-, q-e_-) = -((lambda_+ - lambda_-)/2)^2 + |u|^2 = 0 and eta(n, q-e_-) = -(lambda_+ - lambda_-)/2 < 0 show q - e_- is future null, and e_+ - q is treated identically. The midpoint and distance statements are immediate from the two displays; the positive definiteness of the restriction of eta to n^perp makes |u| well defined. All steps are finite algebra; no choice principle is used.

items.title: Radar synchronization of an inertial observer reproduces its inertial chart
items.statement: Adopt post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light (ideal clocks read proper time; ideal vacuum light rays are exactly the future null straight lines) and the SI conventions of def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions. Let (o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3) be an inertial frame with chart x, put n := e_0 (future unit, eta(n,n) = -1) and let W := x^{-1}({(lambda,0,0,0) : lambda in R}) be the coordinate axis, a straight future timelike worldline whose proper time between the events with coordinates (lambda_-,0,0,0) and (lambda_+,0,0,0) is exactly (lambda_+ - lambda_-)/c; its absolute clock function is tau(lambda)=lambda/c+C for a fixed clock offset C (def-sr-proper-time). Let q be an event whose spatial coordinates r := (x^1(q),x^2(q),x^3(q)) are nonzero, and put lambda_± := x^0(q) ± |r| with |r| the Euclidean norm of def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame. Then: (i) the events e_- := x^{-1}(lambda_-,0,0,0) and e_+ := x^{-1}(lambda_+,0,0,0) lie on W, and q - e_-, e_+ - q are future null; hence the radar protocol of def-sr-operational-radar-protocol applies with emission e_-, reflection q and reception e_+; (ii) the radar assignments are tau_rad(q) = x^0(q)/c+C and rho_rad(q) = |r|, with C the same fixed offset of the observer's proper-time clock; only radar time carries this additive constant: the radar time is the chart time of q and the radar distance is the chart's rest-frame distance; (iii) consequently, on the region of events with nonzero spatial part, radar simultaneity of this observer coincides with chart simultaneity (equal radar times are equal x^0), and the radar distance equals the rest distance in the simultaneity slice H(m,n) of the midpoint event m := x^{-1}(x^0(q),0,0,0); (iv) scope and qualification: this is a conditional statement of the adopted ideal model, showing that the operational round-trip protocol reproduces the inertial chart's time and rest distance, so the operational content of inertial simultaneity is this two-way radar convention; it asserts no one-way light-speed measurement without a synchronization convention, no empirical calibration, no result for accelerated, rotating or dispersive situations, and no deviation from the model. The idealizations of the postulates are carried into the conclusion.
items.strategy: Conditional deduction from the adopted premises. The geometry is lem-sr-radar-midpoint-for-inertial-observer with o := x^{-1}(0,0,0,0), n := e_0 and lambda_± := x^0(q) ± |r|: the events e_± are exactly o + lambda_± n, and the displacement q - o = x^0(q) n + r_vec decomposes as -eta(n,q-o) n + h(q-o) with -eta(n,q-o) = x^0(q) and |h(q-o)| = |r| in the chart coordinates (def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame), so |u| = |r| = (lambda_+ - lambda_-)/2 and the lemma gives q - e_-, e_+ - q future null. By post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light the clock reads tau and the two segments are traversed by ideal rays, so the protocol's assignments of def-sr-operational-radar-protocol apply, and they equal tau_rad(q) = (lambda_- + lambda_+)/(2c)+C = x^0(q)/c+C and rho_rad(q) = (lambda_+ - lambda_-)/2 = |r|, using tau(lambda)=lambda/c+C. The offset cancels from the distance and from equality of two radar times; choosing the chart-matched clock zero C=0 recovers the exact chart-time equality. Clause (iii) restates this as equality of radar times and x^0; the midpoint event m is the orthogonal projection of q onto W. The scope clause records that the statement is conditional on the ideal postulates and carries no empirical claim; no choice principle is used.
items.physical_scope: Ideal radar synchronization of a single inertial observer in flat classical special-relativistic spacetime, conditional on the ideal-clock and ideal-light postulates and the SI coordinate conventions: the round-trip protocol reproduces the observer's inertial chart time and rest-frame distance. Excludes one-way synchronization claims without an explicit convention, accelerated or rotating observers, dispersive media, real clock and light imperfections, detector models, and all empirical and statistical claims.

items.title: Coordinate formulas of a boost: clock rates, rod lengths, simultaneity and velocity transformation
items.statement: Let (o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3) and (o';e'_0,e'_1,e'_2,e'_3) be inertial frames whose bases are related by a boost along the common first spatial direction with parameter v, |v| < c: e'_0 = gamma(e_0 + (v/c)e_1), e'_1 = gamma(e_1 + (v/c)e_0), e'_2 = e_2, e'_3 = e_3, where gamma = (1 - v^2/c^2)^{-1/2}, with charts x, x' (def-lorentz-boost, lem-inertial-chart-transitions-are-affine-lorentz). Write the transition as x'^0 = gamma(x^0 - (v/c)x^1), x'^1 = gamma(x^1 - (v/c)x^0), x'^2 = x^2, x'^3 = x^3. Then: (i) Clock rate. The straight worldline y(lambda) := x^{-1}(lambda, (v/c)lambda + a_1, a_2, a_3) (coordinate velocity (v,0,0), the worldline of a clock at rest in the frame x') is future timelike, and the elapsed proper time between lambda_0 < lambda_1 is (lambda_1 - lambda_0)/(c gamma); equivalently dtau/dt = 1/gamma along y, where t is the coordinate time of x. (ii) Length comparison. For L_0 > 0 let y_a, y_b be the two straight worldlines at rest in the frame x' through the events with x'-coordinates (lambda,0,0,0) and (lambda,L_0,0,0). Then (a) at equal x'-times their x'-coordinate separation is L_0, while (b) at equal x-times their x-coordinate separation is L_0/gamma, so the measuring frame x assigns the length L_0/gamma to a rod of rest length L_0 at rest in x'; (c) symmetrically, for two worldlines at rest in x with x-separation L_0 the separation at equal x'-times is L_0/gamma. In each case the comparison uses events at equal time in the measuring frame; comparing equal times of the other frame is a different pair of events. (iii) Simultaneity. If x^0(q) - x^0(p) = 0 and x^1(q) - x^1(p) = L, then x'^0(q) - x'^0(p) = -gamma (v/c) L; in particular simultaneity in the chart x is not simultaneity in the chart x' whenever v L is nonzero. (iv) Velocity transformation. Let y: J -> A be a C^1 future timelike worldline which in the chart x is t |-> (c t, r(t)) with coordinate velocity w(t) := r'(t) in R^3, |w(t)| < c, and gamma_w := (1 - |w|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}. Then the coordinate velocity w' of y in the chart x' is given by w'_1 = (w_1 - v)/(1 - v w_1/c^2) and w'_perp = w_perp/(gamma (1 - v w_1/c^2)), the denominators being positive; moreover |w'| < c, and |w'| = c exactly when |w| = c.
items.strategy: Finite algebra and one-variable differentiation. (i) y' = (1, v/c, 0, 0) with eta(y',y') = -(1 - v^2/c^2) = -1/gamma^2 < 0, so y is future timelike; the proper-time integral of the constant integrand c^{-1}/gamma gives the displayed elapsed time. (ii)(a) is the constancy of the x'-spatial coordinates; (b) solve the two linear relations x'^0 = gamma(x^0 - (v/c)x^1) = lambda and x'^1 = gamma(x^1 - (v/c)x^0) = L_0 for x^1 as a function of x^0, obtaining x^1 = (v/c)x^0 + L_0/gamma; subtracting the two worldlines gives the constant x-separation L_0/gamma. (c) is the same computation with v replaced by -v. (iii) is direct substitution of Delta x^0 = 0, Delta x^1 = L into the first transformed component. (iv) differentiate the transition along the worldline: d x'^1/d x'^0 = (w_1 - v)/(1 - v w_1/c^2) and the transverse components are x'_perp = x_perp; the subluminality of w' follows from the identity c^2 - |w'|^2 = (c^2 - |w|^2)(1 - v^2/c^2)^2 /(1 - v w_1/c^2)^2 (equivalently from the Lorentz invariance of the causal classification applied to the tangent), with the limiting null case giving |w'| = c. No choice principle is used.

items.title: Time dilation, length contraction, simultaneity and velocity transformation for inertial observers
items.statement: Adopt post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light and post-sr-inertial-covariance, and the SI conventions of def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions; let the inertial frames and charts x, x' with boost parameter v be as in lem-sr-boost-time-length-and-velocity-formulas. Then, as statements about the ideal model and not about any actual apparatus: (i) Moving clocks run slow. An ideal clock carried along the worldline y of clause (i) of the lemma reads between parameter values lambda_0 < lambda_1 the time (lambda_1 - lambda_0)/(c gamma) = (t_1 - t_0)/gamma, where t is the coordinate time of the frame x; equivalently, between two events of the clock's history the coordinate time elapsed in x is Delta t = gamma Delta tau; symmetrically with x and x' interchanged. (ii) Length contraction. For a rod at rest in the frame x' of rest length L_0, with endpoints carried along the worldlines y_a, y_b of the lemma, the length assigned to it by the frame x on a simultaneity slice of x is L_0/gamma; symmetrically, a rod at rest in x has length L_0/gamma as measured by x'. Measured length here is defined by the stated protocol (events of the endpoints at equal time in the measuring frame); it is not the optical appearance of a moving rod, and no claim is made about a rod whose state of motion changes. (iii) Relativity of simultaneity. Two events simultaneous in x (equal x^0) with separation L in the boost direction generally fail to be simultaneous in x', with x'^0-difference -gamma (v/c) L; hence simultaneity is not an observer-independent relation. Each inertial frame's simultaneity is exactly the simultaneity relation of its time axis in the sense of def-sr-simultaneity-slice-and-rest-distance, operationally reproduced by its radar protocol as established in pthm-sr-radar-synchronization-of-inertial-observers. (iv) Velocity transformation. For a worldline with coordinate velocity w in the frame x, the coordinate velocity w' in the frame x' is w'_1 = (w_1 - v)/(1 - v w_1/c^2) and w'_perp = w_perp/(gamma(1 - v w_1/c^2)); relative velocities are therefore not added, and |w'| < c whenever |w| < c. Equivalently w' is the velocity of the worldline relative to the observer x' in the sense of clause (d) of thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition. (v) Scope and qualification. All clauses are conditional on the adopted ideal postulates (ideal clocks, ideal light, inertial covariance, flat spacetime) and on the stated measurement protocols; they carry no statistical or empirical claim, say nothing about real clock errors, real rods, optical appearance, accelerating or deformable bodies, gravity or quantum effects, and do not establish the exclusive truth of the model. The time, length and simultaneity assignments are protocol-relative: they involve the measuring frame and its simultaneity slice, which the radar theorem identifies operationally.
items.strategy: Conditional deduction: each clause is the physical reading of the corresponding mathematical clause of lem-sr-boost-time-length-and-velocity-formulas, with the identification of ideal clock readings with proper time supplied by post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light and the interpretation of the two inertial frames as observers' rest frames supplied by post-sr-inertial-covariance. (i) is lemma (i) with the clock hypothesis. (ii) is lemma (ii) together with the stated protocol definition of measured length as the separation of the endpoint events at equal measuring-frame time. (iii) is lemma (iii) together with the definition of simultaneity relative to a future unit vector; the operational identification of chart simultaneity with radar simultaneity is pthm-sr-radar-synchronization-of-inertial-observers. (iv) is lemma (iv), with the identification of w' as the observer-relative velocity following from clause (d) of thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition. The scope clause records the idealizations, excludes optical-appearance and deformable-body readings, and draws no empirical or statistical inference; no choice principle is used.
items.physical_scope: Ideal clock, rod and signal measurements between inertial observers in flat classical special-relativistic spacetime: moving-clock time dilation, length contraction on the measuring frame's simultaneity slice, relativity of simultaneity, and the relativistic velocity transformation. Conditional on the adopted ideal postulates; excludes real apparatus and clock errors, optical appearance, accelerating or deformable bodies, gravity, quantum effects, and every empirical, statistical or ontological claim.

items.title: Fermi-Walker transport along a timelike worldline
items.statement: Let x: I -> A be a C^2 future timelike worldline with four-velocity U = dx/dtau and four-acceleration A = dU/dtau (def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration), so eta(U,U) = -c^2 and eta(U,A) = 0 (thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition), and let X: I -> V be a C^1 map assigning a vector of T_{x(s)}A=V to each s, with regularity and one-sided endpoint derivatives in the given parameter as in the affine curve calculus. This finite-dimensional along-curve convention needs only C2 x and C1 X, not the smooth-curve bundle-section hypothesis. (a) The Fermi-Walker derivative of X is D_FW X/dtau := X'/tau' - (1/c^2)(eta(A,X)U - eta(U,X)A), where the displayed derivative term is X'/tau', with X' the ordinary V-valued derivative with respect to the given parameter s in I and tau'>0 from the proper-time parametrization supplier (def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space (d)). X is Fermi-Walker transported along x when D_FW X/dtau = 0, i.e. when X' = (tau'/c^2)(eta(A,X)U - eta(U,X)A). (b) The four-velocity is Fermi-Walker transported: D_FW U/dtau = U'/tau' - (1/c^2)(eta(A,U)U - eta(U,U)A) = A - A = 0, using U'/tau'=A, eta(U,A) = 0 and eta(U,U) = -c^2. (c) If A = 0 on an interval then Fermi-Walker transport coincides there with ordinary (parallel) transport X' = 0; if A is not zero, the definition includes exactly the correction that transports the time leg U/c itself. (d) A Fermi-Walker transported tetrad along x is a tuple (E_0,E_1,E_2,E_3) of C^1 fields along x with E_0 = U/c and every E_a Fermi-Walker transported; existence from a prescribed initial tetrad and preservation of the tetrad conditions are proved in the following lemma. The physical interpretation (a nonrotating spatial frame carried by an accelerated observer) is not asserted here; only the transport rule is defined.
items.strategy: Definition item. (i) The transport equation is a first-order linear differential equation for a V-valued field along x with coefficients determined by U and A, continuous when x is C^2; the proper-time derivative is (DX/ds)/tau'=X'/tau'; the ordinary derivative X' is the parameter-s covariant derivative because T_pA is canonically identified with V (def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space (d)). (ii) The identity in (b) is a short computation using eta(U,U) = -c^2 and eta(U,A) = 0 from thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition. (iii) The contrast with parallel transport in (c) is immediate from the definition, and (d) fixes terminology. (iv) Existence, uniqueness and preservation properties are deliberately not claimed here; they are supplied by lem-sr-fermi-walker-transport-existence-and-uniqueness and thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples. No choice principle is used. Multiplying by tau'>0 yields the ordinary-parameter linear ODE X'=tau' M(s)X with M(s)=c^{-2}(U tensor A-flat - A tensor U-flat). Its coefficient is continuous on arbitrary I when x is C2; no proper-time-only domain restriction is imposed. In (b), U'=tau' A gives exact cancellation. For an admitted regular increasing C2 reparametrization s=phi(v), with phi'>0 so that the pulled-back worldline remains C2, tau_new'=phi'(tau' o phi) and X_new'=phi'(X' o phi), so X_new'/tau_new'=(X'/tau') o phi; the transport condition is parameter independent.

items.title: Existence, uniqueness and linearity of Fermi-Walker transport
items.statement: Let x: I -> A be a C^2 future timelike worldline with four-velocity U and four-acceleration A, let s_0 be in I and X_0 in V. Then there is exactly one C^1 field X: I -> V along x with D_FW X/dtau = 0 and X(s_0) = X_0; if x is C^k with k >= 2 then X is C^{k-1}. The map X_0 |-> X from V to the C^1 fields along x satisfying the transport equation is linear. Consequently, for every tetrad (E_0(s_0),...,E_3(s_0)) at x(s_0) with E_0(s_0) = U(s_0)/c there is a unique tuple of Fermi-Walker transported fields with those initial values; whether that tuple remains a tetrad at every time is proved in the following item.
items.strategy: (i) In an inertial chart the equation reads X'^a(s)=C^a{}_b(s)X^b(s), with C^a{}_b(s)=tau'(s)c^{-2}(U^a(s)A_b(s)-A^a(s)U_b(s)), a continuous matrix-valued function on the given arbitrary interval I because x is C^2 and tau'>0 is C1. To apply the actual matrix-valued ODE supplier to a vector, put X_0 in the first column of a4-by-4 initial matrix and all other columns0; its unique matrix solution has those other columns0 by uniqueness, so the first column solves exactly this vector IVP. (ii) On each compact subinterval [a,b] of I containing s_0, lem-linear-matrix-odes-have-unique-global-solutions-on-a-given-interval gives a unique solution with the prescribed initial value; uniqueness on overlaps makes the local solutions agree, so they define a unique solution on all of I. Explicitly for each s in I the closed segment joining s_0 to s is contained in I; the compact-interval supplier gives its unique solution, and uniqueness on overlapping segments defines the value at s without a choice of solutions from a family. Around any interior s use a compact segment containing a neighbourhood of s and s_0; at an included endpoint use the corresponding one-sided segment. This proves C1 locally, including the defined one-sided endpoints, without assuming that I is open, bounded or a proper-time image. (iii) Linearity in the initial value follows from uniqueness applied to linear combinations of solutions; the regularity statement follows because the right-hand side C X is C^{k-2} when x is C^k, so the solution gains one derivative. No choice principle is used.

items.title: Local flow boxes, adapted charts and the Frobenius criterion for rest distributions
items.statement: Let Omega be a nonempty open subset of A. (i) Flow box. If X is a smooth vector field on Omega and X(p) is nonzero at a point p of Omega, then there is an open neighbourhood U of p in Omega and a chart (u^0,u^1,u^2,u^3): U -> R^4 in which X = partial/partial u^0; the integral curves of X in U are therefore the u^0-coordinate lines up to reparametrization. In particular every observer congruence n on Omega admits a local n-adapted chart, and in such a chart n = partial/partial u^0. (ii) Frobenius criterion. For a smooth nowhere-zero one-form alpha on Omega let D := ker alpha be the hyperplane distribution D_p = {v in V : alpha_p(v) = 0}. Then D is integrable on Omega (through every point there passes a local hypersurface whose tangent space at each of its points is the corresponding D_p) if and only if alpha wedge d alpha = 0 on Omega. (iii) Rest distributions of observer congruences. Let n be an observer congruence on Omega, alpha := n-flat, and let theta, omega be its expansion and vorticity (definition of the congruence kinematics). Then: (a) d alpha = 2 nabla_{[a}n_{b]}, i.e. d alpha(X,Y) = (nabla_X n-flat)(Y) - (nabla_Y n-flat)(X) for smooth vector fields X,Y; (b) for every p and all X,Y with alpha(X) = alpha(Y) = 0 one has d alpha(X,Y) = 2 omega(X,Y); consequently (alpha wedge d alpha)(p) = 0 if and only if omega(p) = 0, and on an open set U contained in Omega the following are equivalent: alpha wedge d alpha = 0 on U, omega = 0 on U, and the rest distribution ker alpha is integrable on U; (c) when the rest distribution is integrable on U, its integral hypersurfaces are orthogonal to n at every point and the restriction of eta to each of them is positive definite, so they are rest slices of the congruence. (iv) Scope. All statements are local on Omega; no global foliation, global synchronization, completeness or product structure is asserted, and no claim is made about variable-rank or non-smooth distributions.
items.strategy: (i) is the published flow-box theorem (thm-flow-box-theorem) applied on the manifold Omega, together with the identification of the integral curves with coordinate lines: in the chart X = partial/partial u^0, so the spatial coordinates are constant along the flow. (ii) is the published codimension-one Frobenius criterion (cor-codimension-one-frobenius-criterion) applied verbatim on the open subset of the smooth manifold A. (iii)(a) is the exterior-derivative identity d alpha(X,Y) = X(alpha(Y)) - Y(alpha(X)) - alpha([X,Y]) for a one-form (def-exterior-derivative-by-the-invariant-vector-field-formula) combined with the torsion-freeness nabla_X Y - nabla_Y X = [X,Y] of the flat connection (def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space), giving d alpha_{ab} = nabla_a n_b - nabla_b n_a = 2 nabla_{[a}n_{b]}. (iii)(b) for horizontal X,Y the projections in omega_{ab} = h_a{}^c h_b{}^d nabla_{[c}n_{d]} act as the identity on horizontal arguments, so omega(X,Y) = (1/2) d alpha(X,Y); hence alpha wedge d alpha = 0 at a point (which means d alpha vanishes on all pairs of horizontal vectors there) is equivalent to omega = 0 there, and the integrability equivalence on an open set is (ii). (iii)(c) a leaf has tangent space ker alpha_p = n(p)^perp at each of its points, so it is orthogonal to n there, and the restriction of eta to n(p)^perp is positive definite by thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition (c). All steps are local algebra plus the two cited theorems; no choice principle is used.

items.title: A closed 1-form on a simply connected open subset of the affine model has a primitive
items.statement: Let U be a nonempty open subset of A which, with the manifold topology of lem-affine-minkowski-charts-form-a-smooth-atlas, is path-connected and simply connected (def-simply-connected), and let alpha be a C^1 one-form on U with d alpha = 0 (def-closed-and-exact-differential-forms). Then there is a C^2 function F: U -> R with dF = alpha. Consequently, for any two piecewise C^1 paths gamma_0, gamma_1 in U with the same endpoints the integrals of alpha along them are equal, and the integral of alpha along every piecewise C^1 loop in U vanishes. Here for a C^1 one-form, closedness means in an inertial chart alpha=sum_i a_i dx^i with partial_i a_j=partial_j a_i; the exterior derivative is understood by this coefficient formula. If alpha is smooth, F may be taken smooth.
items.strategy:
Fix one inertial affine chart, identifying U with an open subset of R^4, and write alpha=sum_i a_i dx^i. Closedness for a C^1 form means partial_i a_j=partial_j a_i. All integration below is ordinary integration along finitely piecewise-C^1 paths.
(1) Local C^1 primitive, supplied in full rather than invoking the smooth-only imported Poincare theorem. On any convex ball B contained in U, fix b in B and set phi(x)=integral_0^1 sum_i a_i(b+t(x-b))(x_i-b_i) dt. For x in B and sufficiently small h, the radial segments for x+h e_j lie in a compact subset of B. The parameter derivative of the integrand is continuous on that compact set. The one-variable FTC expresses its difference quotient as the average of that derivative along x+u h e_j; uniform continuity makes these averages converge uniformly in t. Hence taking the integral of the quotient gives partial_j phi(x)=integral_0^1 [a_j(b+t(x-b))+t sum_i (x_i-b_i) partial_j a_i(b+t(x-b))]dt. Closedness and the chain rule identify the integrand with d/dt[t a_j(b+t(x-b))], so FTC gives partial_j phi=a_j. These partial derivatives are continuous, hence phi is C^1; since all a_j are C^1, phi is C^2. Chain rule and FTC on each path piece give integral_gamma alpha=phi(gamma(1))-phi(gamma(0)) for every piecewise-C^1 path contained in B. This is the C^1 radial proof of Lebl Thm 9.3.6, written explicitly here.
(2) Compact small-cell construction. Given a continuous based null-homotopy H:[0,1]^2 -> U of a piecewise-C^1 loop gamma at p, compactness of K=H([0,1]^2) gives finitely many balls B(b_l,r_l) contained in U whose concentric half-radius balls cover K. To obtain this finite family, cover K by all pairs of such balls centered at points of K; use compactness, then finitely many witnesses. Set r=min_l r_l>0. Uniform continuity of H gives delta>0 such that domain distances less than delta imply image distances less than r/2. Choose a finite rectangular mesh with cell diameter less than delta. For each cell, its lower-left image vertex belongs to a half-radius ball; the entire cell image is therefore contained in the corresponding full-radius ball. Only finitely many ball assignments are made. Refine the bottom mesh by the finitely many breakpoints of gamma if desired; this preserves the small-cell property.
(3) Replace each oriented mesh edge by the affine straight segment between its two image vertices. Each cell's four segments lie in its assigned convex ball, so its boundary integral is zero by (1). Every shared edge is exactly the same segment traversed oppositely by the adjacent cell; therefore finite summation cancels all interior edges. The top and vertical boundary segments are constant, since the homotopy is based. Each bottom loop arc and its replacement chord lie in the ball assigned to the corresponding bottom cell, so (1) makes their integrals equal. Thus integral_gamma alpha=0. No differentiability of H or smoothing theorem is used. The argument needs only continuous based null-homotopies, which the simply-connected definition supplies at every basepoint.
(4) For any two piecewise-C^1 paths from p to q, concatenate the first with the reversed second. It is a loop with zero integral by (3); finite concatenation and reversal give equal integrals. Piecewise-C^1 paths between points actually exist: take any continuous path, cover its compact image by finitely many half-radius balls inside U, apply uniform continuity and a finite subdivision as in (2), and replace the successive arcs by chords lying in the full balls. The resulting polygonal path stays in U and has the same endpoints.
(5) Fix p0 in the nonempty U. For each x let F(x) be the unique real value of the integral over a piecewise-C^1 path from p0 to x; existence follows from (4), and path independence makes the value unique. This defines F by a unique-value relation, without choosing a path simultaneously for every x. For any ball B around x contained in U, (1) and path concatenation give F(y)=F(x)+phi(y)-phi(x) for y in B. Therefore F is C^2 and dF=alpha on U. If alpha is smooth, repeated differentiation of partial_j F=a_j makes F smooth. Loop-integral vanishing and path independence were proved in (3)-(4). No AC or countable-choice principle is used. All existential path/homotopy choices concern a single object at a time, all mesh/ball choices are finite, and the global F uses uniqueness rather than a family of selected representatives.

items.title: Fermi-Walker transport preserves the metric, and explicit rigid and non-rigid observer congruences
items.statement: (a) Preservation. Let x: I -> A be a C^2 future timelike worldline and let X,Y: I -> V be C^1 Fermi-Walker transported fields along x (def-sr-fermi-walker-transport). Then s |-> eta(X(s),Y(s)) is constant on the given parameter interval I; in particular Fermi-Walker transport preserves norms and orthogonality, and the unique Fermi-Walker transported family with initial values a tetrad (E_0(s_0),...,E_3(s_0)) with E_0(s_0) = U(s_0)/c is an orthonormal tetrad (E_0(s),...,E_3(s)) at every s with E_0(s) = U(s)/c (observer-adapted tetrad), by lem-sr-fermi-walker-transport-existence-and-uniqueness. (b) Rindler wedge congruence. In an inertial chart (x^0,x,y,z) consider Phi(theta,rho,y,z) := (rho sinh theta, rho cosh theta, y, z) on R x (0,inf) x R^2, with theta in R and rho>0. Then Phi is a smooth bijection onto the right wedge W := {(x^0,x) : x > |x^0|}, with smooth inverse rho = sqrt(x^2 - (x^0)^2), theta = (1/2) log((x + x^0)/(x - x^0)); the pullback of eta is g = -rho^2 d theta^2 + d rho^2 + dy^2 + dz^2; the field n := rho^{-1} partial/partial theta is a future unit timelike field on W whose congruence is Born rigid and irrotational, with acceleration a = nabla_n n = rho^{-1} partial/partial rho, hence eta(a,a) = rho^{-2}; its rest slices theta = const are hyperplanes orthogonal to n with induced metric d rho^2 + dy^2 + dz^2 independent of theta; and the frame (n, partial/partial rho, partial/partial y, partial/partial z) is a tetrad field which is not a coordinate frame, since [n, partial/partial rho] = +(1/rho) n is nonzero (def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields). (c) Rigid rotation, ambient nonintegrability and ring holonomy. Fix real Omega. In the inertial chart let U_Omega be the open timelike region r^2=(x^1)^2+(x^2)^2<c^2/Omega^2 when Omega!=0, and the whole chart when Omega=0. On this four-dimensional open set put K=partial_0+(Omega/c)(-x^2 partial_1+x^1 partial_2), gamma(r)=(1-Omega^2 r^2/c^2)^(-1/2), and n=gamma(r)K. This is a smooth future unit timelike Born-rigid congruence. If Omega!=0, its three-dimensional rest distribution in the ambient open set is nowhere integrable: its vorticity is nowhere zero and no ambient rest-simultaneity hypersurface exists locally. If Omega=0, n=partial_0 is inertial and irrotational, and the rest hypersurfaces are x^0=const. Now fix R>0 with |Omega|R<c and restrict to the timelike ring cylinder r=R, x^3=const, whose rotating angle is varphi=phi-Omega t modulo2pi, x^0=ct. The ring observer phi=phi_0+Omega t has n=gamma(R)(1,-(Omega R/c)sin phi,(Omega R/c)cos phi,0). The induced metric is -(c^2-Omega^2R^2)dt^2+2Omega R^2 dt dvarphi+R^2 dvarphi^2. The ambient rest covector restricted to the cylinder is proportional to -(c^2-Omega^2R^2)dt+Omega R^2 dvarphi, so the one-dimensional rest distribution on that cylinder is locally integrable and satisfies dt/dvarphi=Omega R^2/(c^2-Omega^2R^2). After one positive circuit in the rotating label, its lift starting at t=0 has signed time offset Delta t=2pi Omega R^2/(c^2-Omega^2R^2). For Omega!=0 it returns to the same rotating label at a different time and does not close as a ring rest-simultaneity curve; there is no globally single-valued real rest-synchronization time on the entire cylinder with time-oriented nonzero differential annihilating these rest lines. This global ring holonomy is distinct from the ambient local Frobenius obstruction. For Omega=0 the offset is zero and ring rest lines are t=const. (d) Bell first-order field. Let q: J -> R^3 be C^2 with q(t) = (q_1(t),0,0) and |q_1'(t)| < c, and consider the C1 future unit field of the translated worldlines x_xi(t) = (c t, q(t) + xi) parametrized by xi in an open subset of R^3, with n = gamma(1, q_1'(t)/c, 0, 0), gamma = (1 - q_1'(t)^2/c^2)^{-1/2}, and unit longitudinal rest vector s = gamma(q_1'(t)/c, 1, 0, 0). For this C1 field define the first-order rest projection $h^a{}_b=\delta^a{}_b+n^an_b$ and projected deformation $\theta_{ab}=h^c{}_a h^d{}_b\partial_{(c}n_{d)}$, using the explicit first-order version of def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space. These coordinate formulas need only C1 n, give a continuous tensor, and agree with the smooth congruence definitions when q is smooth; in this first-order sense Born rigidity means theta=0. Then theta(s,s) = s^a s^b partial_a n_b = gamma^3 q_1'(t) q_1''(t)/c^3, which is nonzero exactly when q_1'(t) q_1''(t) is nonzero; hence the congruence is not Born rigid on any neighbourhood of a parameter value with q_1'(t) q_1''(t) nonzero, although for every fixed chart time t the separation between the members labelled xi_1 and xi_2 is the constant |xi_1 - xi_2|. A breaking or fracture conclusion about a material rod would additionally require an elasticity model and a failure criterion and is not a kinematic statement.
items.strategy: (a) Differentiate in the given parameter s: d/ds eta(X,Y)=eta(X',Y)+eta(X,Y'). The corrected transport equation is X'=tau' c^{-2}(eta(A,X)U-eta(U,X)A), and likewise for Y. Substitution gives tau' c^{-2}[eta(A,X)eta(U,Y)-eta(U,X)eta(A,Y)+eta(A,Y)eta(U,X)-eta(U,Y)eta(A,X)]=0, so the continuous scalar is constant on I by the mean-value theorem on every compact connecting subinterval, with the endpoint reading already declared. Equivalently its proper-time derivative divides this identity by tau'>0. The initially orthonormal family remains orthonormal, and E_0=U/c is transported because U'/tau'=A; uniqueness of the arbitrary-parameter ODE is lem-sr-fermi-walker-transport-existence-and-uniqueness. (b); uniqueness is lem-sr-fermi-walker-transport-existence-and-uniqueness. (b) Injectivity of Phi follows from x^2 - (x^0)^2 = rho^2 and the sign of x; the inverse formulas are the standard hyperbolic identities cosh^2 - sinh^2 = 1 and tanh(theta) = x^0/x, and both maps are smooth on their domains because rho > 0 and x - x^0 > 0. Differentiating Phi gives dx^0 = sinh theta d rho + rho cosh theta d theta, dx = cosh theta d rho + rho sinh theta d theta, so -(dx^0)^2 + dx^2 = -rho^2 d theta^2 + d rho^2. The field n is unit future by inspection; a direct computation with the metric gives nabla_{partial_theta} partial_theta = rho partial_rho and hence a = nabla_n n = rho^{-1} partial_rho; the rest slices are the theta-level sets, orthogonal to n because the metric has no theta-rho cross term, with the displayed induced metric independent of theta, so theta_{ab} = 0 and, since the slice is orthogonal to a field whose rest distribution is integrable, omega = 0; the commutator is [rho^{-1}partial_theta, partial_rho] = +(1/rho^2)partial_theta = +(1/rho)n. (c) K is future timelike exactly on the stated U_Omega and is Killing by direct coordinate differentiation. Projecting the symmetric derivative of n=gamma K to its rest space kills the derivative-of-gamma terms (K is parallel to n) and the Killing terms, so theta=0. Put kappa=eta(K,.)=-dx^0+(Omega/c)(x^1 dx^2-x^2 dx^1). Then d kappa=2(Omega/c)dx^1 wedge dx^2 and kappa wedge d kappa=-2(Omega/c)dx^0 wedge dx^1 wedge dx^2, nonzero exactly when Omega!=0. Since n-flat=gamma kappa, n-flat wedge d(n-flat)=gamma^2 kappa wedge d kappa; the stated ambient Frobenius/vorticity result follows, including at the axis by these smooth Cartesian formulas. The Omega=0 limit has the constant unit field. On the ring cylinder, substitute x^0=ct, x^1=Rcos(varphi+Omega t), x^2=Rsin(varphi+Omega t) to obtain the displayed metric and covector. Its one-dimensional kernel is the line field generated by partial_varphi+[Omega R^2/(c^2-Omega^2R^2)]partial_t, whose integral gives the signed holonomy. A globally defined time-oriented rest-synchronization function would have differential a positive multiple of dt-[Omega R^2/(c^2-Omega^2R^2)]dvarphi. Its integral around a fixed-t ring would have nonzero constant sign for Omega!=0, contradicting exactness of that differential. No local nonintegrability is attributed to the cylinder's one-dimensional rest-line field. (d) C2 q makes q1' C1, gamma C1 and n C1. Use the explicitly given first-order projected symmetric derivative of n; no smooth-only congruence or later connecting-field theorem is invoked. Write beta=q_1'/c, beta'=q_1''/c, x^0=ct and n_b=(-gamma,gamma beta,0,0), so partial_0=(1/c)d/dt and partial_1 n_b=0. Differentiation gives partial_0 n_0=-gamma^3 beta beta'/c and partial_0 n_1=gamma^3 beta'/c, using 1+gamma^2 beta^2=gamma^2. Contract with s=(gamma beta,gamma,0,0): s^0[s^0 partial_0 n_0+s^1 partial_0 n_1]=gamma^5 beta beta'(1-beta^2)/c=gamma^3 beta beta'/c=gamma^3 q_1' q_1''/c^3. Projection to the rest space does not change this contraction since s is rest-orthogonal. All transverse expansion components vanish, so it is nonzero exactly under the stated condition, and fixed chart-time separations remain xi_1-xi_2. The material fracture conclusion is excluded. All computations use finite algebra and the declared calculus, with no choice principle.

items.title: The smooth local Herglotz-Noether classification of Born-rigid motions
items.statement: Let n be a smooth future unit timelike field on a nonempty open subset Omega of A with acceleration a = nabla_n n, rest metric h, expansion theta and vorticity omega, and assume that n is Born rigid, theta = 0 (def-sr-observer-congruence-and-kinematics). (i) Preliminary identity. For every smooth vector field X on Omega with eta(n,X) = 0 one has nabla_X n = 0 if and only if theta(X,.) = 0 and omega(X,.) = 0; in particular, if theta = omega = 0 on an open set U then nabla_X n = 0 for every vector field X on U tangent to the rest distribution. (ii) Rotational case. Suppose omega is nowhere zero on a flow box U with adapted coordinates (s,y) and n = partial_s (thm-sr-local-congruence-adapted-charts-and-frobenius). Then the vorticity and the acceleration are basic (their components in the adapted coframe do not depend on s), d(a-flat) = 0 on U, and for any primitive F of the closed one-form a-flat on the star-shaped box U (thm-poincare-lemma-for-differential-forms-on-star-shaped-domains) the field K := exp(F) n is a timelike Killing field, nabla_a K_b + nabla_b K_a = 0, equivalently L_K eta = 0; if U is connected and simply connected with omega nowhere zero, a single positive smooth f on U satisfies L_{f n} eta = 0 (lem-sr-closed-one-form-primitive-on-simply-connected-open-sets). Conversely every future timelike Killing field on a connected open set, normalized as n = K/sqrt(-eta(K,K)), is Born rigid, and its flow is rotational exactly when its vorticity is nowhere zero. (iii) Irrotational case. Suppose theta = omega = 0 on Omega. Then on a sufficiently small neighbourhood U of every point the connected leaves of the rest distribution are open subsets of affine hyperplanes: there are a smooth future timelike curve z: J -> A with eta(z',z') = -1 and a smooth function sigma: U -> J such that, in the sense of the unique label, the leaves are the hyperplanes H_s = z(s) + z'(s)^perp, n = z' o sigma on U, N(x)=1+eta(z''(sigma(x)),x-z(sigma(x)))>0, d sigma(v)=-eta(z'(sigma(x)),v)/N(x), a = (z'' o sigma)/N, and nabla n = dsigma (x) (z'' o sigma); the tubular label has derivative 1 + eta(z'' o sigma, x - z o sigma), which is nonzero (taken positive) on U. Conversely, for every smooth future timelike curve z with eta(z',z') = -1 the field n := z' o sigma on any tubular neighbourhood on which the label sigma is unique with positive derivative is a smooth irrotational Born-rigid congruence with these same formulas. (iv) Scope. All statements are local on Omega; no global classification of rigid motions, no global orbit quotient, no completeness and no global restriction on the size of a rigid body is asserted beyond what the local formulas give. The rotational case is the local form of the Herglotz-Noether statement that a rotational Born-rigid motion is Killing; the irrotational case describes the orthogonal affine-plane families.
items.strategy: The proof follows the research argument in research/first-principles-2026-10-03/relativity/scaffold/sr-supplier-proofs.md S11, which supplies the calculational omissions of Giulini, math-ph/0602018, Section 5.5 pp. 41-49, and avoids both the source's analyticity assumption and its unsafe global orbit quotient. (i) For horizontal X the decomposition gives nabla_X n_b = theta(X,.) + omega(X,.), so vanishing of both is equivalent to nabla_X n = 0. (ii) In adapted coordinates (s,y) with n = partial_s one has h_{ss} = h_{si} = 0, the slice metric h_ij(y) is independent of s by Born rigidity, and one chooses an orthonormal coframe theta^i of the slice metric (thm-gram-schmidt-orthonormalisation), pulled back to the box, together with theta^0 = -n-flat; then g = -(theta^0)^2 + sum (theta^i)^2. Writing a = a_i theta^i and omega = (1/2)omega_ij theta^i wedge theta^j, the kinematic decomposition gives d theta^0 = -theta^0 wedge a - 2 omega and d theta^i = -gamma-bar^i_j wedge theta^j, where gamma-bar is the pullback of the Levi-Civita connection of the slice metric (thm-fundamental-theorem-of-riemannian-geometry). The connection 1-forms of the flat connection in this coframe are gamma^0_i = gamma^i_0 = a_i theta^0 - omega_ij theta^j and gamma^i_j = gamma-bar^i_j - omega_ij theta^0; substituting into the structure equations verifies d theta^A = -gamma^A_B wedge theta^B and the Lorentz skew conditions, and the flatness identity d gamma + gamma wedge gamma = 0 (zero curvature of def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space) has horizontal components 0 = R-bar_ijkl + 2omega_ij omega_kl + omega_ik omega_jl - omega_il omega_jk and 0 = D_k omega_ij - D_j omega_ik - 2 a_i omega_jk, where R-bar_ijkl:=Rm(e_k,e_l,e_j,e_i) is the connection-form coefficient convention, and D is the slice covariant derivative. Here the published def-riemann-curvature-four-tensor uses Rm(X,Y,Z,W)=h(R(X,Y)Z,W), so its same-order Rm(e_i,e_j,e_k,e_l) is not R-bar_ijkl. Indeed the curvature 2-form Omega-bar^i_j(e_k,e_l) equals h(R(e_k,e_l)e_j,e_i), precisely the displayed permutation. All subsequent R-bar contractions use this convention; for example R-bar_1212=-3 omega_12^2 corresponds to Rm(e_1,e_2,e_1,e_2)=+3 omega_12^2, because the last two curvature slots are skew. The slice metric is unchanged, and the basicness argument uses this fixed permutation, not a sign change of Rm. In three dimensions the four-form component identity omega_ij omega_kl - omega_ik omega_jl + omega_il omega_jk = 0 holds, so R-bar_ijkl = -3 omega_ij omega_kl. Since h is s-independent, R-bar is basic; differentiating R-bar = -3 omega (x) omega along n gives n(omega_ij) omega_kl + omega_ij n(omega_kl) = 0, whence n(omega_kl) = 0 for every pair with omega_kl nonzero and then n(omega_ij) = 0 for all pairs: omega is basic. Differentiating the second relation along n (the frame and D are basic) gives omega_jk n(a_i) = 0, so a is basic. Applying d^2 = 0 to theta^0 (thm-the-exterior-derivative-squares-to-zero) gives 0 = 2 omega wedge a + theta^0 wedge da - 2 d omega; Cartan's formula gives i_n d omega=L_n omega-d(i_n omega)=0 since omega is basic and horizontal. Contracting the displayed identity with n, using theta^0(n)=1 and i_n omega=i_n a=0, gives da-theta^0 wedge i_n da=0, hence the horizontal part of da vanishes. Likewise i_n da=L_n a-d(i_n a)=0 because a is basic and horizontal; therefore da=0. No horizontal projection of theta^0 wedge da is used to infer this. On the star-shaped box the Poincare lemma gives a-flat = dF; with f = exp(F) one computes L_{f n} eta = f L_n eta + df (x) n-flat + n-flat (x) df = -f(n-flat (x) a + a (x) n-flat) + f a (x) n-flat + f n-flat (x) a = 0 using L_n eta = -(n-flat (x) a + a (x) n-flat) and a = dF = d log f, so K = f n is Killing. The global simply connected version replaces the star-shaped primitive by the path-integral primitive of lem-sr-closed-one-form-primitive-on-simply-connected-open-sets. The converse is immediate from L_K eta = 0 and (L_{fn}eta) = f L_n eta + df (x) n-flat + n-flat (x) df. (iii) With theta = omega = 0, (i) gives nabla_X n = 0 for leaf-tangent X; on a connected leaf n is therefore constant (the ambient parallel transport is trivial and the leaf is connected), so the leaf's tangent space is the fixed subspace n^perp and integrating the constant tangent shows the leaf lies in the affine hyperplane through any of its points with direction n^perp. Choose a flow line z(s) with z' = n; the leaf through z(s) is z(s) + z'(s)^perp. Put F(x,s)=eta(z'(s),x-z(s)) in an inertial chart and consider the smooth 5-dimensional Euclidean map H(x,s)=(x,F(x,s)). Its derivative is block triangular with upper block the4-by-4 identity and lower s-coefficient N=1+eta(z''(s),x-z(s)); at a center event x=z(s), N=1. The explicit inverse of the derivative sends (v,r) to (v,(r-D_xF(v))/N), so the choice-free smooth Euclidean inverse lemma [[lem-choice-free-smooth-inverse-function-theorem-in-euclidean-space]] gives a local smooth inverse. Because H preserves the first four coordinates, evaluating that inverse at (x,0) gives (x,sigma(x)). Shrink to product neighbourhoods where this inverse and N>0 hold; local injectivity gives unique sigma and the same hyperplane labels. This uses the ZF Euclidean supplier, not the AC-assuming Banach implicit theorem; implicit differentiation gives d sigma(v)=-eta(z'(sigma),v)/N and therefore n(sigma)=1/N; the field derivative is nabla n=d sigma (x) z''(sigma), and its acceleration is nabla_n n=z''(sigma)/N, not z''(sigma) away from the centre curve. These same formulas verify the converse: sigma-level sets are affine hyperplanes, n is constant along each leaf, so theta=omega=0. The positivity of N fixes the future-oriented tubular label. No choice principle is used; all objects are finite-dimensional and the cited ODE/flow suppliers are those of the published mathematics library.

items.title: Worked radar round trip: emission, reflection and reception at exact rational parameters
items.statement: Worked computation. In an inertial chart (x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3) with metric diag(-1,1,1,1) let the observer be at rest at the spatial origin (the worldline x^1 = x^2 = x^3 = 0), let T > 0 and let q := x^{-1}(cT, (3/5)cT, 0, 0), an event of chart time T and spatial distance 3cT/5 from the observer. (a) With e_- := x^{-1}((2/5)cT, 0, 0, 0) and e_+ := x^{-1}((8/5)cT, 0, 0, 0) one has q - e_- = ((3/5)cT, (3/5)cT, 0, 0) and e_+ - q = ((3/5)cT, -(3/5)cT, 0, 0); both have eta = -9c^2T^2/25 + 9c^2T^2/25 = 0 and positive time components, so both are future null. (b) The radar assignments are tau_rad(q) = (tau_- + tau_+)/2 = (2T/5 + 8T/5)/2 = T, the chart time of q, and rho_rad(q) = c(tau_+ - tau_-)/2 = c(6T/5)/2 = 3cT/5, the chart distance of q from the observer. (c) The same computation for q' := x^{-1}(cT, (4/5)cT, 0, 0) gives e'_- = x^{-1}((1/5)cT,0,0,0), e'_+ = x^{-1}((9/5)cT,0,0,0), radar time T and radar distance 4cT/5. Hence the two events q and q' of equal chart time are radar-simultaneous, with radar distances equal to their chart distances, in agreement with lem-sr-radar-midpoint-for-inertial-observer.
items.strategy: Direct exact evaluations: the nullity and future orientation of the two segments are single evaluations of the diagonal form and the sign of their time components; the radar time and distance are the midpoints and half-differences of the displayed rational parameters, and the last clause checks clause (iii) of the cited theorem on exact numbers. All arithmetic is rational.

items.title: Worked time dilation at speed 3c/5
items.statement: Worked computation. In an inertial chart x with metric diag(-1,1,1,1) let v = 3c/5, gamma = (1 - v^2/c^2)^{-1/2} = 5/4, and consider the worldline y(t) = (ct, (3c/5)t, 0, 0). (a) y'(t) = (c, 3c/5, 0, 0) and eta(y',y') = -c^2 + 9c^2/25 = -(16/25)c^2, so y is future timelike and its proper-time rate is tau'(t) = (1/c) sqrt((16/25)c^2) = 4/5: between coordinate times t_0 < t_1 the clock reads (4/5)(t_1 - t_0) = (t_1 - t_0)/gamma, i.e. it runs slow by the factor 4/5 = 1/gamma. (b) The four-velocity is U = y'/tau' = (5c/4, 3c/4, 0, 0) with eta(U,U) = -25c^2/16 + 9c^2/16 = -c^2, and the dimensionless velocity is u = U/c = (5/4)(1, 3/5, 0, 0) = gamma(e_0 + (3/5)e_1) for the chart's coordinate basis vector e_0: this is exactly the boost relation of clause (i) of lem-sr-boost-time-length-and-velocity-formulas. (c) Described in the boosted chart x' in which the clock is at rest (boost speed 3c/5 along the first axis), its x'-time rate equals its proper-time rate, and the inverse statement Delta t = gamma Delta tau holds with gamma = 5/4.
items.strategy: Exact rational evaluation of the diagonal form on y', of the proper-time rate and of the four-velocity; the boost relation in (b) is read off from the coefficient gamma = 5/4 by comparison with the definition of the boost. Every step is finite arithmetic with the exact rationals 3/4, 4/5, 5/4.

items.title: Worked length contraction of a rod of rest length 5 at speed 3c/5
items.statement: Worked computation. In an inertial chart x let the chart x' be related to x by a boost of speed v = 3c/5 along the first spatial axis, gamma = 5/4, so x'^0 = (5/4)(x^0 - (3/5)x^1) and x'^1 = (5/4)(x^1 - (3/5)x^0). Let L_0 = 5 and let the rod at rest in x' have endpoints on the worldlines x'^1 = 0 and x'^1 = 5 (with the transverse coordinates zero). Solving the transition for x^1 as a function of x^0 gives x^1 = (3/5)x^0 for the first worldline and x^1 = (3/5)x^0 + 4 for the second, so at every equal x-time the endpoints are separated by 4 = L_0/gamma in the frame x. Explicit witness: the events p := x^{-1}(5,3,0,0) and r := x^{-1}(5,7,0,0) are simultaneous in x (both have x^0 = 5) and separated by 4; their x'-coordinates are x'(p) = (4,0,0,0) and x'(r) = (1,5,0,0), so they are not simultaneous in x' but their x'-separation is 5 = L_0. Comparing events at equal x'-time instead: the events of the two worldlines with x'^0 = 4 are x^{-1}(5,3,0,0) and x^{-1}(35/4,37/4,0,0), the second of which has x'^1 = 5; at equal x'-time 4 the endpoints are separated by 5, the rest length. Thus the frame x assigns length 4 to a rod of rest length 5 at rest in x', exactly the contraction L_0/gamma of clause (ii) of lem-sr-boost-time-length-and-velocity-formulas, and the comparison uses the simultaneity slice of the measuring frame in the sense of def-sr-simultaneity-slice-and-rest-distance.
items.strategy: Exact rational computation: solve the two linear transition relations for x^1 as a function of x^0 on each worldline and subtract; verify the witness events by substituting into the transition, obtaining the exact values 4, 0, 1 and 5; the equal-x'-time event is obtained from x'^0 = 4 on the second worldline x^1 = (3/5)x^0 + 4, which gives x^0 = 35/4, x^1 = 37/4 and x'^1 = 5. All arithmetic is rational.

items.title: Worked velocity transformation: collinear, transverse and null cases
items.statement: Worked computation. Let x and x' be inertial charts related by a boost of parameter v = 3c/5 along the first axis (gamma = 5/4). (a) Collinear case: a worldline with coordinate velocity w = (4c/5, 0, 0) in x has, by lem-sr-boost-time-length-and-velocity-formulas (iv), w'_1 = (4c/5 - 3c/5)/(1 - (3/5)(4/5)) = (c/5)/(13/25) = 5c/13, so |w'| = 5c/13 < c; the Galilean sum 7c/5 is not the transformed velocity. (b) Transverse case: a worldline with w = (0, c/2, 0) has w'_1 = (0 - 3c/5)/(1 - 0) = -3c/5 and w'_2 = (c/2)/((5/4)(1 - 0)) = 2c/5, hence |w'| = sqrt(9/25 + 4/25) c = (sqrt(13)/5) c < c. (c) Null limit: for w = (c, 0, 0) the formula gives w'_1 = (c - 3c/5)/(1 - 3/5) = c and |w'| = c: a null worldline is null in every inertial chart. The three cases verify the velocity transformation and the subluminality statement of clause (iv) of lem-sr-boost-time-length-and-velocity-formulas.
items.strategy: Exact rational evaluation of the transformation formula in the three cases; the norms are exact square roots of rational multiples of c^2, and the null limit is the case in which numerator and denominator vanish together at |w| = c.
