items.title: Worked Rindler wedge congruence: chart, metric, acceleration, rigidity and non-coordinate frame
items.statement: Worked computation. In the inertial chart (x^0,x,y,z) with metric diag(-1,1,1,1) consider Phi(theta,rho,y,z) := (rho sinh theta, rho cosh theta, y, z) on R x (0,inf) x R^2, with theta in R and rho>0. (a) x^2 - (x^0)^2 = rho^2 and x = rho cosh theta > 0 give that the image is the right wedge W = {x > |x^0|}, and the inverse rho = sqrt(x^2 - (x^0)^2), theta = (1/2)log((x + x^0)/(x - x^0)) is smooth on W; both maps are smooth, so Phi is a diffeomorphism onto W. (b) Differentiating gives dx^0 = sinh theta d rho + rho cosh theta d theta and dx = cosh theta d rho + rho sinh theta d theta, so the pullback metric is -rho^2 d theta^2 + d rho^2 + dy^2 + dz^2. (c) The field n := rho^{-1} partial_theta satisfies eta(n,n) = -1 and is future. Computing with the pullback metric, the nonzero connection coefficients are Gamma^rho_{theta theta} = rho and Gamma^theta_{theta rho} = Gamma^theta_{rho theta} = 1/rho, so nabla_{partial_theta} partial_theta = rho partial_rho and the congruence acceleration is a = nabla_n n = rho^{-1} partial_rho, with eta(a,a) = 1/rho^2; for example at rho = 2 one has |a| = 1/2 in reciprocal-length units. (d) The slices theta = const are hyperplanes through the origin with induced metric d rho^2 + dy^2 + dz^2, independent of theta; hence the congruence is Born rigid. It is also irrotational: the rest distribution is the tangent distribution of the theta-slices, hence integrable, and omega = 0 by thm-sr-local-congruence-adapted-charts-and-frobenius. (e) The tetrad field (n, partial_rho, partial_y, partial_z) is not a coordinate frame: [n, partial_rho] = [rho^{-1}partial_theta, partial_rho] = +(1/rho^2) partial_theta = +(1/rho) n is nonzero, and a coordinate frame's members commute (def-sr-chart-tetrad-and-congruence-distinction). This realizes the Rindler congruence of thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples with exact formulas.
items.strategy: Exact computation in the given chart: the hyperbola identity x^2 - (x^0)^2 = rho^2 and the sign of x give bijectivity, and the inverse is read off from cosh^2 - sinh^2 = 1 and tanh(theta) = x^0/x; the differentials are read off from the definitions of sinh and cosh; the Christoffel symbols are computed from the displayed metric; rigidity is the theta-independence of the slice metric; the commutator is a two-term differentiation. All identities are exact symbolic computations in the variable pair (theta,rho). In the bracket, partial_rho(rho^-1)=-rho^-2 and the convention [f partial_theta,partial_rho]=-partial_rho(f)partial_theta gives the positive sign.

items.title: Worked rigid rotation: rest-space holonomy around the ring and failure of ring synchronization
items.statement: Worked computation. Fix R > 0 and Omega with Omega R = 3c/5, so gamma = (1 - 9/25)^{-1/2} = 5/4. (a) In the inertial chart the ring observer at angular position phi = phi_0 + Omega t (chart time t) has unit tangent n = gamma(1, -(3/5)sin phi, (3/5)cos phi, 0) = (5/4)(1, -(3/5)sin phi, (3/5)cos phi, 0), which is future unit because gamma^2(9/25 - 1) = -1. (b) Write the cylinder r = R in the rotating angular coordinate varphi := phi - Omega t, so that the point has inertial coordinates (ct, R cos(varphi + Omega t), R sin(varphi + Omega t)). Substituting into -(dx^0)^2 + (dx^1)^2 + (dx^2)^2 gives the induced flat metric g = -(c^2 - Omega^2R^2)dt^2 + 2Omega R^2 dt dvarphi + R^2 dvarphi^2 = -(16/25)c^2 dt^2 + (6/5)cR dt dvarphi + R^2 dvarphi^2. (c) The rest-space covector of n is proportional to -(c^2 - Omega^2R^2)dt + Omega R^2 dvarphi = -(16/25)c^2 dt + (3/5)cR dvarphi, so a curve tangent to the rest spaces satisfies dt/dvarphi = Omega R^2/(c^2 - Omega^2R^2) = 15R/(16c). Integrating over one turn varphi in [0,2pi] gives Delta t = 2pi Omega R^2/(c^2 - Omega^2R^2) = 15 pi R/(8c), which is nonzero: the curve tangent to the rest spaces that starts at the observer with varphi = 0 returns to the same rotating angular label at the later chart time 15 pi R/(8c), so the rest simultaneity of the rotating congruence does not close up around the ring and no globally single-valued real rest-synchronization time with time-oriented nonzero differential exists on the whole cylinder. (d) Extend the ring observers to the ambient smooth future unit rotating field on r<c/|Omega|, with Cartesian formula n=gamma(r)[partial_0+(Omega/c)(-x^2 partial_1+x^1 partial_2)]. Its three-dimensional rest distribution is nonintegrable by the nonzero Frobenius three-form of thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples. The cylinder's restricted rest distribution is one-dimensional and locally integrable; its nonzero global holonomy is the different obstruction checked in (c). The ring motion and the ambient field are Born rigid. This preserves the distinction between ambient local nonintegrability and global ring synchronization failure.
items.strategy: Exact rational computation: verify eta(n,n) = -1; expand the substitution into the flat form; read the rest-space covector from g(n,.); solve for dt/dvarphi and integrate around the circle; compare with the nonzero value 15piR/(8c). The vorticity statement is the finite computation of the antisymmetric part of nabla n along the ring. Ambient Frobenius uses kappa=-dx^0+(Omega/c)(x^1dx^2-x^2dx^1) and kappa wedge d kappa=-2(Omega/c)dx^0 wedge dx^1 wedge dx^2; multiplying by gamma(r) does not change whether it vanishes. On the cylinder the line field is locally integrable, and the global offset is instead the explicitly integrated one-turn holonomy.

items.title: Worked Bell-type translated congruence: constant launch-frame separation without Born rigidity
items.statement: Worked computation. In an inertial chart let q(t) = ((1/2)alpha t^2, 0, 0) with alpha > 0, and consider the congruence of translated worldlines x_xi(t) = (ct, q(t) + xi) for xi in an open subset of R^3, defined while |q_1'(t)| = alpha |t| < c. Then n = gamma(1, alpha t/c, 0, 0) with gamma = (1 - alpha^2t^2/c^2)^{-1/2}, and the unit longitudinal rest vector is s = gamma(alpha t/c, 1, 0, 0). (a) Direct computation gives theta(s,s) = s^a s^b partial_a n_b = gamma^3 alpha^2 t/c^3, which is nonzero for every t != 0. Hence the congruence is not Born rigid on any neighbourhood of a time t != 0: the longitudinal expansion does not vanish. (b) Nevertheless, for every fixed chart time t the separation between the member labelled xi_1 and the member labelled xi_2 is |xi_1 - xi_2|, constant in t: the congruence has constant launch-frame separation while failing Born rigidity. (c) At t = 0 one has q'(0) = 0 and theta(s,s) = 0, and the failure appears immediately on both sides of t = 0. This is the Bell-type translated congruence of thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples (d); a physical conclusion about a breaking thread or rod would additionally need an elasticity model and a failure criterion.
items.strategy: Put beta=alpha t/c and beta'=alpha/c. With x^0=ct, partial_0 n_0=-gamma^3 alpha^2t/c^3 and partial_0 n_1=gamma^3 alpha/c^2. Contract with s=(gamma alpha t/c,gamma,0,0): theta(s,s)=gamma^5 alpha^2t(1-alpha^2t^2/c^2)/c^3=gamma^3 alpha^2t/c^3. This vanishes exactly at t=0 on the two-sided subluminal domain |t|<c/alpha. At c=1, beta=3/5 and beta'=1 the general contraction is75/64, while the discarded extra factor gives3075/1024. The translated members differ by the constant vector xi_1-xi_2 at a fixed chart time. items.title: Counterexample: a Born-rigid congruence need not be a Killing congruence
items.statement: Statement refuted: 'every smooth Born-rigid future unit timelike field n is locally a positive multiple of a Killing field'. Fix a length scale L_0>0 and use a geometric proper-length parameter lambda (the model's proper-time parameter is tau=lambda/c). Put psi(lambda)=lambda^2/(2L_0^2), e_0(lambda)=(cosh psi,sinh psi,0,0), e_1(lambda)=(sinh psi,cosh psi,0,0), and z(lambda)=(integral_0^lambda cosh psi(s) ds,integral_0^lambda sinh psi(s) ds,0,0), so z'=e_0 and eta(z',z')=-1. Define Phi(lambda,xi,y,zeta)=z(lambda)+xi e_1(lambda)+y e_2+zeta e_3. On a sufficiently small open coordinate box around0 this is injective with smooth inverse and N=1+k(lambda)xi>0, where k(lambda)=lambda/L_0^2; its pullback metric is -N^2 d lambda^2+d xi^2+dy^2+d zeta^2. The unit field n=N^-1 partial_lambda is future, irrotational and Born rigid: its rest slices lambda=const have fixed Euclidean induced metric. Its acceleration one-form is a-flat=[k(lambda)/N]d xi, and d(a-flat)=[1/(L_0^2N^2)]d lambda wedge d xi is nowhere zero. For a positive smooth f, the Killing equation for K=f n and Born rigidity imply d log f=a-flat, impossible because d^2 log f=0. Thus no positive smooth multiple of this n is Killing even locally; irrotational Born rigidity does not force a Killing rescaling. The Rindler congruence is not this counterexample: rho n=partial_theta is Killing for its theta-independent metric. The rotational classification of thm-sr-smooth-local-herglotz-noether is preserved; this example concerns its irrotational branch.
items.strategy: The hyperbolic identities give an orthonormal pair (e_0,e_1), with e_0'=k e_1 and e_1'=k e_0. The FTC defines z'=e_0. Differentiating Phi gives partial_lambda Phi=N e_0, partial_xi Phi=e_1 and the constant transverse vectors; at0 the derivative is invertible, so the choice-free smooth inverse-function theorem gives an injective local chart. Shrink to a coordinate box with |lambda|,|xi|<epsilon L_0 and epsilon<1 to ensure N>=1-epsilon^2>0. The metric follows directly; its rest-slice metric is lambda-independent, so theta=0, and its rest distribution is the lambda foliation, so omega=0. Its Christoffel/flat-coordinate derivative gives a=(k/N)partial_xi, hence a-flat=(k/N)d xi. Differentiate k/(1+k xi) in lambda: k'/N^2=1/(L_0^2N^2), proving the displayed nonclosed acceleration form. For Born-rigid n, sym nabla n=-n-flat sym-tensor a-flat. The equation L_{f n}eta=0 is n-flat sym-tensor(df-f a-flat)=0; evaluation twice on n and once on n plus a rest vector forces df-f a-flat=0, hence d log f=a-flat. Applying d and the exterior-square-zero theorem contradicts the everywhere nonzero displayed two-form. This replaces the false Rindler counterexample while preserving the full intended claim. Its explicit local construction has no global quotient, tube completeness or material-model assumption, and uses no choice principle. The nonlogical Rindler clarification is checked directly from the A theorem: its metric −rho^2 dtheta^2+drho^2+dy^2+dz^2 is theta-independent, hence partial_theta is Killing and rho n=partial_theta. It is not an example premise.

items.title: Counterexample: simultaneity is relative to the observer vector
items.statement: Statement refuted: 'the simultaneity relation eta(n,q-p) = 0 between events of the affine model is independent of the future unit timelike vector n.' Counterexample: in an inertial chart let p := x^{-1}(0,0,0,0) and q := x^{-1}(0,1,0,0), so d := q - p is spacelike with eta(d,d) = 1, and let n := e_0 = (1,0,0,0) and n' := gamma(e_0 + (3/5)e_1) = (5/4)(1,3/5,0,0), a boost of speed 3c/5 along the first axis; n' is future unit because eta(n',n') = (25/16)(-1 + 9/25) = -1. Then eta(n,d) = 0, so p and q are simultaneous relative to n and lie in the slice H(p,n), while eta(n',d) = (5/4)(3/5) = 3/4 is nonzero, so p and q are not simultaneous relative to n' and lie in different slices for n'. The two slices H(p,n) and H(p,n') are distinct three-dimensional affine hyperplanes through p. Hence simultaneity in the sense of def-sr-simultaneity-slice-and-rest-distance depends on the observer vector, so it is not an observer-independent relation.
items.strategy: Exact rational evaluation of eta on the displayed vectors; both n and n' are verified future unit by the diagonal form, and the two pairings with d are computed exactly (0 and 3/4). The slices are distinct because their direction subspaces n^perp and n'^perp differ (the already displayed d=e_1 lies in e_0^perp since eta(e_0,e_1)=0, but not in n'^perp since eta(n',e_1)=3/4).

items.title: Worked Fermi-Walker transport along uniformly accelerated hyperbolic motion
items.statement: Worked computation. In an inertial chart with metric diag(-1,1,1,1) let alpha > 0 and consider the worldline x(tau) = (c^2/alpha)(sinh(alpha tau/c), cosh(alpha tau/c), 0, 0) parametrized by proper time tau. Write theta := alpha tau/c. (a) U := x' = c(cosh theta, sinh theta, 0, 0) satisfies eta(U,U) = c^2(-cosh^2 theta + sinh^2 theta) = -c^2, and A := U' = alpha(sinh theta, cosh theta, 0, 0) satisfies eta(A,A) = alpha^2 and eta(U,A) = 0. (b) Put X_0 := U/c = (cosh theta, sinh theta, 0, 0) and X_1 := (sinh theta, cosh theta, 0, 0); then eta(X_0,X_0) = -1, eta(X_0,X_1) = 0 and eta(X_1,X_1) = 1, so (X_0,X_1) is an orthonormal pair. (c) X_0' = (alpha/c)(sinh,cosh) = A/c, and the Fermi-Walker right-hand side for X_0 is (1/c^2)(eta(A,X_0)U - eta(U,X_0)A) = (1/c^2)(0 - (-c)A) = A/c, because eta(A,X_0) = alpha(-sinh cosh + cosh sinh) = 0 and eta(U,X_0) = c eta(X_0,X_0) = -c; hence X_0 is Fermi-Walker transported. (d) X_1' = (alpha/c)(cosh,sinh) = (alpha/c)X_0, and the Fermi-Walker right-hand side for X_1 is (1/c^2)(eta(A,X_1)U - eta(U,X_1)A) = (1/c^2)(alpha U - 0) = (alpha/c)X_0, because eta(A,X_1) = alpha(-sinh^2 theta + cosh^2 theta) = alpha and eta(U,X_1) = c(-cosh sinh + sinh cosh) = 0; hence X_1 is also Fermi-Walker transported. (e) X_1 is not parallel transported: X_1' = (alpha/c)X_0 is nonzero for alpha > 0, so Fermi-Walker transport differs from parallel transport for accelerated motion (they coincide exactly when A = 0). (f) The norm eta(X_1,X_1) = 1 is constant along the worldline, an instance of the preservation clause of thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples; adding the constant fields partial_y and partial_z gives a Fermi-Walker transported orthonormal tetrad (U/c, X_1, partial_y, partial_z) along the hyperbolic worldline.
items.strategy: Exact symbolic computation: differentiate x, U and X_0, X_1; evaluate the diagonal form on all displayed vectors; compare X_0' and X_1' with the two Fermi-Walker right-hand sides. Every step is finite algebra in the hyperbolic functions, using cosh^2 - sinh^2 = 1.

items.title: Inertial and piecewise inertial worldlines of the affine Minkowski model
items.statement: Let (A,V,eta,C^+) be an oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space (def-sr-affine-minkowski-model), let I be an order-convex subset of R with at least two elements (def-interval), and let curves x: I -> A and their derivatives be as in def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline. (a) Inertial worldline. A curve x: I -> A is inertial (also called uniform or straight) when there are a parameter value s_0 in I, an event p in A and a vector d in V, with d future timelike, such that x(s) = p + (s - s_0) d for every s in I. Then x is a future timelike worldline whose tangent is the constant vector d at every parameter value (the derivative is read in the coordinate calculus of def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral in any inertial chart, as in def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline (a)), the image x[I] is the set of events p + lambda d with lambda = s - s_0 for s in I, and every restriction of x to a subinterval is inertial. If two inertial worldlines have the same image and the same direction of traversal, then each is an increasing affine reparametrization of the other: with x(s) = p + (s - s_0) d and y(t) = p' + (t - t_0) d' one has d' = alpha d with alpha > 0 and p' = p + mu d, hence y(t) = x(s_0 + mu + alpha(t - t_0)). (b) Piecewise inertial worldline. Let a < b be real numbers with [a,b] contained in I. A curve x: [a,b] -> A is piecewise inertial when there are a finite partition a = s_0 < s_1 < ... < s_m = b, events p_1,...,p_m in A and future timelike vectors d_1,...,d_m in V such that x(s) = p_i + (s - s_{i-1}) d_i for every s in [s_{i-1}, s_i] and every i = 1,...,m, and consecutive pieces agree at the partition points, that is p_{i+1} = p_i + (s_i - s_{i-1}) d_i = x(s_i) for i = 1,...,m-1. Then x is a piecewise C^1 future timelike worldline on [a,b] in the sense of def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline, the tangent on the open piece (s_{i-1},s_i) is the constant d_i, the one-sided tangents at the interior partition point s_i are d_i (from the left) and d_{i+1} (from the right), and x is C^1 on [a,b] if and only if d_1 = d_2 = ... = d_m; the events x(s_i) with 0 < i < m are the corners of the itinerary, and the itinerary is called a two-leg itinerary when m = 2. The definition asserts the existence of no further worldlines and attaches no clock reading to the curves; readings are the subject of the model's postulates.
items.strategy: A definition item: it fixes the model's inertial and piecewise inertial vocabulary and makes no proof claim beyond well-definedness. Obligations: (i) the affine formula x(s) = p + (s - s_0) d is a well-defined map I -> A because the affine action of def-affine-space-and-displacement is defined for every real parameter and every vector; (ii) its derivative is the constant d: in the chart x_A of an inertial frame the coordinate path is the affine function s |-> x_A(p) + (s - s_0) E^{-1}(d), whose difference quotients are the constant E^{-1}(d) (def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral, thm-unique-coordinates-with-respect-to-an-ordered-basis), so x'(s) = d by def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline (a); the same computation gives C^k regularity for every k; (iii) future timelikeness of the constant tangent is part of the hypothesis, so x is a worldline and not merely a curve; (iv) in (b) the joining condition makes the piecewise formulas define one function on [a,b], and the one-sided derivatives at the corners exist by the two constant formulas; the equivalence with C^1 is immediate because the derivative is constant on each open piece; (v) clause (c) records the interface with the proper-time and endpoint-bound items of this pair. No choice principle is used: the objects are finitely parametrized and every operation is finite-dimensional.

items.title: The reversed Cauchy-Schwarz inequality for future timelike vectors
items.statement: Let (A,V,eta,C^+) be the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space and let v,w in V be future timelike vectors. Put a := sqrt(-eta(v,v)) > 0 and b := sqrt(-eta(w,w)) > 0, the timelike lengths of v and w. Then: (i) -eta(v,w) >= a b > 0; (ii) equality -eta(v,w) = a b holds if and only if v and w are positive proportional, that is w = t v for some real t > 0 or v = t w for some real t > 0; (iii) consequently -eta(v,w) > a b whenever v and w are not positive proportional, and eta(v,w) < 0 in every case; (iv) for two past timelike vectors v,w the same inequality -eta(v,w) >= sqrt(-eta(v,v)) sqrt(-eta(w,w)) holds, with equality if and only if they are positive proportional, because -v and -w are future timelike and eta(-v,-w) = eta(v,w). The statement uses only eta and the future cone C^+ and involves no chart, frame or choice principle.
items.strategy: Proof strategy, in an arbitrary inertial frame. Fix an inertial frame (o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3) (lem-future-oriented-inertial-frames-exist, def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart) and write v = v^0 e_0 + v_s, w = w^0 e_0 + w_s with v_s,w_s in the spatial three-space S. Future timelikeness of v and w is, in these coordinates, v^0 > |v_s| and w^0 > |w_s| (lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components, whose coordinate description applies because e_0 is future). Bilinearity gives -eta(v,w) = v^0 w^0 - delta(v_s,w_s) where delta is the Euclidean form on S (def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame), and the finite Cauchy-Schwarz inequality (thm-cauchy-schwarz-finite) gives delta(v_s,w_s) <= |v_s| |w_s|, so -eta(v,w) >= v^0 w^0 - |v_s| |w_s|. The algebraic identity (v^0 w^0 - |v_s||w_s|)^2 - ((v^0)^2 - |v_s|^2)((w^0)^2 - |w_s|^2) = (v^0 |w_s| - w^0 |v_s|)^2, together with a = sqrt((v^0)^2 - |v_s|^2) and b = sqrt((w^0)^2 - |w_s|^2) (def-rational-power, thm-of-square-roots), shows that v^0 w^0 - |v_s| |w_s| is a nonnegative real whose square dominates (ab)^2; monotonicity of squaring on the nonnegatives (lem-of-square-monotone) gives (i). For (ii), equality in the two-step estimate forces both delta(v_s,w_s) = |v_s||w_s| and v^0 |w_s| = w^0 |v_s|. The equality case of the finite Cauchy-Schwarz inequality (thm-cauchy-schwarz-finite) makes v_s and w_s nonnegatively proportional; if one of them is 0 then the second equality forces the other to be 0 as well and v,w are positive multiples of e_0; otherwise v_s = t w_s with t > 0 and v^0 |w_s| = w^0 t |w_s| gives v^0 = t w^0, hence v = t w. The converse is a direct substitution: eta(t w, w) = t eta(w,w) gives -eta(t w,w) = t b^2 = (t b) b. Clause (iv) applies (i)-(ii) to -v,-w, using that the negative of a past timelike vector is future timelike (def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets). No step uses the Axiom of Choice: the frame is finite-dimensional and the only inequality is the finite-sum Cauchy-Schwarz theorem.

items.title: The reversed triangle inequality and convexity of the future timelike cone
items.statement: Let (A,V,eta,C^+) be the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space. (a) Sum of two future timelike vectors. If v,w in V are future timelike then v + w is future timelike and sqrt(-eta(v+w,v+w)) >= sqrt(-eta(v,v)) + sqrt(-eta(w,w)), with equality if and only if v and w are positive proportional. (b) Convexity and concavity along segments. If v,w are future timelike then t v + (1-t) w is future timelike for every real t in [0,1], so the future timelike set is convex; moreover sqrt(-eta(t v + (1-t) w, t v + (1-t) w)) >= t sqrt(-eta(v,v)) + (1-t) sqrt(-eta(w,w)) for every t in [0,1], with equality for 0 < t < 1 if and only if v and w are positive proportional. (c) Nonempty finite sums. Let k>=1. If v_1,...,v_k are future timelike then v_1 + ... + v_k is future timelike and sqrt(-eta(sum_i v_i, sum_i v_i)) >= sum_i sqrt(-eta(v_i,v_i)), with equality if and only if all v_i are positive multiples of one single future timelike vector. The inequalities are those of the model's eta and are independent of any chart; they are the reversed (Lorentzian) forms of the triangle inequality of the spatial Euclidean structure. The separate k=0 convention gives the empty sum0, whose Lorentz length is0 and which belongs to the closed future cone but is not timelike; no positive-ray equality characterization or timelike assertion is applied to that empty case.
items.strategy: Proof from lem-sr-reverse-cauchy-schwarz-for-future-timelike-vectors and the coordinate description of the cone. (a) Future direction and timelikeness: in an inertial frame write v = (v^0,v_s), w = (w^0,w_s); the coordinate description of the future cone (lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components) gives v^0 > |v_s| and w^0 > |w_s|, so (v+w)^0 = v^0 + w^0 > |v_s| + |w_s| >= |v_s + w_s| by the triangle inequality for the Euclidean norm (cor-triangle-inequality-for-inner-product-norm), which is exactly the coordinate description of future timelikeness for v + w. Inequality: sqrt(-eta(v+w,v+w))^2 = -eta(v,v) - 2 eta(v,w) - eta(w,w) = a^2 + b^2 + 2(-eta(v,w)) with a := sqrt(-eta(v,v)), b := sqrt(-eta(w,w)); by the reverse Cauchy-Schwarz inequality -eta(v,w) >= ab, so the square is at least (a+b)^2, and monotonicity of squaring on the nonnegatives (lem-of-square-monotone, thm-of-square-roots) gives the claim. Equality requires -eta(v,w) = ab, which by clause (ii) of the reverse Cauchy-Schwarz lemma is exactly positive proportionality. (b) For 0 <= t <= 1 the vector t v is future timelike when t > 0 (its coordinates are (t v^0, t v_s) with t v^0 > t|v_s| = |t v_s|) and 0 when t = 0; applying (a) to the two future timelike vectors t v and (1-t) w (with the zero vector case handled directly) gives both the membership and the inequality, and the equality statement reduces to the equality case of (a) applied to those two vectors, which are positive proportional exactly when v and w are. (c) For k=1 the sum is the given future timelike vector and equality is immediate. Induct from this nonempty base using(a) and thm-induction-principle; the equality case is the conjunction of the equality conditions at each step, which forces all vectors onto one positive ray. All arguments are finite-dimensional and no choice principle is used.

items.title: Existence of an inertial frame whose time axis is a prescribed future timelike direction
items.statement: Let (A,V,eta,C^+) be the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space, let d in V be a future timelike displacement and put T := sqrt(-eta(d,d)) > 0 and n := d/T. Then: (i) eta(n,n) = -1 and n is future timelike, so n is a future unit timelike vector; (ii) for every event o there is an inertial frame (o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3) of the model with e_0 = n; (iii) for the inertial chart x of any such frame one has x(o + lambda d) = (lambda T, 0, 0, 0) for every real lambda; in particular x(o) = 0 and x(o + d) = (T, 0, 0, 0). Consequently, for any two events p,q with q - p = d, the chart of such a frame represents the displacement q - p by the coordinate vector (T,0,0,0): the spatial coordinates of p and q agree and their time coordinates differ by T.
items.strategy: Proof. (i) Bilinearity gives eta(n,n) = eta(d,d)/T^2 = -1 (def-lorentz-form-and-inertia, def-rational-power), and n is future timelike directly from the coordinate cone criterion of lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components: d^0>|d_s| and 1/T>0 give d^0/T>|d_s|/T=|d_s/T|. This is positive homogeneity, not a deduction of arbitrary positive scaling from convex combinations. (ii) Fix any inertial frame with origin o, with basis (f_0,f_1,f_2,f_3) (lem-future-oriented-inertial-frames-exist). Let (n^0, n_s) be the coordinates of n in this frame. Since n is future timelike, the coordinate description of the future cone (lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components) gives n^0 > |n_s| >= 0, and eta(n,n) = -(n^0)^2 + |n_s|^2 = -1 gives (n^0)^2 = 1 + |n_s|^2 > 0, so the boost parameter beta := n_s/n^0 (a vector of R^3) satisfies |beta| = |n_s|/n^0 < 1 (def-lorentz-boost). Let B := B(beta) be the passive boost of the frame. By lem-boost-is-proper-orthochronous-with-inverse (iv), B n = f_0; by the same lemma (i) and (iii), B is a proper orthochronous Lorentz map with inverse B^{-1} = B(-beta). Define the ordered basis e_0 := n and e_i := B^{-1} f_i for i = 1,2,3; then it is the image under the Lorentz map B^{-1} of the eta-orthonormal basis (f_0,f_1,f_2,f_3) with B^{-1} f_0 = n = e_0, so it is eta-orthonormal with eta(e_0,e_0) = -1 and eta(e_0,e_i) = 0 (lem-lorentz-map-preserves-metric-and-causal-structure (i),(iii)); its first vector is future, and it is positively oriented because B^{-1} is proper, hence preserves the oriented volume form and the orientation class (lem-lorentz-map-preserves-metric-and-causal-structure (iii)). Therefore (o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3) is an inertial frame with first vector n (def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart). (iii) For its chart x(p) = E^{-1}(p - o) with E(u) = sum_a u^a e_a one has E(1,0,0,0) = e_0 = n, hence x(o + lambda d) = E^{-1}(lambda d) = lambda T E^{-1}(n) = lambda T (1,0,0,0), and x(o) = 0. No choice principle is used: the construction uses one finite-dimensional basis and the explicit boost of def-lorentz-boost.

items.title: The displacement of a future timelike worldline is future timelike
items.statement: Let c > 0 and let x: [a,b] -> A be a future timelike worldline with a < b that is piecewise C^1 with partition a = s_0 < s_1 < ... < s_m = b in the weak sense of def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline, with future timelike interior and finite one-sided quotient tangents. Put p := x(a), q := x(b) and d := q - p. Then d is future timelike. More precisely, writing xi^a := x_A^a o x for the coordinate path of the chart x_A of any inertial frame, xi^0(b) - xi^0(a) > 0 and |xi_vec(b) - xi_vec(a)| < xi^0(b) - xi^0(a), where |.| is the Euclidean spatial norm of def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame. Consequently p is not equal to q, the number sqrt(-eta(d,d)) is a positive real number, and in every inertial chart the time component of d is positive and dominates the Euclidean norm of its spatial part, which is exactly the coordinate description of future timelikeness in that chart. No completeness, compactness beyond the given compact interval, or choice principle is used.
items.strategy: Apply lem-sr-weak-piecewise-causal-integrability in an arbitrary inertial chart xi=(xi0,xi_vec). Finite one-sided quotient derivatives give continuity at the corners; on every compact interior truncation each derivative is continuous and the ordinary FTC applies. The lemma proves absolute improper integrability and the exact finite telescoping endpoint increments. Since every interior tangent is future timelike, xi0'-|xi_vec'|>0 throughout each open piece. It is continuous and positive on a compact interior neighborhood, giving a positive integral there; the rest contributes nonnegatively. The improper vector norm inequality proved by truncation gives |xi_vec(b)-xi_vec(a)|<=sum_i integral |xi_vec'|<sum_i integral xi0'=xi0(b)-xi0(a). Therefore the displacement is future timelike and nonzero in the arbitrary frame, its Lorentz norm gives a strictly positive square root, and all claimed coordinate inequalities follow. No continuous extension of the derivative, closed-piece Riemann integrability, or (H) is used; the former (H) cases remain included.

items.title: The endpoint bound for proper time and the maximality of the straight worldline in affine Minkowski space
items.statement: Let c > 0 and let x: [a,b] -> A be a future timelike worldline with a < b that is piecewise C^1 with partition a = s_0 < s_1 < ... < s_m = b in the weak sense of def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline, with total proper time Delta tau(x) of def-sr-piecewise-proper-time. Put p := x(a), q := x(b) and T := sqrt(-eta(q-p,q-p)), a positive real number (lem-sr-endpoint-displacement-of-a-future-timelike-worldline). Then: (i) Endpoint bound: c Delta tau(x) <= T. (ii) Equality case: c Delta tau(x) = T if and only if x is a strictly increasing reparametrization of the straight segment from p to q, that is: there is a continuous strictly increasing surjection sigma: [a,b] -> [0,1] with sigma(a) = 0 and sigma(b) = 1, C^1 on every open piece of a finite weak piecewise partition of [a,b], with sigma'(s) > 0 at every point of each open piece and finite positive one-sided difference-quotient derivatives at both endpoints of every piece, without any requirement that sigma' extend continuously there, such that x(s) = p + sigma(s)(q - p) for every s in [a,b]; equivalently x'(s) is a positive multiple of q - p at every point at which x is differentiable. (iii) Strictness: if the image of x is not contained in the straight segment {p + lambda(q-p) : 0 <= lambda <= 1}, then c Delta tau(x) < T; in particular, if x is piecewise inertial and its piece tangents d_1,...,d_m are not all positive multiples of one another (equivalently, its image is not contained in the straight segment), then the inequality is strict, while a piecewise inertial itinerary whose piece tangents are all positive multiples of one another has the straight segment as image and attains the bound. (iv) Straight worldlines attain the bound: for the inertial worldline x_s(s) := p + ((s-a)/(b-a))(q-p) one has c Delta tau(x_s) = T, in agreement with the straight-segment value of def-sr-proper-time; more generally every worldline whose image is the straight segment and which is traversed in the future direction attains the bound. (v) Scope: the theorem concerns the affine Minkowski model with a fixed positive constant c; it is a statement about the weak piecewise C^1 future timelike class, including the ordinary Riemann special case (H), it does not identify proper time with any clock reading, and it asserts nothing about maximality of geodesics in curved spacetimes or in Lorentzian manifolds with different global structure.
items.strategy: By lem-sr-endpoint-displacement-of-a-future-timelike-worldline, d=q-p is future timelike and T=sqrt(-eta(d,d))>0. Choose the rest inertial frame with e0=d/T by lem-sr-rest-frame-of-a-future-timelike-displacement; the coordinate endpoint increment is (T,0,0,0). On each open piece xi=(xi0,z) has xi0'>|z'|. Put f=sqrt((xi0')^2-|z'|^2) and h=xi0'-f>=0. The integrability lemma gives finite improper integrals of xi0', f and h, the exact coordinate endpoint increment, and subdivision additivity. Hence c Delta tau=sum_i integral f<=sum_i integral xi0'=T. For equality the finite nonnegative sum of integrals h is zero, so every such integral is zero. If h were positive anywhere in an open piece, continuity would give a compact interior neighborhood of positive integral, contradiction. Therefore z'=0 inside every piece. The zero-derivative theorem and continuity at the corners make z constant throughout, while xi0'>0 implies strict time increase. Set sigma(s)=(xi0(s)-xi0(a))/T. Then sigma is continuous, strictly increasing, onto [0,1], C1 with positive derivative on every open piece, and has finite positive one-sided quotient derivatives at the corners because x does and those tangents now lie along d. This gives x=p+sigma d. Conversely that displayed weak parametrization has density T sigma' and the integrability lemma gives sum_i integral sigma'=sigma(b)-sigma(a)=1, attaining T. This proves (i)-(ii). Clause (iii) follows because a history outside the straight segment fails the equality case; for piecewise inertial histories the constant tangents are all positive multiples exactly when all legs have the same future line, and then the image is the full endpoint segment. Clause (iv) is the constant derivative d/(b-a) calculation or the equality case with affine sigma. Clause (v) preserves purely affine mathematical scope and all prior (H) special cases; no clock reading, curved-spacetime maximality or choice principle is introduced.

items.title: Same-endpoint clock comparison: the inertial clock is slowest to age
items.statement: Adopt as physical assumptions the postulates post-sr-inertial-covariance, post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light and post-sr-free-trajectories-and-clock-hypothesis, and let c and the SI conventions be those of def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions. Let p and q be events with q - p future timelike, put T := sqrt(-eta(q-p,q-p)) > 0, and let x_s: [a,b] -> A be the straight (inertial) future timelike worldline from p to q, x_s(s) := p + ((s-a)/(b-a))(q-p). Let x: [a,b] -> A be a piecewise C^1 future timelike worldline from p to q in the weak sense of def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline, with total proper time Delta tau(x) defined by def-sr-piecewise-proper-time. Then, as conditional statements about ideal clocks of the adopted model and not about any actual apparatus: (i) an ideal clock carried along x_s from p to q reads between the parameter values a and b the time c^{-1} T; (ii) an ideal clock carried along x from p to q reads Delta tau(x), and Delta tau(x) <= c^{-1} T, with equality if and only if x is a strictly increasing reparametrization of the straight segment from p to q in the sense of thm-sr-endpoint-proper-time-bound-and-flat-maximum (ii); (iii) if x is piecewise inertial (def-sr-inertial-and-piecewise-inertial-worldline) and its image is not contained in the straight segment from p to q, then Delta tau(x) < c^{-1} T strictly, so among ideal clocks carried between the same two events along future timelike piecewise C^1 histories of the weak class of def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline (including its ordinary Riemann special case (H)) the straight inertial clock records the largest reading, and every history whose image is not the straight segment records a strictly smaller one; (iv) the two numbers Delta tau(x) and c^{-1} T are determined by the parametrized histories and the model's conversion constant alone: the integrand sqrt(-eta(x',x')) of def-sr-piecewise-proper-time involves no chart, so the comparison is a definite pair of clock readings attached to the same pair of endpoint events and involves no simultaneity convention. Scope and qualification: the statement inherits the idealizations of its postulates (ideal pointlike clocks with no acceleration-dependent reading term, prescribed histories, flat classical spacetime, the fixed conversion constant c); it asserts no measurement outcome, contains no statistical inference, and carries no claim that real clocks or the physical world are exactly described by the model. The conclusion is conditional on the named postulates and does not follow from the geometry alone.
items.strategy: Conditional deduction from the adopted postulates; the mathematical engine is the weak-class thm-sr-endpoint-proper-time-bound-and-flat-maximum, whose endpoint FTC and equality argument use the local causal integrability supplier. All former (H) histories remain included. (i) The straight history has constant tangent (q-p)/(b-a), so its proper-time function has the constant rate c^{-1} T/(b-a) (def-sr-proper-time straight-segment value) and the clock hypothesis of post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light identifies the reading with that integral, giving c^{-1} T. (ii) For a piecewise C^1 history with finitely many kinks the reading is the total proper time of def-sr-piecewise-proper-time (post-sr-free-trajectories-and-clock-hypothesis (ii) states the clock hypothesis for exactly this class, referring to the piecewise integral, and post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light fixes the reading for smooth restrictions and the extended clock formulation identifies the finite improper-piece sum); the bound, equality case and strictness are clauses (i)-(iii) of thm-sr-endpoint-proper-time-bound-and-flat-maximum. (iii) A piecewise inertial itinerary with pieces not all in one direction has an image that is not contained in the straight segment from p to q: the image of a straight segment is a straight set, while the itinerary contains its corner event, which is an event of a piece's line not on the other piece's line; hence the strict case of the theorem applies. (iv) The proper-time integrand is built from eta and the tangent alone, so no chart enters either number. Scope obligations: repeat the idealizations and the conditionality in the conclusion; do not upgrade the conditional statement to a claim about real clocks, and do not attach any empirical or statistical content; no experiment is cited and none can strengthen the deduction. No choice principle beyond the published suppliers is used.

items.title: The piecewise inertial twin reunion: conditional differential aging
items.statement: Thought experiment: the piecewise inertial twin reunion of the adopted model, with its conditional conclusion. Adopt post-sr-inertial-covariance, post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light and post-sr-free-trajectories-and-clock-hypothesis, and let c and the SI conventions be those of def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions. Fix an inertial frame (o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3) with chart x, a duration T > 0 in seconds and a speed v with 0 < |v| < c; put gamma := (1 - v^2/c^2)^{-1/2}. Define two histories (coordinate time t in seconds, space and time coordinates in metres with x^0 = c t): (stay-at-home) x_stay(t) := x^{-1}(c t, 0, 0, 0) for t in [0, 2T]; (traveler) x_travel(t) := x^{-1}(c t, v t, 0, 0) for t in [0, T] and x_travel(t) := x^{-1}(c t, v(2T - t), 0, 0) for t in [T, 2T]. Then: (i) x_stay is the inertial future timelike worldline from p := x^{-1}(0,0,0,0) to q := x^{-1}(2cT,0,0,0), and x_travel is a piecewise inertial future timelike worldline from p to q whose two pieces have the constant tangents (c, v, 0, 0) and (c, -v, 0, 0), with the corner r := x^{-1}(cT, vT, 0, 0); the image of x_travel contains the three events p, r, q, which are not collinear in the affine model, so the image of x_travel is not contained in the straight segment from p to q. (ii) Conditional on the postulates, an ideal clock carried from p to q along x_stay reads 2T, while an ideal clock carried from p to q along x_travel reads 2T/gamma = 2T sqrt(1 - v^2/c^2); hence at the reunion event q the traveling clock is behind the stay-at-home clock by 2T(1 - 1/gamma) = 2T(1 - sqrt(1 - v^2/c^2)) > 0. (iii) The conclusion is a comparison of two clock readings at the common events p and q; it does not depend on a simultaneity convention or on the inertial frame used to describe the histories, because both readings are proper-time integrals of the two histories. (iv) Scope and idealization: the scenario is a conditional model statement; the instantaneous turn at r idealizes a turnaround of finite duration, the clocks are ideal with no acceleration-dependent reading term, spacetime is flat, and no gravitational, quantum, apparatus or statistical effect is modeled; no measurement is reported. The conclusion is conditional on the adopted postulates and does not assert that nature is exactly described by the model.
items.strategy: Conditional deduction with the two explicit histories as witnesses. Step (i): differentiate the coordinate formulas; the coordinate derivatives are (c,0,0,0), (c,v,0,0) and (c,-v,0,0) respectively; each has -eta equal to c^2, c^2 - v^2, c^2 - v^2, all positive, and positive time component, so each piece is future timelike (def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors, def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets, def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart); hence x_stay is inertial and x_travel is piecewise inertial in the sense of def-sr-inertial-and-piecewise-inertial-worldline with corner r, and both are worldlines through p and q. Non-collinearity: p, r, q have coordinate vectors (0,0,0,0), (cT,vT,0,0), (2cT,0,0,0); since vT is nonzero, r is not on the affine line through p and q (whose second coordinate is 0), so the three are not collinear and the image of x_travel is not contained in the straight segment (an affine line maps to an affine line under the chart, so collinearity is exactly collinearity of the coordinate vectors). Step (ii): the straight history has displacement q - p with coordinates (2cT,0,0,0) and -eta(q-p,q-p) = 4c^2T^2, so its reading is c^{-1} 2cT = 2T (def-sr-proper-time straight-segment value and the clock hypothesis of post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light); each leg of x_travel has a constant tangent with -eta = c^2(1 - v^2/c^2) = c^2/gamma^2, so its proper time is T/gamma by the same straight-segment value applied to the leg restricted to its closed parameter interval, and the two-leg total is 2T/gamma by the constant-tangent special case (v) and concatenation additivity (vi) of the extended def-sr-piecewise-proper-time. Constant leg derivatives satisfy (H), so these improper values are the same ordinary Riemann values; the clock hypothesis of post-sr-free-trajectories-and-clock-hypothesis (ii) identifies the reading with this total proper time. The comparison 2T/gamma < 2T for v nonzero is the strict case of pthm-sr-same-endpoint-clock-comparison (iii), whose equality case is excluded by the non-collinearity of step (i); it can also be read off directly since 0 < 1 - 1/gamma. Step (iii): both readings are given by proper-time integrals built from eta and the tangents alone, so no chart or simultaneity convention enters; the events p and q are common to the two histories. Step (iv): record the idealizations and the conditionality; do not infer any measured outcome, and do not upgrade the statement to a claim about real clocks.

items.title: Acceleration is not an aging term, and the twin comparison is not symmetric: scope caveats
items.statement: Scope and interpretation caveats for the proper-time comparison of the twin reunion (texp-sr-piecewise-inertial-twin-reunion) in the adopted model. (1) Acceleration is not an additional aging term. In the model the reading of an ideal clock between two events of its history is the proper-time integral of its worldline (post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light (i), post-sr-free-trajectories-and-clock-hypothesis (ii)); no term depending on the four-acceleration or any higher derivative of the history appears, and the clock hypothesis is precisely the exclusion of such terms. The corner of the piecewise inertial history is an idealization: a physical turnaround occupies a finite parameter interval, the worldline is then C^1 or smooth there, and its proper time is still the integral; the endpoint bound thm-sr-endpoint-proper-time-bound-and-flat-maximum still gives the comparison with the stay-at-home clock, and the strict inequality remains because such a smoothed itinerary still does not have the image of the straight segment. (2) The two histories are not symmetric in the model. One is the straight segment from p to q; the other contains the corner event r of texp-sr-piecewise-inertial-twin-reunion, and the three events p, r, q are not collinear. Every change of inertial chart is an affine bijection (lem-inertial-chart-transitions-are-affine-lorentz) and maps collinear triples to collinear triples; so no change of inertial frame maps the image of x_stay onto the image of x_travel or fixes both endpoints and exchanges the histories. The two twins are therefore not related by an inertial change of description, and the difference of readings is a model consequence of the different histories, not a consequence of who is 'really moving'. (3) The synchronization bookkeeping. In each momentary inertial rest frame of the traveler the stay-at-home clock runs slow by the factor 1/gamma, and the traveler may legitimately apply the time-dilation relation between events that are simultaneous in that momentary frame (lem-sr-boost-time-length-and-velocity-formulas (i), def-sr-simultaneity-slice-and-rest-distance). But the two legs use different inertial frames: the outbound rest frame's simultaneity slice through the turn event r meets the stay-at-home worldline at the event with coordinate time t = T(1 - v^2/c^2) = T/gamma^2, while the inbound rest frame's slice through r meets it at t = T(1 + v^2/c^2); the two slices differ by 2Tv^2/c^2 in coordinate time, and inserting this gap reconciles the traveler's two leg-by-leg accounts of the stay-at-home clock with its total reading 2T at the reunion. The naive reciprocity statement 'each twin judges the other's clock to run slow' therefore compares different pairs of events for the two travelers (events simultaneous in different frames) and does not apply to the reunion comparison, which concerns the two clock readings at the single common event q. (4) Empirical qualification. All of (1)-(3) are conditional statements about ideal clocks in the adopted model; no measurement, apparatus, calibration, sampling or uncertainty model is involved, and no claim is made about real clocks or about nature. Real clock comparisons would additionally require apparatus and uncertainty analysis and are outside this remark.
items.strategy: A remark: it delimits the scope and interpretation of the pair's conditional results and supplies no proof obligations. Obligations of precision: (1) records that the model's reading rule has no acceleration term (the cited postulate clauses), that the corner is an idealization, and that the endpoint bound survives the smoothing of the corner; (2) verifies the asymmetry claim with the chart-transition supplier: inertial chart transitions are affine (lem-inertial-chart-transitions-are-affine-lorentz), affine maps send collinear triples to collinear triples, and p, r, q are not collinear by the coordinate computation of the thought experiment, so no affine transition takes one image onto the other; (3) computes the two simultaneity slices with the boost formula of lem-sr-boost-time-length-and-velocity-formulas inside the notation of the thought experiment: the outbound chart x' with x'^0 = gamma(x^0 - (v/c)x^1) assigns to the turn event r the time coordinate gamma cT(1 - v^2/c^2), so its slice x'^0 = const meets the stay-at-home worldline x^1 = 0 at x^0 = cT(1 - v^2/c^2), and the inbound chart x'' with x''^0 = gamma(x^0 + (v/c)x^1) gives x^0 = cT(1 + v^2/c^2); both events are on the stay-at-home worldline whose clock reads coordinate time, so the two assignments differ by 2Tv^2/c^2; the reconciliation arithmetic is 2T = T(1 - v^2/c^2) + 2Tv^2/c^2 + T(1 - v^2/c^2) = 2T/gamma^2 + 2T(1 - 1/gamma^2); (4) restates the absence of empirical content. The remark cites only quantified suppliers for its numerical claims and marks every statement about real apparatus as outside the model. The broadened endpoint bound still applies to every stated smooth or piecewise inertial turnaround; the existing clock assumptions, simultaneity numbers and empirical exclusions are unchanged. The proper-time reference now resolves to the earlier weak-piecewise definition, with constant-tangent legs as its (H) special case.

items.title: Worked reverse Cauchy-Schwarz and reverse triangle inequalities
items.statement: Worked computation in an inertial frame with eta = diag(-1,1,1,1). (a) For v := (5,3,0,0) and w := (5,-3,0,0): eta(v,v) = -25 + 9 = -16 and eta(w,w) = -16, so the timelike lengths are sqrt(16) = 4; eta(v,w) = -25 - 9 = -34, so -eta(v,w) = 34 >= 4*4 = 16, and the inequality is strict because v and w are not proportional. (b) For w' := 2v = (10,6,0,0): eta(w',w') = -100 + 36 = -64, sqrt(-eta(w',w')) = 8, eta(v,w') = -50 + 18 = -32 (twice eta(v,v) = -16), and -eta(v,w') = 32 = 4*8, the equality case of the reverse Cauchy-Schwarz inequality for the positive proportional pair (v, 2v). (c) Reverse triangle: v + w = (10,0,0,0) has -eta(v+w,v+w) = 100, so sqrt = 10 >= 4 + 4 = 8, again strict since v and w are not proportional. For u := (5,0,0,0), of timelike length 5, one has -eta(v,u) = 25 >= 4*5 = 20 and v + u = (10,3,0,0) with sqrt(-eta(v+u,v+u)) = sqrt(100-9) = sqrt(91) >= 4 + 5 = 9. (d) The two vectors v and w are both future timelike (5 > 3 and 5 > 3 in the first coordinate), so all inequalities are instances of the future timelike hypotheses.
items.strategy: Every line is a finite evaluation of the displayed diagonal form: squares of the coordinate entries, the diagonal metric, and a comparison of exact integers or of the square root of 91 with 9 (via 91 > 81 and monotonicity of the square root). The equality check evaluates -eta(v,2v) = 8^2 - 4^2 + ... directly: -eta(v,2v) = 2*16 = 32 = 4*8. No limiting, continuity or choice argument occurs.

items.title: Worked two-leg itinerary against the straight clock at speed 3c/5
items.statement: Worked computation in the inertial chart x with metric diag(-1,1,1,1). Let T > 0, let v with 0 < |v| < c and put gamma := (1 - v^2/c^2)^{-1/2}; let p := x^{-1}(0,0,0,0), r := x^{-1}(cT, vT, 0, 0) and q := x^{-1}(2cT, 0, 0, 0). (a) The straight worldline from p to q has displacement d = (2cT,0,0,0), -eta(d,d) = 4c^2T^2 and elapsed proper time c^{-1} 2cT = 2T. (b) The two-leg itinerary p -> r -> q has first leg displacement (cT, vT, 0, 0) with -eta = c^2T^2(1 - v^2/c^2), hence proper time c^{-1} cT sqrt(1 - v^2/c^2) = T/gamma, and second leg displacement (cT, -vT, 0, 0) with the same value; its two-leg total proper time is 2T/gamma. (c) Comparison: 2T/gamma < 2T for every v with 0 < |v| < c, in agreement with the endpoint bound and with its strictness clause, since the image of the two-leg itinerary contains the event r = (cT, vT, 0, 0), not on the straight segment from p to q. Numerical specialization v = 3c/5 (gamma = 5/4): the readings are 8T/5 and 2T, with difference 2T/5. (d) Equality without affine parametrization: on [0,1] let mu(s) := (s^2 + s)/2, a strictly increasing C^1 surjection of [0,1] onto itself with mu'(s) = s + 1/2 > 0; the worldline y(s) := x^{-1}(2cT mu(s), 0, 0, 0) has the straight segment pq as image and elapsed proper time c^{-1} integral_0^1 2cT mu'(s) ds = 2T: equality in the endpoint bound does not require the affine parametrization, only a future-directed strictly increasing one.
items.strategy: Finite computations from the definitions: the displacements are read off the coordinate formulas, -eta is the diagonal quadratic form, and each straight leg's proper time is the straight-segment value of def-sr-proper-time; the two-leg total is the sum of the two leg values by def-sr-piecewise-proper-time (v). The strict comparison uses 1/gamma < 1 and the strictness clause of the endpoint bound. In (d) the tangent is y'(s) = 2cT mu'(s) e_0 with positive coefficient, so the length integrand is 2cT mu'(s) and the integral over [0,1] evaluates to 2cT(mu(1) - mu(0)) = 2cT = 2T after division by c. All numbers are exact rationals in the specialization v = 3c/5.

items.title: Worked simultaneity gap of the traveler's two momentary rest frames at the turn
items.statement: Worked computation in the notation of ex-sr-two-leg-itinerary-versus-straight-clock, specialized to v = 3c/5 and gamma = 5/4; the stay-at-home worldline is x^1 = 0 and its clock reads coordinate time t, and the turn event is r := x^{-1}(cT, 3cT/5, 0, 0). (a) Outbound rest frame: the chart x' of the boost with parameter 3c/5 has x'^0 = (5/4)(x^0 - (3/5)x^1); at r this is (5/4)(cT - 9cT/25) = (5/4)(16cT/25) = 4cT/5, so the slice x'^0 = 4cT/5 through r meets the stay-at-home worldline at (5/4)x^0 = 4cT/5, that is x^0 = 16cT/25, i.e. coordinate time t = 16T/25 = T(1 - 9/25). (b) Inbound rest frame: the chart x'' of the boost with parameter -3c/5 has x''^0 = (5/4)(x^0 + (3/5)x^1); at r this is (5/4)(cT + 9cT/25) = (5/4)(34cT/25) = 17cT/10, so the slice x''^0 = 17cT/10 through r meets the stay-at-home worldline at (5/4)x^0 = 17cT/10, that is x^0 = 34cT/25, i.e. coordinate time t = 34T/25 = T(1 + 9/25). (c) The two momentary frames assign to the stay-at-home clock at 'the time of the turn' the two different readings 16T/25 and 34T/25; their difference is 18T/25 = 2Tv^2/c^2, the simultaneity gap. (d) Reconciliation: the traveler's own clock reads 4T/5 = 20T/25 at the turn and 8T/5 = 40T/25 at the reunion; during each leg his momentary frame assigns to the stay-at-home clock the advance 16T/25 (outbound from 0 to 16T/25, inbound from 34T/25 to 2T = 50T/25), and with the gap 18T/25 the total assignment is 16T/25 + 18T/25 + 16T/25 = 50T/25 = 2T, the stay-at-home reading at the reunion, while the traveler reads 8T/5 = 40T/25; the two readings differ by 2T/5 = 10T/25. (e) The two rest frames are distinct: their relative boost parameter is 2*(3/5)/(1 + 9/25) = 15/17, so the traveler's momentary inertial frame changes at the turn.
items.strategy: Direct substitution into the boost transition formula of lem-sr-boost-time-length-and-velocity-formulas: each slice computation is a linear equation in x^0 along x^1 = 0; the arithmetic is exact with gamma = 5/4 and beta = 3/5. The relative boost parameter of the two frames is the collinear composition of lem-sr-collinear-boost-composition-and-velocity-addition (a boost of 3/5 followed by a boost of -3/5 in the composed description gives 2*(3/5)/(1 + (3/5)^2)). The reconciliation is an addition of the four exact rationals listed. All quantities are evaluations of the model's definitions, not new claims.

items.title: Counterexample: the reversed Cauchy-Schwarz inequality fails outside same-orientation timelike pairs
items.statement: Statement refuted: 'the reversed Cauchy-Schwarz inequality -eta(v,w) >= sqrt(-eta(v,v)) sqrt(-eta(w,w)) holds for every pair of vectors v,w that are individually timelike, regardless of their time orientations, and the analogous reversed form |eta(v,w)| >= sqrt(eta(v,v)) sqrt(eta(w,w)) holds for every pair of spacelike vectors'. First witness: in an inertial frame with eta = diag(-1,1,1,1) let v := (5,3,0,0), future timelike with -eta(v,v) = 16, and w := (-5,3,0,0), past timelike with -eta(w,w) = 16. Then eta(v,w) = 25 + 9 = 34 > 0, so -eta(v,w) = -34, while sqrt(-eta(v,v)) sqrt(-eta(w,w)) = 16; the asserted inequality -34 >= 16 is false. The sum v + w = (0,6,0,0) is spacelike (eta(v+w,v+w) = 36 > 0), so the failure is exactly the failure of the future cone to contain sums of vectors of opposite orientation. Second witness: v := (0,1,0,0) and w := (0,1,1,0) are spacelike with eta(v,v) = 1, eta(w,w) = 2 and eta(v,w) = 1, so |eta(v,w)| = 1 < sqrt(2) = sqrt(eta(v,v)) sqrt(eta(w,w)): the reversed spacelike form fails for a pair whose span contains no null direction. Hence the same-orientation timelike hypothesis of lem-sr-reverse-cauchy-schwarz-for-future-timelike-vectors cannot be dropped, and the spacelike reversed inequality is not universal.
items.strategy: Both witnesses are finite evaluations of the diagonal form: eta(v,w) for the mixed-orientation pair, eta(v+w,v+w), and the spacelike quantities are computed by direct multiplication and addition; the comparisons 34 > 16 and 1 < sqrt(2) are exact (squaring the second). The examples make no claim beyond the failure of the stated universal quantifiers; the positive results are lem-sr-reverse-cauchy-schwarz-for-future-timelike-vectors (same-orientation future timelike pairs) and its past-timelike clause.

items.title: Counterexample: attainment of the endpoint bound does not force the future time orientation
items.statement: Statement refuted: 'if a piecewise C^1 curve x: [alpha,beta] -> A with nonzero timelike tangents from an event p to an event q attains the endpoint bound sqrt(-eta(q-p,q-p)) in the length-integral sense, then its tangents must be future timelike, so that it is a worldline of the model'. Counterexample: in an inertial frame with eta = diag(-1,1,1,1) let d := (5,3,0,0), a future timelike displacement with sqrt(-eta(d,d)) = 4, and put p := x^{-1}(0,0,0,0), q := x^{-1}(-5,-3,0,0) = p - d and x(s) := p - s d for s in [0,1]. Then x(0) = p, x(1) = p - d = q, and x'(s) = -d is past timelike for every s, so x is not a future timelike worldline; but its length integrand is sqrt(-eta(-d,-d)) = sqrt(-eta(d,d)) = 4 and its length integral over [0,1] equals 4, while sqrt(-eta(q-p,q-p)) = sqrt(-eta(-d,-d)) = 4: the bound is attained with equality by a past-directed parametrization. Attainment of the length bound therefore does not force the future time orientation; that orientation is already part of the geometrically selected future-timelike worldline class, while attaching physical clock readings to those histories is a separate adopted interpretation (def-sr-proper-time, def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline). Within the future timelike worldline class the equality case is characterized by thm-sr-endpoint-proper-time-bound-and-flat-maximum (ii).
items.strategy: Direct computation: eta(-d,-d) = eta(d,d) = -16, so the integrand is the constant 4 and the integral over [0,1] is 4; q - p = -d has the same timelike length. The counterexample isolates exactly the quantifier that fails (attainment does not imply future-directedness); it does not contradict the endpoint-bound theorem, which is stated for future timelike worldlines, and it records that the future hypothesis selects the geometric worldline class even though the nonnegative length integrand itself is orientation blind; its physical clock reading is a separate model premise.

items.title: Worked rest frame of the future timelike displacement (5,3,0,0)
items.statement: Worked computation in an inertial frame with eta = diag(-1,1,1,1). Let d := (5,3,0,0), future timelike with -eta(d,d) = 25 - 9 = 16, T := 4 and n := d/T = (5/4,3/4,0,0). (a) n is future unit timelike: eta(n,n) = -25/16 + 9/16 = -1 and n^0 = 5/4 > 3/4 = |n_vec|. (b) The boost parameter beta := n_vec/n^0 = (3/5,0,0) has |beta| = 3/5 < 1 and gamma = 5/4; the passive boost B(beta) of def-lorentz-boost sends n to e_0, as clause (iv) of lem-boost-is-proper-orthochronous-with-inverse requires, since gamma(1, 3/5, 0, 0) = (5/4, 3/4, 0, 0) = n. (c) The basis (e'_0, e'_1, e'_2, e'_3) := (n, B(-beta)e_1, B(-beta)e_2, B(-beta)e_3) has coordinate vectors e'_0 = (5/4,3/4,0,0), e'_1 = (3/4,5/4,0,0), e'_2 = (0,0,1,0), e'_3 = (0,0,0,1); the checks eta(e'_0,e'_0) = -1, eta(e'_1,e'_1) = -9/16 + 25/16 = 1, eta(e'_0,e'_1) = -(5/4)(3/4) + (3/4)(5/4) = 0, eta(e'_2,e'_2) = eta(e'_3,e'_3) = 1 and eta(e'_i,e'_j) = 0 for the remaining pairs show that (o;e'_0,e'_1,e'_2,e'_3) is an inertial frame with first vector n. (d) Its chart x' assigns to d the coordinates (4,0,0,0): d = 4n = 4 e'_0, so E'^{-1}(d) = (4,0,0,0); in particular the two endpoints of any displacement 4n have equal spatial coordinates in x' and time coordinates differing by 4.
items.strategy: Finite computations: the coordinates of B(-beta)e_1 are obtained from the coordinate action of def-lorentz-boost (x''^0 = gamma(x^0 + beta x^1), x''^1 = gamma(x^1 + beta x^0) at (0,1,0,0)), giving (gamma beta, gamma, 0, 0) = (3/4, 5/4, 0, 0); the orthonormality checks are exact rational evaluations of the diagonal form; and the chart value is the definition x'(p) = E'^{-1}(p - o) with E'(1,0,0,0) = e'_0. The example is the concrete instance of lem-sr-rest-frame-of-a-future-timelike-displacement.

items.title: The metric pairing is an isomorphism to the dual, and the raised covector in an orthonormal frame
items.statement: Let (V,eta) be a 4-dimensional Lorentz vector space (def-lorentz-form-and-inertia): eta is symmetric and bilinear, nondegenerate in the sense that both radicals are {0} (def-matrix-radicals-rank-and-nondegeneracy-of-a-bilinear-form), and of inertia (3,1,0). Let V* be the algebraic dual (def-algebraic-dual-and-linear-functional). Then: (a) the map iota: V -> V*, iota(v)(w) := eta(v,w), is linear and injective, since iota(v) = 0 means eta(v,w) = 0 for all w in V, i.e. v lies in the left radical, which is {0}. (b) dim V* = dim V = 4, so iota is a linear bijection (rank-nullity, thm-rank-nullity). (c) Consequently for every covector k in V* there is a unique vector k^sharp in V with eta(k^sharp,w) = k(w) for all w in V; the assignment sharp: V* -> V, k |-> k^sharp, is linear and is the inverse of iota, so (v^flat)^sharp = v for v^flat := iota(v) and (k^sharp)^flat = k for every k; in particular k^sharp = 0 if and only if k = 0. (d) If (e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3) is an eta-orthonormal ordered basis of V (lem-lorentz-form-has-orthonormal-basis) and k_a := k(e_a) are the components of k in it, then k^sharp = -k_0 e_0 + k_1 e_1 + k_2 e_2 + k_3 e_3; that is, in this basis (k^sharp)^0 = -k_0 and (k^sharp)^i = k_i for i = 1,2,3, and eta(k^sharp,k^sharp) = -(k_0)^2 + (k_1)^2 + (k_2)^2 + (k_3)^2. Hence k^sharp is null exactly when k!=0 and (k_0)^2 = (k_1)^2 + (k_2)^2 + (k_3)^2, timelike when the left side is larger, and spacelike when it is smaller; k=0 raises to the zero vector and has no causal character (def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors). No orientation, time orientation or affine structure is used, and no choice principle is used.
items.strategy: Proof strategy. (a) Linearity in v is the bilinearity of eta; iota(v) = 0 is the statement that v lies in the left radical, and the defining nondegeneracy clause says the left radical is {0}. (b) The dual basis theorem (thm-dual-family-is-a-basis-in-finite-dimension) exhibits a basis of V* with one element per basis element of V, so dim V* = dim V; an injective linear map between finite-dimensional spaces of equal dimension is bijective, either directly by thm-rank-nullity (nullity 0 forces rank = dim V = dim V*) or by the equivalent characterization of invertibility. (c) Surjectivity supplies existence, injectivity supplies uniqueness, and the two inverse identities are immediate from the definitions. (d) Evaluate eta(-k_0 e_0 + sum_i k_i e_i, e_b) using eta-orthonormality: eta(-k_0 e_0, e_0) = -k_0 eta(e_0,e_0) = -k_0(-1) = k_0 and eta(k_i e_i, e_i) = k_i (no summation), with all cross terms zero; this equals k_b on the basis, hence the covectors agree by linearity, giving the component formula. The quadratic form is the diagonal evaluation diag(-1,1,1,1); the causal trichotomy is the definition of causal character: negative squared norm corresponds to (k_0)^2 larger than the spatial sum, positive squared norm to smaller, and zero squared norm is null only for k!=0 because the zero vector is excluded. The statement is pure algebra of the Lorentz form and asserts nothing physical. No choice principle is used.

items.title: Affine phase functions and wave covectors on affine Minkowski space
items.statement: Let (A,V,eta,C^+) be the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space (def-sr-affine-minkowski-model), with displacements q - p in V (def-affine-space-and-displacement). (a) A map theta: A -> R is an affine phase function if there are q in A and a covector k in V* (def-algebraic-dual-and-linear-functional) with theta(p) - theta(q) = k(p - q) for all p in A; the covector k is then unique (the differential d theta of theta), and for each fixed q the map theta |-> (k, theta(q)) is a bijection onto V* x R, with theta(p) = k(p - q) + theta(q). In the inertial chart x of a frame (o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3) one has theta(p) = k_a x^a(p) + theta(o) with k_a := k(e_a) the components of k in the frame (thm-unique-coordinates-with-respect-to-an-ordered-basis), and theta(o') = theta(o) + k(o' - o) for two origins. (b) Constant-phase directions: for v in V one has k(v) = 0 if and only if theta is constant on the line p + R v for every p in A, since theta(p + s v) = theta(p) + s k(v); if k is nonzero, the direction subspace ker k := {v in V : k(v) = 0} is a 3-dimensional linear subspace and every nonempty level set Sigma_t := {p in A : theta(p) = t} is the affine hyperplane p_0 + ker k through any of its points p_0; if k = 0 then theta is constant and Sigma_t is empty or all of A. For every C^1 curve gamma: I -> A one has (theta o gamma)'(s) = k(gamma'(s)) (thm-chain-rule, def-derivative). (c) A wave covector on (A,V,eta) is a nonzero element k of V*, and with k^sharp the raised vector of lem-sr-metric-duality-on-lorentz-vector-space k is called null, timelike or spacelike when eta(k^sharp,k^sharp) is zero, negative or positive, and future, past, future null, past null or causal when k^sharp is respectively future causal, past causal, future null, past null or causal in the sense of def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets; a future null wave covector is one that is both future and null. These definitions are well posed because the causal classification of a nonzero vector is by the sign of eta and by membership in the closed cones, and k^sharp = 0 exactly when k = 0 (duality lemma). (d) This item introduces mathematical objects and terminology only: it excludes the zero covector from 'wave covector', it fixes no units and no physical interpretation, and no claim that light or any physical wave is described by such a phase is made here; that identification is adopted in post-sr-ideal-plane-wave-model. No choice principle is used.
items.strategy: Proof strategy. (a) Uniqueness of k: if k and k' both satisfy the defining identity then (k - k')(p - q) = 0 for all p, so k - k' = 0; the bijection with V* x R is the two inverse constructions theta |-> (d theta, theta(q)) and (k, theta_0) |-> [p |-> k(p - q) + theta_0]. The chart formula is the affine chart identity x(p) - x(q) = (x^a(p) - x^a(q)) e_a together with linearity of k. (b) The displayed identity theta(p + s v) = theta(p) + s k(v) is linearity of k in the displacement; the kernel of a nonzero linear functional on a 4-dimensional space is 3-dimensional (thm-rank-nullity) and the level set is a coset of it. The curve derivative is the chain rule for theta o gamma, whose total derivative at p is k for every p (the phase is affine). (c) The definitions transfer verbatim the vector classification of def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors and def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets along the linear bijection sharp of lem-sr-metric-duality-on-lorentz-vector-space; injectivity of sharp makes the zero-covector exclusion and the well-definedness statement true. (d) A definition item carries formulation obligations only, so no proof of a physical claim is manufactured. Scope: pure linear algebra and affine geometry on A; no choice principle is used.

items.title: A future timelike vector pairs negatively with every nonzero future causal vector
items.statement: Let (A,V,eta,C^+) be the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space, let n, v be in V, and recall that a nonzero v with eta(v,v) <= 0 is causal (def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors, def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets). Then: (a) if n is future timelike and v is nonzero future causal, then eta(n,v) < 0; (b) if n is future timelike and v is nonzero past causal, then eta(n,v) > 0; (c) consequently, for a nonzero null vector v and any future timelike n, v is future null if and only if eta(n,v) < 0, and v is past null if and only if eta(n,v) > 0; the sign of eta(n,v) does not depend on the choice of the future timelike n; (d) if n_hat := n / sqrt(-eta(n,n)) is the normalization of a future timelike n, then n_hat is future unit timelike (eta(n_hat,n_hat) = -1) and eta(n,v) = sqrt(-eta(n,n)) eta(n_hat,v) for every v, so the sign statements hold for n_hat as well. The statement is pure affine Minkowski geometry and no choice principle is used.
items.strategy: Proof strategy. Choose an inertial frame (o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3), which exists by lem-future-oriented-inertial-frames-exist with first vector e_0 in C^+; write x = x^0 e_0 + x_vec, where x_vec is the coordinate triple of the frame's spatial three-space with positive-definite form delta and norm |.| (def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame). By lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components, the future timelike set is {x : x^0 > |x_vec|}, the closed future cone is {x : x^0 >= |x_vec|}, and the closed past cone is {x : x^0 <= -|x_vec|}. Hence n^0 > |n_vec| >= 0 for future timelike n, and for nonzero future causal v one has v^0 >= |v_vec| and v^0 > 0 (if v^0 = 0 then |v_vec| = 0 and v = 0, excluded). Then eta(n,v) = -n^0 v^0 + delta(n_vec,v_vec) <= -n^0 v^0 + |n_vec||v_vec| by the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality for delta (thm-cauchy-schwarz-finite), and |v_vec| <= v^0 gives eta(n,v) <= -(n^0 - |n_vec|) v^0 < 0 because n^0 - |n_vec| > 0 and v^0 > 0. This proves (a); (b) applies (a) to -v, which is nonzero future causal exactly when v is nonzero past causal, and eta(n,-v) = -eta(n,v). (c) For a nonzero null v exactly one of 'v future' and 'v past' holds (the closed cones meet only at 0 and every nonzero causal vector is future or past); (a) and (b) then identify the sign cases; the 'for every/some' uniformity is immediate because (a) applies to every future timelike n once v is known to be future. (d) eta(n,n) < 0 makes the square root real and positive, n_hat is future timelike by convexity of the cone and has unit norm, and eta is homogeneous in each argument. Scope note: no physical claim; no choice principle is used.

items.title: Frame data of a future null wave covector: the unique pair (varpi, s) with |s| = 1
items.statement: Let (A,V,eta,C^+) be the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space, let k be a future null wave covector (def-sr-affine-phase-and-wave-covector) and let (o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3) be an inertial frame with inertial chart x. Define varpi := -k(e_0) and s_i := k(e_i)/varpi for i = 1,2,3, and write s := (s_1,s_2,s_3) in R^3 with Euclidean norm |s|. Then: (a) varpi > 0. (b) |s| = 1. (c) for every v = v^0 e_0 + v^1 e_1 + v^2 e_2 + v^3 e_3 in V one has k(v) = varpi(-v^0 + s_1 v^1 + s_2 v^2 + s_3 v^3); equivalently the components of k in the frame are (k_0,k_1,k_2,k_3) = (-varpi, varpi s_1, varpi s_2, varpi s_3). (d) the raised vector is k^sharp = varpi(e_0 + s_1 e_1 + s_2 e_2 + s_3 e_3), with frame coordinates varpi(1,s_1,s_2,s_3); it is nonzero and future null, and k(k^sharp) = eta(k^sharp,k^sharp) = 0. (e) conversely, if a covector k in V* has frame components (-varpi, varpi s_1, varpi s_2, varpi s_3) with varpi > 0 and |s| = 1 in some inertial frame, then k is a future null wave covector and the construction of (a)-(b) applied to k in that frame returns the same varpi and s. (f) the pair (varpi,s) is uniquely determined by k and the frame; it is the complete frame description of a future null wave covector. No choice principle is used.
items.strategy: Proof strategy. (a) k(e_0) = eta(k^sharp,e_0) by the defining property of k^sharp (lem-sr-metric-duality-on-lorentz-vector-space), and eta(k^sharp,e_0) < 0 by lem-sr-future-causal-pairing-negative applied to the future timelike vector e_0 and the nonzero future null vector k^sharp; hence varpi = -k(e_0) > 0. (b) By lem-sr-metric-duality-on-lorentz-vector-space(d), the nullness eta(k^sharp,k^sharp) = 0 reads -(k_0)^2 + (k_1)^2 + (k_2)^2 + (k_3)^2 = 0; with k_0 = -varpi and k_i = k(e_i) = varpi s_i this is varpi^2(-1 + |s|^2) = 0, and varpi > 0 gives |s| = 1. (c) is linearity of k along the unique basis expansion (thm-unique-coordinates-with-respect-to-an-ordered-basis). (d) The component formula of the duality lemma gives k^sharp = -k_0 e_0 + sum_i k_i e_i = varpi e_0 + varpi sum_i s_i e_i; evaluating eta(k^sharp,k^sharp) with the diagonal matrix and using (b) gives 0, and k^sharp = varpi(1,s) in the frame has positive time component varpi > 0 equal to the norm of its spatial part, which is future null by lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components. (e) With the displayed components the duality lemma gives the vector varpi(1,s), which is nonzero future null by the same closed-cone description, and applying (a)-(b) to it returns varpi and s by construction. (f) Uniqueness is immediate because the components k_a = k(e_a) are determined by k and the frame and (a)-(c) invert them. Scope: pure algebra of eta in one inertial frame; no physical interpretation and no choice principle.

items.title: Transformation of the frame data of a future null wave covector under a passive boost
items.statement: Let (A,V,eta,C^+) be the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space, let x and x' be inertial charts whose transition is x' = B(beta) x + b for some beta in R^3 with |beta| < 1 and some b in R^4, where B(beta) is the passive boost of def-lorentz-boost and gamma := (1 - |beta|^2)^(-1/2), and let k be a future null wave covector with frame-x data (varpi,s) as in lem-sr-null-covector-frame-data, so that k has components (k_0,k_1,k_2,k_3) = (-varpi, varpi s_1, varpi s_2, varpi s_3) in x. Then: (i) the components of the same covector k in x' are k'_a = (B(-beta))^b_a k_b, that is k'_0 = gamma(k_0 + beta . k_vec) and k'_vec = k_vec + ((gamma - 1)/|beta|^2)(beta . k_vec) beta + gamma beta k_0 for beta nonzero (and k' = k for beta = 0), where k_vec := (k_1,k_2,k_3). (ii) With varpi' := -k'_0 and s'_i := k'_i/varpi' the frame-x' data is varpi' = gamma(1 - beta . s) varpi > 0 and s' = [s + ((gamma - 1)/|beta|^2)(beta . s) beta - gamma beta] / [gamma(1 - beta . s)] for beta nonzero (and s' = s for beta = 0); moreover |s'| = 1, so k'_a = (-varpi', varpi' s'_1, varpi' s'_2, varpi' s'_3) in x'. (iii) In the axis case beta = b e_1 with b in (-1,1): s'_1 = (s_1 - b)/(1 - b s_1), s'_2 = s_2/(gamma(1 - b s_1)) and s'_3 = s_3/(gamma(1 - b s_1)). (iv) beta . s' = (beta . s - |beta|^2)/(1 - beta . s); in particular beta . s' = 0 if and only if beta . s = |beta|^2, and beta . s' = -|beta|^2 if and only if beta . s = 0. (v) applying the transformation with beta replaced by -beta returns the original data (varpi,s), since B(-beta) is the inverse of B(beta). The statement is pure algebra of eta and the boost; no choice principle is used.
items.strategy: Proof strategy. (i) The transition x' = B(beta)x + b has linear part Lambda = B(beta), which is a proper orthochronous Lorentz matrix representing the inertial frame change (lem-inertial-chart-transitions-are-affine-lorentz, def-lorentz-map-and-lorentz-group); the covector component law k'_a = (Lambda^{-1})^b_a k_b is clause (ii) of thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation (for the constant covector field k, of class C^infinity in the sense of def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space). By lem-boost-is-proper-orthochronous-with-inverse, Lambda^{-1} has entries (B(-beta))^0_0 = gamma, (B(-beta))^0_i = (B(-beta))^i_0 = gamma beta_i and (B(-beta))^i_j = delta^i_j + ((gamma - 1)/|beta|^2) beta_i beta_j (for beta nonzero), which gives the displayed component formulas. (ii) Insert k_0 = -varpi and k_i = varpi s_i: k'_0 = gamma(-varpi + varpi beta . s) = -gamma(1 - beta . s) varpi, so varpi' = gamma(1 - beta . s) varpi; positivity follows from |beta| < 1 and |s| = 1 via the Cauchy-Schwarz bound beta . s <= |beta| < 1 (thm-cauchy-schwarz-finite), so 1 - beta . s >= 1 - |beta| > 0. The numerator for k'_vec is k_vec + ((gamma - 1)/|beta|^2)(beta . k_vec) beta + gamma beta k_0 = varpi[s + ((gamma - 1)/|beta|^2)(beta . s) beta - gamma beta], so dividing by varpi' gives the displayed s'. Finally |s'| = 1 is not assumed but follows from part (b) of lem-sr-null-covector-frame-data applied in the inertial frame x': the same covector k is future null (k^sharp is unchanged by a change of frame; only its components change), and the lemma's construction in x' returns precisely (varpi', s') as computed. (iii) Substituting beta = b e_1 and |beta|^2 = b^2 gives s'_1 = (s_1 - b)/(1 - b s_1) and s'_j = s_j/(gamma(1 - b s_1)) for j = 2,3. (iv) beta . s' = [beta . s + ((gamma - 1)/|beta|^2)(beta . s)|beta|^2 - gamma|beta|^2]/[gamma(1 - beta . s)] = [gamma(beta . s) - gamma|beta|^2]/[gamma(1 - beta . s)] = (beta . s - |beta|^2)/(1 - beta . s); the two equivalences follow since |beta| < 1. (v) By lem-boost-is-proper-orthochronous-with-inverse B(-beta) is the inverse of B(beta), so applying the component law twice returns k'' = k; equivalently substituting -beta in (ii) inverts the explicit formulas. Scope note: pure algebra; the item asserts no physical Doppler statement (that is pthm-sr-null-wave-doppler-and-aberration) and no choice principle is used.
