items.title: The phase rate along a curve, a worldline and an ideal observer
items.statement: Let theta be an affine phase function with wave covector k (def-sr-affine-phase-and-wave-covector). (a) For every C^1 curve gamma: I -> A one has (theta o gamma)'(s) = k(gamma'(s)) for all s in I. (b) If x: I -> A is a future timelike worldline (def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline) with proper-time function tau (def-sr-proper-time) and four-velocity U = dx/dtau (def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration), then d(theta o x)/dtau = k(U) along the worldline (the derivative is taken in the proper-time parametrization; the inverse proper-time parametrization exists by lem-sr-proper-time-parametrization). (c) If k is moreover a future null wave covector, then k(U) < 0 at every point, so theta is strictly decreasing in proper time along every future timelike worldline; the positive number -k(U) is the quantity given physical meaning in def-sr-null-wave-covector-and-observer-frequency. (d) If x is the straight worldline of an inertial observer, so that U = c n for a future unit timelike vector n with eta(n,n) = -1, then k(U) = c k(n) and -k(U) = -c k(n) > 0; conversely every future timelike worldline has eta(U,U) = -c^2 (thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition(a)). No choice principle is used.
items.strategy: Proof strategy. (a) In an inertial chart theta is the affine function x |-> k_a x^a + theta_0; composing with gamma and differentiating is the chain rule (thm-chain-rule, def-derivative), and the derivative of the affine part is the constant covector k applied to gamma'. (b) Write the worldline in proper-time parametrization, x = x(tau); then theta o x has derivative k(x'(tau)) = k(U(tau)) by (a) applied to the reparametrized curve, with the chain rule and the positivity of dtau/ds (lem-sr-proper-time-parametrization). (c) U is nonzero future timelike and k^sharp is nonzero future null, so eta(k^sharp,U) < 0 by lem-sr-future-causal-pairing-negative; by the defining property of k^sharp, k(U) = eta(k^sharp,U) < 0. (d) For an inertial observer, thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition(a),(d) gives eta(U,U) = -c^2 and the unit vector n = U/c; linearity gives k(U) = c k(n), and positivity is (c). Scope note: the item is conditional geometry along worldlines; it asserts no clock reading and no frequency measurement, and no choice principle is used.

items.title: Null wave covectors, frame frequency data and the observer frequency of an ideal plane wave
items.statement: Adopt the SI coordinate and unit conventions of def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions: in every inertial chart x^0 = c t with c > 0 in metres per second and spatial coordinates in metres, so c is the model's conversion constant. Let k be a future null wave covector and theta its affine phase (def-sr-affine-phase-and-wave-covector). (a) Frame data as wave data. In the inertial chart of a frame let (varpi,s) be the frame data of lem-sr-null-covector-frame-data, so varpi = -k(e_0) > 0 and |s| = 1. Define the angular frequency omega := c varpi (unit s^-1), the linear frequency nu := omega/(2 pi) (unit s^-1, hertz), the wave vector kappa := (omega/c) s (unit m^-1; |kappa| = omega/c), the wavelength lambda := 2 pi/|kappa| = 2 pi c/omega = c/nu (unit m), and the propagation direction s (dimensionless). In these conventions the phase is theta(p) = -omega t + kappa . x_vec(p) + const with t := x^0(p)/c the coordinate time in seconds, so the components of k in the chart are k_a = (-omega/c, (omega/c)s_1, (omega/c)s_2, (omega/c)s_3). (b) Observer frequency. For an ideal observer whose four-velocity is U_o = c n with n in V future unit timelike (eta(n,n) = -1; def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration, thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition) define the observer angular frequency of the wave as omega_n := -c k(n) = -k(U_o) in s^-1, and the observer linear frequency as omega_n/(2 pi); by lem-sr-phase-rate-along-worldline this is minus the rate of change of the phase with respect to the observer's own proper time, and the sign convention makes it positive. (c) Well-definedness. varpi = -k(e_0) > 0 and |s| = 1 in every inertial frame (frame-data lemma), hence omega > 0 and lambda > 0 are uniquely well defined for the specified k and inertial frame; they can change when the frame/observer changes; omega_n > 0 for every future unit timelike n and every future null wave covector (lem-sr-future-causal-pairing-negative), so every ideal observer reads a positive angular frequency; omega_n depends only on k and the observer vector n. (d) This item fixes definitions, units and sign conventions only. It does not assert that any physical light is described by such a phase; that identification is adopted in post-sr-ideal-plane-wave-model. It contains no quantum identification of energy with hbar omega, no amplitude or intensity content, no medium or dispersion model, no source or detector model and no measurement or empirical claim.
items.strategy: Formulation obligations, not a proof of a physical claim. (a) The definitions are functions of k and the frame; well-definedness of varpi and s is lem-sr-null-covector-frame-data and the SI conversion is def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions, so the physical names attached to the mathematical numbers are a convention fixed here. The relation theta(p) = -omega t + kappa . x_vec(p) + const is the substitution x^0 = c t in k_a x^a. (b) n = U_o/c is future unit timelike by thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition(a); omega_n = -c k(n) = -k(U_o) by linearity; positivity and the proper-time-derivative reading are lem-sr-future-causal-pairing-negative and lem-sr-phase-rate-along-worldline with the sign convention explicitly chosen here. (c) Positivity is supplied by the quoted lemmas. Frame data (varpi,s), hence omega and lambda, depend on the specified inertial frame. The scalar omega_n=-c k(n) is coordinate independent for the fixed pair (k,n), not invariant under replacing n by another observer; the frame observer is n=e_0. No boost-invariance of frequency or wavelength is asserted. (d) The scope clause records that the physical interpretation (light is described by an ideal plane wave, and the number defined here is the frequency an ideal observer reads) is adopted only in post-sr-ideal-plane-wave-model; the definition item must not be presented as implying it. No proof of a physical claim is manufactured; no choice principle is used.

items.physical_scope: Ideal wave vocabulary in flat classical special-relativistic spacetime: the angular frequency, linear frequency, wave vector, wavelength and propagation direction attached to a future null wave covector in an inertial frame, and the observer-frequency sign convention omega_n = -c k(n) = -k(U_o) for an ideal observer. Conditional on the model's SI conventions; excludes quantum photon and energy identifications, media and dispersion, amplitude and intensity, sources and detectors, real apparatus, and every measurement or empirical claim.

items.title: Adopted ideal plane-wave and frequency-reading model
items.statement: Adopt as physical assumptions of this framework, extending post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light (ideal vacuum light rays are exactly the future null straight lines, with coordinate speed c in every inertial chart) and post-sr-inertial-covariance (the affine Minkowski model, with the model's equations covariant under proper orthochronous affine Lorentz maps): (i) Ideal plane wave. An ideal monochromatic light wave in vacuum is modeled, in any inertial chart, by a dimensionless affine phase theta with future null wave covector k (def-sr-affine-phase-and-wave-covector, lem-sr-null-covector-frame-data): the level sets of theta are the wave fronts, every line p + R k^sharp has constant phase, the complete ray trajectories of this ideal wave are the oriented null lines p+R k^sharp, oriented by the future tangent k^sharp, consistently with the general ideal-light clause. An emission event p selects their future segments p+R_{>=0} k^sharp; a complete line and an emitted half-ray are distinct objects. The model is one ideal plane wave: constant wave covector, no medium, no dispersion, no absorption, no modulation or envelope, no boundary or source model, no intensity or polarization model. (ii) Frequency reading. An ideal observer of the model with four-velocity U_o = c n (n future unit timelike) that receives this wave reads the angular frequency omega_n := -c k(n) = -k(U_o) and the linear frequency omega_n/(2 pi) of def-sr-null-wave-covector-and-observer-frequency, i.e. minus the rate of change of the phase with respect to the observer's own proper time with the sign convention that this number is positive (lem-sr-phase-rate-along-worldline, lem-sr-future-causal-pairing-negative). The reading is attached to the observer's worldline at the event of reception. (iii) Frequency comparisons. Comparing the frequency of one wave between two ideal observers or between two inertial descriptions means comparing omega_n at specified reception events, or the frame data (omega,s) of the same phase function in specified inertial charts; this postulate asserts no Doppler or aberration formula, and comparing events requires propagating the phase along the specified observer worldlines. (iv) Scope and exclusions. These are adopted idealizations, not deductions from experiment and not claims about nature. No quantum photon model and no identification of energy with hbar omega is made (excluded by the conventions of def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions); no claim is made that real light, real clocks, real receivers or real sources are exactly described; dispersive, absorbing, nonlinear or modulated media, finite line width, intensity, polarization, source and detector physics, gravitation, quantum effects and accelerated-observer reception are outside the model. Empirical tests of the model belong to the framework's experimental work and are not asserted here.
items.strategy: A postulate, not a theorem: it fixes the physical interpretation of the mathematical phase functions and of the observer-frequency number, and it fixes the ideal wave and receiver regime. Obligations: (i) the phase functions with future null wave covectors and their level sets are mathematical objects supplied by def-sr-affine-phase-and-wave-covector and lem-sr-null-covector-frame-data; the identification of the level sets with wave fronts and of the future null lines along k^sharp with this wave's rays is adopted, extending the ideal-light clause of post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light; For a future null tangent v, write k^sharp=varpi(1,s), |s|=1, and v=v0(1,r), v0>0, |r|=1, in an inertial frame. Constant phase means k(v)=varpi v0(-1+s.r)=0. Equality in the Euclidean Cauchy-Schwarz inequality gives r=s, so v=(v0/varpi)k^sharp with a positive coefficient. Thus every complete future-oriented constant-phase null line is p+R k^sharp with that orientation; choosing an emission point selects p+R_{>=0} k^sharp, not the whole line. Conversely k(k^sharp)=0 makes both the line and its segments constant-phase. No competing ray system is introduced. (ii) The reading rule is an identification of a physical clock reading of a periodic process with the mathematical number -k(U_o); the mathematical positivity and the proper-time derivative are lem-sr-phase-rate-along-worldline and lem-sr-future-causal-pairing-negative, while the identification itself is adopted. (iii) The postulate is deliberately silent about Doppler and aberration formulas, so it cannot be used to infer them; the comparison protocol is fixed so that downstream theorems state exactly which frequencies at which events they compare. (iv) The exclusions are part of the adopted content and must travel with every conclusion. No proof is manufactured; no choice principle is used.

items.title: Doppler shift and aberration for an ideal plane wave between inertial descriptions
items.statement: Adopt post-sr-inertial-covariance, post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light and post-sr-ideal-plane-wave-model, and the conventions of def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions. Let x and x' be inertial charts whose transition is x' = B(beta) x + b with beta in R^3, |beta| < 1, b in R^4 and B(beta) the passive boost of def-lorentz-boost; write gamma := (1 - |beta|^2)^(-1/2) and beta_hat := beta/|beta| for beta nonzero, so that the frame x' moves with velocity v = c beta relative to the frame x in the direction beta_hat. Let the ideal wave of the model have phase theta with future null wave covector k and frame-x data (omega,s) in the sense of def-sr-null-wave-covector-and-observer-frequency: omega > 0, s in R^3 with |s| = 1 and k_a = (-omega/c, (omega/c)s) in x. Then, conditionally on the adopted model: (i) Frame data in x'. The data of the same covector k in x' is (omega',s') with omega' = gamma(1 - beta . s) omega > 0 and s' = [s + ((gamma - 1)/|beta|^2)(beta . s) beta - gamma beta]/[gamma(1 - beta . s)] for beta nonzero (and omega' = omega, s' = s for beta = 0), so |s'| = 1 and k'_a = (-omega'/c, (omega'/c)s'_1, (omega'/c)s'_2, (omega'/c)s'_3) in x'. In the axis case beta = b e_1 with b in (-1,1): s'_1 = (s_1 - b)/(1 - b s_1) and (s'_2,s'_3) = (s_2,s_3)/(gamma(1 - b s_1)). (ii) Reading and frequency ratios. The rest observers of x and x' (four-velocities c e_0 and c e'_0) read angular frequencies omega = -c k(e_0) and omega' = -c k(e'_0); the linear frequencies and wavelengths of the two descriptions satisfy nu' = gamma(1 - beta . s) nu and lambda' = lambda/[gamma(1 - beta . s)]. More generally, an ideal observer whose coordinate velocity in x is w (a vector of the frame's spatial three-space with |w| < c) reads omega_o = gamma_w(1 - (w . s)/c) omega, where gamma_w := (1 - |w|^2/c^2)^(-1/2); equivalently omega_o = gamma_w(1 - beta_w . s) omega with beta_w := w/c. (iii) Longitudinal cases. If s = beta_hat then omega' = omega sqrt((1 - |beta|)/(1 + |beta|)) < omega, nu' = nu sqrt((1 - |beta|)/(1 + |beta|)) and lambda' = lambda sqrt((1 + |beta|)/(1 - |beta|)): the observer moving in the direction of propagation (away from a source at rest in x and located behind it) reads a red-shifted frequency and lengthened wavelength. If s = -beta_hat then omega' = omega sqrt((1 + |beta|)/(1 - |beta|)) > omega and lambda' = lambda sqrt((1 - |beta|)/(1 + |beta|)): blue shift for an observer moving opposite to the propagation direction (toward such a source). (iv) Transverse protocols. If beta . s = 0 (propagation direction perpendicular to the relative velocity in the frame x) then omega' = gamma omega; this is greater than omega when beta!=0 and equals omega when beta=0. If beta . s = |beta|^2, for beta!=0 equivalently s' . beta_hat = 0 (propagation direction perpendicular to the relative velocity in the frame x'), then omega' = omega/gamma; this is less than omega when beta!=0 and equals omega when beta=0. Both configurations are called transverse Doppler configurations in the literature and the two factors differ for beta!=0 (both equal one at beta=0); the direction and size of the shift are not determined by the word 'transverse' without specifying the frame in which transversality holds. (v) Aberration. For beta!=0, if theta_x, theta_x' in [0,pi] are the angles between the propagation directions s, s' and the boost axis beta_hat, then cos theta_x' = (cos theta_x - |beta|)/(1 - |beta| cos theta_x); the map u |-> (u - |beta|)/(1 - |beta| u) is a strictly increasing bijection of [-1,1] onto itself, and in particular cos theta_x = 0 gives cos theta_x' = -|beta|. (vi) Scope and protocol. All clauses concern one ideal plane wave and ideal observers, and frequencies are compared through the phase model at specified reception events; the results are conditional on the adopted postulates (ideal plane wave, ideal clocks, inertial covariance, flat classical spacetime) and are not empirical claims about nature, sources or apparatus. They exclude media and dispersion, modulation and signal speeds, intensity and polarization, real line widths, accelerating observers (reserved to the framework's accelerated-observer page), gravitation and quantum effects; no statistical or measurement statement is made. If beta = 0 the transition is the pure translation x'=x+b: the inertial axes and wave-covector frame data agree, with omega'=omega and s'=s, while the affine phase constant is transformed as in the covector/phase law.
items.strategy: Proof in dependency order; the mathematical core is lem-sr-null-covector-boost-transformation with the reading lemmas. (i) By def-sr-null-wave-covector-and-observer-frequency the frame data of k in x is (omega,s) with omega = c varpi, varpi = -k(e_0), and k_a = (-omega/c,(omega/c)s). Apply lem-sr-null-covector-boost-transformation(i)-(ii) with (varpi,s): its conclusions give varpi' = gamma(1 - beta . s) varpi > 0 and the displayed s' with |s'| = 1; multiplying by c gives omega' = gamma(1 - beta . s) omega; the axis formulas are clause (iii) of the lemma. The relation beta . s = |beta|^2 <=> s' . beta_hat = 0 is clause (iv) of the lemma, and the identity s' . beta_hat = (beta . s - |beta|^2)/(|beta|(1 - beta . s)) for beta nonzero is its display. (ii) For the rest observer of x, U = c e_0 and omega = -c k(e_0) by the definition; for x' likewise with the frame vector e'_0 (def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart). The wavelength ratio is the reciprocal of the frequency ratio because lambda = c/nu and lambda' = c/nu' by definition. For a general observer write U_o = gamma_w(c,w) by thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition(e); then k(U_o) = c gamma_w k(e_0) + gamma_w k(w), and k(w) = (omega/c) w . s because w lies in the frame's spatial three-space and k_a = (-omega/c,(omega/c)s) (def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame); hence omega_o = -k(U_o) = gamma_w(omega - (omega/c) w . s) = gamma_w(1 - (w . s)/c) omega. (iii) Substitute s = +/- beta_hat into (i): gamma(1 -/+ |beta|) = sqrt((1 -/+ |beta|)/(1 +/- |beta|)) because gamma^2(1 -/+ |beta|)^2 = (1 -/+ |beta|)/(1 +/- |beta|); the wavelength ratios are the reciprocals. The receding/approaching identification uses the fixed protocol: the source is at rest in x and the wave propagates from it, so s = beta_hat means the x'-rest observer moves away from the source and s = -beta_hat means it moves toward it. (iv) beta . s = 0 gives omega' = gamma omega from (i); beta . s = |beta|^2 gives omega' = gamma(1 - |beta|^2) omega = omega/gamma, and the equivalence with s' . beta_hat = 0 is the displayed identity; at beta=0 both read omega'=omega and no direction beta_hat is assigned; for nonzero beta, gamma>1 gives the stated strict inequalities. The two protocols are distinct because a unit s with beta . s = 0 is not a unit s with beta . s = |beta|^2 when |beta| > 0. The existence of both configurations for every |beta| < 1 is exhibited by the examples on the companion page. (v) For beta!=0 set b:=|beta| and use the invariant display s' . beta_hat = (beta . s - b^2)/(b(1 - beta . s)). Substitute beta . s=b cos theta_x and cancel the strictly positive b to obtain cos theta_x'=(cos theta_x-b)/(1-b cos theta_x). No division of a coordinate axis formula by beta is used. The denominator is positive on [-1,1] because 0<b<1, and the derivative of u |-> (u-b)/(1-bu) is (1-b^2)/(1-bu)^2>0; its endpoint values are -1 and1, so it is the stated strictly increasing bijection. At beta=0 frequency/direction data agree and no boost-axis angle is assigned. (vi) The scope clause records the hypotheses and the exclusions; no step uses a source or detector model, and no choice principle is used. The postulate post-sr-ideal-plane-wave-model supplies the physical interpretation of theta, k and the reading rule, and the two other postulates supply the model's light and covariance clauses; the deduction is conditional on all of them.

items.title: Units, coordinate conventions and c restoration for the wave and Doppler formulas
items.statement: Remark on the conventions of def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions and def-sr-null-wave-covector-and-observer-frequency, for use with pthm-sr-null-wave-doppler-and-aberration. (a) Units in the adopted coordinates x^0 = c t: the phase theta is dimensionless; the coordinates x^a, the wavelength lambda and all distances are in metres; the components k_a of a wave covector, the wave vector kappa and varpi = -k(e_0) are in m^-1; the angular frequencies omega and omega_n and the linear frequencies nu are in s^-1 (nu also in hertz); c is in m s^-1; and s, beta, beta_w and gamma are dimensionless. (b) Two coordinate forms. In the adopted coordinates theta = -omega t + kappa . x_vec + const and k_a = (-omega/c, (omega/c)s); in a chart whose time coordinate is t in seconds directly, so that the metric component g_tt = -c^2 carries m^2 s^-2 and the time-space components carry m s^-1, the same phase is theta = -omega t + kappa . x_vec + const with the same omega and kappa, and the component tuple (-omega, (omega/c)s) carries mixed units; formulas derived in one convention are not reused unchanged in the other. This is the general warning of def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions specialized to the wave covector. (c) Natural units and restoration. In natural units c = 1 with x^0 = t one has k_a = (-omega, omega s), lambda = 2 pi/omega, and the Doppler and aberration factors gamma(1 - beta . s) and sqrt((1 -/+ |beta|)/(1 +/- |beta|)) are unchanged; restoring dimensions means replacing k_0 by -omega/c, k_i by (omega/c)s_i, writing every velocity as v = c beta with the dimensionless beta, and replacing lambda by 2 pi c/omega = c/nu. The dimensionless factors gamma(1 - beta . s) and the longitudinal square roots need no c restoration because they contain only beta, s and gamma; the c restoration affects the map between omega, nu, lambda and the components of k, not the shift factors themselves. (d) This remark introduces no quantum identification of energy with hbar omega, no amplitude or intensity content and no measurement claim; it is a units and convention statement carrying the scope of the items it cites.
items.strategy: A conventions and units remark, not a theorem. (a) Each unit is read off from the definitions in def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions and def-sr-null-wave-covector-and-observer-frequency: the phase is dimensionless by (theta(p) = k(p - q) + theta_0 with k in m^-1 and displacements in m), and the wave quantities inherit their units from k, c and the definitions omega = c varpi, kappa = (omega/c)s, lambda = c/nu. (b) Substituting x^0 = c t into k_a x^a gives -omega t + kappa . x_vec; the metric-component statement is the convention clause of def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions for a chart with time coordinate in seconds, and the mixed-unit tuple is displayed to prevent copying formulas across conventions. (c) The natural-unit form is the substitution c = 1 in the same formulas (with x^0 = t), and the restoration list is the inverse substitution; the factors gamma(1 - beta . s) and sqrt((1 -/+ |beta|)/(1 +/- |beta|)) are functions of the dimensionless quantities beta, s, gamma alone, which is why they are invariant under the restoration. (d) The exclusions repeat the scope of the cited items; no step proves a physical claim and no choice principle is used.

items.title: Observer energy, spatial momentum, invariant mass, rest energy and kinetic energy of a four-momentum
items.statement:
Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski model of [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]], $c>0$, and let $n\in V$ be future unit, $\eta(n,n)=-1$, with rest space $n^\perp$, rest projection $h(v)=v+\eta(n,v)n$ and norm $|w|=\sqrt{\eta(w,w)}$ on $n^\perp$ as in [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(c).
(a) For every $P$ in the future closed cone $\mathrm{cl}(C^+)$ define the observer energy of $P$ relative to $n$ by $E_n(P):=-c\,\eta(P,n)$, the observer spatial momentum by $q_n(P):=h(P)$, and, when $P$ is nonzero future causal, the invariant mass by $m(P):=\sqrt{-\eta(P,P)}/c$. Then $q_n(P)\in n^\perp$, $\eta(n,P)=-E_n(P)/c$, and $P=(E_n(P)/c)\,n+q_n(P)$ is the unique decomposition of $P$ as a multiple of $n$ plus a vector of $n^\perp$; equivalently $E_n$ and $q_n$ are the unique pair of a real number and a vector of $n^\perp$ with that property. For future null $P$ the same formula gives $m(P)=0$.
(b) If $m>0$ and $P$ is written as $P=mU$ with $U$ future timelike and $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$ (the four-velocity normalisation of [[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]]), call $m$ the rest-mass parameter of $P$, $mc^2$ its rest energy and $T_n(P):=E_n(P)-mc^2$ its kinetic energy relative to the observer $n$ and the parameter $m$. This parameterized presentation fixes $m$ through the admissible relation $P=mU$, but that relation and $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$ force $m=m(P)=\sqrt{-\eta(P,P)}/c$ uniquely: $\eta(P,P)=-m^2c^2$ and $m>0$. Thus on the future timelike branch $T_n(P)=E_n(P)-c^2m(P)$ is a function of $(P,n)$ alone; no independent choice of $m$ for a fixed admissible $P$ is available.
(c) The definition claims no positivity of $E_n$, no inequality or vanishing property of $T_n$, and no physical measurement. The names observer energy, spatial momentum, invariant mass, rest energy and kinetic energy and the units joule, kilogram metre per second and kilogram belong to the unit conventions of [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]] and to the physical postulates of this framework; the mathematical content asserted here is only the explicit dependence of the four quantities on $P$, $n$ and $m$.
(d) $E_n$ and $q_n$ are functions of the pair $(P,n)$: $q_n(P)$ is an element of the vector space $V$, not a coordinate triple, and no basis of $V$ enters its definition; $m(P)$ depends on the scalar $\eta(P,P)$ alone; $T_n(P)$ in the timelike branch may be presented with $m$, but this parameter is uniquely recovered from $P$ as in(b).
items.strategy: Definition item fixing five quantities and their exact dependence. Obligations: (i) $h$ is the linear projection of [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(c) with image $n^\perp$ and kernel $\mathrm{span}(n)$, so $q_n(P)\in n^\perp$ and the decomposition $P=-\eta(P,n)n+h(P)$ is unique; (ii) $-\eta(P,P)\ge0$ on $\mathrm{cl}(C^+)$ by [[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]], so the square root defining $m(P)$ is well defined for every nonzero future causal $P$; (iii) no positivity, monotonicity or measurement statement is imported here — those are supplied by [[lem-sr-energy-momentum-observer-identities]] and by [[post-sr-massive-particle-dynamics]]; (iv) With $P=mU$, $m>0$ and $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$, bilinearity gives $-\eta(P,P)=m^2c^2$; positivity of $m,c$ and the nonnegative square root give $m=\sqrt{-\eta(P,P)}/c=m(P)$. Therefore the admissible parameter is unique and $T_n$ is a function of $(P,n)$ on this branch. This algebra does not derive physical mass from data; it only identifies the parameter in the specified model. No choice principle is used.

items.title: Positivity, mass shell and kinetic energy of the observer quantities of a four-momentum
items.statement:
Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the affine Minkowski model, $c>0$, $n$ future unit, and let $E_n,q_n,m,T_n$ be the quantities of [[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]].
(a) If $P$ is nonzero future causal, then $E_n(P)>0$, $q_n(P)\in n^\perp$ and
$$\eta(q_n(P),q_n(P))=\frac{E_n(P)^2}{c^2}+\eta(P,P)\ \ge\ 0 .$$
Consequently: (i) if $P$ is future null then $\eta(P,P)=0$ and $E_n(P)=c\,|q_n(P)|>0$; (ii) if $P$ is future timelike with invariant mass $m(P)$ then $\eta(P,P)=-m(P)^2c^2$ and the mass-shell identity
$$E_n(P)^2=m(P)^2c^4+c^2\,|q_n(P)|^2$$
holds. The invariant mass $m(P)$ does not depend on the observer $n$ or on coordinates, being a function of the scalar $\eta(P,P)$ alone, while $E_n$ and $q_n$ do depend on $n$.
(b) Let $P=mU$ with $m>0$ constant and $U$ future timelike, $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$. With $\gamma:=-\eta(U/c,n)\ge1$ and $w:=h(U)/\gamma=c\,h(U/c)/\gamma\in n^\perp$ the relative velocity of [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(d), one has
$$E_n(P)=mc^2\gamma,\qquad T_n(P)=mc^2(\gamma-1)\ \ge\ 0,\qquad q_n(P)=m\gamma w,$$
and $m(P)=m$. Moreover $T_n(P)=0$ if and only if $\gamma=1$, that is $U=cn$, equivalently $P=mcn$ (the particle is at rest relative to $n$). Finally $|q_n(P)|=m\gamma|w|=mc\sqrt{\gamma^2-1}$.
items.strategy: All clauses are algebra in the flat model. (a) Expand $q_n(P)=P+\eta(P,n)n$: bilinearity and $\eta(n,n)=-1$ give $\eta(q_n,q_n)=\eta(P,P)+\eta(P,n)^2$, and $\eta(P,n)=-E_n(P)/c$. Positivity of $E_n$: choose an $\eta$-orthonormal basis with first vector in $C^+$ ([[lem-lorentz-form-has-orthonormal-basis]], [[lem-future-oriented-inertial-frames-exist]]) and write $P=P^0e_0+P_s$, $n=n^0e_0+n_s$; then $n^0>|n_s|$ and $P^0\ge|P_s|$ by [[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]], so $-\eta(P,n)=P^0n^0-P_s\cdot n_s\ge n^0|P_s|-|n_s|\,|P_s|=|P_s|(n^0-|n_s|)\ge0$ using the finite Cauchy-Schwarz inequality ([[thm-cauchy-schwarz-finite]], [[def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame]]); equality forces $P_s=0$, and then $P\ne0$ gives $P^0>0$ and $-\eta(P,n)=P^0n^0>0$. Substitute $\eta(P,P)=-m(P)^2c^2$ for (ii). (b) From $u:=U/c=\gamma(n+w/c)$ of [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(d) one gets $q_n(P)=mc\,h(u)=m\gamma w$ and $E_n(P)=-mc\,\eta(U,n)=mc^2(-\eta(U/c,n))=mc^2\gamma$; the rest is the identity $|w|^2=c^2(1-\gamma^{-2})$ and $\gamma\ge1$ from the same item, with $\gamma=1$ if and only if $u=n$. No choice principle is used.

items.title: Four-momentum components, energy-velocity relation and passive boost transformation in an inertial frame
items.statement:
Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the affine Minkowski model, $c>0$, and let $(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ be an inertial frame with stationary observer $n:=e_0$; let $E_n,q_n$ be as in [[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]].
(a) For every $P\in\mathrm{cl}(C^+)$ the coordinate components of $P$ in the frame are $(P^0,P^1,P^2,P^3)=(E_n(P)/c,\,q^1,q^2,q^3)$, where $q_n(P)=\sum_{i=1}^3q^ie_i$; if $P$ is future timelike then $E^2=m(P)^2c^4+c^2\sum_{i=1}^3(q^i)^2$ with $E=E_n(P)$.
(b) Let $x:I\to A$ be a $C^1$ future timelike worldline whose chart coordinate path is $t\mapsto(ct,r(t))$, with coordinate velocity $w:=r'$ and $\gamma_w:=(1-|w|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$; then $|w|<c$, the four-velocity is $U=\gamma_w(c,w)$ by [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(e), and for $P=mU$ with $m>0$ constant the components are $P=m\gamma_w(c,w)$, that is $E_n(P)=m\gamma_wc^2$ and $q_n(P)=\sum_{i=1}^3m\gamma_ww^ie_i$.
(c) Fix a unit spatial direction $s$, a signed scalar velocity $v$ with $|v|<c$, and $b:=v/c\in(-1,1)$. The passive vector boost parameter is $\boldsymbol\beta:=b s\in\mathbb R^3$, distinct from the scalar $b$. Let $B(\boldsymbol\beta)$ be the boost of [[def-lorentz-boost]], let $\Lambda_b$ be its matrix in the ordered frame, and let $P'$ be the coordinate components of the same vector after $x'=\Lambda_b x$. Put $\mathbf p=(P^1,P^2,P^3)$, $p_s=s\cdot\mathbf p$, $\mathbf p_\parallel=p_s s$, $\mathbf p_\perp=\mathbf p-p_s s$, and $\gamma_v=(1-b^2)^{-1/2}$. Then
$$P'^0=\gamma_v(P^0-b p_s),\quad p'_s=\gamma_v(p_s-bP^0),\quad\mathbf p'_\parallel=\gamma_v(\mathbf p_\parallel-bP^0s),\quad\mathbf p'_\perp=\mathbf p_\perp,$$
equivalently $E'=\gamma_v(E-vp_s)$, $p'_s=\gamma_v(p_s-vE/c^2)$ and $\mathbf p'_\perp=\mathbf p_\perp$. At $b=0$ these formulas give $P'=P$, with any chosen unit $s$; no division by $b$ or choice of a boost axis from a zero vector is used. The quadratic combination is invariant, $E'^2-c^2|\mathbf p'|^2=E^2-c^2|\mathbf p|^2=m(P)^2c^4$ for future timelike $P$, while for future null $P$ one has $E=c|\mathbf p|$ and $E'=c|\mathbf p'|$ in both coordinate systems; in particular the invariant mass is frame-independent.
items.strategy: (a) The decomposition $P=(E_n/c)e_0+q_n(P)$ of [[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]] is already a decomposition in the basis; read components and substitute the mass-shell identity of [[lem-sr-energy-momentum-observer-identities]]\,(a)(ii). (b) [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(e) gives $|w|<c$ and $U=\gamma_w(c,w)$; multiply by $m$ and apply (a). (c) The vector component law of [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]] applies to $x'=\Lambda_b x$, where $\Lambda_b$ is the displayed frame matrix of $B(bs)$. Its time row gives $P'^0=\gamma_v(P^0-bp_s)$, while its spatial block is $I+(\gamma_v-1)ss^T$ and time column $-\gamma_v b s$ for $b\ne0$. Hence $\mathbf p'=\mathbf p_\perp+\gamma_v(p_s-bP^0)s$, which yields all scalar and vector projections without a scalar-vector subtraction. For $b=0$ use $B(0)=I$, so the same projected formulas are identities for arbitrary fixed unit $s$. Proper orthochrony is [[lem-boost-is-proper-orthochronous-with-inverse]]. The invariance is the rearrangement $E'^2-c^2|\mathbf p'|^2=E^2-c^2|\mathbf p|^2$ of the same components, equal to $-c^2\eta(P,P)=m(P)^2c^4$ for future timelike $P$ and to $0$ for future null $P$ ([[lem-sr-energy-momentum-observer-identities]]\,(a)). No choice principle is used.

items.title: Proper-time derivative of a vector field along a worldline and the four-force notation
items.statement:
Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the affine Minkowski model, $c>0$, and let $x:I\to A$ be a $C^1$ future timelike worldline with proper-time function $\tau:I\to J$ and inverse $\rho:J\to I$ ([[def-sr-proper-time]], [[lem-sr-proper-time-parametrization]]).
(a) For a $C^1$ map $P:I\to V$ define its proper-time derivative $\dot P:I\to V$ by
$$\dot P(s):=\frac{P'(s)}{\tau'(s)},$$
where $P'$ is the derivative of $P$ with respect to the worldline parameter, taken componentwise in any ordered linear basis of $V$; the result does not depend on the basis because two ordered linear bases are related by a constant invertible linear coordinate map. Equivalently $\dot P(s)=(P\circ\rho)'(\tau(s))$, so $\dot P$ is the derivative of the proper-time parametrised field $P\circ\rho$. Since $\tau'(s)>0$ by [[lem-sr-proper-time-parametrization]], $\dot P$ is well defined and continuous whenever $P$ is $C^1$.
(b) If $P=mU$ with $m>0$ constant and $U$ the four-velocity of $x$ ([[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]]), then $F:=\dot P$ is called the four-force on the particle; in an inertial frame $F$ has the components of the derivative of the four-momentum with respect to proper time.
(c) This item introduces a derivative and a name only. It asserts no force law, no field equation, no equation of motion and no existence or uniqueness of solutions; the identities satisfied by $F$ for a stipulated four-momentum field are proved in [[lem-sr-four-force-and-work-energy-identities]], and a physical force law requires a further model premise.
items.strategy: Definition item. Obligations: (i) the division by $\tau'$ is legitimate because $\tau'>0$ ([[lem-sr-proper-time-parametrization]]); (ii) the equivalence $\dot P(s)=(P\circ\rho)'(\tau(s))$ is the chain rule along the reparametrisation, $\rho$ being the inverse of the increasing function $\tau$; (iii) componentwise differentiation in one ordered linear basis and change of basis commute because the transition map is constant and linear, so the definition is basis-free; (iv) no dynamics is imported: $F$ is a derived vector field attached to a given $P$, not a prescribed law. No choice principle is used.

S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), Chapter 1; PDF page = printed page + 7; printed p. 27, equation (1.102) (force four-vector f^mu = dp^mu/d tau)

items.title: Four-force identities and the work-energy relation in an inertial frame
items.statement:
Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the affine Minkowski model, $c>0$, let $(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ be an inertial frame with $n:=e_0$, and let $x$ be a $C^2$ future timelike worldline whose chart coordinate path is $t\mapsto(ct,r(t))$, with coordinate velocity $w:=r'$, coordinate acceleration $a:=w'$ and $\gamma:=(1-|w|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$; let $m>0$ be constant, $P:=mU$ with $U=\gamma(c,w)$ the four-velocity, $E:=E_n(P)$, $\mathbf p:=q_n(P)$ with coordinates $m\gamma w$, $F:=\dot P$ the four-force of [[def-sr-proper-time-derivative-and-four-force]] and $\mathbf f:=\frac{d}{dt}\mathbf p$ the coordinate three-force.
Then: (a) $F=mA$, where $A$ is the four-acceleration, and $\eta(P,F)=0$; equivalently $\eta(U,F)=0$ and the mass shell $\eta(P,P)=-m^2c^2$ has vanishing proper-time derivative.
(b) $\frac{dE}{dt}=\mathbf f\cdot\mathbf w$, the Euclidean inner product of the coordinate vectors.
(c) $F=\gamma\,(\mathbf f\cdot\mathbf w/c,\ \mathbf f)$, that is $F^0=\gamma\,\mathbf f\cdot\mathbf w/c$ and $F^i=\gamma\mathbf f^i$ for $i=1,2,3$.
(d) If instead $m:I\to(0,\infty)$ is $C^1$ and $P=mU$ with this variable parameter, then $\eta(P,F)=-mc^2\,\frac{dm}{d\tau}$; the constant-mass identities of (a) use the constancy of $m$ and must not be applied to variable-mass systems.
items.strategy: Direct computation in the frame. With $E=m\gamma c^2$ and $\gamma'=\gamma^3(w\cdot a)/c^2$ ([[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]], [[thm-chain-rule]]) one has $dE/dt=m\gamma^3(w\cdot a)$; together with $\mathbf p=m\gamma w$ and $\mathbf f=m(\gamma^3(w\cdot a)w/c^2+\gamma a)$ this gives $\mathbf f\cdot\mathbf w=m\gamma^3(w\cdot a)=dE/dt$, proving (b). Since $\dot P=\gamma\,dP/dt$ and $dP/dt=(mc\gamma',m\gamma'w+m\gamma a)$, substituting gives (c). For (a), $\dot P=m\dot U=mA$ because $m$ is constant, and $\eta(U,A)=0$ by [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(b); equivalently differentiate $\eta(P,P)=-m^2c^2$ along the worldline. For (d), differentiate $\eta(P,P)=-m(\tau)^2c^2$: $2\eta(P,F)=-2mc^2\,\frac{dm}{d\tau}$. No force law is used; the identities are conditional on the stated four-momentum field. No choice principle is used.

references.title: B. S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), Chapter 1; PDF page = printed page + 7; printed p. 27, equation (1.102) (f^mu = dp^mu/d tau, the tensorial analogue of f = dp/dt)

items.title: Total four-momentum, invariant mass and center-of-momentum frame of a finite system
items.statement:
Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the affine Minkowski model and $c>0$.
(a) For a finite list $(P_1,\dots,P_N)$, $N\ge0$, of vectors of $V$ define the total four-momentum $P_{\mathrm{tot}}:=\sum_{i=1}^NP_i$ as the finite sum of [[def-finite-sum-in-a-commutative-monoid]] in the additive group $(V,+)$; the empty sum is $0$.
(b) If $P_{\mathrm{tot}}$ is future timelike, define its invariant mass $M:=M(P_{\mathrm{tot}}):=\sqrt{-\eta(P_{\mathrm{tot}},P_{\mathrm{tot}})}/c>0$ and its rest energy $Mc^2$; if $P_{\mathrm{tot}}$ is future null, set $M:=0$ and say that the system has no rest frame. For zero, spacelike or past $P_{\mathrm{tot}}$ this convention defines no invariant mass.
(c) A center-of-momentum frame of a nonzero $P_{\mathrm{tot}}$ is an inertial frame $(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ whose first vector satisfies $q_{e_0}(P_{\mathrm{tot}})=0$, i.e. the total spatial momentum vanishes for the frame's stationary observer; by [[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]] this is equivalent to $P_{\mathrm{tot}}=-\eta(P_{\mathrm{tot}},e_0)e_0$, that is, to $P_{\mathrm{tot}}$ being a nonzero real multiple of $e_0$. This multiple is positive precisely when $P_{\mathrm{tot}}$ is future timelike, and negative precisely when it is past timelike; the arbitrary nonzero-vector convention in this clause is retained.
(d) The invariant mass of a single future timelike vector $P$ coincides with $m(P)$ of [[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]]; in particular for $P=mU$ with $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$ it equals $m$.
(e) No existence of a center-of-momentum frame, no physical conservation law and no dynamics are asserted by this definition; position, event and simultaneity data do not enter $\sum_iP_i$, and only the total vector carries the invariant mass.
items.strategy: Definition item. Obligations: (i) the finite sum is the one of [[def-finite-sum-in-a-commutative-monoid]] in the abelian group $(V,+)$; (ii) $-\eta(P_{\mathrm{tot}},P_{\mathrm{tot}})>0$ for future timelike $P_{\mathrm{tot}}$ by [[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]], so the square root is well defined; (iii) since P_tot!=0, the coefficient -eta(P_tot,e_0) is nonzero when the rest projection vanishes; its sign distinguishes future and past. The equivalence in(c) follows from $q_{e_0}(P)=h(P)=P+\eta(P,e_0)e_0$; (iv) no frame is produced here — existence is [[lem-sr-center-of-momentum-frame]], so the definition is not circular; (v) clause (d) compares the two invariant-mass conventions, both functions of the scalar $\eta(P,P)$. No choice principle is used.

items.title: Finite sums of future causal vectors and additivity of observer energy and momentum
items.statement:
Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the affine Minkowski model and $c>0$.
(a) If $v,w\in\mathrm{cl}(C^+)$ then $v+w\in\mathrm{cl}(C^+)$; if in addition $v\in C^+$ or $w\in C^+$, then $v+w\in C^+$. Moreover $-\eta(v,w)\ge0$ for $v,w\in\mathrm{cl}(C^+)$, with equality if and only if $v=0$, or $w=0$, or both $v$ and $w$ are future null and parallel (equivalently $w=\lambda v$ for some $\lambda\ge0$).
(b) If $P_1,\dots,P_N$ with $N\ge1$ are nonzero future causal vectors, then $P_{\mathrm{tot}}=\sum_{i=1}^NP_i$ is a nonzero future causal vector; if at least one $P_i$ is future timelike, then $P_{\mathrm{tot}}$ is future timelike. The converse implication does not hold: two future null vectors that are not parallel have a future timelike sum.
(c) For every future unit $n$ and all $P_1,\dots,P_N\in\mathrm{cl}(C^+)$,
$$E_n\Bigl(\sum_{i=1}^NP_i\Bigr)=\sum_{i=1}^NE_n(P_i),\qquad q_n\Bigl(\sum_{i=1}^NP_i\Bigr)=\sum_{i=1}^Nq_n(P_i),$$
where $E_n,q_n$ are the observer quantities of [[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]]; if the $P_i$ are nonzero future causal, then $E_n(P_{\mathrm{tot}})>0$.
items.strategy: Work in an $\eta$-orthonormal basis whose first vector lies in $C^+$ ([[lem-lorentz-form-has-orthonormal-basis]], [[lem-future-oriented-inertial-frames-exist]]), so that $\mathrm{cl}(C^+)=\{v:v^0\ge|v_s|\}$ and $C^+=\{v:v^0>|v_s|\}$ by [[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]]. For (a), $(v+w)^0=v^0+w^0\ge|v_s|+|w_s|\ge|v_s+w_s|$ by the triangle inequality, with strict first inequality if one summand is timelike; $-\eta(v,w)=v^0w^0-v_s\cdot w_s\ge|v_s||w_s|-v_s\cdot w_s\ge0$ by Cauchy-Schwarz ([[thm-cauchy-schwarz-finite]]), and equality forces $v_s,w_s$ collinear with $v^0=|v_s|$, $w^0=|w_s|$ unless a vector vanishes, i.e. both are null and parallel. For (b), apply (a) repeatedly by induction on $N$ ([[thm-induction-principle]], [[def-finite-sum-in-a-commutative-monoid]]); nonzeroness follows from $\mathrm{cl}(C^+)\cap(-\mathrm{cl}(C^+))=\{0\}$ of [[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]]: if $P_{\mathrm{tot}}=0$ then $P_N=-\sum_{i<N}P_i$ lies in $\mathrm{cl}(C^+)$ and in $-\mathrm{cl}(C^+)$, hence is zero, contradicting the hypothesis. For the failure of the converse, in an orthonormal basis take $P_1=(1,1,0,0)$ and $P_2=(1,0,1,0)$ times a common positive energy over $c$: both are future null and not parallel, and their sum $(2,1,1,0)$ times that factor has $v^0=2>\sqrt2=|v_s|$, hence is future timelike. For (c), $\eta(\cdot,n)$ and $h$ are linear ([[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]], [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(c), [[def-linear-map]]); positivity is [[lem-sr-energy-momentum-observer-identities]]\,(a) applied to the nonzero future causal total of (b). No choice principle is used.

items.title: Existence and uniqueness of the center-of-momentum frame of a future timelike four-momentum
items.statement:
Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the affine Minkowski model, $c>0$, and let $Q$ be a future timelike vector with invariant mass $M:=\sqrt{-\eta(Q,Q)}/c$; put $n_Q:=Q/(Mc)$, so that $\eta(n_Q,n_Q)=-1$, $n_Q\in C^+$ and $Q=Mc\,n_Q$.
(a) There exists an inertial frame $(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ with $e_0=n_Q$; in every such frame $q_{e_0}(Q)=0$, $E_{e_0}(Q)=Mc^2$ and the components of $Q$ are $(Mc,0,0,0)$. Such a frame is a center-of-momentum frame of $Q$ in the sense of [[def-sr-total-four-momentum-and-invariant-mass]]\,(c).
(b) Conversely, if an inertial frame satisfies $q_{e_0}(Q)=0$, then $e_0=n_Q$. Hence the time vector of a center-of-momentum frame of $Q$ is unique, and two center-of-momentum frames of $Q$ differ only by the choice of origin and by a positively oriented $\eta$-orthonormal change of the spatial basis $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ of $n_Q^\perp$; in particular the center-of-momentum frame is unique up to spatial rotations.
(c) If $Q$ is a nonzero future null vector, then no inertial frame satisfies $q_{e_0}(Q)=0$: a nonzero future null vector has no center-of-momentum frame.
items.strategy: Existence: $n_Q$ is future unit. By [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(c) the restriction of $\eta$ to $n_Q^\perp$ is positive definite, so by [[cor-finite-dimensional-inner-product-spaces-have-orthonormal-bases]] choose an orthonormal basis $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ of $n_Q^\perp$ for the restricted inner product; then $(n_Q,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ is $\eta$-orthonormal, and if its orientation class is negative replace $e_1$ by $-e_1$ ([[def-oriented-minkowski-volume-form]]), which preserves orthonormality and the first vector; [[lem-future-oriented-inertial-frames-exist]] and [[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]] give an inertial frame with this basis. Then $q_{e_0}(Q)=h(Q)=Q+\eta(Q,n_Q)n_Q=Q-Mc\,n_Q=0$ and $E_{e_0}(Q)=-c\eta(Q,n_Q)=Mc^2$. Uniqueness: $q_{e_0}(Q)=0$ says $Q=-\eta(Q,e_0)e_0$ with $-\eta(Q,e_0)>0$ ([[lem-sr-energy-momentum-observer-identities]]\,(a) applied to the single vector $Q$), so $Q$ is a positive multiple of $e_0$; comparing with $Q=Mc\,n_Q$ and $\eta(e_0,e_0)=-1$ gives $e_0=n_Q$. The remaining freedom is the spatial basis of $e_0^\perp=n_Q^\perp$, which must be positively oriented and $\eta$-orthonormal. (c) $q_{e_0}(Q)=0$ would again exhibit $Q$ as a nonzero multiple of the timelike vector $e_0$, contradicting nullity. No choice principle is used (the orthonormal basis is obtained by finite Gram-Schmidt over the positive definite $n_Q^\perp$).

items.title: Collision data and four-momentum conservation
items.statement:
Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the affine Minkowski model and $c>0$.
(a) A collision datum is a triple $(p;(P_1,\dots,P_N);(P'_1,\dots,P'_K))$ consisting of an event $p\in A$, a finite nonempty list of incoming vectors in $V$ and a finite nonempty list of outgoing vectors in $V$, with side totals $Q_{\mathrm{in}}:=\sum_{i=1}^NP_i$ and $Q_{\mathrm{out}}:=\sum_{j=1}^KP'_j$ formed as in [[def-sr-total-four-momentum-and-invariant-mass]]; the datum conserves if $Q_{\mathrm{in}}=Q_{\mathrm{out}}$. Two-sided data may be compared only through these totals.
(b) A leg $P$ is massive with mass $m>0$ if $P=mU$ for some future timelike $U$ with $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$, and null if $P$ is a nonzero future null vector. A datum is on-shell if every leg is massive with a recorded mass or null; a mass-specified datum records the mass $m>0$ of each massive leg or the value $0$ for each null leg. The mass sum of a side is the sum of the recorded positive masses of its massive legs; a side is massive-only if all its legs are massive.
(c) A datum is causal if every leg lies in $\mathrm{cl}(C^+)$; two-leg if both sides have two legs; equal-mass if in addition both sides are two-leg and the recorded masses agree pair by pair.
(d) The definition is purely mathematical: it neither asserts that any datum describes a physical process, nor that a conserving datum exists for a prescribed list of legs, nor any law of nature. Position, simultaneity, mechanism and interaction strength are not part of a datum; only the event, the two finite lists and their recorded masses are.
items.strategy: Definition item. Obligations: (i) the side totals use the finite sums of [[def-finite-sum-in-a-commutative-monoid]] in the additive group $V$; (ii) the massive-leg clause uses the four-velocity normalisation of [[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]] and the null-leg clause the causal classification of [[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]; (iii) no physical content is smuggled in: conservation is an equation between two vectors, and the existence of a conserving datum with prescribed masses is a separate mathematical question answered only in special cases by [[lem-sr-collision-necessary-conditions]]; (iv) the definition is not the adopted conservation law of the physical model, which is a postulate of its own. No choice principle is used.

items.title: Invariant mass, center-of-momentum frame and necessary conditions for conserving collision data
items.statement:
Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the affine Minkowski model, $c>0$, and let $\mathcal D=(p;(P_1,\dots,P_N);(P'_1,\dots,P'_K))$ be a mass-specified conserving collision datum of [[def-sr-collision-datum-and-conservation]], causal and on-shell, all of whose legs are nonzero; write $Q:=Q_{\mathrm{in}}=Q_{\mathrm{out}}$.
(a) If $Q$ is future timelike with invariant mass $M$, then $M$ is the common invariant mass of both sides, $Q$ has the center-of-momentum frame with $e_0=Q/(Mc)$ of [[lem-sr-center-of-momentum-frame]], and in that frame
$$Mc^2=\sum_{\text{legs of a side}}E_{e_0}(\text{leg})\qquad\text{for each side};$$
each massive leg $\ell=mU$ has $E_{e_0}(\ell)=mc^2\gamma_\ell\ge mc^2$ with equality if and only if $U=ce_0$, and each null leg has $E_{e_0}>0$. Hence for each side $S\in\{\mathrm{in},\mathrm{out}\}$,
$$M\ \ge\ \sum_{\text{massive legs }\ell\in S}m_\ell,$$
with equality if and only if $S$ is massive-only and every massive leg of $S$ has four-velocity $ce_0$ (all massive particles of that side at rest in the center-of-momentum frame).
(b) If $Q$ is future null, then every leg is null, all legs are mutually parallel in one null direction, $M=0$ by the convention of [[def-sr-total-four-momentum-and-invariant-mass]], and no center-of-momentum frame exists.
(c) Suppose the incoming side is two-leg, $P_i=m_iU_i$ with $m_i>0$, and put $n_2:=U_2/c$ (the future unit observer comoving with the second leg), $\gamma:=-\eta(U_1/c,n_2)\ge1$ and $E:=E_{n_2}(P_1)=m_1c^2\gamma$. Then
$$M^2=m_1^2+m_2^2+\frac{2m_2E}{c^2}.$$
Consequently, if the outgoing side is mass-specified with massive masses $\mu_1,\dots,\mu_L$, $L\ge1$ (it may also contain null legs), the datum can conserve only if
$$E\ \ge\ \frac{c^2}{2m_2}\Bigl[\Bigl(\sum_{l=1}^L\mu_l\Bigr)^2-m_1^2-m_2^2\Bigr],\qquad\text{equivalently}\qquad T:=E-m_1c^2\ \ge\ \frac{c^2}{2m_2}\Bigl[\Bigl(\sum_{l=1}^L\mu_l\Bigr)^2-(m_1+m_2)^2\Bigr].$$
(d) [null legs] If $P_1,P_2$ are future null and there is an inertial frame with $P_i=(E_i/c)(e_0+s_i)$, $E_i>0$, $s_1,s_2$ unit spatial vectors with $s_2=-s_1$, then $Q$ is future timelike and $M=2\sqrt{E_1E_2}/c^2$. More generally, with $s_1,s_2$ unit vectors making Euclidean angle $\theta\in[0,\pi]$, $Q$ is future timelike for $\theta\ne0$ with
$$M=\frac{\sqrt{2E_1E_2(1-\cos\theta)}}{c^2},$$
while for $\theta=0$ the total $Q$ is future null, $M=0$ and no center-of-momentum frame exists. In particular, a conserving on-shell collision datum whose incoming side is a single null leg and whose outgoing side contains at least one massive leg does not exist.
(e) All clauses are conditional implications from the hypotheses of a conserving, causal, on-shell datum. They assert no interaction, no existence of a conservation process for prescribed legs, no cross section, amplitude or probability, and no empirical fact.
items.strategy: Assemble the local suppliers. By [[lem-sr-finite-future-causal-sums]] each side total is a nonzero future causal vector; if some leg is timelike the total is timelike, and observer energy and momentum are additive with $E_{e_0}(Q)>0$. (a) For timelike $Q$, [[lem-sr-center-of-momentum-frame]] supplies the frame $e_0=Q/(Mc)$ with $E_{e_0}(Q)=Mc^2$; additivity gives $Mc^2=\sum E_{e_0}$ on each side; [[lem-sr-energy-momentum-observer-identities]]\,(b) gives $E_{e_0}(\ell)=mc^2\gamma_\ell\ge mc^2$ with equality exactly for $U=ce_0$, and clause (a)(i) gives $E_{e_0}(\ell)=c|q|>0$ for null legs; summing yields the inequality and its equality case. (b) If one leg were timelike, the total would be timelike; and for future causal $v,w$ one has $-\eta(v,w)\ge0$ with equality exactly for zero or parallel future null pairs by [[lem-sr-finite-future-causal-sums]]\,(a), so a null total forces every pair of nonzero legs to be parallel future null; [[lem-sr-center-of-momentum-frame]]\,(c) excludes a center-of-momentum frame. (c) From $P_2=m_2c\,n_2$ and $\eta(P_1,n_2)=-E/c$ one gets $\eta(P_1,P_2)=-m_2E$ and $\eta(P_2,P_2)=-m_2^2c^2$, $\eta(P_1,P_1)=-m_1^2c^2$, so $-\eta(Q,Q)=m_1^2c^2+m_2^2c^2+2m_2E$; divide by $c^2$. The threshold inequality applies (a) to the outgoing side, $\sum_l\mu_l\le M$, and rearranges. (d) In the displayed frame $\eta(P_1,P_2)=(E_1E_2/c^2)(-1+\cos\theta)$, so $-\eta(Q,Q)=2E_1E_2(1-\cos\theta)/c^2$, and for $\theta=0$ the total is a positive multiple of the null vector $P_1$; the one-null-leg statement follows because a sum containing a timelike leg is timelike while a single null leg leaves $Q$ null. No choice principle is used; all arguments are finite-dimensional and algebraic.

items.title: Adopted massive-particle momentum, observer measurement and isolated-collision conservation
items.statement: Adopt as physical assumptions of the relativistic particle model, on top of the flat spacetime model, the ideal-clock and ideal-light postulates and the SI unit conventions: (i) Mass and momentum. Every massive classical particle carries a positive constant invariant mass parameter $m>0$ and has four-momentum $P=mU$, where $U$ is the four-velocity of its future timelike worldline; $P$ is a vector of $V$ whose SI unit is kilogram metre per second. The formula is adopted only for $m>0$; the case $m=0$ is not defined by it and is a separate premise. (ii) Observer measurement identification. Relative to a future unit observer $n$, the model identifies the measured energy of the particle with $E_n(P)$, its measured spatial momentum with $q_n(P)$, its kinetic energy with $T_n(P)=E_n(P)-mc^2$ and its rest energy with $mc^2$, where $E_n,q_n,T_n$ are the quantities of [[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]]; the units are the joule, kilogram metre per second and kilogram of [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]]. This clause is a formulation convention identifying mathematical quantities with the quantities the model calls measured; it is not a measurement report and no experiment is claimed. (iii) Isolated collision balance. In an isolated collision of particles at an event -- the interaction being confined to that event, with no external agent acting -- the sum of the incoming four-momenta equals the sum of the outgoing four-momenta, in the sense of [[def-sr-collision-datum-and-conservation]]. No particular collision is asserted to occur, and no mechanism, probability, cross section or amplitude is supplied by this clause. (iv) Equation of motion. Whenever an interaction is described by a stipulated force, the model's particle equation is $m\,dU/d\tau=F(x,U)$ with $F$ the four-force of [[def-sr-proper-time-derivative-and-four-force]]; a particular force law (the dependence of $F$ on position and four-velocity) and the existence, uniqueness or domain of solutions are not adopted here and belong to a separate model.
items.strategy: Postulate: an adopted physical premise, not a theorem. Obligations: (i) $P=mU$ uses the four-velocity of [[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]] with its normalisation $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$ of [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]; (ii) the measurement identification names the mathematical quantities $E_n,q_n,T_n$ of [[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]] and the SI units of [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]] and explicitly disclaims observation; (iii) conservation is stated for an isolated collision only, as an equality of the side totals of [[def-sr-collision-datum-and-conservation]], with no existence or mechanism claim; (iv) the equation of motion form is adopted only for a stipulated force, and no force law is adopted. Empirical support for the assumptions is a nonlogical relation of the framework, not a proof; the idealisations of point particles, ideal clocks and flat spacetime are inherited and must travel to consumers.
items.physical_scope: Classical massive point particles with positive constant invariant mass in flat Minkowski spacetime, with ideal clocks and ideal light and the SI conventions: the model identifies the observer quantities E_n, q_n, T_n as the measured energy, momentum and kinetic energy, and adopts exact four-momentum conservation for isolated collisions at one event. Excludes massless particles, internal structure, spin, radiation reaction, variable mass, gravity, continuum matter, quantum and statistical effects, and every empirical or measurement claim; a force law and any interaction mechanism are separate premises.

items.title: Adopted momentum model for an ideal massless particle
items.statement: Adopt as a separate model premise for ideal massless particles, independent of [[post-sr-massive-particle-dynamics]] whose formula $P=mU$ uses $m>0$ and does not define a massless case: (i) An ideal massless particle is described by a nonzero future null vector $P$ in $V$, with the SI unit kilogram metre per second of [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]]; it is not of the form $mU$ for any $m>0$ and any future timelike $U$ with $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$, and it has no four-velocity, no proper-time parametrisation and no rest frame. Its scale is fixed by a measured energy in an observer's frame. (ii) Relative to a future unit observer $n$, the model identifies the measured energy and spatial momentum of the particle with $E_n(P)$ and $q_n(P)$ of [[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]]; necessarily $E_n(P)=c\,|q_n(P)|>0$ by [[lem-sr-energy-momentum-observer-identities]]\,(a), and no rest mass, rest energy or kinetic energy is assigned. (iii) The ideal massless particle is not identified here with light, with a classical wave or with any quantum object: no frequency, wavelength, quantisation, polarisation or $\hbar$ enters, and the identification of light with massless particles requires the wave model and its own postulates on a separate page. (iv) This premise asserts no interaction of massless particles and no decay or production process; such processes require a stipulated dynamics.
items.strategy: Postulate for the massless case, kept separate because $P=mU$ at $m=0$ degenerates to $0$ ([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]: the zero vector is neither timelike, null nor spacelike) and cannot describe a nonzero null momentum. Obligations: (i) the object is a nonzero future null vector, using the causal classification and time orientation; (ii) the identification of $E_n$ and $q_n$ is a formulation convention, with the mathematical identity $E_n=c|q_n|$ supplied separately by [[lem-sr-energy-momentum-observer-identities]] and not adopted; (iii) no identification with light or with quantum concepts is made; (iv) no process is asserted. Empirical support is a nonlogical relation, not a proof.
items.physical_scope: Ideal classical massless point particles in flat Minkowski spacetime, modelled by a nonzero future null four-momentum whose energy is fixed by observation, with the model identification of measured energy and momentum. Excludes four-velocities, proper time and rest frames, any massive limit m -> 0, the identification with light or classical waves, quantum properties, and every interaction, decay, production or empirical claim.

items.title: Energy, momentum, invariant mass and four-force of relativistic particles, and necessary collision thresholds
items.statement:
Adopt [[post-sr-massive-particle-dynamics]] and [[post-sr-ideal-massless-particle-momentum]]. Then the following conditional physical claims hold in the flat classical model, with the units of [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]].
(a) Massive particle. Let a massive particle have constant mass $m>0$, four-momentum $P=mU$ and a future unit observer $n$. Its measured energy $E_n(P)=-c\eta(P,n)$, spatial momentum $q_n(P)=h(P)$ and kinetic energy $T_n(P)=E_n(P)-mc^2$ satisfy $E_n(P)>0$, $T_n(P)\ge0$ and the mass-shell identity $E_n(P)^2=m^2c^4+c^2|q_n(P)|^2$; $T_n(P)=0$ if and only if the particle is at rest in the observer's frame ($U=cn$). In an inertial frame whose stationary observer is $n=e_0$, the components are $P=(E/c,\mathbf p)$ with $E=E_{e_0}(P)=m\gamma_wc^2$ and $\mathbf p=q_{e_0}(P)=m\gamma_w\mathbf w$ for the coordinate velocity $\mathbf w$, and under a passive boost the components transform as the components of the vector $P$; the combination $E^2-c^2|\mathbf p|^2=m^2c^4$ is frame-independent.
(b) Four-force. Along a $C^2$ worldline with four-acceleration $A$, the four-force $F=\dot P$ satisfies $\eta(P,F)=0$ and $F=mA$; in an inertial frame $F=\gamma\,(\mathbf f\cdot\mathbf w/c,\mathbf f)$ and $dE/dt=\mathbf f\cdot\mathbf w$, where $\mathbf f=d\mathbf p/dt$ is the coordinate three-force. The constancy of $m$ is used; if instead $m$ is a $C^1$ variable mass parameter, then $\eta(P,F)=-mc^2\,dm/d\tau$, and the constant-mass identities are not transferred to variable-mass systems.
(c) System mass. For a finite nonempty system of particles all of whose four-momenta are nonzero future causal and whose total four-momentum $Q$ is future timelike, the invariant mass $M=\sqrt{-\eta(Q,Q)}/c$ satisfies: in the center-of-momentum frame with $e_0=Q/(Mc)$ one has $Mc^2=\sum_iE_{e_0}(P_i)$; every massive constituent has $E_{e_0}(P_i)\ge m_ic^2$, with equality exactly when it is at rest in that frame, and every massless constituent has $E_{e_0}(P_i)>0$. Hence $M\ge\sum_im_i$ over the massive constituents, with equality if and only if the system is massive-only and all its constituents are at rest in the center-of-momentum frame. If $Q$ is future null, then $M=0$, all constituents are massless with parallel momenta, and no center-of-momentum frame exists.
(d) Massless particle. An ideal massless particle has $E_n(P)=c\,|q_n(P)|>0$, has no rest frame and is not $mU$ for any $m>0$; it is not obtained from the massive formula by setting $m=0$.
(e) Necessary collision thresholds. Suppose that, under the adopted isolated-collision balance, an isolated collision occurs whose incoming legs are massive particles of constant masses $m_1,\dots,m_N$ and whose outgoing legs are massive particles of masses $\mu_1,\dots,\mu_K$ and possibly ideal massless particles. Let $M$ be the invariant mass of the common total four-momentum $Q$ when $Q$ is future timelike. Then the necessary inequalities $M\ge\sum_im_i$ and $M\ge\sum_j\mu_j$ hold; if the incoming side is a projectile of mass $m_1$ and a target of mass $m_2$ at rest in the observer frame of the target, with projectile energy $E$ and kinetic energy $T=E-m_1c^2$ in that frame, then
$$E\ \ge\ \frac{c^2}{2m_2}\Bigl[\Bigl(\sum_{j=1}^K\mu_j\Bigr)^2-m_1^2-m_2^2\Bigr],\qquad T\ \ge\ \frac{c^2}{2m_2}\Bigl[\Bigl(\sum_{j=1}^K\mu_j\Bigr)^2-(m_1+m_2)^2\Bigr],$$
and a single incoming massless particle cannot collide into an outgoing state containing a massive particle. These are kinematic necessity statements under the adopted conservation: they do not assert that any collision occurs, do not fix probabilities, amplitudes or cross sections, and are not empirical findings.
(f) Scope. All clauses are conditional on the two postulates and on the stated idealisations; the conclusions carry the same idealisations. No measurement, precision, statistical or empirical claim is made.
items.strategy: Conditional deduction assembling the page's suppliers, in this order. (a) The measurement identification is the postulate clause (ii); the identities are [[lem-sr-energy-momentum-observer-identities]]\,(b) and [[lem-sr-four-momentum-in-inertial-frame]]\,(a)-(c), with the frame-independence of $m$ from [[lem-sr-energy-momentum-observer-identities]]\,(a)(ii). (b) [[lem-sr-four-force-and-work-energy-identities]]. (c) [[lem-sr-finite-future-causal-sums]] gives the character of $Q$ and additivity, [[lem-sr-center-of-momentum-frame]] the frame and $E_{e_0}(Q)=Mc^2$, and [[lem-sr-collision-necessary-conditions]]\,(a)-(b) the constituent inequalities and the null case. (d) [[post-sr-ideal-massless-particle-momentum]] with [[lem-sr-energy-momentum-observer-identities]]\,(a)(i) and the degenerate $m=0$ computation. (e) The postulate clause (iii) makes the collision data a conserving collision datum; [[lem-sr-collision-necessary-conditions]]\,(a),(c),(d) gives exactly the displayed necessary inequalities and the one-null-leg impossibility, with the target's rest observer $n_2=U_2/c$ of clause (c). No step asserts existence of an interaction, and no empirical premise is used, so no empirical qualification is carried. Units are those of the model conventions. No choice principle is used.
items.physical_scope: Massive particles with constant positive mass and ideal massless particles described by future null four-momenta in flat Minkowski spacetime with ideal clocks and SI conventions; measured energy, momentum and kinetic energy are the model quantities E_n, q_n, T_n; isolated collisions obey the adopted four-momentum balance at one event, and the stated thresholds are necessary kinematic conditions only. Excludes variable mass, internal structure, spin, radiation reaction, force laws and interaction mechanisms (a separate premise), continuum matter, gravity, quantum and statistical descriptions, and every empirical claim, measurement value or precision statement.
